Casino Xtravaganza is a classic UK pub fruit machine manufactured and published by Mazooma Games. Released in the 2000s, it is a highly regarded piece of nostalgic arcade history built on the popular Scorpion 4 hardware platform.

True to the Mazooma style, Casino Xtravaganza blends traditional reel-spinning with a multi-layered casino-themed feature board. Players typically look to climb a cash/feature ladder, utilize standard "Nudges" and "Holds", and trigger a streak-based main event designed to mimic high-stakes casino games.
Castaway
Castaway is a video slot fruit machine by Atronic in 2002.
Castle of Dracula

Castle of Dracula is a puzzle game, developed and released by Yun Sung in 1994.

Story
The game is set in 17XX, and Dracula kidnap Lydia, a daughter of an unnamed elder from the city of Goidel. Then, the elder asks for an valiant knight called Sonnie to rescue her from Dracula's hands. Sonnie will go on to Dracula's Castle, but he (and an unnamed Player 2 palette swap character) will face numerous opponents until they reach on her.

Overview
The game is a puzzle game where you must find a way to get a key to go onto the next stage. In order to do this, you must throw a block into his respective figure. And you must do this in a certain time limit, as well with a certain number of tries.

The game is a clone of Plotting, a puzzle game for Arcade machines made by Taito in 1989. It was also released on Famicom and Game Boy as Flipull (the first one is a Japan exclusive release).
Castle Shikigami 2

Castle Shikigami 2 is a vertical shoot 'em up which puts you in control of a small fighter as you attempt to make your way past several stages filled with enemy ships charging and attacking you in different patterns.

The game features 7 distinct characters with psychic powers (which manifest in-game as bomb-type attacks and other special moves) and unique fighters, and the game features a story mode for each character, in which they have different dialogues and plot sequences for each boss fight.
Castlevania

A PlayChoice-10 arcade game.

You play Simon who must battle his way through the castle using his trusty whip. The object is to fight off the evil enemies on your way to find the Count, and if you're lucky, destroy him.
Castlevania: The Arcade

Castlevania: The Arcade is an arcade game, part of the Castlevania franchise by Konami. The game was announced on July 23, 2008. The game was released in Japan on October 2, 2009. A European release was announced for 2009 but only appeared at test locations in 2008.

The gameplay is similar to light gun shooters such as The House of the Dead. Players utilize a special LED whip remote. The remote has two buttons. A top thumb button used to activate the whip, prompting players to swing the remote at the screen to damage enemies. A bottom button for the index finger is used to activate subweapons, such as knives or crosses. Subweapons are refilled by collecting hearts (up to 25) strewn about each stage in the form of destructible candles and wooden crates.

Up to two players can play the game at once. Characters in the game include the Vampire Hunter, the Lady Gunner, and the Little Witch.
Cat 'N Mouse

Cat'N Mouse was produced by Zaccaria in 1981.

A colorful game where a cat chases and tries to catch mice while avoiding deadly enemies.
Catacomb
Catacomb is a rare, early vertical shooter arcade game released in 1982 by the manufacturer MTM Games.
Catapult

Catapult was produced by Photar in 1982.

The player controls a dog named Bruno who must catapult cats and mice out of his owner's house before the cats destroy all the furniture.
Catch

Catch was a prototype produced by Atari in 1977.

Move a stack of paddles left and right to catch falling rocks. This was an early prototype version if 1978's Avalanche.
Caterpillar
Caterpillar is a Centipede bootleg import game from Italy by a company named Olympia.
Caterpillar (Phi)

This game is a hack of "Hangly Man", itself a "Pac-Man" hack.

You are a little caterpillar, trying to eat enough to grow into a butterfly. Four spiders are crawling around, trying to catch you to eat. Keep running, and even you may live to eat spiders (thanks to energizers).
Cats & Mice

Cats and Mice Hammer Game where various targets rotate as they pop up! One side is a cat, the other a mouse! You can link up to 8 games for group play! Great sound effects and very colorful graphics. Adjustable timer and ticket awards!
Cavelon

Gather up all the pieces to escape the castle then battle the dark wizard. Use the Magic Sword to destroy all enemies on the screen. Grab the floating sword to get a second Magic Sword in the same level.

In this horizontally-scrolling maze game, You the heroic knight must reach the top floor of Castle Cavelon, rescue a fair maiden and do battle with the Black Wizard! Armed with bow and arrow and a magic sword, you must avoid or kill the castle security guards while collecting the 8 pieces of the exit door that are scattered around the corridors, in order to proceed to the next floor.

While this game wasn't massively popular, it did have a cult following in Europe, particularly in the UK. It even got ported to most of the popular 8-bit microcomputers such as the ZX Spectrum and C64 at the time.﻿
Caveman Clobber

Caveman Clobber is a redemption game from Bay-Tek. Gameplay involves the player dropping eggs one at a time onto the cavemen below. Two eggs on one caveman ends the game. Games can be banked and a 3-D progressive can be added. The machine also has a prehistoric red bird which rotates from side to side.
Caveman Ninja

Joe & Mac also known as Caveman Ninja, is a 1991 platform game released for the arcades by Data East. It was later adapted for the Super NES, Genesis, Nintendo Entertainment System, Game Boy, Amiga, and PC.

The game stars the green-haired Joe and the blue-haired Mac, cavemen who battle through numerous prehistoric levels using weapons such as boomerangs, bones, fire, flints, electricity, stone wheels, and clubs. The objective of the game is to rescue a group of women who were kidnapped by a rival tribe of cavemen.
Cavemania

The Cavemania arcade machine is a rare prehistoric-themed ticket redemption cabinet manufactured by Meltec, Inc. and released around 2000. Unlike traditional pixel-art video games from the era, this unique machine blends the manual skills of a rolling ball game with the mechanics of a casino-style attraction to reward players with tickets.

Players pull or trigger a mechanism to time the release of physical balls down the playfield.
Celebration Club

Topping out twenty one years of machine manufacturing success Barcrest announce CELEBRATION CLUB.
A fitting salute, CELEBRATION CLUB offers more than ever before – a superb casino-style cabinet, a magically attractive card-fan display and a pack of prize-winning features designed to keep any player deliriously happy and shouting – 3 cheers for BARCREST.
The only question-mark about CELEBRATION CLUB is the one the reels that introduces FOUR fast ways to complete the card-fan – BOOST, SUPER-FILL, LINK and SKILL.
Once the player has turned over all the cards in the fan he’s on the prize filled featured ladder and only a HI-LO gamble away from success every time. To make life easier he can even request ANOTHER CARD to improve his gamble chances and climb the big-money ladder.
Center Court
Released in July 1988 in Japan. Prototype game (MC-8123B)
Centipede

Centipede is a fixed-screen shooter in which the player controls a Bug Blaster defending the lower portion of a mushroom-filled playfield from waves of giant insects. In the arcade version, a trackball moves the Bug Blaster freely within its restricted area, while the fire button launches darts and can be held for rapid fire. The objective is to survive for as long as possible and earn points by destroying the centipede and the other creatures that enter the screen.

The centipede begins at the top and travels horizontally until it reaches a mushroom or the edge of the playfield, causing it to descend one row and reverse direction. Shooting one of its segments converts that segment into a mushroom. If a middle segment is destroyed, the centipede separates into two independently moving sections, with the rear section developing a new head.
Centipede / Millipede / Missile Command

This 'Team Play' Retrocade game brings "Centipede", "Millipede" and "Missile Command" back together in one cabinet. Players are transported back to the early 1980's to stop the marauding insect invasions of "Centipede" and "Millipede" or prevent total world annihilation in the Cold War classic game of Armageddon, "Missile Command".
Centipede / Millipede / Missile Command / Let's Go Bowling

Centipede/Millipede/Missile Command was produced by Team Play in 2001.

A new combo game containing three Atari classics in one, plus a bowling game that has the look and feel of the early 1980's.
Centipede Chaos

Centipede Chaos, the hit 80’s classic crawler game is back to take over arcades around the globe! Cosmetically this game has some incredible features that make it stand out from the crowd. The three LED-lit stools not only provide comfort for the players but are also very appealing in the game room. The huge 75-inch monitor brings the graphics to life and “Chaos” even closer. The oversized joysticks offer intuitive gameplay for all ages!

Players must use the joystick and fire button to move their ship and blast down the creepy crawlies. Incorporating many fun power-ups and challenging bosses adds excitement as well as depth to the gameplay. Get through all 10 waves using the continue feature, to defeat the Mega Spider Boss and win the mega ticket bonus.
Ceptor
Ceptor is a electromechanical slot machine from Barcrest. The year of release is not currently known.
Cerberus
The player controls a planetary salvage ship high above a planet. He/she must capture as many pods as possible before the time runs out or alien ravagers take the pods for themselves.
Chack'n Pop

Chack'n Pop was developed and released by Taito in 1983.

Chack'n Pop is considered a predecessor of Bubble Bobble. It is a platform game where a roundish yellow creature, named Chack'n, must fight against Monstas and Mightas in order to reclaim hearts that were stolen during a romantic encounter with Miss Chack'n.

The Monstas themselves hatch from eggs hanging from the ceilings and the Mightas push a rock that is used as the game's timer. The Monsta eggs have three phases: if it's blue, it's completely harmless, if it's yellow it will pop within 10 seconds and if an egg turns red it will pop almost immediately.

Chack'n uses bombs to blow up the Monstas and their eggs and he also uses them to release the captured hearts from their cages. When the heart is released, it will fly up and destroy the separator block and reveal the exit to the level.

Most versions of the game contain 14 levels to play through, however the Famicom version only includes 9.
Chain Reaction

Magical Drop, is a series of puzzle games first released in the arcade, and later primarily for several platforms such as the Neo Geo Arcade, Super Famicom, Sega Saturn, PlayStation, Bandai WonderSwan, GBC and the Neo Geo Pocket Color; most of which were published by Data East.

 The game received an updated version named Magical Drop Plus 1!. Which adds a Solo Play mode that challenges players to obtain a high score without having to battle an AI opponent. Magical Drop Plus 1! was released in English as Chain Reaction.
Challenger

A frantic single-screen shoot'em'up in the vein of Jeff Minter, Challenger has you in your craft at the bottom of the screen, shooting bursts of three shots at 45° angles at flashing polygons. When hit, the polygons split into smaller ones, like in Asteroids or Pang. Your task is interrupted by incoming squiggly lines which will destroy your ship unless you hit it before it reaches the floor. Furthermore, a walking car or robot creature like the AT-ATs of Star Wars sometimes enter the screen, giving you bonus points if you locate your ship below it. As a safety measure, you have a smart bomb that damages everything onscreen, as well as the ability to change sides to the top of the screen if it gets too crowded at the bottom.
Chameleon

A colorful platform game where the player controls a chameleon that loves eating eggs produced by the antagonist, who is a giant hen. There are also other chickens to contend with, which can kill you if they touch any part of your body aside from your tongue, which can kill them. Also there are bombs you can use to kill chickens as well.
Chameleon 24

Chameleon 24 is a piece of hardware made by Amusement Game and released in 2002. It is a multi-game Arcade machine, but in reality, is just a Famiclone in an arcade cabinet.

The machine contains 24 games onto the PCB:

01. Star Soldier
02. Goonies (The Goonies)
03. Bros. II (Super Mario Bros. with world selection enabled)
04. Grading (Gradius with power-ups already available hack)
05. Legendry (The Legend of Kage)
06. B-Wings
07. Exerion (with infinite rapid-fire single shots hack)
08. Front Line
09. Macross (Choujikuu Yousai Macross)
10. Arkanoid (with normal Pad hack)
 11. Islander (Takahashi Meijin no Bouken Shima, known Overseas as Hudson's Adventure Island)
12. Nut's & Milk (Nuts & Milk)
13. Pacman (Pac-Man)
14. Battle City
15. Digdug (Dig Dug)
16. Pooyan
17. TwinBee
18. Donkey Kong
19. Spartan-X (known as Kung-Fu overseas)
20. Galaxian (with rapid-fire hack)
21. Star Force (Famicom version with rapid-fire hack)
22. Xevious
23. Galaga
24. Pinball
Chameleon RX-1

Chameleon RX-1 is an arcade machine marketed by Covielsa with exclusive distribution for Europe of the game from the Korean company Digital Sunnil. 18-inch LCD monitor, a body with a Woofer system.

It includes two game modes: Apache (Star Fall), with three different scenarios, and Tank Hunter, a tank simulator with which you can defend a strategic position in 3 scenarios. Both games include the possibility of playing online and interconnecting up to 4 machines.
Champion Baseball

Champion Baseball (チャンピオン ベースボール) is a 1983 baseball arcade game developed by Alpha Denshi and published by Sega. The game was a sophisticated sports game for its time, displaying the playfield using multiple camera angles, including a close-up shot of the batter and pitcher, and giving players the option of selecting relief pitchers or pinch hitters, while an umpire looks on attentively to make the game calls. The game became very popular in Japanese arcades when released in 1983, at one point enjoying a level of popularity comparable to Space Invaders according to Sega.
Champion Baseball II

Champion Baseball II (チャンピオンベースボールII), also known as Champion Base Ball Part-2: Pair Play is the sequel to Champion Baseball developed and released by ADK in 1983. It was originally distributed in Japan by SNK, however US distribution was handled by Sega, who in turn passed on responsibilities to Wico.

Champion Baseball II was not ported to home systems and is not thought to have been as successful as its predecessor. A further sequel, Super Champion Baseball, was released in 1989 but Sega was not involved in that release.
Champion Boxing

A straightforward championship boxing game from Sega. You can select several punches during a boxing match: straight, jab or upper. Don't get cornered and if you get hit then get up your defenses or step back. The matches can be played at four different levels of difficulty. In the game there is a referee, who counts when your opponent or you are down. The matches can be set at four difficulty levels.
Champion League
Champion League is a video casino poker card game by IGS in 2000.
Champion Number
An Italian pirate video casino game from 1999, it is a clone of the Champion Super 3 configuration and two versions were released in 1999, the first in October. The manufacturer is unknown.
Champion Poker
Champion Poker is an Italian video poker game developed and manufactured by IGS in 1993.
Champion Poker 2
Champion Poker is an Italian video poker game developed and manufactured by IGS in 2000.
Champion Pro Wrestling

A straightforward Pro Wrestling game from Sega in the Champion sport series. You always start at rank C and have to fight your way up to rank B and A. To play for a rank you 'll have to fight three matches. Winning two out of three matches promotes you to an higher rank. During a match several moves can be selected: chop, kick, pile driver, dropkick. The referee does a countdown when your opponent or you are down.
Champion Skill

The "Champion Skill" fruit machine (often classified as an SWP or Skill With Prize machine) is a classic piece of amusement history originally manufactured by IGS (International Games System) in the late 1980s and early 1990s.

Unlike a standard pub fruit machine (AWP or Amusement With Prize) which relies heavily on chance, spinning reels, nudges, and programmed payout percentages, Champion Skill was engineered as a video-based card/poker and symbol game that legally incorporated a "skill" or "ability" dynamic to comply with or navigate gaming legislation.
Champion Super 2

Champion Super II (often stylised as Champion Super 2) is a classic Italian video poker game originally released on arcade cabinets in January 1999. Operating on specialized JAMMA-compatible boards, it became a staple of European bar and arcade gambling culture in the late '90s and early 2000s.

The game functions as a standard "draw poker" machine with highly customisable arcade system limits and payout logic:

• The Draw: Players place a bet, are dealt five cards on a CRT raster display, and choose which cards to "Hold". Pressing draw replaces the unheld cards to build the final poker hand.
Champion Super 3

Champion Super 3 is a 1999 video slot/casino arcade game that runs on traditional arcade hardware and can be emulated via platforms like MAME.

It is classified as a casino/cherry master style video game rather than a standard fighting or racing arcade cabinet. It features traditional luck mechanics, credit banking, and risk features like a "Double Up Bonus" (W-UP BONUS).
Champion Wrestler

Champion Wrestler is a wrestling game where you have the choice of eight fighters to become champion. You have various moves to use to beat your opponent into submission including kicks, punches and throws. The action is viewed from the side at an elevated angle showing the whole ring. If you leave the ring you have a small time limit to get back into the ring or it's fight over. Up to four players can play and the multi-player options are one player versus the computer, two players fighting each other, two players fighting together against the computer or four players split into two teams fighting each other.
Championship Bowling
A bowling game by Romstar. This game also got a port to the NES in the same year as the arcade version.
Championship Sprint

This is the sequel to the coin-op hit Super Sprint. One or two players race the 8 new tracks which once again are shown from an overhead view of the racetrack. There are some obstacles, like the whirlwind or oil-slicks, which should keep you from going around the track too easily. But Championship Sprint is not only an update with 8 new tracks. The main improvement is a complete track editor. With this you have the freedom to construct unlimited tracks, with all kind of obstacles and you even can set options like number of laps and number of players.
Champiyon Pinball

Champiyon Pinball (também conhecido em japonês como Tsuukai! Goraku Katsugeki: Champiyon Pinball) é um jogo de pinball eletrônico lançado originalmente em 2003 exclusivamente no Japão. O título foi desenvolvido pela SSD Company LTD e distribuído pela gigante dos brinquedos Tomy.

Diferente dos consoles tradicionais, ele foi concebido como um sistema Plug n' Play TV Game, um hardware dedicado em que o próprio controle/console é conectado diretamente nas entradas de áudio e vídeo da televisão. O jogo roda sob a arquitetura clássica dos chips multiprocessadores XaviX, uma tecnologia inovadora da época focada em interatividade e sensores de movimento. Na emulação moderna, o título é totalmente preservado e executado por meio de drivers do ecossistema MAME (arquivo tomcpin.zip).
Chan Bara

Chan Bara is a fighting game, developed and published by Data East, which was released in Japan in 1985.

You play a student samurai and defend the dojo temple. One joystick controls the movement, one controls the katana. In the first level, enemies attack from two different floors. You can switch between the floors to stop the enemies on the upper floor hitting you from above. One hit and you are dead. There are several gruesome ways to die.
Chance Kun

Arcade Video game published 38 years ago:

Chance Kun © 1982 Unknown.

A one player game of gambling bet based on a baseball game, starring by fun cats.
Chance Thirty Two
Chance Thirty Two is an adult themed video card game developed and published by PAL System in a thus far unknown year.
Change Air Blade

Change Air Blade is a 2D vertical scrolling shooter, based on a "boss rush" idea. The player can select one from eight different ships (each ship has its own special form), and fights against another ships. Basically, each normal enemy is boss, with a long life bar, and has support from smaller minions. The player has the main gun and several bombs to use, and must win an air duel with the boss to progress.
Change Lanes

Change Lanes is a racing arcade game which was released by Taito America Corporation in 1983.

The player must use a steering wheel and gear shifter to take control of an amphibious red car (with a single pedal, to make it accelerate). It can drive anywhere, on roads and in rivers, and can crash into CPU-controlled cars or scenery objects countless times; however, doing so consumes fuel and once the car runs out of fuel, the game is over.
Changes

The player controls a caterpillar that crawls along the branches of a maze-like tree eating nuts and strawberries while avoiding deadly bugs and a hungry bird. The caterpillar changes into a butterfly after everything has been eaten.

The game is quite similar to Pac-Man.

The caterpillar must eat all the nuts and strawberries in order to become a butterfly.
Eating a strawberry temporarily makes the caterpillar invincible allowing it to kill the deadly bugs and score bonus points. The caterpillar can only run away from the hungry bird when it appears on the screen. Whenever the caterpillar leaves a turning branch, all the turning branches will rotate at once, and any bugs that are on those branches will fall off and score 400, 800, 1600 and even 3200 points. The caterpillar can also eat the beautiful flowers to score bonus points.

After you have clear the entire screen of all the nuts and strawberries, the caterpillar will change into a colorful butterfly.
Chao Ji Da Heng 2

"Chao Ji Da Heng 2" (Chinese: 超級大亨 2 / "Super Tycoon 2") is an arcade gambling and video slot/poker game developed by the Taiwanese amusement manufacturer IGS (International Games System). Released in the early 2000s, it runs on specialized IGS036-based hardware and is predominantly found in East Asian arcade markets, featuring Chinese text and voiceovers.
Chaoji Da Manguan II

Chaoji Da Manguan II (超级大满贯II) is a classic Mahjong arcade game released in 1997 by the Taiwanese developer International Games System (IGS). It belongs to a popular genre of token-based or gambling-style ("BET") Mahjong arcade machines that were widely distributed across China and other parts of Asia during the late 1990s.
Chaoji Dou Dizhu

Chaoji Dou Dizhu is a single player game of the traditional Chinese game, Dou Dizhu (Fighting the Landlord). A popular gambling card game that is easy to learn but hard to master. The player plays against 3 CPU players. All players review and appraise their own cards. Then everyone bids on the strength of their cards. Highest bidder bidder takes the role of landord and the game plays out.
Chaoji Dou Dizhu Jiaqiang Ban

Chaoji Dou Dizhu Jiaqiang Ban (Super Landlord Enhanced Edition) is an arcade adaptation of the Chinese card game Dou Dizhu (“Fight the Landlord”). Players compete to win rounds of card play while wagering credits.

The game follows standard Dou Dizhu rules for three participants. Cards are dealt, and one player becomes the “landlord” while the other two act as opponents. Players must form valid combinations such as singles, pairs, straights, or bombs to play cards and deplete their hands before others.

In the arcade version, bets are placed before each round, and payouts depend on winning hands and multipliers. The interface displays cards, bet amounts, remaining credits, and action prompts such as “Pass.” The system allows timed decisions and animated opponents to maintain play flow.
Chaos Breaker

Running on Taito's Type X arcade board, Chaos Breaker is a fantasy-themed sprite-based 2D fighting game with characters that look to be out of the Dungeon's & Dragons or World of Warcraft realm. Players select a team of three characters, much like in the King of Fighters series. There are six different races featured in the game including: human, dark elf, elf, ork, dwarf and undead.
Chaos Code
Chaos Code (カオスコード Kaosu Kōdo) is a fighting game developed by FK Digital and published by Arc System Works. The game was released for Sega's RingWide arcade system board on August 4, 2011.
Chaos Code: New Sign of Catastrophe

CHAOS CODE -NEW SIGN OF CATASTROPHE- is a simple yet highly flexible hi-speed 2D Fighting game, where players can enjoy the thrill of fighting with all the flashy moves!
There are 7 game modes in the game. Online play is also available for players connected to the internet.
Choose from 16 unique characters, and fight in the Rank Matches to claim the top!
Chaos Field

The technological advancements of mankind discover a dimension of absolute chaos that its discoverers soon called the Chaos Field. Upon its discovery, the overly destructive inhabitants of the Chaos Field, known as the Abo, invaded Earth which is considered the Orderfield. The war raged so long that special pilots were selected to fly the best star fighters equipped with trans-dimensional technology to combat the Abo and save the Orderfield.
Chaos Heat
Chaos Heat is a 3D hack 'n slash with modern weapons like flamethrowers, machineguns, and grenades. Players have to battle against zombie like creatures in a biotech lab.
Charlie Ninja

Charlie Ninja is a 2D side-scrolling platform game that puts players in the shoes of a ninja that throws throwing stars and other typical eastern weapons at enemies. The player can also cloak himself so that he becomes invisible for enemies and can evade attacks. Melee attacks are also possible.

Each of the stages has a different theme and a boss with a bounty at the end. The settings for the stage are the wild west, army, dilapidated industrial zone, football stadium and a mad scientists lab. Enemies attack the player directly or shoot projectiles at them. Weapon power-ups can be collected from defeated enemies and sometimes fire walls have to be circumvented. The game can be played solo or with a friend.
Chase

Chase (often catalogued as Chase1) is an incredibly rare, first-person air combat arcade game released in 1976 by the US-based manufacturer Allied Leisure Industries.

The game tasks the player with piloting a jet plane through first-person aerial combat, maneuvering to lock onto and shoot down enemy aircraft. It was released alongside a sister biplane combat game named Ace. Though highly advanced for 1976, Allied Leisure went into bankruptcy shortly after its release, which prevented Chase from receiving wide distribution.
Chase 1929
An unreleased Sammy Atomiswave game that was created in 2004.
Chase Bombers

WELCOME TO THE CUSTOMIZED CAR CARNIVAL!
Choose your Vehicle and one of the challenging race courses. Rev your engine and get ready to roll. Be careful - there are mines and steel poles as obstacles to slow you down. Rival racers attack and obstruct you with items. You must avoid their traps and use your own items to your advantage. Pick them up on the Item Gates spread across the course. Use your specialized arsenal to crash the enemy drivers and race for the checkered flag!

There are five customized vehicles to choose from, including a Formula-One machine and a custom truck.
Chase Chase Jokers

Chase Chase Jokers is an action game where players race in a maze collecting keys and have to avoid being tagged by their opponents. It can be played up to 6 players simultaneously, in a 3vs3 tag mode. The game is divided into two teams; the "Human" team and the "Monster" team, each team consisting of 3 players. Teams are randomly attributed at the start of the game.
Chase H.Q.

Chase H.Q. (Chase Headquarters) is a 1988 arcade racing game, released by Taito. It is a spiritual successor of Taito's 1987 Full Throttle. The player assumes the role of a police officer named Tony Gibson, member of the "Chase Special Investigation Department." Along with his partner, Raymond Broady, he must stop fleeing criminals in high-speed pursuits.
Chase H.Q. 2

The player takes control of three main vehicles. One of which is a modern stock sports car, a patrol sports car and a striped muscle car. Each level consists of one simple goal of racing to the end with the intent of defeating the villain vehicle, which has to be damaged enough to be taken down and the criminals taken into custody. Some villains have tricky tactics that make gameplay more challenging. Gameplay is also based on a point system.
Chase Invaders

"Super Animation Chase Invaders" is a rare, classic UK pub club fruit machine manufactured by Barcrest in the 1990s. It originally featured a low-tier jackpot typical of its era (such as a £6 jackpot version) and is highly sought after by retro arcade enthusiasts and collectors today.
Chav It!

The Chav It! fruit machine is a classic UK pub slot game manufactured by Bell-Fruit Games. It is heavily themed around British "chav" subculture stereotypes from the 2000s, featuring satirical graphics, sound bites, and gameplay elements.
Check Man

You control a man who must walk over blocks to get the time bombs.

The screen is broken up into 14 x 13 tiles or checks. When the player passes over the tiles, they disappear so each tile can only be walked over once per level. Some tiles are taken up by skull and crossbones which kill the player if walked into. The skulls turn to time bombs one at a time and the player must walk over them to defuse them before they explode. They must avoid the skulls and make sure they do not block off a possible future route by circling it. Some tiles are also flags which can be collected for bonus points. When all skulls have turned to bombs and been defused, the level is complete and begins again at a harder level. As the game develops, stomping boots are introduced that move around the playing area. These are also deadly to the player.
Checkmate

Checkmate is an arcade game, that was released by Midway Games in 1977. 

It utilizes an Intel 8080 microprocessor (running at 1.9968 MHz), and was the first game from the company that allowed up to four players to play simultaneously. All four players must use a 4-way joystick and take up control of a snake-like line which leaves a trail behind it (if there are less than four players, the remaining lines will be controlled by the CPU) - and the objective is to force all other lines, regardless of whether they are player- or CPU-controlled, into the walls or your own trails (much like in Gremlin Industries' Blockade, Comotion and Hustle).

Every time one line gets forced into a wall or another line, the text "PLAYER X CHECKS OUT/MEETS HIS MAKER/PRONOUNCED DEAD" (X being 1, 2, 3, or 4), will appear at the bottom of the screen; once there is only one line left, it's declared the winner of the current round and will receive a single point.
Cheeky Mouse
Try to hit the mouse with a hammer when it comes out from one of many holes in the wall. The mouse is trying to get from its hole to the cheese on the other side of the house.
Cheese Chase

In this arcade game developed by French company Art & Magic, you play a mouse who must avoid rats and bombs while collecting cheese in a maze. You are able to open and close doors to help you elude your enemies. The game uses an overhead perspective with very big sprites and a multi-directional scrolling playfield.
Chequered Flag
Chequered Flag is a racing game, released by Konami in 1988.
Cherry Angel

Cherry Angel is a classic 8-liner / Cherry Master electronic fruit machine game that was highly popular in bars, truck stops, and amusement venues throughout the 1990s and 2000s. Originally built on standard CGA arcade hardware boards, it features traditional fruit symbols, card-based double-up gambles, and localized bonus

The game typically runs on an 8-line grid layout where players bet credits across horizontal, vertical, and diagonal patterns to trigger specialized bonuses like "Fruit Bonus 96" or "Pot-O-Gold" mechanics.
Cherry Bingo

Cherry Bingo generally refers to online gaming platforms or specific slot machine styles that blend classic British fruit machine mechanics with bingo-style bonus structures. In the world of traditional coin-operated gaming, "fruit machines" are known for their nostalgic icons—most notably cherries, which historically served as the original low-stakes payout symbol.
Cherry Bonus 2001

The Cherry Bonus 2001 (often cross-referenced with the Fruit Bonus 2000 / New Cherry 2000 series) is a classic 8-liner video slot game developed by Amcoe. Falling under the umbrella of "Cherry Master" style games, these fruit machines were staple fixtures in convenience stores, gas stations, bars, and clubs during the late 1990s and early 2000s.
Cherry Bonus III

Cherry Bonus III is a legendary retro arcade slot machine (fruit machine) developed and published by DYNA in 1990 (often cataloged alongside earlier late-70s and 80s Cherry Master iterations). It features a classic 3x3 reel matrix, an 8-line betting system, and a signature card-based "double-up" bonus game that defined 90s arcade and pub gambling halls.
Cherry Chance

The Cherry Chance fruit machine series by Aruze Gaming is a popular lineup of classic-style stepper slot machines found in casinos, known for their traditional reel style combined with a unique bonus feature.
Cherry Master

The Cherry Master fruit machine is a legendary 8-liner video slot game that became a staple of bars, clubs, and grey-market gaming locations during the late 1980s and 1990s. Unlike traditional mechanical slot machines, Cherry Master pioneered the use of a electronic CRT video display and a 3x3 grid layout with up to 9 selectable paylines, allowing players to match classic fruit, bar, and lucky number 7 symbols.
Cherry Master '91

Cherry Master '91 is a highly influential, classic electronic video slot machine released in 1991 by Dyna. Operating on the specialized "Golden Star" hardware platform, it became a staple of bars, clubs, amusement arcades, and bowling alleys during the early to mid-1990s. Classified heavily as a "redemption game," players could win tickets, tokens, or accumulated credits rather than direct cash payouts depending on regional gambling laws.
Cherry Master '97

The Cherry Master ’97 is a highly popular, classic 8-liner video slot game manufactured by Dyna Corporation. In the amusement industry, "Cherry Master" became a genericized trademark used to describe almost all 8-liner and multi-liner fruit machine boards that followed it.

Unlike traditional casino slot machines, these were typically operated as "amusement with prize" machines in convenience stores, bars, gas stations, and clubs.
Cherry Master '99
The Cherry Master '99 is a classic electronic 8-liner video slot / fruit machine that was widely popular in bars, arcades, and "grey-market" gaming venues during the late 1990s and 2000s.
Cherry Master I

The Cherry Master (often associated with original 8-liner boards by companies like Amcoe or Dyna) is one of the most iconic electronic fruit machines and arcade-style slot games ever made. Known globally as a staple of bars, clubs, and amusement arcades, it popularized the "8-liner" format. This format uses a grid where players win across 3 horizontal, 3 vertical, and 2 diagonal lines.
Chess Partner 2000
Originally released as two different models of Chess Computer in 1980 by Novag and SciSys respectively. The program can now be emulated in a MAME software environment with a Graphic User Interface.
Chewing Gum
Chewing Gum is a video slot fruit machine by an unknown company.
Cheyenne

A shooting game, with a western motif. The player uses a gun (mounted to the cabinet) to escort the sheriff through a variety of dangers, gathering bounty for capturing criminals.

In this game, you must protect lawman Buster Badshot from some of the most wanted outlaws in the West. Each level has three or more stages that can be chosen in any order by simply shooting the hanging picture. These stages are set in places like saloons, mines, deserts, forests, ghost towns, graveyards and canyons. After all the stages have been completed, you move on to a bonus target practice stage where if all the objects are hit within the time limit, you are awarded a Bonus Buster. At the conclusion of the bonus stage, you increase levels where new stages await.
On each stage, Buster Badshot will encounter many perils and be attacked by a variety of enemies as he travels. You must shoot any attacker or object that will harm him.
Chi-Toitsu

Chi-Toitsu: Ichiman Satte Mata Ichiman is a classic Japanese mahjong arcade game released in February 1988 by the developer Yuga.

The game centers around traditional Japanese Riichi Mahjong, where you play matches against various anime-styled schoolgirl characters. It runs on a classic Zilog Z80 CPU and was built for standard tabletop arcade cabinets utilizing a specialized mahjong keyboard layout rather than a typical joystick setup.
Chibi Maruko-chan ~Minna de Sugoroku Asobi~ no Maki

Chibi Maruko-chan ~Minna de Sugoroku Asobi~ no Maki is a rare Japanese medal arcade game (video-based prize/coin pusher machine) developed and published by Capcom. Initially released around 2004, the game runs on Capcom's proprietary Medalusion arcade hardware architecture.
Chibi Marukochan Deluxe Quiz

Chibi Maruko-chan Deluxe Quiz is a quiz game released in 1996 by Takara for the Neo Geo in Japan only. It is based on the Chibi Maruko-chan manga series.

Overview
Chibi Maruko-chan Deluxe Quiz is framed as a trivia variety TV show, with the many characters competing on it. Players must pick two characters from the twelve available characters to form a team of three along with the protagonist Maruko, with each character having its own special attributes. In between the rounds of questions the player will also have to beat small minigames in order to progress.
Chicken Draw

Chicken Draw was produced by Merit Industries in 1984.

A poker game from Merit that features a chicken.
Chicken Farm

Chicken Farm was produced by LAI in 1999.

A simple and easy to understand video redemption game. Incorporates cute characters, great music and sound effects.
Chicken Shift

Chicken Shift is an arcade game which was released by Bally and Sente (in 1984); it was one of the initial batch of eight games to run upon their then-new SAC-I hardware (a Motorola M6809 running at 1.25 MHz with a Zilog Z80 running at 4 MHz). 

The players must use two buttons to make metal pipes which are coloured blue (for 1P) or red (for 2P) turn to face left or right, so the eggs the four chickens at the top of the screen shall be laying shall roll down the pieces of wood (some of them have arrows saying "TERMITES" pointing at them which means that they will crumble after a single egg rolls over them), and into the basket at the bottom of the screen - because if one should fall off and splatter on the ground below, it will cost both players one shared life.
Chickendales

The Chickendales fruit machine is a retro casino slot game originally created by the manufacturer Atronic in 2001 and later adapted/published by UK-based Mazooma Games. A parody of the famous "Chippendales" male dance troupe, the game features cartoon dancing chickens dressed in collars and cuffs.
Chiller

Chiller is a first person shooter for one or two players. Back in the middle ages a castle on the outskirts of town has been invaded by an evil force which is causing the dead to come back to life! You need to stop this force before it can create a large army and take over the town. As you make your way to and eventually inside the castle, numerous dead creatures will be trying to stop you.

Each level has a monster counter, and you need to shoot this many monsters before the timer runs out to continue on. Each level also has 8 talismans hidden in it; you need to find and destroy these to stop the monsters from appearing. If you complete a level without destroying all of the talismans, you will need to return to the level later on. There are 32 talismans in all that need to be destroyed in order to rid the town of the monsters!
Chilli Con Cash

Chilli Con Cash is slot fruit machine by AGI (Austrian Gaming Industries) in 2003.

Got the taste for something hot? Get into the swing of the party and experience the excitement of the FIESTA Feature. The reels heat up as each swing at the PIÑATA delivers an explosion of burning hot CHILLIS across the screen increasing your winnings. Let your players party with this 9-line 5-reel video slot. There's no siesta while Chilli Con Cash is around.

CHILLI substitutes for all symbols except PIÑATA and MAN. Scattered MAN and PIÑATA trigger the FIESTA Feature. MAN hits PIÑATA for CHILLIS to fly out as the reels respin. The Free Game Fiesta ends when no more CHILLIS come out of the PIÑATA.
Chimera Beast

Chimera Beast takes place on a planet which is described as distant and Earth-like. The planet is overrun by animals known as eaters, capable of eating other creatures and acquiring their abilities or characteristics. The player controls one of these eaters and progresses through the game by means of the Food chain, consuming microscopic organisms in the first stage, fish in the second, and so on. 
There are two possible endings: one in which the player is able to stop the eaters from escaping the planet, and one in which the eaters do escape and, we are told, will eventually make their way to Earth.

The chief innovation of Chimera Beast is its power-up system; The eater enhances itself by eating other creatures and assuming their abilities and defenses. Consuming a crustacean might give the player's eater a hard protective shell, for example, while an insectoid creature might offer a poisonous tail instead. The game even includes the ability to use cancer as a weapon.
China Gate

China Gate is a 2D side-scrolling beat 'em-up game with platform elements for one or two players. The game offers a roster of three characters to choose from who have to recover a stolen book. These are the monkey man Gocoo, pig man Hakai and bird man Gojou.

There are 3 buttons, one to jump, another to attack and another for power-ups. There is a limited time to defeat the numerous enemies that appear and jump through the platforms to harm the player. At the end of each level there is final boss. It is possible to obtain power-ups like beams that neutralize all the visible enemies of the screen.
China Town

Line up three tiles in a row either vertically, horizontally or in an 'L' like shape. The tiles must be three the same or in sequential order by either Japanese character or numerical. You are trying to create a mahjong set or hand in a limited amount of time.

The game looks like a cross between mahjong and Tetris. After completing a level on some games you can play a pump game where you try to pump up your opponent's balloon until it bursts.
Chinese Casino
Chinese Casino is a mahjong gambling game. It was developed by V-System and released in Japan in 1987.
Chinese Hero

Kung-Fu masters Jacky and Lee (Lee and Loo in the arcade version) return to their kingdom from a long trip. They discover that in their absence, Princess Min-min has been kidnapped and the 10 treasures of the kingdom stolen. Jacky and Lee must fight their way into eight different castles in order to defeat the monsters and rescue the princess.

Chinese Hero is a top-down action game for one or two players, both playing on the same screen. Each ninja has the ability to move in any of four directions: up, down, left and right, as well as punch directly in front of them and do a "Moon Sault Kick" (which can be powered up to a "Miracle Kick") whereby they jump and somersault directly in front. Both punches and the Moon Sault Kick can harm enemies. Defeating a certain number of enemies on each level will open the doorway into the next level. Occasionally extra passages (named "Quick Passage Zone") can be found to take shortcuts through areas with stronger enemies.
Chip'n Dale: Rescue Rangers

Chip 'n Dale Rescue Rangers is a platformer video game developed and published by Capcom based on the Disney animated series of the same name. Originally released for the Nintendo Entertainment System in Japan and North America in 1990, it came to Europe the next year, and was ported to the Nintendo PlayChoice-10 arcade system
Choky! Choky!

Yet another clone of Buster Brothers / Pang! / Pomping World - this one featuring low-budget music and sound effects, and split-screen competitive two-player action, somewhat reminiscent of Twinkle Star Sprites.
Choplifter

Choplifter is a side-scrolling action/arcade game that puts you in command of an attack chopper. Your mission: Go behind enemy lines and rescue up to 16 hostages per level. Be careful, though, because tanks and enemy aircraft will try to stop you - and they won't stop shooting while you are rescuing those hostages!

Originally released for Apple II home computers, Choplifter was later ported to the arcades and a number of video game consoles. Many imitators and homages would follow.
Chopper

Released by Allied Leisure Industries in 1974, Chopper is a rare, electro-mechanical and early solid-state motorcycle drag-racing arcade machine. Rather than using a video monitor, the game features a physical, fluorescent plastic 1970s chopper motorcycle figurine enclosed inside the cabinet. Players race down a simulated track trying to shift through gears and beat the computer's speed.
Chopper I

Chopper I is an 1988 arcade hall video game, developed by SNK.

The objective of the top-down game is to infiltrate enemy territory and essentially destroy all objects. The game can be played with 1 or 2 players; both players, each occupying one helicopter, play simultaneously.
Choro Q Hyper Racing 5
Choro Q Hyper Racing 5 (チョロQ ハイパーレーシング5) is an arcade machine by Sega. Released in December 1998 in Japan.
Chou Chabudai Gaeshi!

Cho Chabudai Gaeshi is an arcade game by Taito, equipped with a small plastic tea table that the player must pound on and then flip over. The goal is to propel characters through walls and into objects, causing as much destruction as possible. The game's name roughly translates to "Upending Tea Tables."

The game is based on a well-known theme and trend in Japanese pop culture, the upending or flipping of tea tables. The action is seen throughout Japanese television, manga, and films. The term chabudai gaeshi is also used as an expression to describe a quick reversal of a situation, much like the English expression "to turn the tables".
Choy Sun Doa

Choy Sun Doa is an Aristocrat-powered slot machine featuring a standard 5x3 layout and offering 243 ways to win. Its name translates to the God of Prosperity or Wealth and it is themed on Caishen, the Chinese God of Wealth. The reels are home to high paying symbols including golden dragons, jade rings, golden coins, Koi fish and red packets with golden coins. Playing card symbols from 9s through As award low-value prizes.

The God of Wealth himself stands for Wild that appears on the reels 2, 3 and 4 only to replace all the symbols except for Scatter. Scatter is depicted as the golden ingot and you have to land 3, 4 or 5 of these on the reels left to right to trigger the Free Games feature.

Once the feature is triggered, you will be offered to choose from 5 options. The Yellow Fish feature awards 20 free spins with Choy Sun Doa Wild acting as a 2x, 3x or 5x multiplier when included in a winning combo.
Chrono Regalia

Chrono Regalia is a high-fantasy real-time strategy game developed and released by Sega for arcades (using their ALLS UX hardware) in Japan on February 21, 2019.

Using only the game's touchscreen for its controls, Chrono Regalia has players battling others in a one-on-one match that combines turn-based strategy games with collectible card games. It is unique for its real-time "step" approach, in which player turns are done automatically in a first-come approach. The game later received a major revision on July 24, 2019, titled Chrono Regalia EX, adding a new game mode (Tansaku Mode) and new Units.

Players choose four Units to control, each with a customizable assortment of six cards in their "deck" (including weapons and spells), and must maneuver them across a four-lane bridge in order to directly attack the opponent's character (or "Chronos") while defending their own.
Chuck E. Cheese's Match Game

Manufactured by Coastal Amusements exclusively for ShowBiz Pizza Time, Inc.

A children's memory matching game.
Chuckles the Clown

Chuckles the Clown is a ticket redemption game aimed at children which features a colourful clown cabinet and circus sound effects.

The object of the game is to accumulate points by placing lightweight colourful balls into the mouth of the clown as the clowns head rotates from side to side. Players earn tickets depending on the amount of points they accumulate.
Chuka Taisen

You play a small character who floats about on a cloud and shoots small balls of energy at bad guys who fly at you from the left and right of the screen. You can collect powerups and visit shops to upgrade your offensive and defensive powers. There are a number of different stages which are punctated by a mini-boss half way through and a big (literally) boss at the end.

This is one of the only games ever made which features flying noodle bowls and bears with guns.
Chunithm

Chunithm (portmanteau of words chūnibyō (basically a slang term that describes teenagers that have an edgy behaviour) and "rhythm"), is a rhythm game for the arcades. Players use a wide touch panel to hit the notes at the correct time, following the rhythm of a particular song/track. Originally, the game only supported the touch panel, but later versions added other mechanics, such as the "Air" mechanic, where players must hover their hand over certain notes when promted. The game supports simple hitting of notes, long presses, sliding and hover. The harder the difficulty level, the more the player experiences these new movements that they must master to win.

The game features a comprehensive list of songs to choose from, from game and anime soundtracks to J-Pop hits. Players can play as a guest, or they can make a profile using Sega's Aime card to store player data. Registering a profile allows for important bonuses for progression.
Chunithm Amazon

Chunithm Amazon is a rhythm game for Japanese arcades developed and published by SEGA, released in 2018. The game uses the traditional "falling notes" style of gameplay, as notes scroll down the screen. For each note, the player must hit the corresponding part of the "Ground Slider" controller. Tap notes require the note to simply be tapped, Hold notes require holding down the necessary part of the slider until the note ends, Slide notes are similar to Hold notes but the player must drag horizontally along the slider, and Flick notes require the player to slide across the part of the slider corresponding to the note.
Chunithm New

Chunithm New is a sequel to the music-based arcade game released by Sega in Japan in 2021. Updated cabinets were also released along with the new game, with improvements such as:

• 120fps monitor
• Upgraded speaker, earphone jack, and touch panels
• Digital payment support
• Avatar and arena battle
• Level adjustments, extending from level 14 to level 15.
• These new cabinets are called "Gold Model" while old cabinets are now called "Silver Model. Old "Silver Model" cabinets can be converted using conversion kits to run "CHUNITHM NEW"
Chunithm PARADISE

In Chunithm, players use touch and motion-based sensor bars to input commands that correspond to the notes scrolling down from the top of the screen. Depending on the type of note, players may be required to tap, hold, or slide their fingers against the bottom sensor bar or wave their hands in the air between the sensors located on either side of the machine. There are seven types of notes.
Circus

Circus was one of the first games produced by Exidy that used a CPU (6502) to control the game logic instead of hand-crafted hard-coded logic circuits. It ran on a black & white monitor with a color overlay that gave each row of balloons at the top of the screen a different color. It was designed and programmed by Edward Valeau and Howell Ivey of Exidy in 1977.

Circus came in an upright dedicated cabinet, and may have also been available in a cocktail configuration as well. Circus machines had white sides with red painted sideart of several balloons in flight. The front of the machine was decorated with a large ornate monitor bezel that also doubled as a marquee (or nameplate). This bezel showed several clowns in a circus scene and had the game title spelled out with multicolored balloons. The control panel was unadorned, save for an analog spinner and a start button. The whole machine was finished off in black T-molding.
Circus Charlie

In the game there are six regular stages (plus an extra stage) of differing tasks that are to be completed by Charlie. Grabbing money bags, performing dangerous tricks, avoiding enemies, completing stages, etc., earns Charlie points. After the sixth stage is completed, the game starts over again but with a faster pace and more difficult (but exactly the same in terms of task to be completed) levels.
Charlie also races against time. Bonus points are awarded according to the time remaining, but running out of time will cost the player a life.
Cisco Heat

In this racing game, the players get to race in police cars instead of the usual racing cars driven by speed freaks (like in the Crazy Cars series). Break the law instead of upholding it, while racing through the streets of San Francisco (Cisco for short, hence the name). Take in the Golden gate Bridge, China Town and the Twin Peaks.

Avoid collisions with trams, other cars (driven by annoying citizens), buildings and road blockades etc., while trying to reach the next checkpoint before the time runs out! Use your horn to alert other road-users of your presence.
City Attack
City Attack is an arcade machine manufactured by the company Petaco, it's a bootleg from Pleiads.
City Bomber

In City Bomber, the player is in pursuit of a gang of criminals. In order to keep the criminals from escaping, the player must reach checkpoints within a specified amount of time. At the start of the game, the player's car can shoot missiles at enemy vehicles and is also able to jump over enemies or obstacles. When some enemy cars are destroyed, power-ups are released that augment the car's abilities. Missiles improve the destructive power of the car's weaponry, wings extend the car's jumping distance, rocket boosters speed up the car and buzzsaws allow the car to ram obstacles without damage for a short time.

Collisions with other cars are not generally harmful to the player, although they may slow down the car. Oil slicks dropped by enemies will spin out the car and slow it down significantly. Collisions with obstacles or falling off the course will destroy the player's car.
City Cats

City Cats is a 1990s vintage arcade ticket redemption game manufactured by Quick Silver Development Co., Inc. and distributed by SEGA Enterprises, Inc. It was part of a line of electro-mechanical redemption machines released alongside sister titles like Turbo Pusher and Hollywood Stars.

 An electro-mechanical ticket redemption game built for arcade and family entertainment centers.
City Connection

In City Connection you must drive along on roads, painting them a different color. When you have all the roads painted, you go on to the next level. Cops are frequent along the roads, but oil cans will quickly stop them in their tracks. Avoid cats and spikes, and collect balloons to warp to further levels.
City Love

"City Love" is a rare, adult-themed Japanese arcade video game released in 1986 by the developer Nichibutsu. It is an incremental, strip-mahjong game where players compete against cartoon female opponents.

The game features a standard mahjong tile layout where players attempt to defeat various "city girls". Winning hands triggers a rock-paper-scissors bonus mini-game or reveals adult cartoon graphics.
Ckidzo

Ckidzo is a Pong variant with a twist. The paddles in the game are subject to inertia. They take some time to get to top speed and also can't come to a standstill immediately. The paddles can move in all directions and the ball must be led into goals (one for each team). The game allows for four players.
Clash-Road
Clash-Road is a bicycle racing game produced by Wood Place in 1986. It was published by various companies in different countries under license. Data East published the game in the US.
Classic American Road Trip

Classic American Road Trip is a bright and exciting coin pusher machine. This dedicated ticket payout, single player pusher is themed around the classic Hollywood to Chicago Route 66 and features a unique bonus feature that result in big ticket wins.

At each destination players will light up postcards of the iconic location and get the opportunity to receive a bonus splash of coins that convert into greater ticket wins. On reaching the journeys end the player can win up to a 500 ticket bonus.
Clay Champ

Clay Champ (クレイチャンプ Kurei Chanpu) is an electro-mechanical game released by Namco in June 1979. It is very much like the company's own Shoot Away, and was licensed to Allied Leisure Industries for US manufacturing (later renamed Centuri).

Players use the mounted lightguns (which resemble actual shotguns) to shoot the clay targets on-screen. The player only gets two shots to shoot the targets, but can earn bonus points by shooting both targets with one shot or by shooting them right as they appear on-screen. If the player shoots all targets, he or she gets an extended play time; the player can earn another one by shooting all targets during extended time. The game is over if the player fails to shoot all of the clay targets in time, or when the second exntended time ends.
Clay Pigeon

The object of Clay Pigeon was to shoot as many clay targets as you can, using an arcade light gun that was shaped like a shotgun. At the start of the game you are given the choice of selecting either Trap Shooting or Skeet Shooting. Trap shooting is where the clay target is thrown directly away from the shooter, while in skeet shooting the target is launched across the shooter's field of vision. The graphics are done in Exidy's realistic style, each round is played against a decent looking outdoor background, and an extremely repetitive announcer yells 'pull' to warn you of each and every target being launched. After several rounds of targets, you finally get to go after some real live animals! The real live animals are of course, ducks! The ducks are small and fly onto the screen in small groups of up to around a half dozen or so, and unlike the earlier title "Vs. Duck Hunt", you cannot miss any of these.
Clay Shoot
A clay shooting game developed and manufactured by Allied Leisure Industries in 1979.
Claybuster
Claybuster is an Action game, developed and published by Model Racing, which was released in 1978.
Clean Sweep

In Clean Sweep, players control a paddle at the bottom of the screen and hit a ball into a field of dots. The field of dots are arranged as a 14x14 grid and each time the ball hits a dot it disappears and the player earns points to their score, The ball will keep going in the direction its shot until it ricochets off the sides or top of the screen and returns back to the bottom of the screen where the player either hits it back up into the field of dots or misses the falling ball and loses a ball. Players are given a total of three or five balls depending on the setting. The goal of the game is to clear all of the dots and get a clean sweep.
Cleopatra Fortune

Cleopatra Fortune is a falling-block puzzle game featuring a cutesy anime Egyptian theme. Groups of stones and gems of different shapes fall from the top of a well. Gems can be cleared by enclosing them within a group of stones, and stones can be cleared by making complete rows from them. Blocks will fall when those under them are cleared, which can create chains for more points.

The game includes three different play modes. First is a standard endless mode where play continues until the player is overwhelmed by the blocks. Second is a versus mode for two players. Last is a puzzle mode where the player is given a set field, a set sequence of drops, and a specific goal such as clearing all the gems or achieving a chain of a certain length. The puzzle mode has the player rescuing Cleopatra's friends who have been trapped in a pyramid by the evil Sphinx.
Cleopatra Fortune Plus
Cleopatra Fortune Plus (クレオパトラフォーチュン プラス) is a puzzle game developed by Altron and published by Taito for the Sega NAOMI arcade system. It is the sequel to Taito's 1997 game Cleopatra Fortune.
Clever Cogs

Clever Cogs is a classic UK pub fruit machine developed by QPS Interactive (a brand under the Novomatic Group). Released in the early 2000s under the official model number PR2522, it became a familiar fixture in British arcades and pubs.
Cliff Hanger

Cliff Hanger is a laserdisc video game that was released by Stern Electronics in 1983. It uses animation from two Lupin III films, most prominently The Castle of Cagliostro, as well as The Mystery of Mamo. Like many laserdisc games, it is a reactive game which requires the player to press a button or move the joystick in a particular direction when prompted by the game to progress the storyline. The segments from The Mystery of Mamo use the original English dub commissioned by Toho, while the segments from The Castle of Cagliostro use a dub created for the game.

The game's plot is based very loosely on that of The Castle of Cagliostro, and follows Cliff (Arsène Lupin III) as he attempts to rescue Clarissa (Lady Clarisse d'Cagliostro) from the evil Count Draco (in some materials called "Dreyco" and in the instruction manual "Dragoe"), who wants to marry her. Cliff is aided in his quest by Jeff (Daisuke Jigen) and Samurai (Goemon Ishikawa XIII).
Cloak & Dagger

Cloak & Dagger is an arcade game released by Atari in 1983 The game is based on the film of the same name where it is critical to the plot. The game saw limited arcade release as a conversion kit for Robotron 2084 cabinets.
The Cloak & Dagger game screens from the movie are mostly from the arcade version, and not the Atari 5200 game console as it would appear in the film. Although a 5200 version of the game was planned, it was never released due to the video game crash of 1983 and eventual sale of Atari. Because the Atari 5200 version of Cloak & Dagger wasn't complete during filming, the cartridge props are actually other 5200 games with a Cloak & Dagger label stuck on them.
Clockwise
Clockwise is a 1986 video casino game developed and published by Ainsworth Nominees.
Cloud 9

Cloud 9 was an arcade prototype produced by Atari in 1983.

A gallery shoot 'em up game where a shoot clouds in the sky. Avoid rain drops and other enemies. Try to destroy all clouds before your chamber is flooded.
Cloud Nine Club

The Cloud Nine Club (often referenced alongside its popular standard counterpart Cloud 9 or Cloud 999) is a classic UK fruit machine produced by Barcrest Games during the 1990s. Built on the legendary Barcrest MPU4 tech hardware platform, it remains an affectionately remembered piece of retro British arcade and pub culture.
Clown
A slot machine game developed and manufactured by Russian company, Atronic, in 2002.
Clown Around

The Clown Around (often discussed or found as Clowning Around) fruit machine is a classic UK pub amusement machine manufactured by the legendary Bell-Fruit Mobility / Bell-Fruit Games (BFM). Operating on traditional UK fruit machine logic, these machines historically featured a 30p-per-play setup with classic 3-reel gameplay alongside a rich, circus-themed upper feature board.
Clown Roll Down

The Clown Roll Down arcade machine (also spelt Clown Rolldown) is a classic ticket-redemption arcade game originally manufactured by Bay Tek Entertainment in 1995. It seamlessly combines the nostalgia of traditional carnival midway attractions with mechanical arcade engineering.

Unlike typical throwing games, the objective is to hit a specific mathematical score. Each lane corresponds to a numeric value, and players must achieve a perfect high score or a perfect low score to maximize their ticket output.
Clowns

Gameplay in Clowns shares some similarities with Breakout, but this time the bricks has been replaced with balloons that you get points for popping. To reach the balloons at the top of the screen you have to move a seesaw under a jumping clown. This will launch away the clown already standing on the seesaw, hopefully towards the balloons. 

Balloons comes in three different: yellow, green and blue. Yellow balloons are the easiest to reach, while the blue are the hardest. Therefore you also get more points for the harder to reach balloons. If you manage to clear all balloons of a color, you'll get bonus points. Balloons of that color will then be replenished. You have five jumpers to your disposal, and you will lose one every time you miss to catch the landing clown. Clearing all blue balloons will give you an extra jumper.
Club Class

The Club Class fruit machine is a classic UK pub and club slot machine manufactured by Bell-Fruit. Known for its traditional reel-based gameplay, it belongs to a memorable generation of UK amusement-with-prizes (AWP) machines.
Club Clouseau

Club Clouseau is a classic UK club-style fruit machine based on the iconic Inspector Clouseau character from the Pink Panther franchise. Manufactured by QPS (Quality Play Systems), this high-tech machine was a staple in British social clubs, snooker halls, and members-only establishments during the eras of the Bell-Fruit Scorpion 4 hardware platform.
Club Connect

The Club Connect fruit machine is a classic UK club-style gaming machine manufactured by Barcrest that originally ran on the popular MPU4 tech platform. It is well-remembered by arcade enthusiasts for its traditional mechanical reels, vibrant lighting, and characteristic "gamble sandwich" feature style common to late-90s and early-2000s club machines.
Club Explosion
Club Explosion is a slot machines developed and released by BFM (Bellfruit)
Club Jenna Presents: Jenna Jameson's Strip Poker

Club Jenna Presents: Jenna Jameson's Strip Poker is a strip poker simulation starring 90's and early 2000s adult film star Jenna Jameson. It was developed and manufactured by Shiggles, Inc. However, the year of release is currently unknown. It was, however, released sometime in the early-mid 2000s.
Club Kart for Cycraft

Club Kart for Cycraft is a specialized version of Sega's 2001 go-kart racing game, Club Kart: European Session, specifically adapted in 2003 to run on the Cycraft motion simulator cabinet. Developed in collaboration with Simuline, the Cycraft cabinet utilized a specialized inverted 3 Degrees of Freedom (DOF) electric motion system to physically tilt and move the player, mimicking the intense G-forces of racing.

Because the Cycraft version was ported from the 2003 revised software edition, it handles features differently than the original 2001 standalone Club Kart dedicated cabinets.
Club Kart Prize

Club Kart Prize is the kart racing game released for Sega NAOMI 2 hardware in 2003 and a sequel (or spin-off) of sorts to Club Kart: European Session. As the name suggests, this version of Club Kart will award the player with prizes depending on how well he or she plays - you collect coins during the race and these will be awarded to you at the end. Club Kart Prize only seems to have seen a limited run, and at present has only been spotted in the United Kingdom (the player collects pennies and is paid in pounds sterling). It may have released in Japan under the name clubkart THE MEDAL.
Club Kart: European Session

Club Kart: European Session is a go-kart racing arcade game released by Sega in 2001 (with development spanning 2000). Powered by the Sega NAOMI 2 hardware, the game stands out for its realistic approach to kart physics, licensing real-world karting manufacturers, and pioneering Sega's early magnetic card saving systems.

Unlike arcade racers that rely on drift-heavy mechanics, Club Kart leans heavily into realistic racing lines and strict momentum management due to the karts' lower top speeds compared to supercars.
Club Moneybags

The Club Moneybags fruit machine (often associated with the popular emulated version Club Monopoly Moneybags) is a classic UK club-specification fruit machine. It was originally designed for the higher-stake environment of British working men's clubs and private members' clubs, which allowed for larger jackpots than standard pub fruit machines.
Club Shuffle

Club Shuffle is a classic UK club fruit machine (an Amusement with Prizes / AWP machine) manufactured by Barcrest. Released primarily in the 1990s, it operated on the popular MPU4 tech hardware platform, which was a staple system for many beloved arcade and pub fruit machines of that era.
Club Temptation

Club Temptation is a classic UK club-category fruit machine manufactured by Bell-Fruit Manufacturing (BFM). First released in May 1991, this popular machine originally ran on BFM's Scorpion 1 hardware platform before seeing later hardware revisions like the Scorpion 4 technology housed inside the iconic "Smiley" cabinet style. As a dedicated members-club machine, it offered significantly higher stakes and prizes than standard pub fruit machines of its era, featuring various configurable setups including 5p play with a £75 jackpot, 20p play with a £200 jackpot, and high-tier emulator conversions climbing to a £500 jackpot.
Club Vegas
Club Vegas is a slot machine developed and manufactured by Barcrest.
Club X
A slot machine developed and manufactured by UK based Barcrest.
Cluster Buster

The ball is used to dislodge an ever-changing array of 'grapes' in this souped-up breakout proto-Arkanoid style game. Cluster Buster or Graplop was released in November 1983. It was known as the 28th video game (Cassette no. 28) made for the Deco Cassette System.
Clutch Hitter

Clutch Hitter is a baseball video game released by Sega in 1991. It was released in video arcades as well for Sega's portable Game Gear. The Japanese version of the game features players and teams from Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball league. 

The American version of the game sports a license from the Major League Baseball Players Association and has rosters composed of actual professional baseball players
Cobra Command

Terrorists are threatening the Free World and have amassed a diabolical force. Only the brave pilot of Cobra Command can vanquish the terrorist threat and save the free world from total destruction. The player assumes the role as pilot of the LX-3 Super Cobra helicopter.

The missions go across the New York City streets, the Statue of Liberty, the Atlantic Ocean, Italy, the Grand Canyon and the enemy's headquarters on the Easter Island.
Cobra Gunship

Cobra Gunship is an action game in which the player controls a gunship and must destroy targets. Targets include tanks, jeeps, half-tracks, helicopters and gunships. The player can strafe and climb and enemy sprites grow in scale when they get closer. The game can be played by one or two players in hot-seat mode.
Cobra-Command

Not be confused with the 1984 Data East game of the same name, which was a LaserDisc game. Cobra-Command is a 1988 arcade game developed and published by Data East that was later ported to the NES. It is a side-scroller in which the player flies a heavily armored helicopter through six stages to destroy enemy tanks, cannons, submarines, and gunboats.

There are missions to Sumatra, Java, Borneo, the South China Sea, Siam and the enemy's headquarters.
Cobra: The Arcade

Cobra The Arcade is a rail shooter video game developed and published by Namco. It is based on Buichi Terasawa's manga Cobra and the TV series Space Cobra but with an original story.

Like the Time Crisis series, Cobra The Arcade uses a foot pedal to take cover and reload the gun. Like Time Crisis II and Time Crisis 3, it uses the same "crisis flash" system for all life-threatening shots and one life is lost due to hit by a critical bullet or an obstacle, or if the timer reaches zero. If a continue is used after all lives are lost, the score is reset to 0.
Coco Loco
A Spanish Pac-Man clone that actually gives you 2 credits for the price of one and adds a turbo boost button.
Coco Louco
Unlicensed Pac-Man game with gambling feature
Code Name: Sector

Code Name: Sector is a dedicated game in which one through four players track a hidden submarine. The computer controls the submarine, which is located in a grid and can move only a single tile after each ship's turn. Players use crayons and a parallel ruler to plot out paths and plastic submarines to keep score. The players' ships can change direction and speed and the computer will display their location and the proximity to the submarine using a LED display. Players use this information to deduce the position of the submarine and fire at it by giving a direction and range. When firing the player must also guess at the depth of the submarine or the shot will miss. On a miss, the submarine moves in a random direction.
Code of Joker

Code of Joker is an arcade card game developed by Sega R&D1 and manufactured by Sega. Unlike past card based arcade games, the trading cards only appear digitally, and the game is played solely with the touch screen. It's a standard one on one card battler, with no genre or spin mixed within. 

You have 7 characters to choose from with all their specific joker cards with all their special abilities. Then you have the Unit Card, which are the monsters which are divided into warrior, monster, genius, devil, angel, machine, hero and more. Combination monsters can also be summoned to help the units, just like the character you choose. Non-monster cards are the Trigger cards, which activate when you attack and then there are Inticaptor cards that activate on enemy players.
Code One Dispatch

Code One Dispatch is a racing game with emergency vehicles such as a police car, fire truck and ambulance, with similar over-the-top gameplay as Crazy Taxi.

Players can choose a vehicle from police car, bio hazard semi truck, fire engine, limousine, ambulance and undercover police car, with a helicopter and tank as extra unlockable vehicles. The mission depends on which vehicle was selected. The ambulance has to take someone from a traffic accident in a car crash to the hospital. The semi truck has rush to a tanker truck that spilled chemical waste to quarantine the waste. The helicopter has to fly over the road to a sail boat where someone fell overboard in a storm and rescue the survivors. and similar missions for each of the vehicles. Each vehicle has a separate high score list.
Coinmaster Roulette P497 V75

The Coinmaster Roulette P497 V75 is a single-player, casino-style arcade gambling game released in 2001 by Coinmaster-Gaming, Ltd.

 It emulates a traditional double-zero roulette wheel. Players touch the screen to place bets on specific numbers, red, or black. The game features an automated audio track that calls out "no more bets" before simulating the ball spin, accompanied by electronic casino music and sound effects.
Colony 7

Colony 7 is a single screen arcade shooter where you, the player is in charge of defence of the colony. There is a shield that protects the settlement's power generators that is under constant attack from 'Jarvian' alien invaders. There are two pulse cannons that can be used to shoot down the Jarvians, but an innovation of the time is that you can buy additional weapons for extra credits. The player has at his disposal a range of more powerful weapons that can be set off for a limited amount of times per game. A Mega-Blaster can be set off that destroys everything within its radius using up fuel reserves on the ground and a once per game 'Eradicator' that destroys every alien on screen.
The game mixes the play style of a conventional fixed screen shooter with that of Missile Command since your pulse cannons can be taken out, rendering you defenceless.
Colorama
Colorama is a casino gambling game developed and released by Coinmaster-Gaming in 2000.
Colour Mania

A three-reel electromechanical fruit\slot machine game from Bell-Fruit games released some time in the 2000's. It had multiple betting lines, nudge and many other betting options, essentially a clone of Hit Shot set on 30p play and £25.00 Jackpot.
Columns

Columns is loosely derived from Tetris, as it involves arranging falling blocks in such a way as to clear them. However, in columns they are groups of 3 same-size but varying color blocks, which must be arranged into sequences of 3 or more, either horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Sequences of 4 or 5 count for double or triple points, and diagonal sequences score the most. The real trick is to set up 'combos' - where one line causes other blocks to drop so as to create other lines.

As well as the normal game mode, there is also a 'flash' mode, in which the aim is simply to remove a particular block from the base of the pre-formed pile of bricks. The difficulty of this can be determined by increasing the number of complete rows which are already in place.
Columns '97

Published and Developed by Sega in 1996.

In Columns '97 sets of colored jewels fall in random order. The object of the game is to arrange the jewels vertically, horizontally or diagonally in rows of three or more to make them disappear.
Columns (Mega-Tech)

Columns is loosely derived from Tetris, as it involves arranging falling blocks in such a way as to clear them. However, in columns they are groups of 3 same-size but varying color blocks, which must be arranged into sequences of 3 or more, either horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Sequences of 4 or 5 count for double or triple points, and diagonal sequences score the most. The real trick is to set up 'combos' - where one line causes other blocks to drop to create other lines.

As well as the normal game mode, there is also a 'flash' mode, in which the aim is simply to remove a particular block from the base of the pre-formed pile of bricks. The difficulty of this can be determined by increasing the number of complete rows which are already in place.
Columns II: The Voyage Through Time
