Hana to Ojisan (花とおじさん) is a Japanese arcade game released in 1991 by Nichibutsu. It belongs to the tabletop/gambling category and blends traditional Hanafuda card game mechanics (specifically Koi-Koi) with adult-themed Mahjong gameplay features.
Hana wo Yaraneba!

Hana wo Yaraneba! is a Japanese Hanafuda video game released for arcade cabinets in July 1991. The game was developed and published by Dynax, a company well-known for producing adult-oriented Mahjong and Hanafuda arcade titles during the late 1980s and 1990s.
Hana Yayoi

Released in January 1987.

The title of this game translates from Japanese as 'March Flowers'.

This game is also known as "Hana Fubuki".
Hanabi de Doon!: Don-chan Puzzle

Don-chan Puzzle: Hanabi de Doon! is a rare, fireworks-themed falling-block puzzle arcade game released by Aruze in December 2003. Developed by Takumi Corporation, it runs on the Aleck 64 hardware (an arcade system board based on the Nintendo 64 architecture). The game features characters from Aruze's popular Hanabi series of pachislot machines, most notably its mascot Don-chan.
Hanafuda Hana Ginga

Hanafuda Hana Ginga (華銀河, translated as "Great Galaxy Hanafuda") is a 1994 Japanese arcade game published and developed by Dynax. Classified as a "medal game" or betting arcade title, it adapts traditional Japanese Hanafuda (flower card) mechanics for competitive, two-player arcade environments.

The game is distinct within retro arcade circles for its unique fusion of cosmic/galaxy thematic presentation with traditional Japanese card aesthetics, featuring character designs by the famous Japanese manga artist U-jin.
Hanafuda Hana Gokou

Hanafuda Hana Gokou (華五光) is a classic Japanese arcade board game released in December 1995. It was developed by Alba and published by Dynax.

The title translates to "Flower Five Lights," which is a direct reference to Gokou (Five Lights)—the highest-scoring card combination (Yaku) you can achieve in traditional Hanafuda games like Koi-Koi.
Hanafuda Hana Gokou Bangaihen

Hanafuda Hana Gokou Bangaihen (花札:華五光 番外編) is a Japanese gambling arcade game released in 1995. It translates to Hanafuda: Flower Five Lights Extra Edition and is centered around traditional Japanese playing cards.
Hanafuda Hana Tengoku

Hanafuda Hana Tengoku (華天国) is a classic Japanese arcade game released in 1992 by Dynax. Dedicated to the traditional Japanese "flower card" game Hanafuda, this electronic adaptation was a staple in 1990s Japanese game centres.
Hanaroku
Hanaroku (花六) is a Japanese tabletop arcade game released in 1988. The game was developed and published by the studio Alba.
Handle Champ

Handle Champ (ハンドルチャンプ Handoru Chanpu?) is an arcade Bishi Bashi game released on 1998 exclusively in Japan. It was developed and published by Konami.
Handle Champ is a racing game where cars are fueled by "Cola" instead of petrol and drive around normal and not so normal tracks.

Players compete head to head on the one cabinet. Controls is attained with the steering wheel and accelerator pedal.

Normal tracks include your typical grand prix circuits. Unusual tracks include a bowling alley, where players actually drive their cars down bowling alleys.
Hang Pilot

Hang Pilot is an hangliding racing game developed and published by Konami and released on Arcade on February 1997

The game is an hangliding simulation racing game and features three pilots that can be choosen from and three stages. Each of them represents a level of difficulty; Beginner, Medium and Expert. The player runs against three others opponents and the goal is to finish in first place. Each track have a time limited, but passing through checkpoints will extend the time.
Hang-On

Hang-On is a racing game and the first arcade games to use 16-bit graphics and uses the Super Scaler arcade system board, created with design input from Yu Suzuki, as technology to simulate 3D effects.

Using a behind the motorcycle perspective, the player races a linear race track divided into several stages within a limited time. Players have to lean the motorcycle to turn, with tighter corners requiring a further lean. A throttle similar to a motorcycle has to be twisted to accelerate the bike. The game has one track, pieced together in segments. Reaching a checkpoint at the end of each segment extends the time limit, and remaining time is carried over into the next stage. Running off the track results in the motorcycle crashing and the rider is launched into the air. The game ends if the time runs out or all five stages are completed.
Hang-On Jr.

Hang-On Jr. is a point-to-point 3D racing game in which players take control of a superbike and must race over five twisting, road-based circuits, avoiding rival bikers and trying to reach each end-of-stage checkpoint before the time limit expires.

The game is a cut-down version of its legendary parent, "Hang-On", and while it features similar gameplay, it's rendered in more primitive graphics due to the vastly inferior host hardware. As with the parent game, collisions with roadside objects will see the rider thrown from his bike as the bike then explodes, costing valuable seconds waiting for a replacement to appear. Contact with rival racers should also be avoided.

A new addition from Hang-On is the presence of water puddles on the road, which slow the rider down. Any time remaining when a checkpoint is reached is carried over to the next stage. The game consists of two sets of five identical stages. Completing the first set (Novice) unlocks the second set (Advanced).
Hangly-Man

Released in July 1981. Hangly Man is presumed to be a mangling of the title 'Hungry Man'.

Hangly Man contains not one, but two different mazes. The first maze appears on the first stage and every even numbered stage thereafter. The second maze appears on the third stage and every odd numbered stage thereafter.

The first maze is an alteration to the original maze. While an extra bump has been added to the once-open bottom row, the top row has been opened up. The areas near the mouths of the escape tunnel are no longer single width tunnels, but more open. This can cause players to miss the tunnels if they are not lined up exactly right. The first maze also contains two extra sets of tunnels, one each above and below the original tunnel. Eating a power pill in the first maze can sometimes make the maze turn invisible. In some versions of Hangly-Man, the maze never reappears until you die.

The second maze is a wide-open maze, with no borders except around the very edges.
Hangman
Hangman was produced in 1984 by Status. It is an arcade version of the popular pen and paper game of the same name.
Hangzo
Unreleased video game. Last prototype version from January 1992.
Happy 6-in-1
A gambling arcade game that featured several card games and some mahjong games.
Happy Fruits

Happy Fruits is a popular fruit machine style slot game available across multiple variations, spanning from traditional 3-reel physical pub variants to modern 5-reel online video slots. Originally finding its fame as a low-jackpot arcade and pub favorite, the concept has transitioned heavily into the digital gaming space.
Happy Fruits Club
Happy Fruits Club is a fruit machine style video slot machine game developed and released by BFM.
Happy Jackie

Happy Jackie is a classic arcade game board released in 1993 by the Taiwanese gaming company International Games System (IGS).

It is an 8-Liner Cherry Master-style slot/fruit machine game board. It is technically a PCB (Printed Circuit Board) intended to be housed inside video fruit machine cabinets.
Happy Notes Casino
The Happy Notes casino fruit machine is a classic pub-style slot game originally manufactured by the prominent UK gaming company Bell-Fruit Games.
Hard Drivin'

Hard Drivin' is a 3D arcade hit from Atari Games. You are in control of a high-performance sports car. Your objective is to race around the course as fast as possible and hit as many checkpoints as possible. If you hit a checkpoint you gain extra time to go farther. You will see traffic on the road both in your direction and coming down the opposite direction, so be careful when you pass... 

The course has two sections: speed track, and stunt track. Speed track is longer, but you can usually achieve higher speeds. Stunt track requires you to perform several stunts such as jumping bridges, driving through a loop, and so on. 

Crashing the car has no serious consequences and indeed shows a replay of your crash from a cinematic angle. Admire your crash head-on into the cement truck, or clipping the minivan, or flying off the bridge in the wrong angle... You lose several seconds as your car is "reset" and you get up to speed again.
Hard Drivin's Airborne

Hard Drivin's Airborne was a prototype produced by Atari Games in 1993.

You control a car that transforms into a glider in this racing game.
Hard Dunk
A colorful 3D three-on-three street baketball game from Sega.
Hard Hat

Hard Hat is a unique logic game with an educational puzzle to solve. It was designed and programmed for Exidy by Larry W. Hutcherson Sr. and released in 1982. Touted as the “First Educational Coin-Op Game”, you play a busy carpenter that is constantly being chased by hammers and whirlwinds throughout a grid of scaffolding while manipulating letters to spell “E-X-I-D-Y” or “H-A-R-D-H-A-T”. Controls consist of a simple 4-direction joystick, both players alternating use during a two player game.

The hardware is identical to another Exidy game, Pepper II.
Hard Head

Hard Head is a 2D side-scrolling platform game that puts players in the shoes of a 'Hard Head' - it's similar to Super Mario Bros.

As you traverse the sixteen stages, you have to navigate through an obstacle course. 

You have the ability destroy blocks with your head that sometimes contain power-ups and sometimes walls have to be destroyed with a hammer. 

The various stages are filled with strange enemies like Indians, ducks, scissors, insects, cat like creatures and monsters. You fight these creatures with your bubble gun that forms a bubble a round them and lifts them up. 

The bubble will break after a while, and jumping them on the head will kill them permanently. A stage can be completed if you kick a soccer ball in a goal at the end of each stage. You can play solo or with a friend.
Hard Head 2

Hard Head 2 is a 2D side-scrolling platform game that puts players in the shoes of a Hard Head and it is a sequel to Hard Head. Before the game starts your girlfriend is kidnapped by a monster and now you have to rescue her.

As you traverse the eight stages, you have to navigate through an obstacle course. The various stages are filled with strange enemies like apes, snakes, lizards, birds and monsters. The gameplay differs from the original game. You fight these creatures with either a club, swinging a mace or bubble gun. Power-ups for these weapons can be found along the way and you have to fight various bosses to reach your girlfriend. Sometimes you have to climb, jumping enemies on the head will also kill them. You can play solo or with a friend.
Hard Times
A one or two player shooting game with a prohibition-era mobster theme. Italian company Playmark essentially hacked and reskinned TADCorp's Blood Bros.
Hard Yardage

Four-player football game featuring great digitized graphics and awesome TV-like exciters.

This game is an official licensed product of the NFL (National Football League). It features the voice of the Chicago Bears announcer Wayne Larrivee.
Harem

You are the Sheikh of the Desert, and your 6-bed harem is looking empty. Take on the ultimate rescue mission across treacherous sands! Snatch odalisques from speeding jeeps, passing camels, and hidden tents, then race them back to safety. But watch out! Angry servants are on your tail, a nasty monkey is throwing monkey wrenches into your plans, and a deadly, fast pink snake is ready to strike! Can you survive the hazards and complete your harem?
Harem Challenge

Harem Challenge is an adult-themed puzzle arcade game released in 1995 by the developer CD Express. It was specifically designed to run on the Cubo CD32 hardware, an arcade system built using modified Commodore Amiga CD32 home console. 
It is a classic "Qix-like" partition puzzle game. Players draw lines on a grid to capture territory and gradually reveal a hidden adult background image.
Harley-Davidson & L.A. Riders

In Harley-Davidson & L.A. Riders, the player rides one of five Harley-Davidson models. The objective is to complete a series of checkpoints around Los Angeles under a time limit. The objective is similar to the later Sega arcade game, Crazy Taxi (1999).
Harley-Davidson: King of the Road

Harley-Davidson: King of the Road (ハーレー ダビッドソン キング オブ ザ ロード) is a motorcycle game released for Sega Lindbergh arcade hardware in 2009. It is the second Harley-Davidson-inspired arcade game to be produced by Sega, following 1997's Harley-Davidson & L.A. Riders.
Hasamu

An interesting twist on solitaire mahjong, with movable tiles in certain circumstances. You must clear 2 tiles of the same suit, but they have to be either right next to each other or on the same row.
Hashire Patrol Car

Hashire Patrol Car (Run! Patrol Car) is a niche, Japanese arcade game released by Sega in 2001. Running on Sega's ST-V (Sega Titan Video) arcade hardware, it functions as a video-based kiddie ride and a ticket redemption game rather than a traditional racing simulator.

The gameplay focuses on a simplified highway chase to catch fleeing criminals. Reviewers and arcade archivists note that the mechanics are largely predetermined, operating similarly to a video-based crane or ticket redemption machine.
Hat Trick
Hat Trick is a two-on-two hockey game. Each player controls a goalie and a skater. The object is to shoot the puck into the opposing teams goal. Each game lasts two minutes.
Hat Trick Hero

European Football Champ was released to coincide with the 1992 European Championships. The game scrolls horizontally at a slight angle, and recreates the coin-op's close-up zoom effect after a player scores. Only a small area of the pitch is on screen at a time, but there is a scanner to show the whole pitch.

Although the game has a referee, he often loses attention, and these moments give you a chance to foul, punch or side-swipe opposition players. One and two player options are included.
Hat Trick Hero '93

Football Champ is an arcade-style football (soccer) video game. The game was produced by Team Dogyan developers in Japan, and originally released in the arcades by Taito Corporation in 1990. Euro Football Champ and Hat Trick Hero are versions of this game with minor variations.

Subsequent arcade releases of this game include Hat Trick Hero '93 (Japan) and Hat Trick Hero '95 (Japan, also released as Taito Power Goal).
Hat Trick Hero '94

Hat Trick Hero '94 was produced by Taito in 1994.

A cool soccer game from Taito.
Hat Trick Hero '95

Hat Trick Hero '95 was produced by Taito in 1994.

An updated version of the previous game (Hat Trick Hero '94)
Hatch Catch

Shoot the colors on the same colors of the screen. When three or more same colored blocks draw a line, they dissapear. By terminating all blocks, the stage is clear. After the 50th stage, the game is over.
Hatris

In Hatris, the falling blocks of Tetris are replaced by falling hats which are top hats, cowboy hats, baseball caps, derbys, party hats and crowns. The setting is a hat factory, where hats are dropped down from a conveyor belt two at a time and must be stacked on one of six mannequin heads. Once five hats of the same kind have been stacked on top of each other, they fall down onto another conveyor belt below and are shipped out of the factory, rewarding the player with a cash bonus (the game keeps track of score as money, not simply points). Once you ship out enough hats out of the shop, you go up a level to the next shop. The higher shop number you get to, the more types of hats start appearing to make it more difficult for you to accomplish your task. The game ends when one of your stacks of hats reaches the top of the screen.
Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA Arcade

Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA Arcade is a port of the Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA with updated visuals

As the game is a port of the PlayStation Portable games, the gameplay is relatively the same as the original. The signature PlayStation buttons are now the 4 large buttons on the machine's panel, and players push those buttons to play the games. Unlike the handheld versions of the game, players can hold a button or buttons for an unlimited time when the game indicates to hold a certain note and multiple buttons can be hit at the same time. The arcade version features songs from both Project DIVA and Project Mirai, along with a variety of original songs not included in either series. The Promotional Videos for the game have been updated and re-rendered for the game bearing a similar resemblance to the Dreamy Theatre versions. The four difficulties are Easy, Normal, Hard, and Extreme, as seen in Project DIVA 2nd.
Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA Arcade Future Tone

Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA Arcade Future Tone is the sequel to the original arcade version of Project Diva.

Like its predecessor the gameplay is mostly the same as the original portable titles in the series. Notable changes from the first game include upgraded graphics and physics, a Touch Slider panel for the arrow shaped notes, new songs, and running on the more powerful Sega Nu arcade board.
Haunted Castle

Haunted Castle is a 2D arcade platform game, part of the Castlevania game universe. It's the first game in the series for arcade machines.

The game's main hero is once again Simon Belmont. He wants to rescue his wife Selena from Dracula. The gameplay is simple - Simon goes from left to right and fights against various enemies - skeletons, zombies, bats, and others. Belmont has his trusty whip and can carry one sub-weapon, like bombs. Hearts are ammo, required to use any type of sub-weapon The game has 6 levels, every one ending with a boss fight.
Haunted House (Midway)

Haunted House is a legendary 1972 electro-mechanical (EM) rifle arcade game manufactured by Midway Manufacturing Co.. Standing as a pinnacle of pre-video game arcade entertainment, it is celebrated for its highly innovative audio engineering and spooky immersive aesthetics. Unlike modern screen-based games, it utilized physical targets, mirrors, and blacklights within a 3D diorama cabinet.
Haunted Museum

Haunted Museum (Panic Museum in Japan) is a Light Gun Game by Taito. In it you play two agents who have come to investigate mysterious disappearances in a local museum. Though once they get inside they find that a supernatural force has a hold over the building, bringing the exhibits to life that are not shy about attacking them. If that wasn't enough, the exhibits have worlds of their own that transport the two into different settings no matter how implausible (such as space or underwater). With each world conquered, an orb falls into place on a monument in the lobby of the building. So the agents head out to find out who or what is exactly affecting the museum.
Hayaoshi Quiz Grand Champion Taikai
Hayaoshi Quiz: Grand Champion Taikai is a Japanese quiz arcade game released in 1994 by the video game company Jaleco. The title roughly translates to "Fast-Buzz Quiz: Grand Champion Tournament."
Hayaoshi Quiz Nettou Namahousou

Hayaoshi Quiz Nettou Namahousou is a Japanese quiz arcade game released in 1994 by Jaleco. The game was built for the Jaleco Mega System 32 arcade hardware platform, which was known for handling advanced 2D sprite scaling and featuring high-quality audio driven by the Yamaha YMF271 sound chip.

The title translates roughly to "Fast-Finger Quiz: Fierce Live Broadcast Battle", framing the quiz game around a high-energy television studio broadcast theme. Players compete in trivia rounds using specialized arcade control panels typically outfitted with large "buzzer" buttons (hayaoshi buttons) to ring in quickly against opponents or the clock.
Hayaoshi Quiz Ouza Ketteisen: The King Of Quiz

Hayaoshi Quiz Ouza Ketteisen: The King Of Quiz (早押しクイズ ～王座決定戦～) is a Japanese arcade quiz game developed and published by Jaleco.

The title roughly translates to "Fast-Press Quiz: Throne Decision Match." True to its name, players must test their trivia knowledge and reflex speed to hit the buzzer and correctly answer questions before their opponents do.
Hayaoshi Taisen Quiz Hyhoo

A Japanese quiz game.

Released in July 1987.

The title of this game translates from Japanese as 'Quick Response Competition Quiz HYHOO'.
Hayaoshi Taisen Quiz Hyhoo 2

Hayaoshi Taisen Quiz Hyhoo 2 is a competitive trivia arcade video game developed and published by Nichibutsu (Nihon Bussan Co. Ltd.) and released exclusively in Japan in November 1987. The title translates roughly to "Fast-Paced Battle Quiz Hyhoo 2," with "Hyhoo" intended to be pronounced like "Hi-Ho". It served as a quick follow-up to the original Hayaoshi Taisen Quiz Hyhoo, which debuted earlier that same year.
Hayauchi Gun Kids

Hayauchi Gun Kids is set in a Wild West–inspired environment where the player faces off against cartoonish outlaws in quick-draw contests. 

Players insert medals to join a round, wagering up to three medals at once. Enemy figures appear on screen, and the player fires “gum bullets” at them to score hits. Timing is important, but outcomes are partly controlled by the game’s internal probability system, meaning not every well-timed shot succeeds. Successfully defeating enemies rewards medals, with a maximum payout of 42 medals per round.
Head On 2

Head On 2 (ヘッド-オン2) is an arcade sequel to Head On, and was developed and released by Gremlin/Sega for VIC Dual hardware in 1979.

The gameplay is the same as in the original but the design of the race circuit is different. The centre part of the playfield is like the original tracks but with only four lanes. On both sides of the screen there are two additional lanes. These additional lanes affect the gameplay as they allow the player or the AI car to turn around and move in the reverse direction. This means that the player not only has to watch out for cars in front of him but also cars chasing from behind. Another difference from the original game is that later levels can have as many as four AI controlled cars.
Head Panic

Head Panic is a platform game in which you throw balls to kill the enemies. Very similar to the Snow Bros. Saga.

Follow Polly & Sally as they go round the world defeating monsters, complete with landscapes & landmarks from all around the world.
Head-On

Head-On (ヘッド-オン) is a 1979 arcade racing game, developed and published by Sega/Gremlin for VIC Dual hardware. It's the first known game where the player has to collect dots (a year before Pac-Man).

Viewed from a top down perspective, the player has to race around a circuit consisting of five lanes and collect all the dots that lies scattered around. At the same time he has to watch out for the jam cars that move in the opposite direction. To dodge the jam cars the player swap lanes which can only be done in the middle of each straight. To move faster it's possible to accelerate but then it's only possible to change one lane at a time. At normal speed two lanes can be crossed in one move.

A level is completed when all dots have been collected and when colliding with a jam car a life is lost. The game is over when all three lives are lost. As the player progresses through the levels he will come across more and faster jam cars.
Heart Attack

Heart Attack was produced by Century Electronics in 1983.

Fill the maze with dots. Drop a plug to block the enemy or freeze the enemy for five seconds. You must complete the maze before time runs out.
Heat of Eleven '98

Heat of Eleven '98 (released in Japan as World Soccer Championship) is a soccer game developed and published by Konami and released on Arcade platforms in 1998. It was one of the five titles ran on the Konami M2 Hardware.
Heat Up Hockey Image
Heat Up Hockey Image (ヒートアップ ホッケー イマージュ) is an air hockey table manufactured by Sega.
Heated Barrel

Heated Barrel is a Western themed side-scrolling shoot 'em up game that supports up to four players at the same time. The game offers four typical Western characters to choose from: Howdy Pardner with his shotgun, the Mexican Chi Chi Gringo throwing boomerangs, the axe throwing Indian Little Plum and Billy Six Guns a revolver shooting guy. As you make progress you fight cowboys, Indians and ghosts.

While shooting in all directions you walk across towns, deserts and rivers blasting everything that crosses your path. Along the way, you can pick up several items, including power-ups that make your bullets stronger, a double star item that gives your character a second weapon, so you can shoot both at the same time, extra lives and a barrel, which you can use to blow up everything near you and makes you invincible for a brief amount of time, this is useful when you are surrounded. Some levels have large mid-bosses and all of them have an end-of-level boss.
Heaven's Gate

Heaven's Gate (ヘブンズゲート) is a 1996 3D fighting arcade game with an arcade and Vs. mode, developed by Racdym (now known as Racjin) and published by Atlus. It is both Atlus and Racdym's first attempt in the 3D fighting game market.

The player can choose from one of the eight combatants that are available at the start, with a few more characters being available once their unlocked. Each character has a different nationality, specialty, and lineage. Each character represents either a good or an evil alignment and depending on the character chosen, it affects which final boss the player will have to fight against. 

Defending, punching and kicking are on three separate buttons. There are variations of each of these moves depending on how quick the button is pressed.

Consistently damaging or taking damage from an opponent will add to a sol or lunar (depending on the character the player is playing as) power gauge.
Heavy Barrel

Heavy Barrel is a shooter with a top-down view similar to Commando and Ikari Warriors. Terrorists have seized the underground control complex of a nuclear missile site. It is up to the player to infiltrate the installation and eliminate the leader of the terrorist army before they can launch the missiles. To stop the terrorists you will need the powerful weapon Heavy Barrel. The problem is that the weapon still is in the installation. Before the fortress fell the weapon was taken apart and locked in six different storage lockers. To defeat the terrorists you must collect all keys and reassemble the weapon.

The name of the game is from an in-game weapon. The Heavy Barrel is found in six pieces and is an energy cannon capable of destroying any enemy in the game with a single shot (except the final enemy, and possibly one other boss that may have required two shots).
Heavy Metal

Heavy Metal is a top-down, vertically-scrolling shooter in the same vein as Vindicators from Atari. You guide a tank from the bottom to top through four levels vertically shooting foes along the way.

The screen scrolls automatically and there is free movement for the tank. A radar on the left side screen scans at a constant rate, showing the tank's position and incoming enemies by pinging them. Four different power-ups can be picked up along the way: a shield (yellow), super shot (orange), a super missile (blue) and speed up (green). There are several lives, but a single hit is immediately fatal.
Heavy Metal: Geomatrix

Based on the Heavy Metal world created by Kevin Eastman and Simon Bisley, this fighting title allows you to take control of a team of three fighters, ranging from a basic all-rounder, or a lightning fast female to a huge bulky mass of power. Of course, they are all a mix of human and humanoid, and depending on their strengths, have a range of different moves and styles.

The main aim of the game is to defeat each of the opposing 3-man teams ahead of you, and dominate cyberspace.

The game mixes a little of Street Fighter with a dash of Virtual On, allowing you to fight in close or use long range attacks all inside a 3D landscape.
Heavy Smash

Heavy Smash portrays a futuristic, armored, no-rules version of handball. The player is allowed to select one of various national teams (plus a robot team with a space station as home turf), some of them with an unique armor design reflecting some kind of perceived national tradition (a samurai armor for Japan and a sort of sci-fi football outfit or USA, for example) and some other being just palette swaps. Each team has a distinctive special shot, which has to be loaded up with a power gauge and each team member, in addition to tackling and roughing up opponents with no penalty whatsoever, can even perform a ranged attack in order to gain ball control.

At its core, it's the typical “win or go home” coin-op sports game, with increasing difficulty and opponent skill each match.
Heavy Traffic
A vertical motorcycle racing game from Digital Games.
Heavy Unit

The human colony "Le Tau" is under attack by some strange aliens. It is the player's job to use a special starship and destroy everything which moves. Heavy Unit is a typical side-scrolling shooter with six levels filled with enemies, mid and end bosses. 

Destroyed enemies may leave behind items which have beneficial effects when collected: increased speed, better weapon power, a shield, extra lives or transformation into a robot. The robot has a more powerful weapons system (laser beam and homing energy balls instead of a vulcan gun), but also a downside: its large size makes it easier to be hit by enemies or crash into the environment. If that happens, a life and all collected upgrades are lost and the ship is reset at the last checkpoint.

While the level layouts are identical in all versions, there are some minor differences in enemy placement, graphics (e.g. the Genesis version has more colours and bigger enemies) and sound.
Heavyweight Champ (1976)

The 1976 release of Heavyweight Champ is a discrete logic arcade fighting game released by Sega. It was later remade as the more commonly known Heavyweight Champ from 1987.

To play, the game, grab the controller in the shape of a glove, move it up and down to change the arm height, push it in and release it. Eat a punch and the player's character goes down with a comical sound. The number of downs is displayed on the screen. The closer you hit the opponent, the higher the score value is—and a score for a right punch is twice as high as the left punch. The game ends in 45-80 seconds.
Heavyweight Champ (1987)

Heavyweight Champ is a boxing game that's a spiritual sequel to the identically named arcade title released by Sega in 1976.

That game was a monochrome, side-view boxing game, but in this title, the perspective changes to camera behind our player (a boxer).The arcade cabinet has a lever for each hand (left-right). To play, you can hit or defend with both hands and move from side to side. 

To use your fists, the system uses a controller rod that measures 3 vertical positions: low-medium-high. Some of the possible moves are hooks, uppercut and straight jab.

Heavyweight Champ challenges the player to win and defend the title of the Heavyweight Championship. Our protagonist is called Kid "K.O." Crusher and the 4 adversaries are: Sammy "Smasher" Smith, Jerry "Cyclone" Charger, George "Iceberg" Cooler and the champion Willie "Vulture" Wilson. 

There are 3 levels of difficulty and we start on the left of the screen, the blue corner, and our opponent on the right side, the red corner.
Hebereke no Popoon

Hebereke's Popoon is a falling block puzzle game which is always played against an opponent, either AI or human. Just like in Dr. Mario, there is always a pair of two blocks of varying colours falling down from the top of the screen. As long as they are falling, the blocks can be rotated. The goal is to bring three or more blocks of the same colour together; then they disappear and cause a special block to appear on the opponent's side. After a block vanishes, the blocks over it fall down. The match is lost, when the space the pair of blocks appear in is filled by another block, i.e. the screen is full.

The game has eight characters and the special block mentioned above is the head of the own character. It can be only removed when matched with a block of the same colour. However, when the player manages to create a chain reaction one of two special attacks may be unleashed against the opponent, e.g. reversing the controls or obscuring the vision for 10 seconds.
Heiankyo Alien

Heiankyo Alien (平安京エイリアン) is a 1979 arcade game produced by Denki Onkyo. The game runs on cloned Head On hardware.

Heiankyo Alien was retooled by Gremlin/Sega for western audiences as Digger. Unlike Digger, Heiankyo Alien uses slightly different graphics in some sections and places all of the enemies on screen at once (as opposed to Digger's method of filtering them in after a period of time).

1000 years ago the city of Kyo was suddenly invaded by aliens. A Kebiishi (knight of the past) was entrusted to defend the city.

The game starts with a maze where the kebiishi and some aliens appear. The aliens start moving through the maze wherever they please. While trying to keep from getting eaten, the kebiishi digs holes where the aliens will likely travel. If an alien comes to a finished hole, it will fall in an be trapped for a while. While the alien is trapped in the hole, you can fill the hole to bury it. If all aliens are buried, the round ends and you can proceed to the next round.
HeliFire

In HeliFire, the player controls a submarine under attack by helicopters and aquatic undersea life. The goal is to dodge the helicopter bombs and the marine fauna and fire back at the helicopters. Different colored helicopters move at different speeds. As the game progresses, the number of helicopters, sea creatures, and bombs increases.
Hellfire

In the year 2998, humanity has finally reached the stars, and was able to build a prosperous, peaceful society. However, a space matter known as the Black Nebula began to spread, threatening to engulf the galaxies controlled by humans. It turned out that a robotic dictator named Super Mech was behind this occurrence. The Earth sends Captain Lancer, a skillful pilot navigating the powerful CNCS1 aircraft, equipped with the most powerful weapon: the Hellfire...

This is a horizontal space shooter, with the traditional premise of a lone pilot traversing hostile areas and out-manoeuvring and/or destroying quick and numerous enemies. What sets this shooter apart from many other horizontal space shooters is that you choose the direction of your shots at any time between forward, backward, upward+downward and 4-way diagonal.
Hello! Pop'n Music

HELLO! POP'N MUSIC also known as simply POP'N MUSIC in North American release, is an arcade-exclusive game of the Pop'n Music series. Its location test initiated on March 23, 2011. 

Unlike all of the original Pop'n Music series, HELLO! POP'N MUSIC was developed into four buttons (red, blue, green, and yellow, instead of adding white), and eight buttons in two-player mode. If you hit a token Pop-kun, you will receive more tickets.

This game introduces a new gameplay mechanic called the TOKIMEKI METER, when you use one of all of the characters who appeared in HELLO! POP'N MUSIC. As the TOKIMEKI METER increases, you will receive initial cutscenes. Also on the Konami DX mobile, you can also receive an e-mail from the character you've played.
Hells Bells

Hell's Bells is a classic UK pub fruit machine originally manufactured by Bell-Fruit (Bell-Fruit Games). Originally released as a low-jackpot classic (such as the popular £5 jackpot version), it has remained a favorite among retro arcade enthusiasts and emulator communities.
Herbie at the Olympics

Try to qualify in various Summer Olympic events.

This game was also available as a conversion kit for Donkey Kong and Donkey Kong Jr cabinets. The kit contained ROMs and a daughter card to replace the original ROMs and CPU on the Donkey Kong board set.
Hero
Wander through a maze and collect the heart, diamond, spade, club and in later stages 'J' to move to the next level on your way to rescuing Esmeralda. Avoid the fireballs and arrows.
Hero in the Castle of Doom

Hero In The Castle Of Doom was developed by Seatongrove and licensed to Crown Vending in 1984.

The game featured (once again) Quasimodo’s attempts to rescue Esmeralda (or, in this case Ezzmerelda). This one is basically a rip-off of Tutankham (though not a blatant one). Interestingly, the original flyers for the game referred to it as Hero in the “Temple” of Doom and featured the image of an Indiana-Jones-like character, complete with fedora (one wonders if they changed the name and character in an effort to avoid litigation).
Heuk Sun Baek Sa

Heuk Sun Baek Sa (흑선백사) is a rare, Korean tabletop puzzle arcade game developed by Oksan and published by F2 System in August 1997. The title roughly translates from Korean to English as "Black first, kill white", giving a major clue to its gameplay structure.

Rather than a traditional action or fighting game, Heuk Sun Baek Sa centers around localized puzzle tactics, heavily inspired by the traditional board game Go (Baduk).
Hexa

Hexa is an arcade puzzle game. The player needs to match 3 identical or more tiles in a row (horizontally, vertically or diagonally), as long they match each other, based on Sega's Columns rules, as the Hexa is a clone of it. The more matches you get, the faster the blocks fall, but they eventually revert to their normal speed. Unlike Columns "Magic Jewels" work differently and are called "Pobys". Instead of appearing once the jewels get close to the top of the screen. The player has a supply of Pobys (Either 2 or 4 depending on the DIP Switch) and they can spawn them anytime they want.
Hexion

Hexion is a variant of the falling block puzzle game Hextris which in turn is a variant of Tetris that uses shapes made of hexagons instead of the usual tetraminoes. The aim of the game is still to align the falling blocks so that lines are created. They are then removed and points are earned. As the game goes on the level increases which leads to faster falling blocks. The game ends when blocks reach the top but the continue option allows the player to keep playing on the same level but with the score being reset.

In addition to the normal mode there are three additional game modes with their own playing fields. There is one that is extra wide, one that is extra long and one that is diagonally shaped as a slash. There are also three multiplayer modes for two players. There is a normal mode and a battle mode that both are played in split screen and there is also a co-op mode where the players share a wide playing field.
Hi Lo Silver

Hi Lo Silver is a classic UK fruit machine known for its distinct gambling mechanics, produced in older variants by manufacturers like Bell Fruit Games and later configurations by companies such as Red Gaming or Quest Gaming.
Hi Pai Paradise
Hi Pai Paradise is your typical Asian tabletop style Mahjong gambling game. This one was developed and manufactured by both Aruze and SETA in 2003.
Hi Pai Paradise 2
Hi*Pai Paradise 2 is a mahjong game, developed and published by Aruze Corp, which was released in Japan in 2004.
HI-LO Double Up Joker Poker

HI-LO Double Up Joker Poker is a classic 1980s coin-operated electronic gambling machine.

 The game was prominently manufactured by SMS Manufacturing Corp. (based in Lakewood, New Jersey) starting around 1982/1983, as well as Kramer Manufacturing
Hi-Way

Hi-Way is a driving arcade game. Atari's first sit-down cabinet, this game has the simple goal of driving a car down a road, staying on the road, and avoiding other cars. If the player crashes, they will be momentarily stopped. The car can drive off-road, but it's extremely slow. The score awarded depends on the distance the car travels.
Hickory Dickory Dosh

Hickory Dickory Dosh is a slot fruit machine by Mazooma.

The base game features traditional three-reel fruit machine symbols like sevens and various fruits, accompanied by a loud, full-throated arcade soundtrack. Triggering the main feature takes you to a classic British "trail" or bonus board style game centered around the clock graphic.
Hidden Catch

Hidden Catch is a classic photo-puzzle arcade videogame franchise originally developed and published by South Korean company Eolith. Debuting in 1998, the game introduced a digital twist on the classic "spot the difference" puzzle game concept.

The series is well-remembered for its hardware gimmick: instead of using traditional joysticks or buttons, players used an attached interactive pen to click directly on the screen. The pens contained a built-in force-feedback motor that delivered a strong physical vibration whenever a mistake was made or a level failed.
Hidden Catch 2

Hidden Catch 2 is a puzzle arcade video game developed and published by the South Korean company EOLITH in 1999. It is part of the popular Hidden Catch franchise, which specializes in "spot-the-difference" photo-hunting gameplay where players compare two images side-by-side to find discrepancies before time runs out.

The game features a colorful fantasy narrative where the "peace of Picture World" has been broken by a wicked wizard. Players guide "colour pencil knights" on an adventure to defeat the evil force.
Hidden Catch 2000

'Hidden Catch' is a directly experiencing puzzle game by comparing scenes on the left and right and finding non-matching parts with a pen. You can feel the fun with the powerful vibration generated from the pen, when you did not find 5 non-matching pictures or when you incorrectly found.
Hidden Catch 3
Hidden Catch 3 is a puzzle game developed and manufactured by South Korean arcade company Eolith and released in 2000.
High Impact Football

High Impact Football is American football arcade game that was released by Williams Electronics in 1990; it runs on Midway Games's Y-Unit hardware (only with two DACs, instead of just one), features fifteen teams to select from (Atlanta, Miami, Africa, Chicago, New York, Oakland, Denver, Pittsburgh, Europa, Detroit, San Francisco, Cincinnati, Kansas, Texas, Vegas, Los Angeles, Washington DC and Buffalo), and allowed up to four players to play it simultaneously (1P and 2P play against 3P and 4P).
High Seas Havoc

High Seas Havoc, known in Japan as Captain Lang (キャプテン ラング Kyaputen Rangu) and in Europe as Capt'n Havoc, is a video game that was made for the Sega Mega Drive/Genesis by Data East. It was also released in the arcades running on a Sega Mega Drive/Genesis based arcade cabinet.

The story is about an anthropomorphic pirate seal named Havoc (Lang in the Japanese version), his young sidekick Tide (Land in the Japanese version), a girl named Bridget, and an evil pirate named Bernardo.[4] Bernardo is looking for Emeralda, a gem with powers that can cause whole armies to be toppled.[4] A map shows where Emeralda is located, and Bernardo is looking for the map.[4] Havoc and Tide discover Bridget unconscious at a beach.[4] When she wakes up in a dwelling, she instructs Havoc to keep her and the map safe.[4] Havoc hides the map in a cliff.[4] After Bernardo's henchmen kidnaps Bridget and Tide; Havoc, the playable character, sets off to rescue them.[4]

Each level apart from the first two and las...
High Voltage

Mankind has conquered much of the universe and brought many alien races under their dominion. But now, in the year 3030, a rebellion has broken out centered about the planet of Regit. You have been dispatched in the star-ship "High Voltage" to quell the insurrection.

High Voltage is a first person space shoot-em-up with a 3D perspective. Each stage starts in space, and ends up on the surface of the planet, culminating in a fight with a boss machine. At any time, enemy vessels may approach and fire at you. You may either fire back after aiming at the enemy or a missile with the cross-hairs, or avoid by moving the cross-hairs off to one side causing your vessel to turn in that direction. Being hit with a projectile will cause enough damage to crack your view-port, and lose one of your lives. In addition to the standard rapid-fire lasers, which may overheat if used excessively, you have a limited supply of bombs which cause greater damage to a larger area.
Highway

The player controls a car that must avoid the other cars, as they will try to take you out of the road. The car can jump to avoid the cars and to finish the course, as the finish is after a roadless zone. If you manage to time your jump, press button two to free the parachute and land safely. After finishing the four courses, the game starts again with increased difficulty. The game is over when the player runs out of fuel.
Himeshikibu
Japanese Hanafuda cards\tile matching game.
hiphopmania complete MIX

hiphopmania Complete MIX is a rhythm arcade game where the player performs as a DJ mixing tracks on stage. It recreates the atmosphere of a live club performance, with visuals and gameplay designed around timing music samples to the beat. The game is the export version of beatmania complete MIX, which compiles music from earlier beatmania releases into one title.

beatmania complete MIX combines content from beatmania 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Mix, along with several new tracks. hiphopmania Complete MIX retains the same structure and mechanics but localizes the presentation for overseas markets. It serves as a collection entry in the series, bringing together existing music and gameplay into a single arcade release.
hiphopmania complete MIX 2

hiphopmania complete MIX 2 is the American version of Beatmania Complete MIX 2. It includes all but 10 songs from the Japanese version.

This is a music game, where you are given notes to play on the screen, and translate them through a series of buttons and the phonograph in front of you.
Hippodrome

Hippodrome is a mythologically-themed gladiator game with simple controls, allowing players to move left and right, jump, and attack. Players choose one of two human fighters, who must overcome eight terrifying and monstrous fantastic opponents (eg. dragon, wizard, scorpion-man) in the ring to win a tournament and rule the kingdom for one year.

Between bouts, players can visit a store and upgrade their equipment, granting them different health, range and damage bonuses. A second player can join in at any time to challenge the current player, but only the winner can proceed in the tournament.
Hissing Quid

The Hissing Quid is a classic UK pub fruit machine (Amusement with Prize / AWP) manufactured by QPS (Quantum Amusement Products).

 It features standard UK pub slot mechanics, including traditional physical reels, a cash/nudges prize ladder, and a complex digital "feature board" filled with mini-games, cash boosts, and strategy choices.
Hit 'n Miss

This shooting gallery game is made for younger players. There are seven different types levels, with different ways of how the player should do the shooting. One level requires the player to time shots to drop apples on passing targets, other levels has straightforward shooting of moving targets in the shortest time or otherwise shoot only specific targets. When a level ends, bonus points are adding for the time remaining. If the time runs out or the conditions for shooting specific targets are not met, then the game is over.
Hit Me

Use your gambling prowess to master the game of blackjack and beat the dealer as often as you possibly can in the fantastic Hit Me! The objective is to get a hand that is as close to the number 21 as possible. Set the stake for each hand and decide whether to gamble on, adding more cards to your hand or stick with what you have. Starting with a small stack of chips strategically play hands to increase your pot and become super rich!
Hit the Ice

Hit the Ice is a hockey video game originally released by Williams to arcades in 1990. Featuring a cartoonish representation of the sport, Hit the Ice features games with three players on each team (forward, defense, and goalie). Unlike standard hockey, there are very few rules, as players are encouraged to trip, elbow and kick opponents.
Hoccer

You are Andrew, the one man team. Ord and Clee are robots whose goal is to destroy you any way they can (by driving you against the boards, into a spinner, or by hitting you with a supercharged ball). Knock out Ord and Clee with your ball or by hitting them against the sides. Points are also scored by hitting the goal and hitting the targets on the sides.
Hockey

Hockey was produced by Ramtek in 1973.
One goalie and two wings move simultaneously for each player. The first player to score nine goals wins.
Hog Wild

A chase oriented driving game where the player assumes the role of a cop who attempts to arrest motorcycle-riding criminals. The game has four selectable characters, each with their own vehicles and three selectable courses: Easy, Medium and Hard. The object of the game is to arrest a quota of criminals and cross the finish line before time runs out. The player arrests criminal motorcyclists by ramming his or her car into them from the left or rear. Every arrest adds time as well as to the car's turbo gauge. When the gauge reaches maximum, the vehicle can pull the turbo lever and use either the all or half of the gauge. After three course are completed, the player can be one of the motorcyclists in a special bonus course.
Hogan's Alley

Hogan's Alley involves the use of the Nintendo Light Zapper. You are in the police station doing target practice, either with three targets at a time with at least one innocent person, or in an alley with both good and bad targets in windows and walking on the sidewalk. Then there's Trick Shot, where you shoot the cans, trying to make them land in a slot for points, or at least not let them fall to the ground.

The game was released on both the Nintendo VS. System and PlayChoice-10 Arcade systems.

PlayChoice-10 is an arcade machine that can consist of as many as 10 different games previously available only on the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) home console. The games for this system are in the modular form of circuit boards that are plugged into one of the ten open slots on the PlayChoice-10's motherboard.
Hokuha Syourin Hiryu no Ken

Hokuha Syourin Hiryū no Ken (北派少林 飛龍の拳, lit. "North Faction Shaolin - Fist of the Flying Dragon") is a historically significant 1985 arcade fighting game developed by Nihon Game (which later became Culture Brain). Released in Japan by Taito and internationally by Data East and Memetron under the title Shanghai Kid, it stands as the very first entry in the long-running Hiryū no Ken (Flying Dragon) franchise.
Hole Land

Hole Land is an arcade fixed shooter developed by Tecfri and released in Japan in 1984.

Player controls a multi-colored robot able to move to right and left, jump and shoot enemies such as small humanoids, rats, ghosts and snakes that come from holes above on the screen, vertically far away from the player, who stands always at the bottom of the stage and has to eliminate them all before they reach the bottom or simply avoid them to complete each level. Enemies are able to attack the player with bombs, making him unable to jump, move and shoot for a short time.The player can also become defenseless getting hit by incoming rocks from vulcans. A life is lost when enemies touch the player and take away the robot's lower half, which can be avoided by jumping over them without touching them.

The game has three stages. In the first two, each time the robot is damaged by rocks and bombs, a friendly, short, old man appears to help fix it.
Holosseum

Holosseum (ホロシアム) is a 1992 fighting arcade game developed and published by Sega. The name is a portmanteau of holography and colosseum, due to it being a fighting game created exclusively for Sega's hi-tech hologram theater cabinet, and is the second and last game created for it after Time Traveler. It was one of Sega's earliest attempts at creating a competitive fighting game along with Dark Edge, after the success of Capcom's Street Fighter II.

Holosseum plays similarly to other 2D versus fighting games during its release, which the player's character fights against his or her opponent in best two-out-of-three matches in a single player tournament mode with the computer or against another human player. The player has a character roster of four selectable fighters to choose from, each with their own fighting style and special techniques. Unlike most characters in Street Fighter II, these four characters lack fictional moves.
Homura

An evil fallen angel steals the Divine Crystal, one of Heaven's untouchable treasures. With this crystal he gains the power to control the thoughts of Shogun Ieyasu Tokugawa, and forces him to occupy Osaka castle and put himself in power using his newfound powers. In Heaven, the leaders of the individual heavenly families form a council with one aim... to regain the Divine Crystal. But they can't do this alone, so they decide to use the prisoner Homura to aid them. While they don't want to release him, he is the only one who's blood is half that of an angel and half human making him immune against the Crystal's powers. Homura refuses at first, but when he finds out that his mother was one of the victims at Osaka he picks up his sword and is ready to fight once again...

Homura is a top-down shoot'em up of the bullet-hell persuasion. The player takes on the role of Homura as he fights his way through 4 levels filled with demons.
Honey Doll

Honey Doll is a adult puzzle game based on Dharma Dōjō. The objective is to clear the stage of all blocks on screen by matching identical blocks underneath the platform. The number of consecutive matching blocks you have to put together increases as the stages advance. Matching blocks of the same kind reveal letters that float to the top of the screen. Grab enough of these to spell "Go Honey" and you can play one of the three different bonus stages. Unlike Dharma Dōjō where only the leftmost block of the row could be knocked, in this game you can punch blocks from both sides. Clearing the stages reveal pictures of naked women (this feature can be turned off via a DIP switch setting).
Honky Tonk
Honky Tonk is a classic video slot machine released by the prominent Australian gaming manufacturer Aristocrat Leisure in 2001.
Hook

Hook is a side-scrolling, weapon based beat'em up, based on the movie with the same title. The player takes the role of a grown-up Peter Pan, whose kids have been kidnapped by Captain Hook. Tinker Bell takes Peter back to Neverland where he must again become Pan and reclaim his children.

The players must hack their way past Hook's denizens through 11 levels. These include forests, icy regions, and towns which Peter will have to jump, climb, and swim through. Magic items such as apples and pixie dust can be collected for special powers. When enemies are attacked, they simply put their hands up in surrender rather than dying, so as to make the game more child-friendly.
Hoops '96

Similar to regular basketball games, with one major exception the players have super powers which allow them to perform incredible feats.

A standard basketball game where you view a scrolling court from the sidelines. The major difference in this game is that your players (on offense or defense) have super powers which allow them to make incredible shots, or incredible blocks. Your power reserve is diminished each time you use a special power. An interesting take on what otherwise would be yet another non-descript basketball game.
Hopper Robo

Hopper Robo (ホッパーロボ) is an arcade game released by Sega in 1983. The player controls a robot who can run and jump around a factory with the goal of knocking packages onto conveyor belts below while avoiding enemies. The game runs on Marine Boy hardware, developed by Orca one year prior.
Hopping Mappy

Hopping Mappy is an arcade game that runs on Namco System 86 hardware. It's the sequel to Mappy, which was released three years earlier.

In Hopping Mappy players control the Micro Police mouse, Mappy, as he bounces on a pogo stick to run circles around pink cats, called Meowkies, who patrol either vertically or horizontally. There is also Goro, a cat who patrols in a zigzag pattern, but he needs to take occasional breaks. There are eight treasures that a player must grab to complete a round, except on the bonus round where the player will just want to collect all the balloons that he can. The main intrigue here is getting past a blockade of Meowkies. The player controls are simple - he can bounce in any of the four directions, the only places he can land are the centres of the checkerboard squares (making for very few locations overall), and he will move at the same speed as the cats. If the player pushes the accelerator button and runs around, he will go twice as fast.
HopStar

HopStar Arcade Machine is a ticket redemption video game from Bay Tek which uses game play based off the old sidewalk game, Hop-scotch.

With its interactive, skillful game play, bright, colorful cabinet and the durable infrared hop pad, HopStar is a must-have for all game rooms.

Coin up and hop as far as you can on the hopscotch course in a set amount of time. The player-paced hop detection allows you to challenge yourself to improve— the faster you hop, the farther you get! You can even add time to your game by hopping on the bonus time clocks.

The variety of 3-dimensional courses on the 42" screen provide new challenges for every game. The progressive jackpot feature, course time and difficulty controls are adjustable in the operator menu, making the game a perfect fit for any location.
Horizon: Moon Patrol II

A horizontally scrolling shooter, Horizon is the spiritual sequel to Moon Patrol. Both were developed by Irem; Moon Patrol was licensed to Williams. There is no mention of Moon Patrol on the title screen as Williams still had the license at that time.

Players take control of a hover vehicle armed with a turret and a cannon, rolling over the terrain and alternating their position and perspective on three different lanes to destroy enemies and dodge attacks while avoiding obstacles and picking up fuel and other items.

Though never commercially released outside of Japan, it did at least make it to a location testing phase.
Horse Racing: Victory Furlong

Horse Racing: Victory Furlong (also known as Net Select Keiba Victory Furlong) is a rare horse racing arcade game developed and published by Sammy Corporation in 2005. It was released exclusively in Japan for the Sammy Atomiswave arcade platform.

Unlike large, physical motion simulators like Namco's famous Final Furlong series, Victory Furlong is a traditional arcade-cabinet experience that focused heavily on online network functionality via Sammy’s "AWNet" system, which allowed online matchmaking and card-based data tracking for Japanese arcade players.
HorseRiders 2
Horse Riders 2 is a card based horse racing game developed and published by Konami and released on Arcade on July 22, 2009 in Japan. It is the sequel of Horse Riders.
Host Invaders

Host Invaders is an extremely rare 1998 light-gun arcade video game developed by The Game Room and licensed to I.C.E. (Innovative Concepts in Entertainment) for sales in the United States.

Unlike fixed-shooter classics (such as Space Invaders), Host Invaders is a fast-paced, two-player joint optical gun shooter.
Players must save the crew stranded aboard the "Star Dart" space shuttle from an aggressive alien takeover.
The gameplay focuses on blasting hordes of hostile alien creatures and other unearthly, supernatural menaces.
Hot Blocks

Hot Blocks (also known as Hot Blocks: Tetrix II) is an adult-themed arcade game released in 1993 and published by the Spanish company NIX (sometimes credited as Nics).

It is a competitive 2-player Tetris clone. Players arrange falling blocks to clear horizontal rows.
Clearing lines and completing levels rewards players by slowly revealing adult/erotic background images of women.
Hot Body I
Puzzle arcade game showing bikini clad women between levels.
Hot Bubble
A Korean Puzzle Bobble/Bust-A-Move clone/knockoff by Pandora/Afega in 1998. There are two versions, one with adult themes, and one without
Hot Chase

Hot Chase is an arcade game released in 1988 by Konami. In the game, players drive a white Porsche out of an enemy country to the Border crossing of a friendly one. The car has a bomb attached to it that explodes in a set time. If the bomb explodes, players must restart. There are many obstacles along the way, including railroad crossings, military checkpoints, helicopters that shoot at the car and other cars. The gameplay is said to be similar to Chase HQ.

Completing the game resulted in a scene where the hero exits the car, takes his machine gun, and fires at the car to add to the damage before the bomb explodes. Then the game played the following message: "Mission Complete. You have succeeded in stealing the enemy armored super car and have crossed the border to freedom. After a few days the enemy surrendered to our country. You will be remembered for your brave deeds. Thanks a million!"
Hot Chilli
A five reel, single-player slot\fruit machine released by Pacific Gaming Pty, Ltd. in 1995 with dual coin sensor.
Hot Memory

Hot Memory is a mature-themed retro arcade video game released in Germany on November 30, 1994. Developed by the prominent American studio Incredible Technologies exclusively for the German distributor Tuning Electronic Entertainment, it operated on a standard Motorola 68000 arcade cabinet architecture.

Hot Memory is a direct, stripped-down clone of the 1994 Strata/Incredible Technologies arcade game Pairs. It functions as a digital tile-matching memory game.
Hot Mind
Hot Mind is a puzzle game developed by Playmark in 1995 for the Arcade.
Hot Property

The Monopoly Hot Property fruit machine is a highly popular, classic UK pub gaming machine originally made by Mazooma (and often associated with the Bell-Fruit / Barcrest group). Based on the iconic board game, it blends standard reel spinning with a feature-rich board game bonus round where players collect classic colored properties (like dark blue, green, and yellow) to climb the win plan.
Hot Rod

A hot rod racing game from Sega. Upgrade your car with the money awarded from completing races quickly.

There are two types of cabinets for this arcade classic. There is the three player upright style, or there is the table top four player version.
Hot Shocker

Hot Shocker is an action game, developed by E.G. Falaco and published by Domino, which was released in 1982.

Dudley must change the color of the web by walking on it while being chased.
Hot Shots Tennis

Hot Shots Tennis is an arcade based tennis game for one or two players that is played on a vertical split screen. The game features 32 opponents with different skills, from beginners to pros. Playing is done with a joystick and two buttons: one for hard shots and one for soft shots. Pressing both buttons together leads to a lob. When serving, either button is pressed and the joystick is moved left or right to aim. When the ball is in the air a blue spot shows where it will land. The spot will ultimately turn red and the player should then attempt a swing. To hit the ball to the left the swing should be as soon as it turns red while to hit to the right the swing should happen shortly after.

The game has a time limit based on how many coins have been spent. By default one coin gives one minute of play time in a single player game and 90 seconds in a two player game. When time runs out the player has to use more coins to continue playing.
Hot Toppings

Hot Toppings is a classic, pizza-themed video slot machine released by WMS Gaming in the year 2000. It became highly popular in casinos during the early 2000s due to its distinct interactive bonus rounds and cartoonish pizza chef theme.
Hot Wheels Plug and Play

There are 2 different Hot Wheels Plug and Play units, there's one that's a wheel shaped controller, and is similar to one of the GBA games (clearly using some of the same assets) and then there's this one, a unit with 2 small car shaped controllers. Interestingly this one likely shipped in different configurations as there's a solder pad inside each controller which selects 1 of 2 possible car types. There doesn't seem to be any other footage on YouTube of this Plug and Play at the time of uploading, but there's plenty of the other Hot Wheels one (that still isn't dumped / emulated)
Hot Wheels: King of the Road

Hot Wheels: King of the Road is a fun multiplayer driving game developed by Coin Crew and Adrenaline Amusements. As the name implies, the challenge is to be the “king of the road” by reaching the end first and collecting as many coins as you can along the Hot Wheels track along the way. Drive one of six real Hot Wheels cars, choose from one of the three tracks, then go, Go, GO!

Staying true to the Hot Wheels theme, the multi-lane tracks include ramps for catching big air, loop-de-loops and plenty of obstacles that can get in the way of reaching the end first. Each race is a blast of chaotic fun, as the cabinet was designed to handle up to six players at a time! If any spot isn’t taken by a person when the game beings, then it is filled in by the computer. Use the foot pedal to activate a Nitro boost, but use it wisely to keep your advantage. Bonus coins are awarded based upon your finish spot; collect the most and walk away with the most tickets.
Hotdog Storm

Hotdog Storm is a 2D arcade vertically scrolling shooter. The player controls spaceship and eliminates various enemies - mechas, helicopters, other spaceships etc. He has a basic cannon, limited supply of bombs, and collectable powerups.
House Mannequin Roppongi Live hen

House Mannequin - Roppongi Live hen (ハウスマネキン 六本木ライブ篇) is a Japanese arcade video game released in April 1987.
Developed and published by the veteran arcade developer Nichibutsu (Nihon Bussan), it is an adult-themed Mahjong game that stands as the second entry in their short-lived House Mannequin series.
House of the Dead: Scarlet Dawn

House of the Dead: Scarlet Dawn is the fifth arcade game in the House of the Dead series. It takes place in 2006, between the events of The House of the Dead 4 and The House of the Dead III. The game's story follows AMS agents Kate Green and Ryan Taylor who infiltrate Scarecrow Manor just as a horde of bioengineered creatures attack. From then on they have to fight their way to safety while exploring the mansion and uncovering who is behind the outbreak.

Like in previous games in the series, the player uses a gun controller to shoot enemies as they appear on the screen. Each creature has a weak spot that deals extra damage when hit. In addition to the monsters, there are also civilians that have to be avoided. The player also has to keep track of the partner who at any time might need to be rescued. Failure to do so before time runs out leads to a life penalty.
Huanle Liuhe Yi
Happy 6-in-1 (欢乐六合一) is a PGM arcade game that includes a text-based quiz game, a cooking game, a tile-based game and three playing card games.
Hummer

Hummer is an arcade racing game released by Sega in 2009. The game runs on the Sega Lindbergh platform. There are two game modes: Race Mode and Time Attack Mode. In Race Mode, players choose between 3 Hummers, each with an additional variant, to race against 20 opponents. Two different variants of the cabinet feature two sets of controls side-by-side. This enables co-op play between players on the same cabinet using the "Driver Change System", which swaps the person controlling the vehicle at checkpoints or after collisions. Consequently, it is possible for up to 8 people to race at the same time, if the maximum of four 2-player machines are linked. The game also features a boost meter, which can grant a speed boost when filled. The boost meter is increased by driving through destructible obstacles and landing controlled jumps.
Hummer: Extreme Edition

Hummer: Extreme Edition is an off-road racing game from Sega. The game is licensed by General Motors and puts you behind the wheel of a Hummer SUV. Players must navigate a variety of different terrains including snow, mud, and dirt.

A single cabinet can operate as a 2-player game using the "Driver Change System". The driver changes according to the timing of checkpoints and contact with other cars. Courses available are Bluster Canyon (beginner), Isolated Jungle (intermediate), Calibou Valley (advanced), and Industrial Hill (pro). There are various obstacles throughout each course which can be destroyed to accumulate boost. Once the gauge reaches maximum, players can use the boost button which makes the player speed up and become indestructible for a short period of time.
Hunchback

The game is set on a castle wall. The player must cross the screen from left to right avoiding obstacles in order to ring the bell at the far right. Obstacles include pits which must be swung over on a long rope, ramparts which must be jumped (some of which contain knights with spears) and flying fireballs and arrows (to be ducked or jumped). Eventually, after completing a number of screens, the player must rescue Esmeralda. If this final screen is completed, the game begins again at a faster speed. The game had several official ports to just about every 8-bit microcomputer during the 1980s, as well as a number of clones with various names.
Hunchback Olympics

The Games of the XXIII Olympiad were held in Los Angeles in 1984 and for the first time since the advent of the video game industry, this king of sporting competitions was to be held in a first-world nation. In simpler times, this might have inspired people to head out to a track or gymnasium to try their stuff, but now for the first time an industry was poised to let the hands of the middle-class masses do all the work virtually, through joysticks, needing no facilities or specialised equipment (beyond a video game console) to try the whole gamut of events.

Since numerous companies realised this around the same time, from a marketing perspective, the only serious question is: what's going to make your Olympiad game stand out from the rest? Will you have an expensive celebrity endorsement by a Gold medal-winner? Will you implement the flags and national anthems of all participating countries? Perhaps you've been beaten to the punch.
Hustle

Hustle is an arcade game released on Blockade hardware that is effectively the first version of Snake. The player directs a snake-like object moving around the play field. Each game lasts for 90 seconds. Periodically, targets will appear with a point value. You must aim for the target while avoiding your opponent's tail - and your own. 

One or two players can play simultaneously. You also have three options pertaining to your targets - a normal game where target values don't change, a countdown where the value slowly falls, and a count up where values slowly climb and delaying can increase your score. There are also three skill levels that alter the speed of the game and the intelligence of the computer player.
Hwy Chase

Hwy Chase is a vertical shoot-em-up in the style of Space Invaders and was released for arcade cabinets fitted with the Data East cassette system. You control a police car that is pursuing automobile driving miscreants in two stages. The first stage consists of a pattern or formation of cars with the occasional cars breaking formation to either shoot at or collide with you. The second stage consists of overtaking small groups of three cars that weave unpredictably between lanes. The two stages alternate until the end of the game.

Hitting a car or one of its shots will lose one of your three lives. You can move the car horizontally or vertically, but you can only shoot a single bullet at a time. Sometimes, the chase enters a tunnel, where you can only see cars within the range of your headlights.

The very similar game Mad Alien was released as a dedicated arcade machine.
Hydra

If being the best speedboat racer in the world were all there was to life, you'd live on easy street. But when the government of Hydra has asked for your help in defeating Hydra's enemies by couriering parts to a secret weapon, and those enemies know you're coming... well then, life gets interesting.

Race down narrow swamp lanes to deliver parts of a secret weapon to bases at the finish of each section. Enemies will be shooting at you, but you can shoot back with Uzi Cannons and Nukes. Collect crystals along the way to boost your speed or shields.
Hydro Thunder

Prepare for the power, speed and thrills of Hydro Thunder super-boat racing! Mighty Hull your way to the finish line of the most treacherous water courses imaginable!
With turbo-charged Boosts and monstrous jumps, only your fears stand in the way!
Hyper Athlete

A sport game where players must qualify across eleven olympic events. The game features 32-bit 3-D graphics, great sound, as well as voice. This arcade game is actually an optimized version of the Playstation game "International Track & Field" and it is a great modernization of Konami's original Track & Field game. World records are kept permanently.
Hyper Bishi Bashi Champ

A collection of short mini-games. It was released in Japan and Europe, possibly other regions but not in the US. The cabinet has three large coloured buttons for each player (as well as a start button), most of the games involve quickly bashing the buttons or pressing the colour corresponding to an object on-screen. There are always three competitors, which can be either human or CPU controlled.
Hyper Crash

Hyper Crash is a 3rd person perspective driving game where you have to drive along a course over various stages destroying as many cars as you can. As you drive along, a fuel gauge slowly decreases and if this empties then it is game over. To re-fuel your car you must destroy the other cars to keep it topped up. There are two ways to destroy them, either by repeatedly ramming a car until its damage meter fills or flip your car in the air to land on them. Flipping your car destroys the other cars in one go but this wastes fuel. As you progress other cars will flip in the air as well and if you are destroyed then it wastes fuel. Other obstacles to look out for are barrels which when hit destroys your car but you can ram other cars into them.
Hyper Duel

In Hyper Duel, the player controls one of three "Buster Gears” pilots: Keith Spader, Lisa Rowling, or Dr. B. Lloyd, and must destroy alien forces.
Buster Gears look like normal spaceships but have two modes - spaceship and robot - with different fire modes. 

The ships can also acquire additional helper units by collecting either the T or G items. The weapon can be upgraded by collecting P items.
Hyper Dyne: Side Arms

The game is mainly a horizontal scrolling shoot-em-up, although some scenes scroll vertically too. Shooting enemies will reveal power-ups and continually shooting them will either change their type or reveal a special weapon. Different weapons are more effective than others when fighting the end bosses.

Originating in the arcades, Side Arms is a horizontally scrolling shoot ‘em up in which you control Lieutenant Henry (a second player can control Sergeant Sanders in some versions), armed with crude weaponry and protective jump-suits. They must save the earth from the mercenary invaders of Bozon. You must first reach Bozon’s territories, then wipe out its forces hidden in caverns and lurking in underground seas, before destroying the main invasion ship. Lots of extra weapons can be picked up, often with similar tokens to those in 1943 and some other Capcom titles. Most weapons can be shot either to the left or the right, giving you more range to launch attacks.
Hyper Pac-Man

This is an updated version of Namco's "Pac-Man", featuring forced-perspective 3-D graphics that allow the players to jump over the enemy ghosts; in a similar fashion to Namco's "Pac-Mania", released in 1987. There are secret items and food to be found on each level that increases the player's power and score. For extra bonus stages, complete a level without eating any of the power dots.
Hyper Sports

Hyper Sports, known in Japan as Hyper Olympic '84 is an arcade game published in 1984 by Konami. It is the sequel to 1983's Track & Field and features seven all-new Olympic events. Like its predecessor, Hyper Sports has two run buttons and one action button per player. The Japanese release of the game sported an official license for the 1984 Summer Olympics.
Hyper Sports (Remake)

Hyper Sports was remade in 2011, based on Konami's original Hyper Sports from 1984. The cabinet was only released in China.The game offers the player several different Olympic events for the player to choose from, inlcuding Ping-Pong, Hurdles, and Long Jump.
Hyper Street Fighter II: The Anniversary Edition

Hyper Street Fighter II: The Anniversary Edition is a fighting game that ran on the same CP System II hardware as its predecessor and was the final game released for the platform.

Created to commemorate the 15th anniversary of the Street Fighter series, it is a modified port of Super Street Fighter II Turbo (1994) in which players can control any versions of the main characters from the five Street Fighter II games previously released for the arcades: The World Warrior, Turbo, Champion Edition, Super, and Super Turbo). This totals to 17 characters with 65 variations.
Hyperdrive

Midway's futuristic arcade hover-racing game. Hyperdrive features custom arcade controls, a sit-down cabinet, and state-of-the-art 3D graphics.

The game has three different tracks with three levels of difficulty:
Track 1, Beginner Level, Orbital Speedway
Track 2, Advanced Level, Asteroid Mine
Track 3, Expert Level, Deep Space

Four different selectable ships are also available:
Ship 1, Beginner, Comprehensive Auto Pilot
Ship 2, Intermediate, High Speed
Ship 3, Advanced, Extreme Acceleration
Ship 4, Expert, Highly Manueverable
I'm Sorry

I'm Sorry, known in Japan as Gombe's I'm Sorry (ごんべえのあいむそ〜り〜 Gonbē no Aimusōrī), is an arcade game released by Coreland/Sega in 1985 for the Sega System 1. This action game stars a caricature of former Prime Minister of Japan, Kakuei Tanaka. The title is actually a play on the Japanese word for Prime Minister, Sōri (総理). The game satirizes Tanaka's greed by making the goal of the game acquiring gold bars. This arcade game made it into some of the United States arcades. It could be considered one of the earliest forms of political satire in a video game. 

The goal is for the greedy protagonist to collect all the gold bars while jumping over or defeating various enemies and obstacles in each maze-like level. Some of these enemies are: Giant Baba (a Japanese wrestler), a moonwalking Michael Jackson, Madonna, Japanese comedian Tamori, Carl Lewis, moving statues (activated when passed by).
I, Robot

The game play consists of moving robot1984 over all of the red tiles while avoiding objects flying at you from the back of the screen. Eliminating the red tiles diminishes the shield at the back of the playfield which prevents you from flying to the next level. To get to all the red tiles, players sometimes need to leap across empty space which creates a permanent bridge between the two points.
