Leaps across empty space have to be timed so that the "eye" of Big Brother in the back of the playfield, which randomly opens and closes, does not see robot1984 and destroy him.
Ibara

Ibara takes place in the 19th century, shortly after the development of the steam engine. Because of their precision crafting, the Northern European country of Edelweiss has excelled in the mechanical industry, and was achieving tremendous amounts of growth.

However, dark clouds would soon rise up over Edelweiss’ horizon, as Professor Teresa Rose spoke to her 5 guardians with a fearless smile on her face. “Let’s destroy this filthy land and its people. We must make this world beautiful. Yes… then we’ll make the entire surface a lovely rose garden.” Teresa began her attack from their fortress, resembling a twisted and jagged mountain of knives.
Under the Rose Garden Emblem, the nails of eerily laughing iron men destroyed buildings, the roars of planes covering the sky burn the Earth. The people’s cries and the rising flames illuminate the fortress, as if it were a beautiful flower blossoming from the scorched earth.
Ibara Kuro Black Label

Ibara takes place in the 19th century, shortly after the development of the steam engine. Because of their precision crafting, the Northern European country of Edelweiss has excelled in the mechanical industry, and was achieving tremendous amounts of growth.

However, dark clouds would soon rise up over Edelweiss’ horizon, as Professor Teresa Rose spoke to her 5 guardians with a fearless smile on her face. “Let’s destroy this filthy land and its people. We must make this world beautiful. Yes… then we’ll make the entire surface a lovely rose garden.” Teresa began her attack from their fortress, resembling a twisted and jagged mountain of knives.
Under the Rose Garden Emblem, the nails of eerily laughing iron men destroyed buildings, the roars of planes covering the sky burn the Earth. The people’s cries and the rising flames illuminate the fortress, as if it were a beautiful flower blossoming from the scorched earth.
Ice Age: Ice Breaker

One of the world’s highest grossing animated movie licenses of all time is now a stunning two player skill redemption game. ICE and Play Mechanix are proud to unveil one of the most eye-catching and alluring redemption attractions to ever hit the market.

Ice Age boasts a 42” horizontally mounted LCD panel for game play and two 23” vertically mounted LCD panels, in the marquee, that display the upcoming movie trailer while at the same time showing players how to win. Never before has a redemption game had such a captivating marquee that attracts players from all over the game room.

The game features two sets of interactive acorn “pads” where the player tries to win the big ticket bonus by timing his hit of the acorns to crack the ICE all the way through to the center BONUS ring. Crack the ice into the center ring and you win the operator adjustable super bonus!
Ice Cold Beer

Ice Cold Beer is a mechanical arcade game released by Taito in 1983. The game is in a similar cabinet to an arcade video game, but where the screen would normally be there is a vertical wooden playfield dotted with holes. Two joysticks on the control panel control the height of the two ends of a metal bar that moves up and down the playfield, with a ball bearing rolling back and forth on the bar. The playfield is an amber color, and the holes in the playfield are suggestive of bubbles rising in a mug of beer.

The objective of the game is to use the two joysticks to tip the bar back and forth and maneuver the ball up to a specific lit hole on the playfield, while avoiding unlit holes. When the player deposits the ball in the lit hole, the ball and the bar return to the bottom of the playfield, and the next target hole is lit. The game begins with the bottom-most hole lit, and subsequent lit holes become more and more difficult to reach while avoiding unlit holes.
Ice Man

Ice Man is a two-player, coin-operated water-gun arcade ticket-redemption game (videmption) developed by Guangzhou Superwing Animation Technology and distributed by Coastal Amusements.

 Players use physical, mounted water cannons to spray and freeze waves of incoming cartoon zombies across multiple stages (such as islands, deserts, and cemeteries).
 The mechanics are heavily inspired by Plants vs. Zombies, replacing pea-shooters with a water and ice theme.
Ichi Ban Jyan
Ichi Ban Jyan is a Japanese mahjong-themed arcade board game released for arcade systems and frequently emulated on MAME (Multiple Arcade Machine Emulator).
Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai II

The third installment in the Suchie-Pai series of mahjong games. More beautiful girls are ready to be your opponent in a game of strip mahjong.

A girl named Shiho Katagiri has been kidnapped, and it's up to Suchie-Pai to save her. Suchie-Pai will need to beat several opponents in mahjong in order to progress. The strip scenes are animated this time. You are also joined by some of your opponents, who can transform into heroes themselves.
Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai III
Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai III is a mahjong video game was developed and published by Jaleco as the third game in the series.
Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai Special

Idol Janshi Suchie-Pai Special is a Japan-exclusive adult riichi mahjong arcade game developed and published by Jaleco, released in December 1993.

Serving as a revamped arcade follow-up to the Super Famicom title Bishōjo Janshi Suchie-Pai, the game focuses on a two-player mahjong variant. Players select from one of six female characters to face off against opponents in high-stakes tiles matches. The visual style and character designs were created by renowned manga artist and illustrator Kenichi Sonoda.

Unlike its console predecessor, the 1993 arcade release is classified as an eroge (erotic game) because losing opponents undress for the player, introducing stripping and full nudity to the gameplay loop.
Idol Mahjong Final Romance

This game is the first in a series of strip mahjong games by Video System. Unlike the rest, this one used digitized photos of real models, while its successors use anime girls. The gameplay is standard for the genre, playing mahjong against computer opponents. It is possible between rounds to purchase features to turn the odds in your favor.
Idol no Himitsu
A mahjong game. The title of this game translates from Japanese as 'Idol's Secret'.
Idol-Mahjong Housoukyoku

Idol-Mahjong Housoukyoku (アイドル麻雀 放送局) is an eroge (adult-themed) mahjong arcade game published by System Service and released exclusively in Japan in 1988. Translated as Idol-Mahjong Broadcasting Studio, it is historically recognized as the very first entry in the Idol Mahjong subgenre, laying the groundwork for more famous subsequent series like Video System's Idol Mahjong Final Romance.
Iemoto

A mahjong game where the player battles mercenaries to save girls.
The title of this game translates from Japanese as 'Principal'.
IGMO

IGMO was developed by Magic Conversations, Inc. and published by EPOS Corporation in 1984.

In IGMO the player controls the dragon-slayer Igmo to rescue the beautiful Princess Iggy from the clutches of the evil dragon Sintar from the underworld. There is a limited time to traverse through the level and save the princess. Igmo can shoot in one out of eight directions. To cross a river, the player must shoot Bergs in positions that form a bridge. In the middle of the level, the player must watch out for Octoids, Spidoids and Crustoids as well as the Bouncers that form boundaries. When fighting Sintar, his fiery projectiles must be avoided and the dragon must be shot multiple times to be defeated. When the princess is rescued, the player will progress to a more difficult level.
Ikari III: The Rescue

Ikari III: The Rescue (also known as Ikari Warriors III: The Rescue), known simply as Ikari III (怒Ⅲ) in Japan, is an arcade beat 'em up. It was ported to the NES, DOS, and C64. It is the second sequel to the original Ikari Warriors, following Victory Road.
Ikari Warriors

Ikari Warriors is a 1986 arcade game by SNK, published in the United States and Europe by Tradewest. Known simply as Ikari (怒 ?, literally "fury") in Japan, this was SNK's first major breakthrough US release and became something of a classic. The game was released at the time when there were many Commando clones on the market. What distinguished Ikari Warriors were rotary joysticks and the two-player mode.
Ikaruga

A shoot-em-up arcade game which brings a perfect blend of classic arcade shooting and original gameplay. The player's ship can switch between two different 'polarities': White and Dark. The Dark polarity can absorb dark colored enemy bullets while the White polarity can absorb white-colored enemy bullets. If the player kills 3 enemies of the same color in a row, a combo is built up that adds to the score.
Il Galeone
A slot machine gambling game published by San Remo Games in 2000.
Il Pagliaccio

"Il Pagliaccio" is an Italian casino/gambling game (frequently classified under the "casino" or "slot" genre in emulation databases). Because it ran on custom hardware found in commercial cabinets rather than standard home consoles, it has been preserved by arcade enthusiasts.
Illvelo

Trapped inside a computer operating system, the player's ship shoots their way out one stage at a time. Illvelo's distinct system focuses on the player's options (aka support ships). Options normally follow the player's ship like in other shmups. However, when the player presses their second button, the options launch foward and stay at the location they land at. They will continue to fire when the player presses the primary shot button, allowing them to effectively place a stationary attack that can continue to fire bullets in place while the player dodges enemy bullets. Holding down the second button lets the player reposition their option when it's in the field, and tapping it recalls them so that they begin following the player again. Each stage has several warps which suck the player into a bonus stage when they get near.
Image Fight

Image Fight is a 1988 vertically scrolling shooter arcade game developed and published by Irem. It was ported to the Nintendo Entertainment System, PC Engine (Japan-only), Sharp X68000 (Japan-only), and FM Towns (Japan-only) in 1990.

On a fateful day in 20XX, the Earth's moon exploded into four large fragments and a multitude of meteors. Aliens from afar had succeeded in destroying the West's moon base. One after another, mankind's other military industrial space complexes were being lost. What mankind dreaded had come to pass. Scores of unidentified fighters were in the area. In addition, the moon's main computer, still intact after the explosion, had a strange vegetation coiled around it. Their trademark evil exploits being a dead giveaway, invaders from the Boondoggle Galaxy had arrived to take over the Earth. To counter these evil forces, leading scientists from all over the globe created the "OF-1" Fightership.
Imago
A shooting 'em up game developed and published in 1984. It's kind of a mix of Centipede and Galaga.
Imekura Mahjong
An adult mahjong game. From the racy pictures, I would say that when you win the woman disrobes.
Imola Grand Prix
Imola Grand Prix is a Racing game, developed and published by Leante Games, which was released in Europe in 1981.
In the Groove 2

In the Groove 2 is the sequel to Roxor Games' 2004 arcade game In the Groove. It was released to arcades officially on June 18, 2005. It was available as an upgrade kit and as a dedicated cabinet developed by Andamiro. 

There are a total of 137 songs available in the arcade version.

The Novice difficulty level is a feature added to the home version of In the Groove, carried over to In the Groove 2. On this difficulty level, all songs are rated as ones (including the hardest and fastest songs on other difficulties), and play in Novice mode places a traffic light graphic on the screen that tells players when to step. As always, two players can select different difficulty levels for the same song, but if one selects Novice, then the traffic light always appears instead of the normal backgrounds. It is also worth noting that on ITG2, Novice always forces a constant speed of 120 BPM (a "C120" mod).
In the Hunt

In the Hunt is a 2D side scrolling shooter in which you take control of a small attack submarine and engage in underwater combat. The Dark Anarchy Society's forces threaten to destroy the earth's most important cities and only you can get past their defenses and destroy their secret underwater lair.

In the Hunt follows the classic template for 2D shooters, with the added feature of being able to control scrolling speed. Includes seven levels of underwater action (and keep an eye out for threats from above the surface), upgradeable weapons, and two player cooperative gameplay.
In Your Face
In Your Face is a one-on-one (or two-on-two) half court street basketball game. It appears to be based on a previous basketball game published by Jaleco on the NES known as Hoops.
Incan Pyramid
A 5-reel video slot machine with an Inca theme by Konami Gaming.
Indian Battle
A Western-themed game that features a battle between cowboys and Indians in a desert.
Indian Dreaming

Indian Dreaming is one of the most iconic and enduring slot machines (or "pokie" machines) ever developed by Aristocrat Gaming, an Australian casino software giant. First released for land-based casinos back in 1999, this physical cabinet became a massive staple in pubs, clubs, and casinos globally, later transitioning into a highly popular online adaptation. It is celebrated for introducing Aristocrat's revolutionary "243 ways to win" system.
Indian Dreaming: Maximillion$
Indian Dreaming: Maximillion$ is a specific regional software variation of the iconic Indian Dreaming slot machine, developed by Aristocrat Leisure in 2003.
Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom

Indiana Jones and The Temple of Doom is a 1985 action arcade game developed and published by Atari Games, based on the 1984 film of the same name, the second film in the Indiana Jones franchise. It is also the first Atari System I arcade game to include digitized speech, including voice clips of Harrison Ford as Indiana Jones and Amrish Puri as Mola Ram, as well as John Williams' music from the film.
Indoor Soccer
Indoor Soccer is a Sports game, developed and published by Universal, which was released in 1985.
Indy 4

Indy 4 is a 4 player arcade game by Atari, originally released in 1976. It was preceded by its larger 8 player counterpart, Indy 800, in 1975.

Gameplay is a simulation of an Indianapolis 500 style of race, in which players compete by racing each other with simulated IndyCar race cars. The player cars' colors are light blue, green, red, and dark blue. The game uses a full-color RGB display and does not use color overlays.
Indy 500

Indy 500 is a 1995 arcade racing game by SEGA Japan. It follows the format of previous driving games such as Daytona USA. It includes the famous Indianapolis 500. Players can race one of three courses.
INDY 500 Deluxe

Clone of INDY 500 Twin.

Indy 500 is a 1995 arcade racing game developed by Sega AM1. Based on the IndyCar Series, the game possesses a license from the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, home of the Indianapolis 500, and includes the speedway as one of its courses. Indy 500 was AM1's second game developed using 3D computer graphics and their first to utilize color textures. While planned as a Model 3 arcade system board release, delays in the hardware's completion led to use of the Model 2 instead. A Sega Saturn port was planned, but later cancelled.

Gameplay
Indy 500 is a racing game based on IndyCar, and possesses an official license from the Indianapolis Motor Speedway. Players can race one of three courses: Highland Raceway, Indianapolis Motor Speedway (called Indy 500 in the game), and Bayside Street. The race commences after the user has made their choice of automatic transmission or manual transmission with a 2-position shifter.
INDY 500 Twin

Indy 500 is a 1995 arcade racing game developed by Sega AM1. Based on the IndyCar Series, the game possesses a license from the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, home of the Indianapolis 500, and includes the speedway as one of its courses. Indy 500 was AM1's second game developed using 3D computer graphics and their first to utilize color textures. While planned as a Model 3 arcade system board release, delays in the hardware's completion led to use of the Model 2 instead. A Sega Saturn port was planned, but later cancelled.

Gameplay
Indy 500 is a racing game based on IndyCar, and possesses an official license from the Indianapolis Motor Speedway. Players can race one of three courses: Highland Raceway, Indianapolis Motor Speedway (called Indy 500 in the game), and Bayside Street. The race commences after the user has made their choice of automatic transmission or manual transmission with a 2-position shifter. Special features of the cabinet include a steering wheel with haptic feedback.
Indy 800

Indy 800 is an 8 player arcade game by Atari Inc., originally released in 1975. The game was followed up the following year with a smaller 4 player version entitled Indy 4. A scaled down version of Indy 800 was a launch title for the Atari 2600 in 1977, renamed Indy 500.
Inferno

A maze/shooting 'em up game with a maze layout similar to Crystal Castle. You walk around a 3-Point Perspective maze with 4 directions to shoot your enemies. When you shoot the enemies, a dark soul is released and runs away to the monsters mouth. You must touch the enemies soul before it gets to the mouth or a regernerated more difficulty enemies occurs.

The game has 99 levels and it's endless. After 99 levels, the game is restarted to level zero. It never ends. After wave 11, the game repeats from wave 7 again. The difference is harder difficulty.
Inferno (Meadows)

Inferno is a one or two player video game simulating every kids dream at 
one time or another of being a fireman.

The player(s) control the movement and position of the firefighter on the 
ladder moving in a vertical direction on the outside left and right edges 
of the T.V. monitor. The player(s) also control the movement and position 
of the firetruck moving in a horizontal direction on the extreme bottom 
edge of the T.V. monitor.
Infinity Blade FX

Infinity Blade FX brings fantasy RPG action back to the arcade! Based on the popular mobile game Infinity Blade, this game features gorgeous visuals powered by EPIC’s Unreal Engine 3, all controlled using the large multi-touch screen.

Players use basic finger swipe moves to spar with a variety of challenging opponents. You can attack, parry, dodge or block against the various minions as you advance your way towards the sinister God-King and the Infinity Blade. You can also upgrade your skills, weapons and armor to make your quest more exciting and worth playing over and over again.
Initial D Arcade Stage

Initial D Arcade Stage (イニシャルD アーケード ステージ) (commonly referred to as IDAS, followed by the game's version number) is an arcade racing game series developed by Sega, based on the anime and manga series Initial D. In the United States and Europe, the game series is simply known as Initial D.

Based on the popular anime and manga series, the main objective is to race against different characters through various mountain passes featured in the series. The game has 5 licensed Japanese manufacturers to choose from such as Mitsubishi, Toyota, and Subaru. Using the optional magnetic card system, players can save a customized car as well as their progress for future sessions; otherwise, their game progress is deleted. Players can continue growth with their cards on another Initial D cabinet on the same version. However, the card must be renewed every 50 plays. After each race or time attack, a replay is added to show the player's progress on the mode they did.
Initial D Arcade Stage 5

Released in 2009, Initial D Arcade Stage 5 (return to Japanese version) is the fifth release in the Initial D Arcade Stage series. Released for the previous hardware for the second time (The screen mostly like Sega RingEdge). A few notable differences include heavy physics changes. Opposite to Initial D Arcade Stage 4/Extreme Stage, which took on a "drifting" physics, Initial D Arcade Stage 5 had a more realistic driving physics which includes tire and brake wear down. Although the tire and brake wear are not displayed anywhere in game, experienced players can notice the difference in the change in physics as they progress in races.

New characters that appeared for the first time in the game are: Kobayakawa, Satoshi Omiya, Imposter Project D, Kai Kogashiwa (R.T. Katagiri S.V.), and Hideo Minagawa.
Initial D Arcade Stage 6 AA

Initial D Arcade Stage 6 AA was released in March 2011.

A new mode, Tag Battle, was introduced. Like its predecessor, the game saw a change in its driving physics. A drift gauge and an updated tachometer was introduced to help inform players whether they're drifting or not. The tachometer now inform players if their speed is below the gear range. Online network is extended to support regions in which earlier versions of the game was known to be popular in, finally achieving both national wide and international matches. For the first time in series, new cars and courses are added to the game through online updates without upgrade kits like IDAS4 1.5. The game also added a mileage system to show players their total driven mileage. Mileages can be used to redeem exclusive cars that were later available in updates. New characters that appeared for the first time in the game are: Ryuji Ikeda, Hiroya Okuyama, and Go and Rin Hojo.
Initial D Arcade Stage 7 AA X

The 7th game in the long running Initial D Arcade Stage arcade racing game series developed by Sega, based on the anime and manga Initial D. This entry includes the new Operation Kanto Tag Battle mode where you and a friend can tag-team rival characters, with one racing uphill and the other racing downhill.
Initial D Arcade Stage 8 Infinity

Initial D Arcade Stage 8 Infinity ∞ was released July 17, 2014. Like its predecessor, this game carries over all game modes from the previous version with a notable addition of Initial D Factory and D Coins. In Story Mode, the players can play the Team Side or Rival Side to see Driving Training Curiculum or what mission is for each story. The game added a new feature "1 Day 1 Time Continue" to allow players to have a free continue per day without inserting credits. New courses such as Momiji Line, for the first time in Special Stage, also appeared with new layout and Hakone, the place for battle between Ryosuke's FC and Rin Hojo's R32. Arcade Stage Ver.3/Street Stage characters such as Miki, Atsuro Kawai and The Lan Evo Teams also appeared.
Initial D Arcade Stage Ver. 2

Initial D Arcade Stage Ver. 2 is an arcade racing game. It is based on the Initial D manga and anime series. The game runs on the Sega NAOMI 2 arcade system and serves as the second entry in the Initial D Arcade Stage series.

Two new mountain pass courses are added—Akagi and Irohazaka—bringing the total number of selectable tracks to six. Each course features unique layouts and difficulty tiers, ranging from beginner-friendly routes like Myogi to expert-level challenges such as Irohazaka. The game also introduces rainy weather conditions. Seven new characters are added to the Legend of the Streets story mode, expanding the narrative to include rivals such as Kyoko Iwase, Kenta Nakamura, and the infamous "Two Guys From Tokyo."
Initial D Arcade Stage Ver. 3

Initial D Arcade Stage Ver. 3 is the third entry in the Initial D Arcade Stage racing game series. Based on the popular Initial D manga and anime franchise, the game runs on Sega's NAOMI 2 arcade hardware and marks the final title in the series to utilize that system.

The game features a revised handling model that provides more nuanced vehicle control and improved realism, especially in how cars respond to drifting and road surfaces. Two new mountain passes are added: Shomaru Pass and Tsuchisaka, both adapted from Initial D: Special Stage. Additionally, Akina Snow is introduced as a challenging weather-based variant of the Akina course, demanding careful throttle control and precision from players. Three new rivals (Miki, Ichijo, and Aikawa) are added to the Legend of the Streets story mode.
Initial D Arcade Stage Ver. 3 Cycraft Edition

Initial D Arcade Stage Ver. 3, known as Initial D Arcade Stage Ver. 3 (頭文字 D ARCADE STAGE Ver.3) in Japan, is an arcade sequel to Initial D: Arcade Stage Ver. 2. 

A special version of this game was released for the Cycraft arcade cabinet titled Initial D: Version 3 Cycraft. The Cycraft is a special arcade cabinet developed by Simuline and Sega and released in 2003. The cabinet is a motion simulator which offers a greater degree of movement than a standard sit-down cabinet. These cabinets can be linked together for competitive multiplayer gameplay.
Initial D Arcade Stage Zero

Released for the Sega Nu2 arcade system board on October 9, 2018. Unlike its predecessors, this game now uses a 6-speed gear shifter (similar to the ones found in the Wangan Midnight Maximum Tune games) as opposed to the sequential ones. The character designs are taken from New Initial D the Movie with entirely new BGMs that are rock songs from the films such as Backdraft Smiths, Clutcho, The Hug Me, The Valves, and Gekkou Green. A small number of Eurobeat songs from previous games are also featured but have to be unlocked. Also, the vehicles have been reduced by original ones featured in the last games, except for the Toyota 86, which was featured in the films. However, more vehicles were added through free updates later in the year.
Initial D The Arcade

Initial D The Arcade is a 2021 arcade racing game based on the Initial D series. It is the tenth Initial D arcade game, although it is separate from the Arcade Stage series. Unlike previous games, which used proprietary game engines, the game makes use of Unreal Engine 4.
Unlike the previous one-on-one experience of the Arcade Stage games, Initial D The Arcade features up to four players racing at any one time. Despite this, one-on-one battles are still available, with several appearing in the story. The game was also the first to use a different player avatar model as opposed to the same ones reused from Arcade Stage 4 to Arcade Stage Zero.

This game was first playable on the 23rd and 24th of July 2020, in its location test, or "Ignition". More information was revealed on the 11th of December 2020 in its first "official live broadcast". It was officially playable again from the 8th through to the 18th of January 2021 during its final test.
Initial D4

Initial D Arcade Stage 4 (also known as Initial D4 in the US) is a 2007 arcade racing game based on the Initial D series. It is the fourth game in the Initial D Arcade Stage series. A limited edition, called Initial D Arcade Stage 4 Kai, also exists. This is the last entry to have a full English localization.

Unlike the older games in this series, which were revisions of the original title, Initial D Arcade Stage 4 has a completely new physics engine written for the Sega Lindbergh arcade system. This new system allows cars to actually slide, or drift, across the track when clearing corners.
Injustice Arcade

The heroes and the villains of the DC Comic universe come head-to-head in this new card vending arcade experience by NetherRealm Studios and Raw Thrills – Injustice Arcade!

Based upon the mobile version of Injustice: Gods Among Us, Injustice Arcade has been specially modified to offer something unique that you can get at home or on your phone. Each play vends one of 200 collectible cards starring one of the DC comic universe characters that can then be played in the game. Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, The Flash, Green Arrow – it goes on and on! Scan your card into the game using the dashboard card reader.
Insector (Prototype)

Insector © 1982 Gottlieb.

You are a can of bug spray. Collect the jewels on the screen and destroy all the bugs.
This was Skelly's second game for Gottlieb, but it was never released. Number produced estimated at 1 or 2 units. This game represents Skelly's own answer to "Robotron - 2084".

The cool thing about Insector is the three-letter code in at the start. Tim Skelly used this value as a seed for each player's pseudo random number generator. That way, if you want exactly the same game every time, you enter the same three letters. If you wanted to handicap yourself, you would enter different letters and let the other player enter their usual letters, etc.
Insector X

Insector X is a side-scrolling shooter by Taito, released in 1989.

The player controls an insect-sized warrior named "Kai", who takes on a vast army of cyborg insects to free the insect world from the dark ruler queen. The game uses two buttons: an upgrade-able main shot and a seemingly random selection of secondary weapons.
Interceptor

Interceptor is a jet fighting game. The player controls a jet fighter from a first person perspective. Enemy aircraft fly around and must be shot down. The pitch and yaw of the aircraft is adjusted with an 8-way joystick. Enemies fly in formation and will try to evade the player's fire. The size of their crafts scales based on the distance to the player.
Intergirl

Intergirl is a rare arcade video game released in 1995 by the developer Barko Co., Ltd.

 It is a bootleg or modified hack of Dynax's 1989 rock-paper-scissors arcade game Dragon Punch.
Similar to Barko's other 1995 release, Zip & Zap, Intergirl features adult-themed puzzle/variety graphics, often utilizing anime-style artwork.
International Cup '94
International Cup '94 is a soccer game released by Taito in 1994.
International Toote

The International Toote (sometimes referred to as International Toote II) is a vintage, video-based horse racing simulation slot machine released in 1998 by the manufacturer Coinmaster.

Unlike traditional fruit machines that use spinning reels with cherries or bars, this machine is themed around a "Tote" betting system, allowing players to place bets on various virtual horse race combinations.
International Toote II

International Toote II is a rare, vintage horse racing-themed arcade and betting machine originally distributed by Coinmaster around 1993.

The game itself is an unauthorized modification (hack) built on Seta hardware. Specifically, it is a clone/hack of Seta's popular 1993 arcade game Jockey Club (and its sequel, Jockey Club II). Because it functions primarily as a casino or amusement-style betting machine, it features distinct multi-player or two-player layouts allowing users to place simulated bets on virtual horse races.
Intersecti

Intersecti is an obscure, unreleased or highly rare pinball arcade game that is documented as a digital ROM within the M.A.M.E.

Because it was a niche prototype or limited-run machine from an unknown manufacturer and an undocumented release year, finding an original physical cabinet is extremely difficult. However, its digital legacy lives on through software emulation.
Interstellar Laser Fantasy

Interstellar Laser Fantasy was a laserdisc game manufactured by Funai in 1983. The laserdisc background images were created by Japan-based company, Gakken.

In Interstellar, you fly the starship, "Ferald Runner". Your mission is to fly to distant worlds battling alien spaceships and destroying alien bases. Armed with lasers and bombs, you travel across alien deserts, through space caverns, and into bizarre wire framed cities to find and destroy the Delta UFO.
Intrepid

Controlling an agent, your mission is to enter an embassy, maneuver throughout each of the embassy's first four floors using the stairs, or the elevator, search the rooms behind a door on each floor for items, eventually finding and obtaining stolen secret plans from the embassy's vault, and escaping as quickly as possible, while avoiding the embassy guards.

Scattered throughout the rooms behind the doors in the embassy (rooms are concealed from view until your spy enters them), are various items to aid your agent. The key, allowing your agent past the locked door on the fifth floor, the combination, which opens the vault door, the I.D. card, that bypasses the security system to the vault door preventing electrocution, and the disguise, which gets you past the sentry without being detected are required to complete the mission.
Intruder

A shooter for one or two players (against each other) in which you have to kill your rival. However obstacles get in your way of your progress and you must blast them as well to clear a path for your laser to hit your rival. This game was developed by Taito and published by Game Plan
Inu No Osanpo

Inu no Osanpo (犬のおさんぽ), (lit. "Walk the Dog") is a dog-walking simulation game developed by Wow Entertainment and published by Sega for the Sega NAOMI arcade system in 2001. Players "walk" a virtual dog by walking on a treadmill and control the pet with a leash attached to a plastic dog in front of the player. The game was only released in Japan.

Inu no Osanpo simulates the experience of walking a dog. Players first choose one of six breeds of dog to walk: Poodle, Pug, Pembroke Welsh Corgi, Shiba Inu, Labrador Retriever, or Siberian Husky. The difficulty of the game changes depending on the breed of dog chosen. After selecting a dog, the player selects one of three possible walking routes, each with a unique scenario.

The goal of Inu no Osanpo is to maintain the dog's happiness long enough to complete the entire route.
Invader's Revenge

Space Invaders conversion. Player has to stop invaders from stealing fuel (lined along bottom of screen) while avoiding missiles. Invaders attack individually in patterns, some even spinning on their way down. Includes docking.

This is a Space Invaders conversion that was fairly common in the UK around 1980. It runs on Midway's hardware (EPROM swap), but it has a separate daughter board on the top of the three board sandwich, to provide the unique Invader's Revenge music and sound effects.
Invasion: The Abductors

There was a time, thousands of years ago when 'visitors' arrived on earth and chose humans for a great experiment. They gave humans the ability to learn in order to watch them evolve and expand their minds beyond their primitive means.
Now the experiment is complete and the 'visitors' have returned to harvest their crop. At this moment, their great ships are arriving at major cities around the globe preparing to conquer and claim what is rightfully theirs... the human race.

To stop the invasion you must complete 4 separate missions by defeating the invading aliens that are abducting and mutating humans, snatching monuments and creating havoc in the world. The fate of the plant is in your hands!
Invinco

Invinco (インビンコ) is a Space Invaders clone released by Sega in 1979 for VIC Dual hardware.

Though it is essentially the same game as Taito's, the aliens don't just move left and right - one row blinks in and out of view, one row rolls about making it difficult to hit and another has aliens that turn into exploding bombs when hit, taking out everything around them.

Ippatsu Gyakuten

Ippatsu Gyakuten (一発逆転) is a Japanese arcade machine released in 1986.

The game is classified as a Tabletop Mahjong / Gambling title. It is part of the era of Japanese arcade games that combined traditional Mahjong mechanics with betting elements, utilizing a specialized control panel with a full layout of alphabet keys (A through N for tile selection) alongside betting buttons.
IQ-Block
Numbered blocks descend and must be matched to make sets or runs to earn points.
Iron Clad
This game is a very rare prototype. It was shown in MVS format at the March 1996 ACME show in Orlando, Florida.
Iron Fortress
A maze shoot em up from Eolith where you control a tank that must destroy the enemy tanks.
Iron Horse

Side scrolling platform cowboy train-robber game. Select between fists, pistols or a whip and then work your way down the steam train killing the bad guys and collecting money and special weapons. Cowboy music score.
Issho ni Wan Wan Wai Wai Puppy
Issho ni Wan Wan Wai Wai Puppy (いっしょにワンワン わいわいパピー) is a sequel to Issho ni Wan Wan.
Istrebiteli

Istrebiteli (Russian: Истребители, translating to "Fighters") is an incredibly rare, obscure Soviet arcade air-combat game developed in the 1980s. Manufactured by the Terminal production association, it represents a unique historical artifact from the isolated video game industry of the USSR.
Italian Job

The Italian Job is a classic British pub fruit machine released in June 2001 by the prominent manufacturer Maygay Machines, Ltd.. Based on the iconic 1969 British film starring Michael Caine, this slot machine remains highly popular among arcade collectors, emulator enthusiasts, and home pub-room creators.
Italian Job Club

The Italian Job Club fruit machine is a highly popular, classic UK pub slot game manufactured by Maygay in the early 2000s. Based on the iconic 1969 British film, this machine was built on Maygay's famous EPOCH technology platform and remains a sought-after collectible for home man caves and arcade enthusiasts.
Itazura Daisuki! Sushimaru Kun

Itazura Daisuki! Sushimaru Kun (いたずらだいすき！スシマルくん) is a rare Japanese casino arcade game released in 1997 by Sigma. The title translates roughly to "I Love Pranks! Sushimaru-kun." It runs on Sigma's B-98 hardware and falls under the medal game / casino genre rather than a traditional arcade action game.

The game centers around a betting mechanic. You pick one of three bizarre or improbable customers seated at your counter.
You bet on whether you can successfully trick or surprise that specific customer—often by sneaking a massive dollop of extra-spicy wasabi into their sushi order.
The machine pays out tokens or medals depending on whether your prank succeeds or fails against the chosen character.
Itazura Monkey

Itazura Monkey features mischievous monkeys, reflecting the Japanese word itazura (prank). Players press a button in time with on-screen events to interact with the monkeys and earn medals. The design follows the style of Sammy’s “kids medal” games, emphasizing simple, timing-based play suitable for younger players.
Itazura Tenshi

Itazura Tenshi was produced by Nichibutsu/Alice Co. Ltd. in 1984.

A shoot 'em up with an angel that has to make a constelation. Win the heart of a lovely angel who draws the beautiful constellations in the sky. A fanciful game of romance with a touch of fairy tales.
Ivan 'Ironman' Stewart's Super Off Road Track-Pak

Ironman Ivan Stewart's Super Off Road Track Pak was produced by Leland in 1989.

This game is almost exactly the same as the original except that it has eight brand-new tracks which are Shortcut, Cut-off Pass, Pig Bog, Rio Trio, Leapin' Lizards, Redoubt About, Boulder Hill and Volcano Valley.
Like in the original game, "Ironman" Ivan Stewart drives the white, computer-controlled truck. During the demo play or whenever other players are not in the game, the red truck is driven by "Steamin'" Steve High, the yellow truck is driven by "Hot Rod" John Rowe and the blue truck is driven by "Jammin'" John Morgan.

Another major difference is that before each player begins the game, they each can select their vehicle that they will each race in to be either a dune buggy or a truck. The dune buggy has better shocks and acceleration while the truck has better traction and top speed.
Ivan 'Ironman' Stewart's Super Off-Road

Enter the world of off-road racing as 4 vehicles will face each other, on a series of tracks which are based around flipped and reversed versions of a core selection. Fame, glory and bikini clad women await your victories and the taste of dirt awaits if you fail. Let a computer car beat you and you lose one of your 3 credits.

Successful races bring more money, which can be used to soup up their machine. Boosts to top speed, grip and acceleration can be purchased, and your nitro boost must be kept topped up. If you are desperate for upgrades, you can buy into your spare credits.

Only your off-road driving abilities will be enough to pull you to first place in these races. Play alone or with up to 3 other players (depending on the version) in this classic arcade game.
Ivory Tusk

The Ivory Tusk fruit machine is an obscure, video-based slot machine manufactured by Konami Australia Pty, Limited during the 1990s. In the UK and Australia, these types of gaming cabinets are commonly referred to as fruit machines or pub slots. Today, the game is primarily recognized within retro-gaming circles because its software has been preserved and emulated.
Ixion

Ixion is an unreleased arcade game based on Sega Zaxxon hardware, developed by Sega Electronics set to be published by Sega in 1983.

This is a shoot 'em up game where the player has to collect letters for points.

All the letters must be collected to reach the KAILO round. The player receives 500 to 8000 points for collecting gold letters. Enemies are worth 200 points & crystals are worth 1000 points. The KAILO ball heals tiles while the OLIAK ball destroys tiles. A bonus ship is awarded every 100000 points.
J-League Soccer V-Shoot

J-League Soccer V-Shoot, commonly referred to as just V-Shoot, is a soccer arcade game that was released by Namco in 1994 only in Japan; it runs on their NB-1 hardware, and features the twelve (then-current) teams from the J-League (the Kashima Antlers, JEF United, the Urawa Red Diamonds, Tokyo Verdy, the Yokohama Marinos and Yokohama Flügels, Shonan Bellmare, Shimizu S-Pulse, Júbilo Iwata, Nagoya Grampus Eight, Gamba Osaka and Sanfrecce Hiroshima). All the players' names also reflect the teams' 1993 lineups - and a sequel, J-League Soccer Prime Goal EX, was released in 1996. Sega also released a J-League videogame of their own, The J-League '94 (which was later renamed to Super Visual Soccer).
J. J. Squawkers

Release in 1993, distributed by Able and developed by Athena , J. J. Squawkers is, on the surface, your typical 90s platformer. As Ani (player one) or Ototo (player two), you must resore peace to Pastachioville by beating up pretty much anyone or anything that gets in your way over five (technically four- one's a boss rush) side-scrolling stages.
Jack & Vera

The "Jack & Vera" fruit machine is a classic UK pub slot machine released in the 1990s by Maygay. It was themed around the legendary Coronation Street couple, Jack and Vera Duckworth, who famously managed the show's fictional pub, the Rovers Return Inn.
Jack Potten's Poker
Jack Potten's Poker is a classic retro video poker arcade game originally manufactured as a bootleg/clone system in the 1980s.
Jack Rabbit

Hi there. I'm Jack Rabbit. I love carrots, and I'm very hungry." Jack Rabbit needs to collect carrots while avoiding pits, snakes, obstacles, and the two weasels looking for dinner you. Succeed through three stages and Jack will congratulate you. "We sure showed them, partner.

Jack is a isometric Jump 'n Run in which a rabbit tries to collect carrots while being chased by weasels. The game is played through three different stages:
The first stage is outside Jack's house. Here, the object is to collect all the carrots while avoiding pits, bombs, and the weasels. The second stage is a scrolling stage in the desert. You must now avoid snakes and cacti in addition to pits and weasels. Along the way, you can grab apples for bonus points. The third stage is in the tropics, and you will need to leap from level to level while avoiding weasels and coconuts.
Jack the Giantkiller

Jack the Giantkiller is a 1982 arcade game developed and published by Cinematronics. It is based on the 19th-century English fairy tale Jack and the Beanstalk. In Japan, the game was released as Treasure Hunt. There were no home console ports.

The player controls Jack, who must climb the beanstalk to reach the castle, steal a series of treasures from the giant, and escape. The game used hardware licensed from Hara Industries of Japan, with raster graphics instead of the vector displays Cinematronics was known for.

Nicknamed "Jack the Company Killer," the game was a commercial failure and financial disaster. Cinematronics filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in 1982.

The player uses an eight-way joystick to move Jack. Two buttons are available to allow Jack to jump or throw beans at enemies.

Scaling the beanstalk. The player may use the supply of beans (limited, with his supply indicated by a counter at the corner of the screen) to hit and destroy an enemy for points.
Jackie Chan in Fists of Fire

Jackie Chan in Fists of Fire is an upgraded version of The Kung-Fu Master Jackie Chan. It adds a desperation move system, an improved combo system with a special combo counter above the lifebars that records the highest number of combos during a match, and an "escaping" feature where players can struggle out of combos or stand up as fast as possible by rapidly moving the control stick and tapping the buttons simultaneously. Fists of Fire also makes all three versions of Jackie Chan into playable characters expanding the roster up to nine playable characters, and makes adjustment to the character balance by strengthening and weakening the statistics of certain playable characters from the first game, while adding and removing a few moves to some of them.
Jackie Chan: The Kung-Fu Master
The legendary Jackie Chan assembles Earth greatest martial artists to fight in a tournament to crown a new Dragon Master.
Jackpot Junction

Jackpot Junction is a classic UK pub fruit machine designed and manufactured by the iconic British gaming company Bell-Fruit Games (BFG).
Released in June 2002 (Model PR1304), it was designed as an "Amusement with Prizes" (AWP) / Club style machine.

Like most Bell-Fruit titles of the early 2000s, Jackpot Junction features a multi-reel base game paired with a vibrant upper "feature board" matrix. Players climb a grid or pathway using numbers on the reels to trigger standard UK fruit machine mechanics like nudges, holds, and cash/feature trails.
Jackpot Junction Club
Jackpot Junction Club is an arcade fruit machine
Jailbreak

Jail Break is shooter game produced by Konami in 1985.

"The warden has been taken hostage. Free him, no matter what the cost."

As a policeman, the object of the game is to fire on escaped convicts who have taken the warden hostage, and in order to do this, you must make your way through downtown streets, a park, a bridge, and eventually, a prison. By rescuing hostages along the way, you can obtain a number of weapons, such as a pistol and a tear gas gun, and you can select them by using the weapons select area at the bottom of the screen. Be careful: If you shoot any hostages, you will lose whatever weapons that you have.
Jambo! Safari

Jambo! Safari is a 1999 driving game. Players take the role of one of four safari park rangers (American zoologist George Wildman, Swedish photographer/aspiring professor Marit Söderström, Kenyan native Naftali Ngugi, and English veteran ranger Edward Arniele) studying wildlife.

To conduct animal research, the player must pilot a jeep throughout the Serengeti and use the gear change lever to cast a lasso in order to capture a variety of animal species. The player must carefully "reel in" the animal while lassoing it, taking care not to break the rope. There are two ways to play the game: Beginner mode, which is a two-stage instructional, and Expert mode, which is a two-level, mostly unassisted mode with a final stage.
Jammin'

Jammin' is an unreleased arcade video game developed by Atari Games in 1985, recognized as an early precursor to rhythm-based titles like Beatmania and Dance Dance Revolution. It employs a memory-based gameplay mechanic similar to the electronic toy Simon, in which players must replicate musical sequences demonstrated by on-screen characters using nine input buttons, each corresponding to different notes or beats.
Jan Jan Paradise
Jan Jan Paradise is a strip mahjong game featuring full screen animated characters.
Jan Jan Paradise 2

A mahjong game with 12 selectable player and opponent characters. At the start of the game the player selects his player character. Then, before every match the player selects his next opponent. Unlike in the original, Jan Jan Paradise, the player is allowed to select his character and opponent out of all 12 characters instead of just out of three characters at a time. Each character features three different strip images and one animated strip sequence. When the player defeats an opponent, the final strip image of the opponent is replaced with the animated sequence. But unlike in the original, the player is shown the final still strip images of each character he has defeated in a 'gals collection', shown after the player's game is over. When the player loses he is treated to the booby-prize, all of the player character's strip images are shown excluding the animated sequence.
Jan Oh

Jan Oh (often stylized as Jan Ō) is a Japanese Mahjong arcade game released in 1984. Developed as an "Asiatic board game" style arcade title, it belongs to the early wave of electronic Mahjong adaptions that populated Japanese game centers during the 1980s.

Because it was designed specifically for Mahjong gameplay, a dedicated Jan Oh arcade machine would have originally used a specialized Mahjong control panel (featuring a flat row of lettered buttons from A to N for selecting tiles, along with Reach, Kan, Pon, Chi, and Ron buttons) rather than a standard joystick-and-button setup.
Jangou

Jangou is a classic Japanese arcade mahjong game released in 1983 by the prominent arcade developer Nichibutsu (Nihon Bussan).

As one of the pioneers of the digital mahjong genre in Japanese amusement arcades, Nichibutsu designed Jangou as a tactical, single-player tile-matching game against artificial intelligence opponents. It became a major commercial release for the company and laid the groundwork for a long series of popular arcade sequels, spin-offs, and ports.
Jangou Lady

Jangou Lady is an adult-oriented mahjong arcade game released in 1984 by the prominent Japanese arcade developer Nichibutsu. Operating on specialized tabletop/mahjong arcade hardware featuring a unique 20-button panel, it served as a sequel to Nichibutsu's 1983 arcade release, Jangou.
Janken Game Acchi Muite Hoi!

Janken Game Acchi Muite Hoi! is based on the traditional Japanese hand game janken (rock-paper-scissors) combined with the follow-up challenge “Acchi Muite Hoi,” where the winner tries to make the loser look in a chosen direction.

Players use a special joystick with buttons to select rock, paper, or scissors. Winning the janken round leads to the “Acchi Muite Hoi” sequence, where the player chooses a direction while the opponent turns their head. Success fills a meter, and once the meter is full, the opponent is defeated and replaced by a new challenger. Medals are awarded based on progress and outcomes.
Janken Man Kattara Ageru

Janken Man Kattara Ageru (ジャンケンマン 勝ったらあげる) is a classic Japanese electromechanical arcade cabinet released in July 1991 by the manufacturer Sunwise. The game’s title translates literally to "Janken Man: If you win, I'll give it to you!", referencing the core gameplay hook: beating the machine in Rock-Paper-Scissors to win a prize token.

These compact, kid-friendly "medal games" became iconic fixtures across Japan during the late Showa and early Heisei eras, frequently found outside corner candy stores (dagashiya), inside supermarkets, and across amusement arcades.
Janpai Puzzle Choukou
A prototype puzzle game type mahjong developed by Mitchell and published by Capcom in August 2001 on CP System II. The game rewards you with young topless girls.
Janputer '96

Jan-puter 96 was produced by Dynax in 1996.

A Mahjong game from Dynax.
Janyou Part II

Janyou Part II is a classic Japanese arcade game released in July 1983 by the manufacturer Cosmo Denshi. It is an adult-themed or traditional Mahjong arcade game designed for 2 players.

The game itself is a re-release and variation of the classic "Royal Mahjong" originally developed by Nichibutsu. Like many Japanese Mahjong arcade cabinets of that era, its control panel featured a highly specialized layout rather than a standard joystick—typically utilizing up to 26 distinct buttons to let players select, discard, and make declarations (such as Pon, Chi, or Ron) with specific tiles.
Jet Fighter

In Jet Fighter, two planes fly around with the goal of shooting the other as many times as possible in a dogfight within the time limit. When a plane is hit, an explosion occurs, and the plane recovers after a few seconds. As with many Atari games of the era, if the plane flies off the side of the screen, it comes back on the opposite side.
Jet Rocket

Jet Rocket is a 1970 electro-mechanical arcade flight simulator manufactured by Sega. It uses a projection display system to display targets and the landscape. It is the earliest example of a flight simulator, and is often cited as an ancestor to first-person shooters and open world games.
Jewel Raider

Jewel Raider is a ticket redemption game from Bay Tek where players insert a coin and use three flippers to propel the token through the playfield. The combination of gems collected determines your winnings.
Jiggery Pokery

Jiggery Pokery is a classic UK pub fruit machine running on the Bell-Fruit / Scorpion 4 hardware platform.

Because it is a classic physical machine, it is highly popular in the arcade emulation community. Enthusiasts frequently play digital recreations of it via emulators like MFME (Multiple Fruit Machine Emulator) using community-built custom layouts.
Jikkyou Pawafuru Puro Yakyu EX

Powerful Pro is a baseball video game series, created by Konami, released only in Japan. It is recognizable by its big-headed characters.

This is the earlier release of 1998, with the EX '98 version releasing later in the year .
Jikkyou Powerful Pro Baseball EX

The Jikkyou Powerful Pro Baseball EX (known in Japan as Jikkyou Powerful Pro Yakyuu EX) arcade machine is a classic coin-operated sports game released by Konami in April 1998. Developed by Konami's Diamond Head division, it brought the beloved, cartoonish "Power Pros" console baseball experience into Japanese amusement arcades.

True to the Power Pros franchise, the game features the iconic, stylized "SD" (Super Deformed) legless characters with massive, spherical heads. It traded highly realistic graphics for fast, addictive, arcade-perfect physics, responsive pitching, and snappy batting mechanics.
Jikkyou Powerful Pro Yakyuu '96
A cartoon style arcade baseball game from Konami, for up to 4 players, released in Japan in 1996.
Jikkyou Powerful Pro Yakyuu EX '98
Powerful Pro is a baseball video game series, created by Konami, released only in Japan. It is recognizable by its big-headed characters.
Jin
A "Qix" rip-off, very slow paced, dull graphics, and sounds straight from "Defender".
Jingi Storm: The Arcade

Jingi Storm: The Arcade is a 3D fighting game developed and released by Atrativa for arcades (using the Dreamcast-based Sega NAOMI GD-ROM hardware) exclusively in Japan on September 20, 2006. Although it plays similarly to other 3D fighting games with a martial arts theme, it has a unique twist: each of the main playable characters have an accompanying woman who is displayed in a compromising position (as a hand-drawn picture by a different illustrator) when that player loses a match, similar to arcade eroge. Footage from location test versions of the game shows that these scenes were planned to involve undressing based on the player's performance that match. Characters: Arashi Chad Dr. Daro Paolo Giichi Ryuya Shuperi Landy Gamon Fenrir (sub-boss, playable with cheat code) Asuka (sub-boss, playable with cheat code) Noel (sub-boss, playable with cheat code) Jiao (sub-boss) Xell (final boss)
Jitsuroku Maru-chi Mahjong

Jitsuroku Maru-chi Mahjong: Sugoku H na Kokuhaku Hen (translating roughly from Japanese as "Mahjong True Shameful Story: Super Hentai Confession Book") is an adult-themed, tabletop arcade video game released in Japan in 1993. Developed and published by the manufacturer Windom, it was built for Japanese amusement arcades as a 2-player competitive mahjong game featuring Gekiga / anime-style characters.
Jitsuryoku!! Pro Yakyuu
Jitsuryoku!! Pro Yakyuu is a Sports game (baseball), developed by TOSE and published by Jaleco Entertainment, which was released in Japan in 1989.
Jive Money

Jive Money is a rare, vintage arcade coin pusher and slot machine hybrid released in 2002 by the American manufacturer Jumping Bean.

Key Features & Mechanics
• The "Super Token" Feature: The game utilizes a physical bed of coins combined with special "Super Tokens". When a player successfully drops and pushes a Super Token off the edge, the machine registers the win and automatically triggers a high-value payout offer (typically rewarding 25 coins from the internal hopper).

• Integrated Coin Escalator: Unlike completely mechanical pushers, it uses an internal motorized coin escalator to continuously feed coins up from the hopper to replenish the playing field and handle digital payouts.

• Hybrid Classification: It is classified as an Arcade / Coin Drop machine. It bridges the gap between a traditional fruit machine (relying on a random number generator and electronic payouts) and a physical skills-based coin pusher.
Jockey Club

Jockey Club is a vintage horse-racing arcade game released around 1990, co-developed by the Japanese gaming companies Seta and Visco.

Unlike traditional action video games, it was designed as a mechanical or video-based gambling arcade machine. It typically operated on the Seta 1st Generation arcade hardware and was often distributed in multi-player cabinet configurations where players could place bets on simulated horse races.
Jockey Club II

Jockey Club II is a horse racing simulation arcade game originally released in 1995 by the Japanese video game manufacturer Seta. Unlike traditional joystick-and-button action games, it belongs to the niche category of medal/gambling arcade machines or simulation games that were highly popular in amusement arcades during the mid-to-late 1990s.
Jockey Grand Prix
Jockey Grand Prix was produced by Sun Amusement / BrezzaSoft in 2001.
Joe & Mac Returns

A multi-platform game where cavemen must clear the screen of enemies in order to advance to the next level.

In this sequel to Caveman Ninja, Joe and Mac are in a multi-level platform area and have to jump and club their enemies.
John Elway's Team Quarterback

John Elway's Quarterback, also known as John Elway's Quarterback Challenge and John Elway's Team Quarterback, is a 1987 football video game.

Tradewest developed Quarterback as an arcade game. In 1988 John Elway agreed to endorse it, and the company renamed the game John Elway's Quarterback. Tradewest released a version for the Nintendo Entertainment System and Melbourne House for various home computers such as Commodore 64, ZX Spectrum, IBM PC, and Apple IIGS. The arcade game is an upright that had two player capability.

The controls are different for both the left and right sides (offense and defense). There is a spring-loaded joystick which allows the player to angle and release according to where they were throwing (for the quarterback) or kicking. When possession changes, players switch sides of the console, and play continues. In both cases, players can select from a playbook of formations and plays.
Johnny Nero Action Hero

Johnny Nero Action Hero allows you take on three different missions, and you are able to play all three in what ever order you choose. Each stage has a comic book theme: Space Wars, Curse of the Mummy King, and Ghost Town. The levels all have the same basic gameplay, but in a different setting. The game is able to be played by one or two people. In two player each player uses one gun, but in one player you are able to duel wield the guns in mode called Guns of Fury. The gameplay comprises of the player shooting everything that appears on screen. To keep the player alert there is the occasional ally that can't be shot. There are also some quick time events scattered through levels and the player will either be punished or rewarded depending on there success with the quicktime event. Each stage has at least one bonus level, and the goal of these levels is to shoot a certain amount of objects under a time limit.
Joinem
A one or two player (alternating turns) maze game published and developed by Global Corporation in 1983
JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Heritage for the Future

JoJo's Bizarre Adventure: Heritage for the Future is an updated version, released in 1999, of the JoJo's Bizarre Adventure arcade game. This is a fighting game developed by Capcom based on Hirohiko Araki's Japanese manga of the same title. The game was developed by the same team who are responsible for the Street Fighter III series.

The game combines Capcom's trademark anime-inspired graphics, as seen in the Darkstalkers series, with the colorful characters and events of Hirohiko Araki's creation, resulting in a highly stylized and detailed visual style. It also features many of the gameplay mechanics seen on previous Capcom fighting games, such as the use of power gauges for super moves, as well as a brand new Stand Mode, consisting of a guardian spirit that accompanies each character and can be summoned or dismissed at will by the player, resulting in variations on the character's move list and abilities.
Jojo's Bizarre Adventure: Last Survivor

JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure: Last Survivor is a 3rd person battle royale action game. The game supports up to 20 players in a single match and features characters from Parts 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the series.

The players each control one character and roam in a vast map, whose effective size reduces gradually as a dangerous zone progressively engulfs the environment. The players are deployed randomly on the map in predetermined square zones. They then must fight each other, depleting the enemy's health bar until one is depleted and the enemy is eliminated. Players will need to utilize their Stand powers to be the last person standing. Depending on the mode, players can also be split into distinct sides instead with allies fighting together and being able to be revived.

Unique to Last Survivor is the ability to level up your character. Players level up by collecting poker chips from fallen enemies, similar in style to those produced by Daniel J. D'Arby's Stand Osiris.
JoJo's Venture

Jojo's Venture is a one-on-one fighting game released on the CPS-3 arcade system based upon the long-running Jojo's Bizarre Adventure manga series by Hirohiko Araki. This game adapts Part 3 of the series, Stardust Crusaders. 

The game is a one-on-one fighter, similar in gameplay to most of Capcom's other fighting games. In this game, however, you can call upon your Stand to access an entirely different set of normal attacks and gain additional defense and offensive bonuses. Your Stand's power is not infinite, however - if you take enough damage, it'll break, leaving you open to a devastating counter attack. Every character's Stand has their own special powers which can be used to your advantage.

The game features eight selectable fighters (six heroes and two villains), plus three hidden characters. Other notable villains from the series are also in the game, as unplayable mini bosses.
Jolly Card Professional 2.0

Jolly Card Professional 2.0 is your standard slot machine poker game. Enter credits into the machine, decide how much to bet, and then receive 5 cards face-up. You may then decide to discard some of the cards, and these are replaced by other randomly drawn cards. If certain card combinations (two pairs, three of a kind, a full house, a flush, etc) are in your final hand, then you win extra credits.
Jolly Jogger

Jolly Jogger © 1982 Taito Corp.

It's a nice day to go jogging, and you feel like covering the whole city. So what could go wrong? Oh yeah, three bullies out to beat you up. Thankfully some blocks have things that scare them and allow you to knock them out.
Jolly Jousting

The Jolly Jousting fruit machine is a classic UK pub-style slot machine (AWP) manufactured by Qualsoft Products & Systems (QPS).

 Medieval jousting and knights, featuring traditional fruit machine features like nudges, a cash/feature ladder, and medieval-themed bonus games
Jong Tou Ki

Jong Tou Ki (often romanised in MAME databases as Jantouki) is a Japanese adult mahjong arcade game released in 1990 by the developer Dynax.

The machine features standard single-player, tabletop-style gameplay where the player competes in classic Riichi Mahjong against a series of female opponents. Typical of early-90s "strip mahjong" arcade titles in Japan, progressing through the game and defeating opponents rewards the player with revealing or undressing graphics.
Jong Yu Ki
Jong Yu Ki (often indexed under the ROM name janyuki) is a 1988 tabletop Mahjong arcade game manufactured by the Japanese company Dynax.
Jongkyo

Jongkyo (雀狂) is a classic Japanese arcade mahjong game developed by Toaplan and released in 1985. The name translates closely to "Mahjong Crazy" or "Mahjong Fanatic," which fits its gameplay perfectly as a dedicated, competitive tabletop arcade title.

Because it was a dedicated mahjong cabinet experience, it utilized a specialised arcade control panel variant layout specifically for mahjong inputs (featuring buttons labeled A through N for selecting tile discards) rather than a traditional joystick-and-button gaming setup.
Joryuu Syougi Kyoushitsu

Joryuu Syougi Kyoushitsu (translating to Lady Shogi Classroom) is a rare, Japanese-exclusive tabletop digital shogi board game released for arcades in February 1997. Developed and published by Visco Games, the game's full title is Shimizushi Dai Joryuu Yonkan'ou Kanshuu - Joryuu Shougi Kyoushitsu, which highlights that it was supervised by the prominent female professional shogi champion, Shimizushi (Ichiyo Shimizu), who held four major female titles at the time.
Joshi Volleyball

Joshi Volleyball was produced by Taito in 1983.

A volleyball game from Taito.
Journey

You must recover the instruments for the five members of the rock band Journey. Characters have black and white digitized faces. Plays many Journey songs, including a tape of Separate Ways. Bonus round: you the roadie must push fans away from the concert stage.
Joust

Joust is a fixed-screen action game in which the player controls a lance-wielding knight mounted on a flying ostrich. Each wave takes place across a single arena of floating rock platforms suspended above lava. The player moves horizontally and repeatedly flaps the ostrich’s wings to rise, hover, or slow its descent; flying beyond either side of the screen causes the knight to reappear from the opposite edge.

Combat occurs by colliding with enemy knights riding buzzards. The rider whose lance is higher at the moment of impact wins the joust, while opponents meeting at the same height rebound from one another. The three enemy ranks are Bounders, Hunters, and Shadow Lords, which become progressively more aggressive and valuable. Bounders tend to wander around the arena, Hunters actively pursue the player, and Shadow Lords fly quickly and attempt to gain the superior height before attacking.
Joust 2: Survival of the Fittest

Joust 2: Survival of the Fittest is an arcade game developed by Williams Electronics and released in 1986. It is a sequel to Williams' 1982 game Joust. Like its predecessor, Joust 2 is a 2D aerial combat game with platforms to land on. The player uses a button and joystick to control a knight riding a flying ostrich. The object is to progress through levels by defeating groups of enemy knights riding buzzards. 

Joust 2 features improved audio-visuals and new features such as mutant buzzards created by eggs falling into lava, the ability to transform from an ostrich to a flying horse, and differently themed levels. Waves no longer seamlessly flow into each other; the gameplay is divided into separate screens with transitions between them.
Joy Stand Private

Joy Stand Private is actually not a traditional arcade game, but a vintage Japanese sticker-printing photo booth (Purikura) released in 1997 by the manufacturer Yuvo.

The machine featured a screen, a joystick, and buttons to allow users to select decorative background themes and custom text overlays before printing out their sticker sheets.
Jr. Pac-Man

Jr. Pac-Man features gameplay similar to the original Pac-Man, but with a few changes. As Jr., you need to eat all of the dots in a maze without running into the four ghosts that are trying to get you. The maze is now much larger, and no longer fits on a single screen. The maze will scroll around to follow the action. From time to time a tasty bonus will bounce around the screen which can be eaten for extra points. There are tricycles, kites, drums, balloons, trains, root beers, and other bonuses that appear as the levels progress.

When the bonus items bounce around the screen, any dots they touch will become larger and are now worth 50 points each instead of 10. However, one of these larger dots will cause Jr. Pac-Man to slow down greatly when he eats them making it more difficult to remain one step ahead of the ghosts which constantly pursue him! Located throughout the maze are power pellets; when Jr.
Jr. Pac-Man (Speedup Hack)

The Jr. Pac-Man (Speedup Hack) arcade machine refers to a highly popular, aftermarket hardware modification for the original 1983 Bally Midway arcade circuit boards. This modification, driven by a "Speed-Up Chip," multiplied the main character's traversing speed up to four times faster than standard factory settings without altering the speed of the ghosts or overclocking the main hardware clock. Originally designed by third-party groups like Two-Bit Score in the late 1980s, these hacks were widely installed by arcade operators across North America to dramatically increase difficulty, shorten player sessions, and ultimately drive up quarter intake.
jubeat saucer fulfill

Jubeat (ユビート, Yubīto), stylized as jubeat, is a series of arcade music video games developed by Konami Computer Entertainment Japan, and is a part of Konami's Bemani line of music video games. The series uses an arrangement of 16 buttons in a 4x4 grid for gameplay, a grid also used for the displaying of cues and part of the user interface.

The basic gameplay of the series is similar to Nintendo DS music games such as Osu! Tatakae! Ouendan and Elite Beat Agents and can be considered to be similar to Whac-A-Mole. Animated explosions or other animations, called "markers", that can be chosen at the song select screen are shown within the panels synced to a track of the player's choosing; when they reach a "hot point", which is dependent on the marker chosen, the player must tap the corresponding screen to score points. Taps can be judged as either Perfect, いい感じ (Good), 早い (Fast), or 遅い (Slow). 3 difficulties (Basic, Advanced, and Extreme) are offered for each song.
Judge Dredd (Acclaim)

Trouble in Mega-City One: An unidentified perpetrator has taken hostages, including the mayor. Attempts to apprehend him have already led to the loss of 17 Judges. He states that only one man is allowed to come near: Judge Dredd. There's obviously some history between them. It's time for the toughest lawman of them all to move in and dispense justice via his Lawgiver gun.

Gremlin's Judge Dredd is an 'on rails' lightgun shooter based on the original comics instead of the 1995 movie. The action moves through pre-rendered environments on a fixed path. 14 levels spread over 4 stages must be cleared of lawbreakers. 

Most enemies are polygonal 3D models overlaid over the video backdrop, but the background can also be shot at: gun turrets and some bosses like hovertanks and other heavy machinery are pre-rendered objects. Powerups are hidden in the scenery as well: there are different ammunition types for the Lawgiver, including rapid fire and heat-seekers.
Judge Dredd (Midway)

In 1992, Midway developed an arcade scrolling beat-em-up based on the popular British comic series, Judge Dredd. The game ran on the same hardware as Mortal Kombat II, and utilised a similar digitised graphical style. The game reached a near-complete state, with some odd glitches here and there, but with 3 stages finished, and 3 bonus stages after each ‘main’ level. Each stage was different in some way, such as the first being a normal scrolling brawler-style stage, the second being closer to a platform game, and the third being a unique concept, where Dredd has to fight off waves of ‘block warriors’, making sure that the two ever-decreasing bars never reach the bottom- if one of them is emptied, the stage is over and has to be repeated. After the final level is beaten, the game ends with a preview for the next level, apparently featuring the character Judge Death from the comics.
Jue Zhan Tian Huang

Jue Zhan Tian Huang (決戰天皇, literally as "The war against the Emperor") is a beat 'em up game made by a unknown company (presumably from China) made for Arcade machines in 2000. The game is known to feature four characters from The King of Fighters series as playable characters: Kyo, Iori, Chizuru, Chin, and featuring Street Fighter II: The World Warrior characters as enemies.
Juicy Fruits

Juicy Fruits is a vintage physical casino slot machine created by Betstar Ltd, an early gaming machine manufacturer and distributor that operated in the early 1990s before its assets became tightly intertwined with Atronic.

The Betstar variant of Juicy Fruits was an arcade/casino cabinet that utilized traditional fruit machine elements—such as classic fruit reels and bells—built on hardware distributed in the USA and Europe during the early 1990s.
Juicy Jackpots Club

The Juicy Jackpots Club fruit machine (often associated with classic UK-style club fruit machines or simulated titles like the CASINOCRAZY Club Fruit Machine app series) is a high-payout gaming concept styled after traditional British social club slots. True UK club machines belong to specific regulatory categories, offering unique stake and prize limits that set them apart from standard pub fruit machines.
Jumbo Godzilla

Jumbo Godzilla is a 1995 arcade game developed by Namco and published by Hope for CAVE 68000 hardware. it's a side scrolling kiddie ride game that pits Godzilla against the JSDF and villainous monsters. After dispatching several waves of JSDF forces, Godzilla is stymied by the Super X until another monster arrives to destroy it and challenge him. Buttons mounted on the sides of the screen allow him to tackle, tail whip, and fire atomic breath at his enemies. As a finishing move against monsters, he uses an orange beam reminiscent of the Heisei Godzilla's red spiral heat ray. Once his enemy is defeated, Godzilla returns to the sea.
Jump Bug

Scrolling platformer in the theme of Konami's Scramble, where the player controls a jumping, shooting car. 

You can shoot and dodge creatures of the land, air and sea and collect money bags. Points can also be gained by jumping on clouds. 

The stages include a city, pyramid and ocean. This title predates Irem's Moon Patrol, and may be the first scrolling platformer.
Jump Coaster

You control a caped man who attempts to rescue his girlfriend while attempting to avoid running men and girls on roller coasters. Two scenes make up one round . Pick up all gold bags in both scenes and your off to the next round.
Jump Jump
Jump Jump is a platform arcade game, released by dgPIX Entertainment Inc in 1999.
Jump Kids

Jump Kids is 2D arcade single screen platform game, another clone of Snow Bros. The player controls a kids with big hands, he fights against enemies - grabs them and throws into another enemies. If the opponent attacks him - life lost. After defeating all the enemies on the screen, the player moves on to the next level. Game has 8 big locations available on start, 1 is locked. Each location has different set of enemies.
Jump Kun
Jump Kun is a 1984 prototype run and jump platform game developed by Kaneko. The game has up to two alternating players.
Jump Shot

Jump Shot is a basketball arcade game that ran on Namco Pac-Man hardware. The players must use an 8-way joystick, to take up control of two basketball players, who are codenamed home (blue) and away (red), with two buttons to make them shoot the ball (if they are in possession of it) and block - and if only one player is playing, the second player will be controlled by the CPU.

Just like in real basketball whichever player has the most points once the timer has run out wins the game (except, of course, in the event of a tie game).
Jumping
Jumping is a bootleg version of Rainbow Islands with slightly altered player and enemy sprites. The rainbows have also been replaced with stars. It came out in 1989.
Jumping Break

Arcade game released in February 1999. Game play is similar to Breakout where player controls a character on bottom of screen that is used to bounce a ball to top and destroy various items for points. A jump button also allows the paddle to jump to meet the ball.
Jumping Cross

Jumping Cross is a 2D racing game, similar to Excitebike. The player takes part in motocross (enclosed off-road circuits) races, must travel along the route, avoid obstacles, and stay ahead of opponents. He has limited time to complete the race. The player can jump on specially built up hills.
Jumping Groove
Jumping Groove was produced by Namco in 1998.
Jumping Jack

Jumping Jack is a platformer developed and released by Universal in 1984.

Jump from one place to another. Avoid hitting obstacles. Gather bonus items for points.
Jumping Jack Cash
Jumping Jack Cash is an arcade slot fruit machine by Mazooma.
Jumping Jack Flash
A single player 3 slot\reels machine created in 1998 and developed with later versions released in 1999 and into the early 2000's by BWB. It featured a £1 to up to an £8 payout.
Jumping Jackpots

The Jumping Jackpots video slot machine was manufactured in 2003 by Atronic as part of their popular Cashline cabinet series. While often referred to by collectors in the UK as a "fruit machine" due to its arcade styling, it is technically an upright casino video slot configured for penny denominations and multi-line play.
Jumping Pop

Jumping Pop is a 2D arcade platform game, very similar to Nightmare in the Dark with colorful graphics. Player is a monster hunter with a special, powerful vacuum cleaner - he needs to catch enemies (mummies, skeletons, cavemen, etc.) He can use a captured enemy as a missile to kill other opponents. After killing all the enemies the player goes to the next level. At the end of each "world", the boss is waiting to fight..
Jumping Pop (Nics)

A rip-off of "Plump Pop".
Use a trampoline to bounce a baby animal into the blocks. You can choose from a penguin or frog.
Junai 2: White Love Story
Junai 2: White Love Story (High Rate DVD No.5: Junai 2 - White Love Story) is an arcade game released in Japan in November 1998 by the prominent developer Nichibutsu (Nihon Bussan Company, Limited).
Junai: Manatsu no First Kiss

Junai: Manatsu no First Kiss (純愛 真夏のファーストキッス / Pure Love: Midsummer First Kiss) is a Japanese arcade game released in 1998 by Nichibutsu (Nihon Bussan).
