The game belongs to Nichibutsu's late-90s era of arcade titles that utilised High Rate DVD (HRDVD) hardware to stream high-quality video and FMV sequences directly from a DVD-ROM drive unit mounted inside the cabinet.
Jungle Boy

A prototype of Jungle King, this version is totally different from Taito's Jungle King, so while it counts as a bootleg, it isn't really a ROM Hack. The game featured parallax scrolling and excellent graphics and music.
Jungle Bucks
A Mahjong, Hanafuda style casino game created by Bellfruit Machine (BFM) and published by Bell-Fruit Games and released in 2007.
Jungle Hunt

Jungle Hunt is a one- or two-player side-scrolling arcade platform game produced and released by Taito in 1982. It was also known as Jungle King in early releases.

The player controls a jungle explorer who sports a pith helmet and a safari suit. The player must rescue his girl from a tribe of hungry cannibals. To do this, he must swing from vine to vine, survive a crocodile-infested river, jump or duck falling rocks rolling downhill, and release the girl before she "takes a dip" in the boiling cauldron.

Jungle Hunt is one of the first video games to use parallax scrolling.

History

Jungle Hunt changed names several times during development. The original prototypes were called Jungle Boy and later became Jungle King for release to the arcades. In these earlier versions the playable character was a bare-chested man with a loincloth who resembled Tarzan.

Taito was sued by the Edgar Rice Burroughs estate for copyright infringement for using the character's likeness.
Jungle Jive

The Jungle Jive pusher is the most popular, successful and highest earning pusher in the redemption industry. When you think of pushers, you have to think of Harry Levy Amusement Contractor Ltd., associated with the highest quality and highest earning pushers all over the world.

Jungle Jive is a coin or token operated skill redemption game. The player tries to force coins or tokens off the playfield by skillfully inserting his coin into a moveable coin entry chute and timing the movement of the ever moving "pusher" shelves. Tickets are then awarded for each coin that is pushed off the shelves.
The Jungle Jive game is available in 2, 3, 4 or 6 player configurations. Jungle Jive has been approved for amusement redemption operation in many states and jurisdictions that require game approvals.
Jungle Jungle

Jungle Jungle is a coin-operated arcade machine produced by American Alpha, an amusement company known for manufacturing electronic game boards, multi-game systems, and skill-based sweepstakes cabinets.

While it shares a thematic name with popular action-shooters like Sega's Let's Go Jungle!, the American Alpha title uses a liner or skill-gaming layout rather than a light-gun theater setup.
Jungle King

Jungle King, re-released as Jungle Hunt, is an action game developed by Taito and released for arcades in 1982. It was originally distributed as Jungle King, then quickly modified and re-released as Jungle Hunt due to a copyright dispute over the player character's likeness to Tarzan. Jungle King, along with Moon Patrol released a month earlier, is one of the first video games with parallax scrolling.

The player controls an unnamed character moving through side-scrolling scenes to rescue a woman from a cannibals by swinging from vine to vine, swimming a crocodile-infested river, and avoiding rolling rocks. In the original Jungle King release, the loincloth-wearing character resembles Tarzan. In the rebranded Jungle Hunt, the player character is an explorer, sporting a pith helmet and safari suit. Another re-theming of the arcade version was distributed as Pirate Pete in 1982.
Jungle King 2002

Jungle King 2002 is a video medal game developed and published by IGS Co., Ltd. (International Games System).

Unlike Taito's classic 1982 platforming game Jungle King (which was famously rebranded as Jungle Hunt), the 2002 version by IGS is an entirely different type of arcade cabinet. It is a gambling/gaming machine built on an 8-liner Cherry Master / Pot-O-Gold system, often incorporating roulette-style features and poker mechanics alongside its tropical jungle theme.
Jungler

Jungler is an arcade game where the player controls a snake-like creature in a maze. In the maze are three other such creatures and the aim of the game is to destroy the other creatures before getting killed by them. The enemies will appear in three different colors with different lengths. The red ones are longer than the player who will be killed upon a head-on collision. The yellow ones are the same length as the player and are harmless. The green ones are shorter than the player and can be killed by colliding with their heads. The enemies can be shot at and if one is hit in its tail its size will decrease by one segment. Creatures that are smaller will move faster and be harder to catch. At the same time it is possible to increase the player's size by eating fruits that appear at random locations but it decreases if hit by the enemy creatures' fire.
Junkyard

The 1976 Americoin Junkyard is a rare, highly collectible electro-mechanical (EM) crane arcade game. Unlike modern claw machines designed to dispense plush toys, Junkyard is entirely skill-based; players race against a timer to see how many miniature die-cast "junk cars" they can scoop up and move into disposal hoppers.

Players operate an industrial-style miniature crane and claw using control levers. You scoop up little metal cars ("junk") scattered across the playfield and drop them into a lit left or right hopper.
Juno First

Waves of aliens are trying to destroy your fighter craft. Waves increase in difficulty, with every third or fourth wave being a formation wave where the aliens appear and attack in a particular pattern. Aliens mutate into more dangerous forms the longer they survive, so they should be killed as quickly as possible. The radar at the top of the screen shows what kinds of aliens are approaching and where they will appear.
The aliens usually release white bombs these cannot be shot down, only avoided. They also release homing bombs, which are more dangerous but can be destroyed. Shooting the asteroid and capturing the "mystery" inside will stop the aliens from firing altogether for about 10 seconds, and give you bonus points for each alien you kill.

You have 99 seconds to complete each wave. The quicker you complete the wave, the higher your bonus. An extra ship is awarded every 100,000 points.

Using the warp button lets you escape from sticky situations.
Jurassic Park

Jurassic Park is a rail shooter arcade game based on the 1993 film of the same name. The player is Ingen Commando who goes to Isla Nublar to clean up the Island after the incident in 1993. He/she drives in a car (but doesn't pilot the car - he/she is just a shooter) and must knock out various dinosaurs: Tyrannosaurus, Velociraptor, Dilophosaurus, Brachiosaurus, Triceratops, Ankylosaurus, Gallimimus, Pteranodon and Ichthyosaurus.
Jurassic Park Arcade

Jurassic Park: Arcade is a 3D lightgun shooter played from a first-person perspective based on the Jurassic Park franchise. A volcano has erupted on Isla Nublar leaving the island the park stands on unstable. The player is part of a team send to track down and capture several dinosaur species.

The game offers a total of nine stages and three bosses: a Triceratops, Tyrannosaurus and Spinosaurus. While playing the player has to gun down over thirty different enemies. A total of five different weapons can be used while playing. These are the X-22 Renegade, Titan 2000, Shockbolt, Frostbite cannon and Triple Threat. The game can be played solo or with a friend.
Jurassic Park III

Jurassic Park III is a 3D lightgun rail shooter played from a first-person perspective. It is based on the movie of the same name and like in the movie it takes place on Isla Sorna. The game starts with a two-man rescue team parasailing down to the island. The team receives orders to search for victims of an accident. Apparently things have gone horribly wrong.

The game moves the character automatically while searching the island. Players have to gun down various dinosaurs from the movie like raptors, a spinosaurus and a t-rex. In addition to the lightgun the player can hit an escape button to evade the dinosaurs attacks. The game can be played solo or with a friend.
Justice League: Heroes United
Justice League Heroes United is an arcade game based on the Justice League comic book.
Jyangokushi: Haoh no Saihai
Jyangokushi: Haoh no Saihai is a mahjong game developed and published by Capcom in 1999.
Jyanshin Densetsu: Quest of Jongmaster

Quest of Jongmaster is a mahjong game with role-playing elements. The "RPG mode" follows the story of an apprentice "mahjong warrior", a girl named Chi Fou, who is sent on a quest to defeat monsters that were unleashed on the world. This mode is structured like a traditional medieval top-down RPG, with town and dungeon exploration, NPC interaction, and other familiar elements. The protagonist can equip weapons and armor, cast magic, and purchase healing and status-recovering items. Experience points and money are awarded after each battle.

Random and boss battles in this mode are standard mahjong games, with the addition of special tiles that influence the game's result, e.g. increase the damage inflicted by the equipped weapon. The final damage is calculated after the mahjong game is over, and depends on the characters' levels, equipment, and the winning combination. For example, winning the game with a full mahjong would most likely result in a "critical hit".
K-On! After School Rhythm Selection

K-ON!! Hokage Rhythm Selection (After School Rhythm Selection) is the second card game from Sega based on K-ON! licence coming after K-ON! Hokage Rhythm released in 2013. The game is based on the PSP version named K-ON! Hokage Live. There are 46 different cards, 7 stages and music from the anime.
K-Pop Demon Hunter Hypseuse Singe

A brand new custom arcade fan-game created from scratch for the Hypseus Singe emulator, based on the animated series "K-Pop: Demon Hunters". The game runs beautifully at 1080p resolution on both Windows and Batocera using a customized version of the Kimmy Script Engine framework.
K.G. Bird

"K.G. Bird" (often styled as K G Bird Takes Flight) is a classic video slot machine developed by the well-known Australian manufacturer Aristocrat Leisure. While the term "fruit machine" is commonly used in the UK to describe pub gambling machines, this particular title is a traditional casino-style slot game rather than a UK pub AWP (Amusement with Prizes) machine.
K.O. Drive

Back in 2012, Sega unveiled a new combat driving arcade game called KO Drive at the DEAL 2012 trade show in Dubai. Afterwards, the game made an occasional appearance at other trade shows, but ultimately was cancelled.

This easy to pick up battle-racing game has been designed with multiplayer action in mind. Tracks include London, Vegas, Shanghai, Toronto, Cairo and Rome.
Kabuki-Z

Kabuki-Z is a 2D side-scrolling beat'em up. The player controls a heroic samurai wielding a katana, who battles various common and mythological Japanese foes. Kabuki-Z has typical gameplay - the player goes right and slashes enemies, various bosses wait at the end of the level. The game has blood and "fatalities". Kabuki Z has five levels.
Kageki

In this game, you play a bandage-fisted street boxer who must fight every member of The Motorcycle Gang Warriors, including their leader.

The game has nine rounds where you must face a different opponent. In each round, your opponent must be knocked down three times in order for you to win.

After you have defeated the first eight opponents, you will finally meet face to face with the leader, and if you defeat the leader, you have beaten the entire gang and the game ends.
Kaiser Knuckle

Kaiser Knuckle follows the same fighting game conventions established by Street Fighter II. The player's character fights against his or her opponent in best two-out-of-three matches in a single player tournament mode with the computer or against another human player. The player has a character roster of nine fighters to choose from, and three bosses, each with their own unique fighting style and special techniques. The control layout is set to the six-button standard (a la most Capcom fighting games), but it can be switched to a five-button layout via dip settings. One unique feature is that Kaiser Knuckle was the first and only fighting game that has five strengths of basic attacks.

Another unique feature is that it introduced the power zones, which can be utilized via a successful hit of a special move when a player's "Crush Meter" is full. The power zones (either fire or electric) can affect the certain special move a character has.
Kaiun Quiz
Kaiun Quiz is a manga trivia/quiz video game for Arcade, created and published by Namco in 1999.
Kaleidoscope

Kaleidoscope is a rare, vintage coin-operated arcade/redemption game manufactured by Coastal Amusements (originally known as Coastal Vending).

 It is classified as an arcade/redemption machine featuring a "progressive bonus sign" and prominent rainbow-coloured branding.
Kanatsuen no Onna
Kanatsuen no Onna is an adult themed mahjong game by Panac in 1988
KanColle Arcade

KanColle Arcade is an arcade adaptation of the web-based Free-to-Play game Kantai Collection, also known as KanColle. The game was repeatedly postponed several times from first announcement in February 2015.

KanColle is about organizing fleetships, which are represented as girls, to fight various enemies. The arcade version is an evolved version of the game, with actual physical cards. The cabinet has naval themed controls in the wheel and throttle, as well as a button to fire.

The ships are divided into multiple types such as Destroyer, Battleships and Aircraft Carriers, and you equip different weapons such as torpedoes or short range rapid fire guns. You also have stats for each ship such as how well they can traverse the sea and take down enemies and collect resources. You go through different missions and setting up the right fleet with the right formation is how to clear the mission in the best possible way.
Kangaroo

Baby Roo has been kidnapped by monkeys, and it's up to Mama Roo to come to the rescue! Your kangaroo starts out at the bottom of the screen. You need to guide the kangaroo up the various ladders and platforms to the top where Baby Roo is being held captive. The monkeys will be trying to stop you by throwing or dropping apples and knocking you off the platforms. Your kangaroo has boxing gloves, however, and can knock out the monkeys with a single punch! Along the way various types of fruit can be collected to earn bonus points.
Kankoku Hanafuda Go-Stop

Kankoku Hanafuda Go-Stop is a digital tabletop arcade game published by Visco Corporation and released in 2001. Meaning "Korean Hanafuda Go-Stop," the game adapts Go-Stop (also known as Godori or Matgo in its two-player variant)—the incredibly popular Korean traditional card game played using Hwatu (flower cards originally derived from Japanese Hanafuda). Because physical arcade cabinets for this game are exceptionally rare outside of East Asia, it is primarily known today in the retro gaming community as a playable ROM emulation via the MAME (Multiple Arcade Machine Emulator) platform.

Players take turns matching cards in their hand with cards on the table based on the 12 months of the year (each represented by a specific flower or plant suit).
Kaos

A vertical maze game where a man chases dollars and tries to catch them before they reach the bottom. If the dollars reach the bottom they turn into deadly dragons. If the man reaches the top, he turns into a dragon-slaying king.
Karaoke Quiz Intro Don Don!
Karaoke Quiz Intro Don Don! (カラオケクイズ イントロ ドンドン!) is an arcade quiz game released for Sega Titan Video arcade hardware.
Karate Blazers

Choose among 4 martial arts masters, each with his own distinct killing blow.

Feel the excitement of real fighting as you fight to recover the secret scrolls and save the daughter of your slain master.

Defend the honor of the old master as only you can do.
Karate Champ

Karate Champ is an action fighting game for one or two players.

In one player version the player has to master some skills at a karate school to be able to compete in a karate tournament for the national title. At the end of each match is a bonus round where the winner can earn extra points by knocking down flying objects that are tossed his way, breaking roof tiles/ice blocks or knocking down a charging bull on the beach!

In Player vs Player (two player) version, players compete against each other at twelve different locations to see who has the best karate skills! To win a match, the player must win two of three rounds by knocking down his opponent with a wide variety of karate moves. A full point or half a point is awarded for knocking the opponent down and the first player to gain a two point lead wins the round. When the 30 seconds time limit for a round ends, the player who has the most points wins.
Karate Champ: Player vs Player

Karate Champ — Player vs Player is distinguished from the initial Karate Champ by the addition of a player versus player mode. This version of the game also added new backgrounds, new bonus games, a female character that cheers the player on, and different, clearer voices.

Player vs Player has the characters fighting it out over girls in twelve different locations around the world (similar to the later SNK's Street Smart). A scene runs as a best out of three rounds competition for one girl. After every competition, the player has a chance to earn bonus points by evading a series of potted plants flying at the player, kicking through a series of boards and stopping a charging bull.
Karian Cross

This is an original falling-pieces puzzle game. Get three like-colored objects together to make them disappear. Getting multiple combinations causes more blocks to fall on your opponents side.

Karian Cross is falling-piece puzzle game, similar to Puyo Puyo or Super Puzzle Fighter II Turbo. The player must combine falling blocks - 3 of the same color next to each other disappear from the board. Longer combinations create additional blocks in opponents screen - Just like Tetris, loses the one who cannot insert new elements.
Karnov

Karnov is a 1987 platform arcade game. In the game, players take control of the title character Jinborov Karnovski, or "Karnov" for short. Karnov is a strongman popularly illustrated as being from an unspecified part of the Soviet Union's Central Asian republics as shown on the arcade flyer and again in Karnov's Revenge.
Karnov's Revenge

Karnov's Revenge is a 2D versus fighting game similar to Street Fighter II. It takes place one year after what happened in Fighter's History. After being defeated in The "Great Grapple", a martial arts tournament organized by himself, the mysterious K invites fighters from all over the world once again. The nine characters from the previous game (Ray, Feilin, Ryoko, Matlok, Samchay, Lee, Mizoguchi, Jean and Marstorius) are present, along with two new ones (Yungmie and Zazie). The two hidden characters from the previous game, Clown and Karnov, are also available as playable characters in this game.

Each character has two punches (light and hard) and two kicks (light and hard) and one or more unique throw moves. Special moves are performed by using control sequences such as moving the directional pad down, down-forward, forward and pressing a punch button. Combos can be performed by connecting sequences of moves.
Karous

Karous is a unique vertically scrolling shoot-'em-up developed and published by Milestone Inc. It was originally released on November 15, 2006 for the Sega NAOMI GD-ROM arcade platform. You take the role of a mysterious girl named Karous, who commands a tiny fighter ship and attempts to destroy an evil armada bent on world domination.

The weapon system is based on Radio Allergy, but it uses a unique D.F.S. bomb system.

Bombs can be used when SP gauge is full. When a bomb is activated, a barrier surrounds the player, which can damage enemies within the barrier. For the duration of bomb activation, the player is invulnerable. Enemies destroyed by the barrier provide more experience points to the player.

The player's shot, sword, shield can be upgraded by using experience items dropped from enemies, with a maximum of 100 levels. Weapon levels also act as score multipliers.
Kart Duel

Kart Duel was produced by Namco in 2000.

To increase the competition levels in 2 player mode, Namco has introduced the new "continue system" where the losing driver has to pay for the next continuing play. In addition, 1 free game is given per 4 continuous rounds of 2 player play.

The competition is also increased with players competing each lap time. When a player marks his or her best lap, their position in the top 100 rankings will be displayed on screen during the race.

When a player finishes the race within the regulation position, they can go on to the next circuit. When all the circuits are cleared, the player can challenge the best racer from Namco's R&D staff.

There are a choice of 4 circuits (3 of the circuits are based on actual tracks) to suit the individual's skill level and players can select their kart to suit each circuit, strategy and driving style.
Kasei Channel Mars TV

The game is played with 3 buttons, one blue, one yellow and one red. Throughout different minigames, called channels, these are used to perform various actions, often representing a small choice, a medium choice and a large choice, such as having to clear a stack of bowls in those 3 sizes or counting moving objects of the 3 sizes. Even when size isn't inherently tied to the goal of a channel, the different important objects will usually match these sizes and/or color-coded for convenience. The buttons can also represent more specific actions, such as jumping and ducking, or even be entirely interchangeable.

Up to 3 players can participate, otherwise these spots are filled in by computer players also competing in the minigames. Players are given a choice of 3 channels to choose from at the start and after completion of a channel, chosen with one of the 3 buttons. If the player is idle for 15 seconds, the game defaults to the yellow option.
Kasino '89

Kasino '89 is an incredibly obscure, rare casino-genre arcade video game released in 1989. Built as a dedicated gambling or amusement cabinet, it remains a highly niche piece of arcade history primarily kept alive today through emulation communities.

During the late 1980s, the European arcade market—particularly in Italy—saw a boom in localized video slot, poker, and card game cabinets. SFC s.r.l. produced Kasino '89 to fit into bars and local amusement arcades alongside traditional video games.
Kasiori

A falling object puzzle with a sweets motif of beautiful girls!

-A falling block puzzle game in which cute beautiful girls appear and play against each other with a puzzle with the motif of “sweets”.
If you arrange three sweets that fall from the top of the screen side by side, the sweets will disappear.

● When you hit the bottles against each other, the sweets in the bottle will break and appear. When it breaks, a chain occurs in eight directions.

● You can play in either the one-player mode or the two-player mode, which is tailored to the story.

-Cotton, the main character of the popular “Cotton Rock and Roll”, has also appeared and is used as a player character.
Kattobase Power Pro Kun
Kattobase! Pawapuro-Kun (かっとばせ! パワプロくん?) is a baseball medal game developed by Diamond Head and published by Konami and released on Arcade on 1998 in Japan. It is part of the MLB Power Pros series.
Keep Your Hat On

The Keep Your Hat On fruit machine is a vintage UK fruit machine (or slot machine) designed with a playful comedy and British policing stage performance theme. It is highly sought-after among casino memorabilia enthusiasts and arcade collectors for its nostalgic art style.
Keirin Ou
A racing game released in Japan where the player bets which bicyclist will win the race.
Keith Courage in Alpha Zones

Now the Battle is in Your Hands You are Keith Courage. Struck by a giant meteor, the world has been invaded by strange creatures from another planet. Burrowing deep within the Earth's surface, the Planet of B.A.D. (Beastly Alien Dudes) seeks to take over the world. As a member of N.I.C.E. (Nations of International Citizens for Earth), your mission is to defeat B.A.D. and bring peace back to the world. Armed only with a sword, you must first defeat the outpost guards. Then, enter the Underworld. Here you activate the awesome Nova Suit. A secret force left to you by your fallen father, you are half man, half mechanical monster. Nearly invincible, your sword cracks with the power of lightning, as you wreak havoc on the fearsome Dudes. Your goal is to reach the Robo Zone (the seventh Alpha Zone), headquarters of B.A.D. Succeed here and you will have won the game, recapturing the Earth and restoring humanity's place in the universe. You have help along the way.
Keks
Keks is a 5-reel video slot machine game with bonus and super-bonus games, with an additional possibility of increasing the reward during a risk-game.
Ken Sei Mogura: Street Fighter II
Ken Sei Mogura: Street Fighter II is a spin-off of the Street Fighter series. Gameplay resembles whack-a-mole, but the moles are replaced with M. Bison.
Kero Kero Keroppi no Issyoni Asobou
A one player ticket redemption game published and developed by Sammy Industries in 1993. US version is called Kero Kero Keroppi's Let's Play Together.
Ketsui: Kizuna Jigoku Tachi

In a near-apocalyptic world ravaged by global warming, a global arms dealer company, EVAC Industry, is discovered to be stoking tension and triggering wars in order to boost its weapon sales. In a last act of desperation, the United Nations forms a clandestine squad of four ships to sneak into EVAC's territory to take out their private army and end the war.

Ketsui is a manic (bullet hell) shooter in the classic Cave style with a very heavy focus on scoring. The player has a choice between two ships; the slow-moving Tiger Schwert has a wide shot, while the fast-moving Panzer Jäger has a focused shot. Both ships feature a lock-on mode; by holding down the shot button, the player shoots a tightly focused laser and the player's support ships lock onto the nearest enemy, allowing the player to strafe while continuing to shoot.
Keyboardmania

Keyboardmania was produced by Konami in 2000.

In the spirit of all the other "bemani" games, this version has the player using a 24-key keyboard and effector wheel. Press the keys in tune to the music (and when indicated, spin the wheel) as the bars fall to the bottom of the screen. Complete the song without missing too many of the notes, and you can play another song.

You have DJed, you have danced, but have you played the piano? Konami does it again with Keyboardmania! Play the songs by pressing the keys and spinning the effect wheel as the bars fall to the bottom of the screen. Hit them perfectly (or at least somewhat perfectly) and you can choose a new song to play.
Keyboardmania 2nd Mix

Keyboardmania 2nd Mix was produced by Konami in 2000.

In the spirit of all the other "Beatmania"-style games, this time play using a 24-key keyboard, pressing the keys in tune to the music as the bars fall to the bottom of the screen. Complete the song without missing too many of the notes, and you can play another song.

You have DJed, you have danced, but have you played the piano? Konami does it again with Keyboardmania: 2nd Mix! Just like the original, play the songs by pressing the keys as the bars fall to the bottom of the screen. Hit enough of them perfectly (or at least somewhat perfectly) and you can choose a new song to play.

Select a song, then play! As the bars fall down the screen, press the corresponding key on the 24-key keyboard.
Keyboardmania 3rd Mix

Keyboardmania 3rd Mix was produced by Konami in 2000.

In the spirit of all the other "Beatmania"-style games, this time play using a 24-key keyboard, press the keys in tune to the music as the bars fall to the bottom of the screen. Complete the song without missing too many of the notes, and you can play another song.

You have DJed, you have danced, but have you played the piano? Konami does it again with Keyboardmania! Play the songs by pressing the keys and spinning the effect wheel as the bars fall to the bottom of the screen. Hit them perfectly (or at least somewhat perfectly) and you can choose a new song to play.
New to this version (aside from the music) is support for the 'multi-session base' which allows up to five people to play simultaneously (two players on Keyboardmania 3rd Mix, two on Guitar Freaks 5th Mix, and one Drummania 4th Mix player.
Kick & Kick

A soccer simulation video game, where the player uses a real soccer ball, to control the direction and power of the shot. The sensors on the machine detect the motion of the ball and display on the screen a representation of the player's kick.

The game contains many modes of play including Set plays, Power tests and Target modes. Players can compete against each other for world records.
Kick '4' Cash

Kick 4 Cash is housed in the CashCube video SWP cabinet and tests players skills at free kicks. Players have the chance at each stage to choose the optimum cash win versus risk. A successful shot will add a cash goal bonus to their prize pot. Progressive free kicks will have bigger rewards allowing the player to reach Â£40 in ten goals. The machine is trackball controlled for power and direction, and the player must judge the gravity and curve of the ball. If the player spins too fast, the ball may fly over the bar, and if they kick too slow, the keeper may save. Features include a Bonus Chance, which allows the player to play a joker on one difficult goal - he can choose to double his win, get a second chance or make the defenders half the size.
Kick And Run
A football game where you can either play cooperatively in cup events or head-to-head.
Kick Ball
A volleyball arcade game that also allows kicking of the ball over the net to the opposing player or computer controlled team. Game is a hacked Power Spikes ROM.
Kick Boy

Kick Boy is a re-skinned version of "Dacholer" with some gameplay variations. The main character, for instance, has been switched out for a baseball-cap wearing child, while the setting is a busy harbor. The goal is to kick soccer balls at dogs who are trying to chase and bite you.
Kick Goal

Kick Goal © 1995 TCH.

A five-a-side soccer game.
Kick Off: Jaleco Cup
Kick Off is a 1988 soccer/football game developed and published by Jaleco.
Kick Rider

A road-race game where the view is from above. You control a motorbike with opponents on motorcycles who jostle you with their legs, and the occasional car. Played against the clock with points for passing.

The initial stages of the game are played with a view from above your motorbike, looking down onto the road. Other motorbikes line up with you for a "traffic light" start. Once under way, they jostle you with their legs, and you can jostle back by pressing the button and left or right. With no bikes by your side, you can gain a bit more speed. There are occasional constrictions on left and right, and central islands. There are no sharp corners! Occasionally a car appears in front of you leaving bombs in its wake. You crash if you hit a bomb, hit the car, or hit any area off the road. If you crash, you lose time. The game is played against the clock, with bonus points decreasing as you play.
Kick Start: Wheelie King
Kick Start is a racing game, developed and published by Taito Corporation, which was released in Japan in 1984.
Kicker

The arcade follow-up to Yie Ar Kung Fu switches from the one-on-one style into a platform beat 'em up design.

You play Lee, who has become trapped in the Temple by the Triads, and must escape by over-powering them. Each section of the game is on several levels (which you can jump up and down) and scrolls. Balls of energy are sometimes released when you kill a Triad - grab this and it becomes a powerful weapon you can hurl at an opponent. Most enemies can be killed with standard kicks, but each level has a Super Triad who can only be killed through magic.
Kickle Cubele
Pirate version of "Meikyuujima" aka Kickle Cubicle.
Kickle Cubicle

Meikyūjima or Kickle Cubicle is a sliding puzzle game in the vein of Adventures of Lolo where the Wicked Wizard King covered the kingdom with ice and hid the people and palaces deep within the ice.

Armed with his freezing breath, Kickle sets out to save his friends and attempts to rescue the kingdom from this puzzling predicament of perpetual winter.

Each level has a fixed time limit and enemies that will try and block your progress. The four lands (Garden, Fruit, Cake and Toy) have 17 or 18 puzzles in each. Beat all of those and there is a Special Stage with 30 more challenging puzzles.

Your main options are to move, make a block of ice and slide a block of ice.

Objects appearing in puzzles include:

 Rock: You cannot go over these but you can use them to stop sliding ice cubes.
 Slippery Ice: Enemies can not go there.
 Base Rock: These can not be destroyed and enemies generate from them.
 Spring: Springs an ice cube across the screen.
Kickman

In this game, you're a clown on an unicycle who has to pop balloons that are falling down from the sky. This can be done by moving left and right to catch them all on your head. Further on, you have to form columns instead of popping them. These columns have a nasty habit of getting each time higher, giving you less time to react.

However, if you're close enough to the balloon you can kick the balloon and try again. Another way is to catch the 'Pac-Man' that comes down between the balloons. This will eat the balloons that fall on your head. If you miss, you'll fall from your unicycle.
Kickthrough Racers

Kickthrough Racers is a Racing game, developed and published by Taito Corporation, which was released in Japan in 2011.

Kick Through Racers Arcade Machine is an exiting new racing game that will appeal to the whole family. Players kick down on the scooters pedal to accelerate and race to the finish line.

Collect items around the various courses for power ups such as "extra speed" and "jumps".

Kick through racers can also link 2 cabinets together allowing for up to 4 players to race simultaneously.
Kid Chameleon

The player, as Kid Chameleon, progresses through a series of levels, containing an array of deadly enemies and obstacles. Most levels contain a flag, which is the primary goal of each level, from which the player progresses to the next level. However, a number of teleporters throughout the game can warp the player not only to different places in the same level, but also to different levels, and sometimes to an entirely different path through the game. At the end of the game, Kid fights and defeats the final boss, Heady Metal. Kid Chameleon contains 103 levels, of which only about half are on the "main path" (traversing levels only by flags), and also counts 32 smaller unnamed levels, simply called "Elsewhere". Despite the game's considerable length, there was no password system or other method of saving the game (although re-releases in compilations and the Virtual Console include their own save features).
Kid Niki: Radical Ninja

One day in Feudal Japan, Kid Niki, the most radical of ninjas, is training at his Ninja School. Suddenly, a passing bird is struck down by an arrow and lands at Niki's feet. Attached is a note explaining that Niki's girlfriend, Princess Margo, has been kidnapped by the evil Stone Wizard. With the cry of "Will help you!" Niki bursts through the wall of his school and sets off on his quest to save Margo.
Kidou Senshi Gundam Seed Destiny: Rengou vs. Z.A.F.T. II

Kidou Senshi Gundam SEED Destiny: Rengou vs. Z.A.F.T. II is a fast-paced 2-on-2 3D mecha action game developed by Capcom and published by Bandai Namco. Released in Japanese arcades on June 29, 2006, it features an expanded roster of over 60 mobile suits from Gundam SEED, SEED Destiny, and spin-offs like Stargazer.
Kidou Senshi Gundam Seed: Rengou vs. Z.A.F.T.

Mobile Suit Gundam SEED - Federation VS ZAFT aka Mobile Suit Gundam SEED - Union VS ZAFT is part of the Mobile Suit Gundam series and was developed by Capcom and Published by Banpresto. It used the Capcom System 246 hardware and was released in July 2005.
KiKi KaiKai

KiKi KaiKai is a shoot 'em up action video game developed and published by Taito for arcades in 1986.

Priestess Sayo-chan must repel ghosts in order to rescue Seven Lucky Gods!

The Seven Lucky Gods have been kidnapped by giant ghosts. Armed with talismans and a purification rod, Sayo-Chan must travel to the ghost village and defeat the enemies who are determined to stop her rescuing the Gods.
Kikiippatsu Mayumi-chan

Kiki Ippatsu Mayumi-chan is a mahjong game with cheerleaders and a password feature by Victory L.L.C. in 1988

The title of this game translates from Japanese as 'Mayumi-chan One Shot'.
Killer Comet

Killer Comet was developed by Centuri and manufactured by Game Plan in 1980.

In Killer Comet, you are in a hostile region of space, and beset by space monsters who are trying to devour you and your space-pod. The monsters launch bombs, and contact with these or the monsters themselves will result in the loss of one of your five space-pods. The monsters themselves move fairly randomly, drifting slowly towards the bottom of the screen. Occasionally, the glimmering orb of a killer comet will appear and will purposefully follow you as you move to avoid it. Monsters, bombs and comets are all vulnerable to a short-range laser beam which you carry on-board, and may fire in one of three different directions. If things get too difficult, you can also trust to luck and enter hyper-space, which will teleport your pod to a random location in space.

Monsters appear in waves and after killing 25, a new type will appear. The player score is the total number of monsters vanquished.
Killer Instinct

Killer Instinct is a fighting game developed by Rare and published by Midway and Nintendo. It was released as an arcade game in 1994. The game's plot involves an all-powerful corporation called Ultratech organizing a fighting tournament. The story was adapted in a limited comic book series published under the short-lived Acclaim Comics imprint.
Killer Instinct features several gameplay elements unique to fighting games of the time. Instead of fighting enemies in best-of-three rounds bouts, each player has two life bars. The player that depletes the other player's life bars first wins the match. The game also introduced "auto-seconds", which allows players to press a certain sequence of buttons to make characters automatically perform combos on opponents. Also featured in the game are "combo breakers"; special moves that can interrupt combos.
Killer Instinct 2

Killer Instinct 2 follows on from the plot line that the previous installment ended with. Eyedol's death at the hands of Orchid accidentally sets off a time warp, transporting some of the combatants back in time and allowing the Demon Lord Gargos to escape from Limbo. Now, trapped 2000 years in the past, the warriors that survived Killer Instinct, along with several new faces, fight for the right to face Gargos in combat, but Chief Thunder, Cinder and Riptor did not return. Each character that survived the journey from the first game has a corresponding background story, while new characters on this installment are native inhabitants of this past time period. Some fighters, like T.J. Combo who survives from the original, just want to get home. Others, like new character Tusk, want to bring an end to Gargos and his reign of evil. This time there is no tournament or prize money, just a fight to the finish with the fate of the future hanging in the balance.
Killer Queen

Players are pitted against each other in teams of five, using two back-to-back/side-to-side cabinets. Players pick their roles (Worker, Warrior or Queen) and compete to achieve victory through three possible means: Economic, Military and Snail. Killer Queen inspired the video game Killer Queen Black.
Kimble Double HI-LO

The Kimble Double HI-LO is an obscure, vintage video gambling arcade machine produced during the 1980s by Kimble Ireland (Kimble Manufacturing Ltd). Based on card game elements, it falls into the category of "grey-area" amusement-with-prizes (AWP) or video poker machines that were common in European pubs, arcades, and betting shops at the time.
King & Balloon

King & Balloon is a fixed shooter video game that runs upon the Namco Galaxian hardware, based on the Zilog Z80 microprocessor, with an extra microprocessor to drive a DAC for speech; it was one of the first games to have speech synthesis.

You control a crossbowman that protects his king from being taken by enemy hot-air balloons. You must protect the king and prevent him from being captured and carried far up into the sky by one of the balloons by firing arrows at squads of descending hot air balloons. If the king is actually picked up he will scream "Help", and if he disappears he will say "Bye, bye". Each round is completed when all 42 balloons have been destroyed.
King Derby

King Derby is a classic, video-based horse racing gambling arcade machine released in 1981 by the manufacturer Tazmi (often associated with Tatsumi hardware). Classified as a video slot/gambling hybrid, it allowed up to two players to place bets on simulated horse races.
King Kong Cash

The King Kong Cash fruit machine is a highly popular, classic British Category C pub fruit machine manufactured by Betcom Games (often associated with Blueprint Gaming software licenses). Known for its immersive jungle theme, loud sound design, and an interactive board-game style bonus round, it remains a heavily sought-after machine for collectors and home games rooms.
King of Dynast Gear

King of Dynast Gear is a scrolling platform run 'n' gun game for one or two players in which two starships from the year 2993 AD fall through a time-hole and end up 65 million years in the past, above a prehistoric Earth-like planet. One ship is piloted by hero and 'time patroller', Roger, while the other is piloted by the evil Gustaf. The two ships shoot each down and crash-land onto the planet below, where Roger discovers that Gustaf has transformed many of the planet's dinosaurs into aggressive 'combat dinosaurs'.
King of Football
King of Football is a Casino game published and developed by BMC in 1995.
King of the Monsters

King of the Monsters is a two player (or one player vs. computer) fighting game. Players get to choose any one of six monsters (four in the 16-bit ports) for battle, and two players can join forces to fight the monsters together. Battles end when one of the monsters is pinned for a three count or if time expires (in which case the player loses).

The game consists of 12 total levels: the player first must defeat all six monsters, with the last monster being oneself, but in a different palette. Then the player must defeat the six monsters again, in the same order, but this time in different cities.
King of the Monsters 2

Alien super monsters have returned and are trying to invade Earth again! Now, Super Geon, Atomic Guy, and Cyber Woo must fight to retain control of the planet. Each one has special attacks and powers. Take on monsters that have unique abilities never seen before, including fire breath, aerial spins, and radioactive blasts. Challenge a friend, or have him help you out in the two-player option. Battle your way through seven levels of intense action in King of The Monsters 2.
Kingdom Grand Prix

Kingdom Grandprix is a 2D arcade shooter and racing combination - a continuation of Sorcer Striker. The game has many fantasy creatures and futuristic vehicles. The player chooses 1 of 8 characters - all others are rivals in the race. Player moves faster holding down the fire button (but then he is defenseless), and by getting closer to the top end of the screen. Beside this, the game is a typical vertical-scrolling shooter - player flies forward, shoots enemies and bosses, and collects various power-ups, like extra bombs, homing bullets, or more power to fire the gun. The game has twelve stages, but is non-linear - after completing each level, the player chooses one of the two levels.
Kingpin

"King Pin" is a rare, bowling-themed video arcade game manufactured by Games of Tomorrow in 1980.

The game stands out as a unique piece of amusement history because it used a card game mechanic styled entirely around ten-pin bowling. Games of Tomorrow was a United States-based manufacturer, and "King Pin" is documented as the only arcade machine the company ever released under that trade name.
Kings & Queens Club

The Kings & Queens Club fruit machine is a classic UK club-style slot machine released in the 1990s. While often associated with the Barcrest ecosystem, the game itself was developed by Crystal, running on Barcrest's highly popular and robust MPU4 hardware platform.
Kinnikuman Muscle Grand Prix
Kinnikuman Muscle Grand Prix (キン肉マン マッスルグランプリ) is a series of fighting video game developed by AKI Corporation, based on the popular Kinnikuman manga and anime series from Weekly Shonen Jump.
Kinnikuman Muscle Grand Prix 2

Kinnikuman Muscle Grand Prix 2 is a 3D hybrid wrestling/fighting game developed by AKI Corporation. It was originally released for the Namco System 256 arcade board in Japan on June 21, 2007, and an updated port called Kinnikuman Muscle Grand Prix 2 Tokumori for the PlayStation 2 on September 25, 2008.

MGP2 is a 4-button fighter, with a control scheme reminiscent to Virtua Fighter. It is based on the popular and long-running Kinnikuman anime/manga franchise. This game's roster is focused on the characters from the original 80s series, though it has several characters from the early 2000s sequel Kinnikuman Nisei (known as Ultimate Muscle in the West). Considering the developer's background and Kinnikuman's subject matter, MGP2 has a lot of wrestling game elements, such as ring ropes and an emphasis on throws. However, unlike most other AKI games, MGP2 also has mechanics more at home with your traditional fighting game, like meters, motion inputs and juggles.
Kirameki Star Road

Kirameki Star Road is a Japanese arcade music trivia and idol-raising game released by Taito in 1997. Operating on the Taito F3 arcade hardware system, it uniquely blends the aesthetic of "talent management" simulation games with classic intro quiz mechanics.

 Players choose from three different average girls—often described as a nerd, a popular girl, and the girl next door—and guide them on a path toward musical stardom.
Progression is built around trivia. Players must quickly recognize synthesized musical tracks, anime theme songs, and classic tunes played by the arcade board's sound system to select the correct multiple-choice answers.
Kisekae Hanafuda

Kisekae Hanafuda (着せかえ花札) is a Japanese arcade game released in December 1995 by the publisher and developer I'Max.

The title translates literally to "Dress-up Hanafuda", combining traditional Japanese card gameplay (Hanafuda) with a "dress-up" or digital aesthetic common to adult-oriented mahjong and card arcade titles of that era.
Kisekae Mahjong

Kisekae Mahjong is a 1995 Japanese arcade game developed and manufactured by I'Max. It was released exclusively for the Multi Amenity Cassette System (MACS), a niche cartridge-based arcade platform designed by I'Max to run various mahjong and hanafuda puzzle games in Japanese amusement centers.

 The term Kisekae (着せ替え) translates directly to "dress-up" or "changing clothes." True to its name, the game rewards successful mahjong hands by allowing players to modify or change the outfits of various anime-style opponents.
Kitten Kaboodle

Kitten Kaboodle was produced by Konami in 1988.

Kitten Kaboodle lets the player control a cat as it searches each stage trying to find four hidden keys. The stages are filled with enemies that can be defeated by pushing blocks into them. Blocks can also be jumped over if they get in the way. There are also special blocks that when three of the same kind are lined up it will cause an effect to happen such as clearing the screen of every enemy on it or giving the player temporary invulnerability. Enemies can drop valuables which increase the players points and in turn these points can be spent at a shop which sells various items like running shoes and bombs.
Kizuna Encounter: Super Tag Battle

One year ago, King Leo had made the Battle of the Beast God tournament in order to see on who had what it took to challenge and fight against him from within their own given time and opportunity. Nine fighters had entered the tournament from within sight and that each of them had battled against one another from within a strong and relentless manner, but in the end, Sho Hayate had proven to be the strongest competitor and that he had won the tournament while defeating King Leo (and his fake impersonator King Lion) from within the finals of the tournament.

To seek revenge against Hayate and those who caused his humiliating downfall, King Leo has organized a second version of the Battle of the Beast God tournament, but this time, there's a new rule. Teams of 2 people must work together from within this new tournament so that they can either ensure victory or face defeat.
Kkot Bi Nyo Special

Kkot Bi Nyo Special (꽃비녀 스페셜) is a rare, Korean-release tabletop board/hanafuda arcade game published by Shinwhajin and Dynax in 1997. Built specifically for solo play, it relies on a unique 8-way joystick and a dedicated Hanafuda control layout.
Klax

A puzzle game, the object is to catch assorted color falling tiles and create rows, columns, or diagonals of a single color. Each level requires a different pattern to be made, and the tiles fall faster, more at a time, and in an increasing number of colors as the game progresses.
KlonDike+
A Klondike solitaire tabletop video game much like Freecell.
Knights in Armor

Knights in Armor is a jousting game for two players. The black and white knight face off on their horses. They both move horizontally across the screen in different directions and must try to unsaddle each other by moving their lance into the correct position. A match lasts 8, 10 or 12 jousts depending on the settings.
Knights of the Round

Knights of the Round is a hack and slash game featuring King Arthur. Two other players can join the fight against the enemies. If you gain enough points you gain a level and increase in power: Sir Lancelot and Sir Percival.

The story tells of a man who pulled the mighty sword Excalibur from a rock which no one else could achieve. This feat signified that he should be king of the Britons and lead them to peace. The trouble is there is mass chaos in the land and the only way Arthur can stop it is to find the holy grail which has been hidden for over a thousand years. Aurthur is joined by Percival and Lancelot on his quest to find the grail.

The gameplay involves the player to scroll along the screen fighting of enemies with a sword or axe depending on the character. The player can also block and parry with opponents which is done by a simple button press.
Knights of Valour

Knights of Valour is a 2D (2.5D gameplay) arcade weapon-based side scrolling beat'em up, like Golden Axe or Dungeons & Dragons: Shadow over Mystara. The game is loosely based on the Chinese historical novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms (action starts in 16th year of Han Dynasty) and main enemy is Sun Quan, who kidnapped infant Adou.

Player can choose one from 5 characters ( Five Tiger Generals of Shu, each has various weapon) - Zhao, Zhang Huang, Guan and Ma. The rest is simple - he goes right, kills enemies and bosses. Enemies have various weapons - swords and shields, spears, bows. The player can find various treasures for points.
Knights of Valour 2

Knights of Valour 2 is a scrolling beat-em-up for up to four players set in the same fantasy Romance of the Three Kingdoms setting as its predecessor. Inspired by classics such as Dungeons & Dragons: Shadow Over Mystara, it features complex branching pathways and story scenes that allow players to make choices that affect the outcome of the rest of the game. Players will fight large waves of foes, but by using the game's complex fighting game-inspired combo system they're able to take out enemies in style. In addition to the standard game mode, players can unlock the more difficult "internet ranking mode" which rewards players at the end with a code to input at the official website in order to register their score in the online leaderboards.

The "Five Tiger Generals" are selectable at the start, returning from the previous game - Zhao Yun, Zhang Huang, Guan Yu, and Ma Chao.
Knights of Valour 2 Plus: Nine Dragons

Knights Of Valour Plus is an Action game, developed and published by IGS (Taiwan), which was released in 1999.

The Plus version has 4 more characters to choose from. But the game is the same
Knights of Valour 2: New Legend

A horizontally scrolling beatemup that uses Romance of the Three Kingdoms story as a backdrop. Unlike previous entries in the series this title utilized an electronic card based system that saved a players level and items each time they played the game. This game is an update of Knights of Valour 2 that includes new levels, shops, weapons, and enemies.This may be a duplicate entry with Knights of Valour 2 Bushou Retsuden
Knights of Valour 2: Nine Dragons

Arcade never dies! Experience the side-scrolling, beat 'em up arcade masterpiece!
Knights of Valour 2 is an action-packed and fast-paced beat 'em up, taking place in beautiful, side-scrolling stages.
Choose one of nine different characters, each with unique traits to fit your individual playstyle. Collect equipment and learn lots of new skills to enhance your characters' abilities.
Knights of Valour 3

Knights of Valour is a very classic and popular (especially in Asian countries) side-scrolling action arcade game series from Taiwan. Waiting for ten years after Knights of Valour 2, IGS brought us its orthodox sequel – Knights of Valour 3 in 2011, only released for PolyGame Master 2 (PGM2) platform.

After Japanese Warriors of Fate, Taiwanese Knights of Valour series began a more long-term fashion in all arcade game rooms. Especially the first two works are still the favorite ones for many video game players, which can be considered as a rare flag of arcade games.

Knights of Valour 3 removed the classic character 黄忠, replaced by his made-up ‘daughter’ – 黄芸. The most surprising is, this work new added two playable characters: 刘备 and 周瑜! Plus other familiar generals, a brand-new generation of Knights of Valour did not let KoV fan players down!
Knights of Valour Plus

Knights Of Valour Plus is an Action game, developed and published by IGS (Taiwan), which was released in 1999.

Knights of Valour Plus is an upgrade with some differences:
- The bonus after every stage is higher for the original version.
- The colour of the lifebar is different for the 2 versions (yellow and green).
- The three secret characters in the original version are already unlocked.
- 2 new characters, the white Huang Zhong and the red Zhang Fei.
Knights of Valour: Super Heroes

This is an upgrade to the original Knights Of Valour that features more selectable characters and special moves. Knights of Valour is a 2D (2.5D gameplay) arcade weapon-based side scrolling beat'em up, like Golden Axe or Dungeons & Dragons: Shadow over Mystara. The game is loosely based on the Chinese historical novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms (action starts in 16th year of Han Dynasty) and main enemy is Sun Quan, who kidnapped infant Adou. Player can choose one from 5 characters ( Five Tiger Generals of Shu, each has various weapon) - Zhao, Zhang Huang, Guan and Ma. The rest is simple - he goes right, kills enemies and bosses. Enemies have various weapons - swords and shields, spears, bows. The player can find various treasures for points.
Knights of Valour: Super Heroes Plus

Knights of Valour: Super Heroes Plus (also known as Sangoku Senki Super Heroes Plus in Japan or Sanguo Zhan Ji Luanshi Xiaoxiong in Asia) is a 2004 2.5D weapon-based side-scrolling beat 'em up arcade game developed by International Games System (IGS). Running on the iconic IGS PolyGame Master (PGM) arcade hardware platform, it serves as an enhanced upgrade to the original 1999 Knights of Valour and Super Heroes editions, delivering a significantly deeper roster, refined combos, and reworked mechanics.

The game is loosely based on the classic 14th-century Chinese historical novel, Romance of the Three Kingdoms. Setting its stage around the decline of the Han Dynasty, the plot kicks off with the warlord Sun Quan kidnapping the infant Adou, forcing the legendary generals of Shu to fight their way through hordes of enemy forces and mythical boss encounters to rescue him.
Knights of Valour: The Seven Spirits

Knights of Valour: The Seven Spirits was released for the Sammy Atomiswave arcade cabinet in 2003. It is one in a series of games in the Knights of Valour series.

Despite it’s release being long after the general decline of the Beat ‘Em Up genre, KoV: The Seven Spirits is, at its core, a classic Beat ‘Em Up. You choose your character, walk right, and pummel any and everything in sight. Boss fights await at the end of each ‘chapter.’ Special moves, health & magic pick ups, and treasure pick ups (points) – all general staples of the genre, are found here.
Knights of Valour: Yi Tong Zhong Yuan

In addition to Capcom's "Three Kingdoms", the arcade market has a not very famous Three Kingdoms action game, Taiwan's IGS launched its "Three Kingdoms" version. Although, at the end of the 90s, not many people played the game outside Asia, Taiwan's IGS is still a solid alternative for this type of game, as well as the development of a variety of very rich and quite refreshing arcade games.
Knuckle Bash

Knuckle Bash is a 1993 beat-em-up arcade game, that offers two-player simultaneous action. Developed and published by Toaplan in Japan, later released in North America and Europe by Atari.

Choose between three different wrestlers and try to defeat the evil criminal organization. Join clash, dice and devo as they make their stand against wrestling's underworld! This is the tale of how the young wrestlers saved the sport from evil and corruption.

The Mad Bull Group is a corrupt wrestling organization that profits while draining the purity of the sport. Help the Knuckle Bash team overpower evil and convert the Mad Bulls to their side! Our young wrestlers know how millions of young fans look up to them as role models. It's for them they must TAKE A STAND!
Knuckle Bash 2

A ROM hack/bootleg of the Toaplan original game, Knuckle Bash, and released as a faux sequel. 4 wacky characters go after the Bulls and others who would dare threaten the peace of the city! In this version the football player is selectable from the very beginning and levels have been modified and are in a different order.
Knuckle Heads

Up to four players must choose control for six different characters from: the United States, the game's home country of Japan, Greece, China, Norway, and Brazil in what is described as "America's hottest new game show" on the flyer; they all have different special weapons, moves, and catchphrases, and the show will move to each of the characters' respective home towns (Honolulu, Kyoto, Athens, Hong Kong, Lillehammer and Sao Paulo) for each successive round.
Knuckle Joe

This game, licensed by Taito is an horizontal scrolling brawler, featuring 15 stages. Our protagonist, Joe, has to beat all his enemies and the different final bosses with their corresponding abilities. At the end of each boss, there are bonus stages in which you can drive a motorcycle and shoot other drivers.

The controls consistsof an 8-way direction lever and two action buttons. We can move to the left, to the right, jump (very fast), punch, kick and block (pressing both buttons).
KO Punch

This was a video game update of Sega's first electro-mechanical arcade game, Punching Bag, released in 1962.

KO Punch inspired other similar boxing arcade games, from companies like Kriss Sport and Kalkomat, that are still popular in modern arcades today.

It also introduced large, colourful, 2D character sprites, several years before rival Nintendo's Punch-Out!
Koala Mint

Koala Mint is a classic video slot machine developed by Aristocrat Leisure. Originally released in 2000, it runs on Aristocrat's iconic MK5 (Mark V) hardware platform.

The game was distributed globally across casinos and pub markets—often referred to as a "fruit machine" in the UK or a "pokie" in Australia.
KOF: Sky Stage

KOF Sky Stage is an arcade shooting game based on SNK's franchise The King of Fighters series.

Players can choose to rotate action on the screen horizontally or vertically based on their preferences. A normal story in Story Mode consists of fifteen stages. The player can select Kyo Kusanagi, Iori Yagami, Kula Diamond, Mai Shiranui, Terry Bogard and Athena Asamiya. Among the bosses the player can fight alternative versions of Athena and Kula Diamond, Kusanagi, Orochi Iori, Goenitz, Rugal Bernstein, Orochi Chris, Orochi Yashiro, Orochi Shermie and Orochi. Each character possesses their own special moves from the fighting game series but adapted to the shooting system.
Koi Koi Part 2

Koi Koi Part 2 is a rare, Japanese hanafuda card-matching arcade game released in 1982 by the developer Kiwako.
The game is a direct digital adaptation of the traditional Japanese card game Hanafuda (specifically the Koi-Koi variant), played on a classic green background layout using digitized card images.

Players match flower cards (hanafuda) from their hand with cards laid out on a central grid to form point-scoring combinations (yaku).
Koi Koi Shimasho

Koi Koi Shimasho was produced by Visco Games in 1995.

An adult themed mahjong game from japan.
Koi Koi Shimasho 2: Super Real Hanafuda

Koi Koi Shimasho 2: Super Real Hanafuda (スーパーリアル花札 恋こいしましょ 2) is an adult-themed arcade video game developed and published by Visco Corporation in December 1997 exclusively in Japan. It is a strategic "strip hanafuda" card game where players compete in the traditional Japanese card game Koi-Koi against anime-styled female opponents.

The game requires players to clear rounds of Koi-Koi using traditional hanafuda cards. Compared to its 1995 predecessor, Koi Koi Shimasho 2 expanded the roster to eight beautiful opponents. While the initial character designs were simplified, the game compensated by featuring fully animated dialogue sequences and fluidly animated stripping sequences as rewards for winning card rounds.
Koihime Enbu

The Koihime Enbu arcade machine operates primarily on Sega's digital distribution platforms for arcades, with the modern iteration, Koihime Enbu RyoRaiRai Version 3, running on the Sega ALL.Net P-ras MULTI version 3 (APM3) cabinet. Unlike dedicated older hardware, the game is typically selected from a digital menu on these multi-game cabinets rather than occupying a standalone, single-title machine.
Koihime Enbu RyoRaiRai

Set against the tumultuous backdrop of ancient China's Three Kingdoms era, Koihime Enbu RyoRaiRai delivers fast-paced fighting action featuring an all-female cast of warlords. Engage in intense battles for kingdom supremacy, personal glory, and beyond.

Koihime Enbu RyoRaiRai represents the pinnacle of extensive arcade game updates, meticulously rebalanced to align even more closely with the original vision: a fighter that's accessible to all.

Whether you're a genre veteran or a newcomer, this game has something for you. Veterans will appreciate the streamlined controls that let them dive right into the action, while newcomers can hone their skills through training and challenge modes, preparing them for both online and offline battles.
Koihime Enbu RyoRaiRai Version 3 (Koihime V3)

Koihime Enbu RyoRaiRai Version 3 is the second major revision to Koihime Enbu. It adds a new playable character (Jokō) and assist (Kakuka) to the roster, one new stage (Luoyang), and changes some of the core gameplay systems.

Originally released on April 22nd, 2021 for PC and July 28th, 2021 for PS4, update version 3.10 introduced system and character changes. Most notably, "V3" added a forward run/dash macro mapped to a dedicated button. The PC version required the character/supporter DLC to get the balance changes (similar to how Rev 2 DLC works for Xrd Revelator) whereas PS4 got the balance for free and the DLC was optional. This distinction seems to have been dropped as of patch 3.50.

A second DLC character was teased in late 2022 and version 3.50 was released on March 29th, 2023
Kokontouzai Eto Monogatari
Place up to three of the same item, horizontally, vertically or in an 'L' shape (although the 'L' can be turned in any direction).
Kollon

Kollon was produced by Cyberfront in 2003.

Puzzle Game on Taitos GNET Hardware. A puzzle game series where blocks must be cleared. Every so often new rows of blocks will push up the current ones. Not clearing enough within a set time limit will force the blocks to the top of the screen, where the player will lose. Blocks can be cleared if at least four blocks of the same color are touching. The speed of new rows will increase as the game is played longer. The blocks which get cleared will result in the blocks above falling down.br Also did get a release as PSP game.
Konami 80's AC Special

Konami 80's AC Special (known in Japan as Konami 80's Arcade Gallery (コナミエイティーズアーケードギャラリー, Konami Eitizu Ākēdo Gyararī) is a compilation of arcade video games, originally released in arcades in 1998. It was later ported to the PlayStation in 1999, where it was renamed to Konami Arcade Classics for its North American release. Unlike most of Konami's PlayStation games, the PlayStation version was not released in PAL regions.

While many compilations on home consoles predate Konami Arcade Classics, it is one of the earliest examples of an arcade reissue of classic games, being preceded only by the Namco Classics Collection series. It is also, to date, one of only two arcade compilations with both a coin-op and consumer release (the other being Space Invaders Anniversary, which was only released in Japan and Europe).
Konami GT

The player drives a sports car which must reach various checkpoints without running out of fuel. A turbo mode (activated by the gear shift) increases the car's speed but uses more fuel and puts the player at a higher risk of hitting an obstacle. Fuel power-ups can be found on the road which the player must pick up to make it to the final checkpoint.
Konami's Open Golf Championship

Konami Open Golf Championship was produced by Konami in 1994.

A standard golf game. Quite nice graphics and animation.
Konami's Ping-Pong

Konami's Ping Pong recreates the fast-paced sport of table tennis. To win each match you must get to 10 points with a 2 point lead - if the scores reach 10-9 the game goes on until someone has a 2 point lead or reaches 15, in a similar manner to tennis. There are nine skill levels to beat, with increasing abilities as the game goes on. The human player has the advantage of serving first, and as the serve reverses every five points, you are guaranteed to have more chances to serve than your opponent (remember the significance of 10 and 15 in the scoring). The points system rewards long rallies and large winning margins, as you get points for each hit, for each point won, and for each point of the winning margin.
Konek-Gorbunok

Konek-Gorbunok © 1988 Terminal.

The player controls a boy named Ivan, a peasant's son and his magic steed (Humpbacked Horse) to carry out the many unreasonable demands entrusted by the Tsar. During his adventure he will have to avoid various obstacles and hazards on the level and use your weapon and must try to capture the beautiful magic firebird for the Tsar, to keep his magic horse, and find his love of beautiful Tsar-Maid (Princess) to live happily ever after.

The title of this game translates from Russian as 'Little Humped Horse'.

The game is based on the Russian fairy tale with the same title, written by Peter Pavlovich Ershov.

There is no level 15. Each screen has its own tilemap and code. There is a tilemap for level 15 but there's not any code for this.
Kong

A bizarre Donkey Kong bootleg that runs on Namco's Galaxian hardware. There are various differences between Kong and Donkey Kong, as Kong shows the "Kong" logo upon bootup, and the jumping is a lot more jerky on Kong, color and sprite changes.
Konkyuu no Hoshi

Konkyuu no Hoshi was developed and manufactured by BMC and released exclusively in Japan

The game is a single player bowling game.
Kono e Tako
An action-puzzle game where an octopus at the center of the playfield clears a bunch of barrels that are closing in from both ends of the screen by sucking them in and spitting them out to match.
Koro Koro Quest

Koro Koro Quest is a rare, single-player arcade game published and developed by Takumi. Released exclusively in Japan on February 28, 1999, it is widely categorized as a puzzle game featuring a unique "casino-style twist with an adventure theme."
Korokoro Pensuke
Korokoro Pensuke is a medal game developed and published in 1997 by Konami
Korosuke Roller

Korosuke Roller is a rare 1981 maze arcade video game developed by Alpha Denshi Co., Ltd. and published by Kural Electric, Ltd.. It functions as a unique update or sequel variant to the widely popular arcade game Crush Roller (known as Make Trax in North America).

You control a Squid instead of a paintbrush, swimming through paths to ink the floor of the maze.
Kosodate Quiz My Angel

Kosodate Quiz: My Angel (translated as "My Angel: A Child-Raising Quiz") is a unique Japanese arcade trivia video game released by Namco in 1996. Running on Seta 2nd Generation coin-op hardware, it blends standard multiple-choice trivia with a young life-simulator mechanic.

One or two players take on the role of parents raising a newborn baby girl. The goal is to answer trivia questions correctly to guide her from birth (age 0) up to her adulthood at age 25.
Each round features questions with four selectable answers. Answering correctly raises your "child support expense" funds. Answering incorrectly depletes a life meter; if it runs out, you hit a game over.
Between quiz stages, you make parental choices (such as what book to buy or activities to do). Based on your choices and how well you answer questions, your daughter's personality shifts. She can mature into several archetypes, including "Gentle", "Sexy", "Cult" (nerdy), or "Cheerful".
Kosodate Quiz My Angel 2

Kosodate Quiz My Angel 2 is a unique trivia and life-simulation arcade game released by Namco in 1997 exclusively in Japan. Operating on Seta 2nd Generation coin-op hardware, it combines classic multiple-choice quiz mechanics with an interactive parenting simulation.

Each stage presents a series of trivia questions, each offering four selectable answers. Correct answers generate "child support expenses" (in-game funds). Incorrect answers deplete a life meter. If the meter empties, the game ends.
Kosodate Quiz My Angel 3
Kosodate Quiz: My Angel 3 is a quiz game, developed and published by Namco, which was released in Japan in 1998.
Kot-Rybolov

Kot-Rybolov © 1988 Terminal [Russia]

Russian arcade video game.
Kotekitai Slot

Kotekitai Slot (こてき隊スロット) is a Japanese arcade medal game released in 2001 by Sammy Corporation. It belongs to Sammy's "Kids Medal Series" and is considered part of the "Treasure Fall" redemption machine line.

 Unlike standard adult slot machines (Pachislo), this is a "medal game" aimed at younger arcade visitors. The core mechanics are simple: players prompt a slot mechanic with the objective of aligning three identical musical instruments to win medals.
Kotoba no Puzzle Mojipittan

The Kotoba no Puzzle: Mojipittan arcade machine is the original cabinet for Namco's acclaimed Japanese word-puzzle franchise, launched exclusively in Japan in December 2001. Built on Namco's PlayStation-based System 10 hardware, this standalone arcade setup introduced the series' iconic tile-dropping gameplay before it was ported to home consoles.

The game functions essentially as a real-time, fast-paced single-player or competitive twist on Scrabble.
Koutetsu Yousai Strahl
Koutetsu Yousai Strahl is a horizontal scrolling Shoot 'em up developed by UPL in 1992.
Kozmik Krooz'r

Guide Kapt. Krooz'r into the mothership while either shooting, deflecting (with his shield) or avoiding various attacking enemies. Kapt. Krooz'r can only enter the mothership when it extends down a tractor beam. A bonus round, where Kapt Krooz'r must...
Kozure Ookami

In 1987, video game manufacturer Nichibutsu released a Japan-only beat 'em up based on the Lone Wolf and Cub series named Kozure Ōkami. Players guide Ogami Itto through an army of assassins while carrying his infant son on his back. A baby cart powerup enables Ookami to mow down enemies with blasts of fire. The game is considered a rarity by the Video Arcade Preservation Society.
Kram

Kram was produced by Taito in 1982.

You control KRAM and build walls to prevent the bad guys from getting you. Pick up coins to get points. Use a button to destroy the walls you built.
Krazy Bowl

Krazy Bowl was produced by American Sammy in 1994.

A bowling game with two modes of play: regular and Krazy Bowl. The latter is bowling with various pins missing and is harder

At the beginning of the game, you are given a choice of two different games to play; "Regulation" where you try to knock down all ten pins or "Sweeper" where you try to knock down a random number of pins that are set differently in each frame.

The game play is similar to Capcom Bowling.

This game can also be configured to use a joystick. In this mode a third play button (Shoot) is also added. The cocktail mode supports either joysticks or trackballs.
Krull

Krull is a multi part action game based on the movie of the same name. A beast and his army have traveled through space until finally landing on the distant planet of Krull and ravaging the entire planet. But there is a prophecy which tells of a king and queen who will someday take back the planet. These future rulers are Princess Lyssa and Prince Colwyn. But before their marrage, Princess Lyssa is captured by the beast!

You play the part of Prince Colwyn on a mission to rescue Lyssa and destroy the beast. The game is divided up into several parts.

The first part takes place during the foiled wedding. A large number of slayers arrive at the castle, and you need to defeat as many as you can to earn points. But eventually Princess Lyssa is captured.

In the next section you need to ride your horse towards the Widow's web; on the way you can collect Glaives which may be used to fight the beast.
Kuai Le Xi You Ji

Kuai Le Xi You Ji (快乐西游记 - literally translating to Happy Journey to the West) is an arcade game released in the early 2000s by the prominent Taiwanese arcade developer IGS (International Games System).

Unlike many action-oriented arcade adaptations of the classic Chinese novel Journey to the West (such as IGS's own famous side-scrolling beat 'em up Oriental Legend), Kuai Le Xi You Ji is classified as a Mahjong and puzzle-based video game.
Kung Fu

Kung-Fu Master is a side-scrolling beat 'em up game produced by Irem as arcade game in 1984 and distributed by Data East in North America. The game was initially released in Japan under the title of Spartan X[a] as a tie-in based on the Jackie Chan film Wheels on Meals (which was also distributed under the name Spartan X in Japan); however, the game has no bearing on the plot of the film outside the names of the main protagonist and his girlfriend, allowing Irem to export the game without the license by simply changing the title.

The players control Thomas, the titular Kung-Fu Master, as he fights his way through the five levels of the Devil's Temple in order to rescue his girlfriend Sylvia from the mysterious crime boss Mr. X. Kung-Fu Master is regarded as the first beat 'em up video game. It had a NES port titled Kung Fu, which sold 3.5 million cartridges. The arcade game also inspired a 1988 French film of the same name.
Kung Fu Pounda

The Kung Fu Pounda fruit machine is a highly popular, martial-arts-themed pub slot machine manufactured by G Squared Gaming. Known for its cheeky humor and immersive board-game style feature matrix, it is a staple choice for UK arcade enthusiasts and home games rooms alike.
Kung-Fu Master

Loosely based on a movie, Kung-Fu Master is a side scrolling action game for one or two players, who alternate turns.

Mr. X has captured the pickpocket Sylvia and it is up to Thomas, a kung-fu master who owns a restaurant, to get her back. She is located on the top floor of Mr. X's castle and Thomas will need to fight his way to the top. Of course, this won't be easy as each floor has many opponents to get past and a floor boss at the end of each level.

Thomas is able to move left and right, jump, duck, and punch and kick. Enemy projectiles such as knives can be kicked in the air to rebound them towards the enemy. On the top floor resides Mr. X himself.

History:
The lead developer of Kung-Fu Master was Takashi Nishiyama, who left Irem and joined Capcom, where he led the development of the very first Street Fighter game.
Kung-Fu Roushi

Kung-Fu Roushi is a medal-style arcade attraction themed around a martial-arts master (“Roushi” meaning “old teacher”). The player inserts a coin and activates a large button at the correct time to stop a rotating indicator. Matching or stopping at the target zone awards a small payout or activates the prize chute.

Rounds last only a few seconds, and the machine resets immediately for the next player. Lights, voice samples, and the animated figure of the “Kung-Fu Roushi” respond to success or failure with comic exclamations and gestures.
Kung-Fu Taikun
A one or two player puzzle game published and developed by Seibu Kaihatsu in 1984.
Kuri Kinton

The game stars a police agent who is out to uncover and destroy a terrorist organization, rescue hostages and save the Republic of China. Moves consist of punching, kicking, crouching, jumping and running. Throughout the stage, the player must follow the arrow indicator while fighting off waves of enemies. Deadly traps are also around and must be avoided. The left Power meter indicates the player's health, while the right one indicates a boss enemy's health. Defeating a stage boss takes the player to the next stage. Enemies and bosses get progressively harder through each stage.
Kuru Kuru Pyon Pyon

You can bet to any (or all) of the following 5 characters: Bote, Oume, Pyoko, Kunio, and Pyon Pyon. Press start, and the reels start to roll. You'll win if you can get 3 of the chosen character(s) in a row, column or diagonal.
The black tadpoles behave just like jokers... If you have 2 chosen characters in a row and the remaining one is a black tadpole, it will transform into another character to complete the 3 in a row, allowing you to win.
