Match '98 (specifically version 1.33) is an arcade-style, video casino/fruit machine game released in 1998 by the developer Amcoe.
Designed as a counter-top or cabinet-style machine, the game utilizes a puzzle and matching dynamic layered onto traditional slot-machine mechanics, classified under the "Casino" category in emulator software like MAME.

Unlike standard reel-spinning fruit machines, it leans into tile or symbol matching mechanics—akin to cherry/fruit bonus machines of the late '90s—where players attempt to line up matching icons to secure point credits or prize payouts.
Match Games

Match Games is a coin-operated arcade video game released by Merit Industries in 1982. Merit Industries, a United States-based manufacturer known for creating popular countertop bar and tavern games, released this title as part of its early lineup of video skill and gambling machines.
Match It

Match It is a timed game where a player must uncover all the pairs of tiles until no more tiles remain. You can only pick two tiles that are directly connected, so the best way to remove all the tiles is to begin at the outer sections and continually work towards the inner sections.

All the erotic scenes from the Japanese version has been removed in "Match it" version.
Match It II

Match It II is a puzzle arcade game developed by Tamtex and published by Irem in 1993. The game features boards filled with colorful tiles—jewels, letters, or mahjong pieces—set against decorative backgrounds inspired by Chinese art and symbolism.

The player removes all tiles on the screen by selecting matching pairs. Two identical tiles can be cleared only if they can be connected by a path that bends no more than twice and does not pass through other tiles. When all tiles are cleared, the stage is complete.

Three single-player modes provide different visual themes and difficulty levels:

- Fantasy: the beginner mode, featuring bright jewel-like symbols.
- Girls: an intermediate mode using alphabet tiles that reveal a portrait when cleared.
- Professional: the advanced mode using mahjong-style characters.

A separate Match by Two mode allows two players to compete simultaneously within any theme. Scoring rewards consecutive removals of identical tile types.
Mausuke no Ojama the World

Mausuke no Ojama the World (まうすけのオジャマ・ざ・わーるど) is an incredibly rare, competitive falling-tile puzzle arcade game developed by Data East and released in Japan in 1995/1996. The game is built specifically for the Sega ST-V (Sega Titan Video) arcade hardware, which was a cartridge-based arcade platform sharing a near-identical architecture with the Sega Saturn home console.

The title features mechanics similar to genre staples like Puyo Puyo and Columns, but with a distinct mechanical twist.
Maverik

The JPM Maverick fruit machine is a classic, highly sought-after British pub slot machine (amusement with prizes / AWP) manufactured by JPM (John Purewal Machines). Known for its classic Hi/Lo-based gameplay, it features a retro design, unique "hidden" cheats, and built-in hints that help players reach the jackpot.
Mawasunda!!

Mawasunda!! (known internationally as Turn It Around) is a rare, wacky mini-game collection arcade machine released by Taito in 1999/2000. Styled closely after Konami's popular Bishi Bashi series, it trades standard joysticks for unique, dedicated physical controls that define its rapid-fire gameplay.

The machine features 20 frantic Japanese-style mini-games divided into 5 distinct stages. Each game tests your speed, endurance, and coordination by forcing you to spin the crank left or right as fast or as precisely as possible.
Max RPM

Max RPM is a split-screen racing arcade game that was developed and published by Bally Midway, which was released in 1986.

SHIFT YOUR EARNINGS UP TO HIGH

Max excitement...Max earnings...Max RPM™. Rev up your locations with the highest performance driving game on the street. * Winning driving theme includes drag race, city track and country road events. * Unique split screen...like two games in one.Realistic 4-speed shifter.Road feel steering.*Join-The-Action™, Bally Midway's exclusive money making buy-in feature. * Dramatic digitalized sound effects.Two player interaction.Challenging driving skill features.**
Maximum Force

Maximum Force is a light gun shooter arcade game developed by Mesa Logic for Atari Games in 1997. In 1998, Atari Games re-released the game as part of one machine called Area 51/Maximum Force Duo that also included Area 51, and later ported the game to both the Sony PlayStation and Sega Saturn game consoles.

Like its predecessor Area 51, Maximum Force is notable for its use of digitized video stored on an on-board hard disk, and the bizarrely contrasting unrealistic gibs into which every enemy blows apart when shot, in exactly the same way. While enemies, innocents, and explosions are 2D digitized video sprites, the levels and vehicles are pre-rendered in 3D.
Maximum Speed

Maximum Speedis a car racing game from Sammy. A white-hot racing game that will thrill all your senses! Take part in this extravagant racing game with 8 different racing circuits and 3 kinds of races: formula one style, Indy car style and truck racing. Use your brilliant driving technique to trim your lap time, whilst fighting against the steering feedback.
Maximus Cash

Maximus Cash is a gladiator-themed fruit machine game released by Blueprint Operations in early 2026. The game is rolled out across major digital cabinet lineups, including premium Regal Gaming setups like Velocity, Auroramax, Alphacurve, Ultramax, and Alphamax.
Maximus Cash Club

Club Maximus Cash, was an iconic pub and working men's club fruit machine released in the early 2000s. Built on the popular Scorpion 4 hardware platform, it typically operated with a £200 jackpot and a 20p per play stake. It was a follow-up brother to the highly popular Club Rolling Thunder machine.
Maya

Maya is an extremely rare, wide-release arcade video game released in 1994 by the developer and manufacturer Promat (often associated with Fuuki Co. Ltd.).

Adult puzzle / solitaire tile-matching Mahjong game.
The gameplay features background pictures of women uncovered as you clear tiles.
Mayday

Mayday!! was produced by Hoei in 1981.

The player's ship flies over a horizontally scrolling planet surface. Waves of enemy ships attack and must be destroyed for the player to advance to the next planet. The Mayday button slows the game down for five seconds. The player's ship fires both forward and back.

The game itself is not a direct copy of Defender. It has an 8-Way joystick, two fire buttons (forward and backwards) and a Mayday button. The Mayday button slows everything on-screen down for a few seconds and makes the screen flash. Although it only scrolls from right to left, you can speed up and slow down your ship's forward momentum. The first wave that is over the sea of submarines. The submarines, which look a lot like Baiters in Defender, shoot along the bottom of the screen and fire up at the player's ship. The player's shots are aimed diagonally down at the waves.
Mayhem 2002

Mayhem 2002 is a sports game that is rather like a combination of roller derby and soccer with four goals was produced by Cinematronics in 1985.

A ball is entered into play and you must get the ball into one of the four designated goals the one that is lit up and flashing. Your oponent is trying to do the same. You can elbow your oponent to make them lose the ball then take the ball yourself and either throw it into the goal or run right up to the goal and put it in. Points are awarded for each goal that is made.
Mayjinsen

Mayjinsen (often spelled Meijinsen) is a classic Japanese Shogi (Japanese chess) arcade video game series developed and published by Seta. Originally released in arcades in December 1994, the game features competitive blitz shogi matches against computer AI or opponents.

The original title, Hayazashi Shougi Gogatsu Mayjinsen, translates to "Quick Shogi Championship Series". It ran on specialized hardware featuring a Zilog Z80 and V810 CPU. The series saw multiple updates, including Mayjinsen 2 (1994) and Honkaku Hayasashi Shougi Meijinsen 3 (1999), which was released for the Nintendo/Seta Aleck 64 arcade hardware platform.
Mayjinsen 2
Mayjinsen 2 is a Tabletop / Shougi game developed by Seta in 1994 for the Arcade.
Mayjinsen 3

Mayjinsen 3 (also known as Blitz Shogi Championship 3) is a single-player speed Shogi (Japanese chess) arcade game released in 2000 by Seta and Able Corporation.

The game runs on the Aleck64 arcade hardware, a proprietary system developed by Seta that is closely based on the Nintendo 64 architecture.
Mazan: Flash of the Blade

MAZAN – Flash Of The Blade by Namco puts the player into the role of an ancient samurai warrior. This is one of several arcade titles that pioneered the use of motion sensing / gesture technology years before such ideas were used on home game consoles like the Nintendo Wii or Microsoft Kinect.

Here, the player uses the samurai’s weapon of choice to control the action – a katana sword. Using positional sensors, the game is able to actively track the current position of your sword along with the angle and swing. Your success, score and life, depends your ability to properly manipulate the sword to be at the right place at the right time. Fight your way across three stages against hordes of gruesome undead creatures. Slash objects to unveil hidden items and be ready to parry on-coming attacks! Successful parries allow you to send your enemies reeling before finishing them off. Mazan is truly a unique arcade game that adds some fun variety to any game line-up.
Maze Invaders

Maze Invaders was a prototype produced by Atari in 1981.

A cross between a maze game and a shooter. Collect all of the fruit in mazes with moving walls while avoiding various enemies. Some enemies can be destroyed with shots while others are only stunned.
Maze of Flott

Maze Of Flott is an Action game, developed and published by Taito Corporation, which was released in Japan in 1989.
Traverse a strange and cool city in search of magic keys that will allow you to travel around freely and escape to freedom, beating the game! In the fantastic Maze of Flott you drive around the city streets strategically entering buildings to cruise around their dungeon-like corridors to pick up fuel, find keys and avoid the many hazards and traps! Drive around, gather the keys and avoid hitting any other cool little cars!

More excellently crafted retro racing classics that you'll definitely love ar WipEout XL, Woody Woodpecker Racing and the amazing Moto Racer World Tour.
Mazer Blazer

Mazer Blazer was produced by Stern Electronics in 1983.

Zap the "cosmic attackers" before they reach your base. Slow the enemies by shooting the flashing blocks which open a force field.
Mazin Wars

The story takes place in 1999 where a Bio-Beast by the name of Godkaiser Hell has reigned supreme over Earth, after a nuclear and biological holocaust has disfigured most of the population and formed an army called the Steelmask Force. The survivors have fled underground and are constantly attacked by the Bio-Beast horde until one day a scientist by the name of Dr. Kabuto creates a mech, the Mazinger-Z, that can be used against the monsters. This is where the player takes control of the game's protagonist and pilots the suit in an attempt to reclaim the Earth.

The gameplay is a hack-n-slash game, where the player controls the suit by using the D-pad and using the face buttons to slash at enemy monsters. There is also a Super Attack that the player can use, but it will decrease their health after each use. The enemies consist of mutant animals such as dogs and beetles as well as the Bio-Beast soldiers that can range from regular soldiers, female fighters and even ninjas.
Mazinger Z

Mazinger Z was produced by Banpresto in 1994.

Mazinger-Z is a 2D vertical scrolling shooter, based on manga and anime with mechas (giant Japanese robots) "Mazinger-Z". The player can choose one from 3 mechas from various series: Mazinger Z, Great Mazinger, and Grendizer.

The game has straightforward gameplay - just fly forward and shoot enemies. The player can use 3 attacks - normal shot, energy whip (for close combat), and limited special attack. At the end of each level,a large boss awaits for players. Game has standard co-op for 2 players.
Mazooma Belle

"Red Hot Mazooma Belle" is a classic UK fruit machine released in the late 1990s. While the machine features "Mazooma" in its name, it was actually manufactured by BWB (BWB Holding/BWB Digital Slots).

Because both Mazooma and Bell-Fruit Games were prominent brands under the same parent umbrella (the Danoptra group) in the UK amusement industry, manuals and spare parts for older machines of this era are often catalogued together by collectors under the broader Bell-Fruit / Mazooma umbrella.
Meadows 4 in 1
A combination game that includes four games designed for one to four players.
Meadows Lanes

Meadows Lanes is a bowling game for one or two players. The game is very similar to Robot Bowl. The player controls a bowler at the bottom of the screen and can move him left and right. When the ball is let go it can be made to go fast or slow and hooked right or left. After ten rounds, the player with most points wins the game.
Mechanized Attack

Mechanized Attack is a game where the player uses a machine gun to stage an assault on a tropical island that's home to a cyborg army. Battle through numerous stages beginning with an approach to the island. This first stage is held over the water and features at attack on a number of small gunboats, a helicopter, and an entire battleship. As the player progresses through the stages of the island, the human (and even canine) enemies are revealed to be robots when the flesh is destroyed. At various junctures of the game, the player is allowed to choose which game path to pursue.

In the NES version, the player can use either a gamepad or the NES Light Zapper to carry out the mission. While the arcade version of Mechanized Attack has a miniature machine gun replica for the player to use, the NES version attempts to reproduce the feel by allowing the player to hold down a game pad button or the Light Zapper trigger for automatic fire.
Medal Mahjong Janjan Baribari [BET]

Medal Mahjong Janjan Baribari is a rare, Japanese "medal game" arcade machine developed and released by Nihon Bussan (Nichibutsu) in cooperation with Yubis and AV Japan in 1992.

It is a traditional Mahjong video game featuring an adult-oriented "entertainment club" theme.
Medal Network: Rockman EXE

Medal Network Rockman.EXE (メダルネットワークロックマンエグゼ) is a medal game released only in Japan in 2002 by Banpresto in Japan. The game is first in the Rockman EXE series. The second game in series is Rockman EXE The Medal Operation released in 2005.
Medaru no Gunman
Medaru no Gunman is a medal game released by Sega Corporation. Sega Logistics Service announced it would end service on the machines on March 31, 2017
Mega Blast

Megablast (メガブラスト) is a 1989 horizontally scrolling shooter released in arcades in 1989 by Taito in Europe and Japan. One or two players can control space fighters assigned to deal with an alien invasion using incredible firepower through eight stages. Many of the game's mini-bosses resemble previous Taito game characters.

The game was re-released for the PlayStation 2 as part of Taito Memories II Gekan in 2007.
Mega Force

The player pilots a starship called the Final Star, while shooting various enemies and destroying enemy structures for points.

Unlike later vertical scrolling shooters, like Toaplan's Twin Cobra, the Final Star had only two levels of weapon power, and no secondary weapons like missiles and/or bombs. Each stage in the game was named after a letter of the Greek alphabet. In certain versions of the game, there is an additional level called "Infinity" (represented by the infinity symbol) which occurs after Omega, after which the game repeats indefinitely.
Mega Man 2: The Power Fighters

It's a disaster: Doctor Light's lab has been attacked by Doctor Wily, and stolen some crucial parts for robots. And, if it weren't bad enough already, he has taken Roll as a hostage! Mega Man and Proto Man go to stop Wily and stumble upon Duo, the big alien robot, who is willing to help. And Bass, still angry that Wily has revived more Robot Masters, again teams up with the good side to destroy the enemies...

Mega Man 2: The Power Fighters is a 2D arcade fighting/shooting game and the sequel to Mega Man: The Power Battle. The player must choose one character from four available: Mega Man, Proto Man, Bass (all three returning from the previous game), and Duo. Each character has different attributes and abilities. Gameplay is almost identical to the previous installment, with an emphasis on shooting instead of hand-to-hand fighting and a "boss rush" feel where the player fights against bosses from the main series.
Mega Man III

Mega Man 3 is a traditional side-scrolling platformer: you jump from brick to brick while avoiding pits and shooting robots. It's quite similar, in all respects, to other Mega Man games; however, this is the first time that you get a sidekick. It's also the first time you're allowed to slide instead of merely walking.

Rush is your dog who helps out by offering other modes of transportation when you need it. He starts out with the 'Rush Coil' ability to launch you to the top of the screen like a springboard; later he acquires the 'Rush Jet' ability to turn into a guided, floating platform to carry you wherever you need to go; and he also gets the 'Rush Marine' ability which is a submarine that works just like the jet except underwater and with the added ability to hop around out of the water (you can actually jump while on the jet, but the jet continues to hover beneath you whereas you stay inside the submarine). All of these abilities function just like boss weapons.
Mega Man: The Power Battle

Doctor Wily is up to no good yet again, this time returning with 18 revived and improved Robot Masters. Mega Man and Proto Man proceed to stop him, while Bass destroys the inferior robots to show Wily that he is the only robot he needs.

Mega Man: The Power Battle is essentially a 2D arcade fighting game where characters use various guns instead of hand-to-hand combat. The player can choose between three playable characters: Mega Man, Proto Man and Bass. The game consists in a series of duels with bosses from various Mega Man games, such as Cut Man or Wood Man. After each battle, the player gains a new weapon.
Mega Phoenix

The metallic birds attacks again. With then fly the Megaphoenix, giant winged ships loaded with deadly proton eggs. No longer you are defenseless: yous shield of force is complemented by lateral guns and a frontal turboblaster... but you still need the experience of of the best pilot in the galaxy. 

This is not an official sequel to Phoenix, however it is a port of the computer game of the same name, which was in turn an enhanced clone of the original arcade game.
Mega Twins

The game features two twins who are attempting to re-take control of their land, Alurea, after a monster unexpectedly attacks, destroying everything in its path. The people of Alurea have lived in peace for a thousand years and have forgotten how to fight, yet the land's only survivors, the twin sons of the king, must take up the challenge and return their kingdom to its former glory. The two twins, aged around 15 at the time the game takes place, venture forth in search of a legendary stone known as "Dragon Blue Eyes", which is rumoured to be able to put everything back to rights.
Mega Zone

Mega Zone is a shooter arcade game released by Konami in 1983.

Mega Zone is a vertical scrolling top down shooter. Players go through several zones of enemy territories in order to reach their last destination, the Mega Zone to have a final showdown with the enemies command tower.

Players pilot an amphibious rocket tank and get to shoot at 32 different kinds of enemies. If the player collects twelve power energy pods it causes a "MEG" (short from Mega) power-up to appear. Getting this power-up makes the tank combine with another tank and triples the size and the firepower of the tank. On the way to the Mega Zone, players will occasionally reach a fork in which they can choose which path they want to take.
Megadon
Megadon is a one or two player shooter game developed by Epos and licensed to Photar for distribution in 1982.
Megatack

Players face a multitude of Space Monsters in every other round, beginning with the first. The Monsters start at the top of the screen and make their way downwards towards the players' Spacepods; if they reach the bottom without being shot, they begin hopping towards the players' ships.

Spacepods fire in three directions simultaneously: left and right at about a 45 degree angle in each direction and straight up. However, if the fire button is depressed rapidly, the shots alternate by firing in one direction at a time, rather than three directions simultaneously.

With every other screen, players face a wave of rings that start small, split off into other rings when shot, and gradually grow; if one ends up growing to full size then it will suck the player’s Spacespod in, which that ship will be lost.
Megatouch 5
Megatouch 5 is a one or two player multi game published and developed by Merit Industries in 1997.
Megatouch 5: Tournament Edition

The Megatouch 5: Tournament Edition is a classic coin-operated bartop touchscreen arcade machine released in 1998 by Merit Industries. Building on the massive success of the early Megatouch line, this specific edition introduced dedicated local tournament features, allowing bars and venues to run competitive brackets. The machine is highly sought after by retro collectors for its iconic CRT display monitor, nostalgic early-digital aesthetic, and massive library of quick-play casual games.
MegaTouch Gold
A touch screen multi-arcade game with 48 casino games.
MegaTouch XL 6000
A touch screen multi-arcade game with 36 casino games.
Megumi Rescue

Megumi Rescue (め組レスキュー) is an unreleased Sega System E arcade breakout game developed by EXA Planning and manufactured by Sega. While it failed its location test and went unreleased, it would eventually be ported to the Sega Master System in July 1988 as Megumi Rescue, courtesy of developer Whiteboard.

Megumi Rescue lets you control a rescue party of three to save people from a burning building. The group consists of two people holding a jumping sheet, and a third fire fighter bouncing on the sheet to reach the building's inhabitants at the windows.

The sheet can be moved left and right, and the jumper can enter a square with an open/smashed window for a few seconds. If there is a fire behind the window, it will be put out. If the room is empty, it will be searched, and to certain chance, an item will be dropped. If there are inhabitants in the room, the jumper will take one person with him, which will be rescued on reaching the sheet.
Mello Yello Q*bert

Mello Yello Q*Bert is a rare variant of the arcade version of Q*Bert released in 1982. Only ever given away in a sweepstakes, it is one of the rarest arcade games of all time.

The game plays almost identical to the original Q*Bert, but with intermissions added after a few levels (similar to Pac-Man). These show Q*Bert drinking a giant can of Mello Yello while slurping sound effects play. The title screen is also changed.

When the sweepstakes had been released, Gotlieb released a competition along with it, named "Q*Bert's Snout-Out." If you finished the game 10 times, and sent a picture of the animation of Q*Bert drinking the Mello Yello can, you would get 5 cases of Mello Yello.
Melty Blood: Act Cadenza

Melty Blood follows one year after Tsukihime and some days after of Kagetsu Tohya. In the beginning of August 2001, Shiki Tohno hears of a new series of murders in Misaki Town, similar to the ones that took place Tsukihime, in the last weeks of October 1999. Whilst searching for the murderer he meets Sion Eltnam Atlasia who initiates a fight with him, attempting to capture him. After the fight she reveals that her reason for trying to capture him is to get in contact with the "True Ancestor" (referring to Arcueid) so that she may acquire information on the "cure for vampirism". Shiki then decides to help her with this task.
Melty Blood: Act Cadenza Version B

Melty Blood: Act Cadenza Ver. B is an arcade port of Melty Blood: Act Cadenza with various changes and upgrades, the most notable of which is the inclusion of White Len as a playable character, with a significantly weakened moveset. It also introduced a fifth button that served as a contextual action depending on the situation and the direction held on the joystick when pressed, such as dodging or throwing. This version can be identified by a dual silhouette of Len and White Len in the logo and the phrase "Through the Looking-Glass, Northern Light transparently".
Melty Blood: Actress Again

Melty Blood: Actress Again, is the third game in the Melty Blood fighting game series. It was released in the 4Q 2008 on Sega Naomi hardware. Compared to Act Cadenza, the game features three entirely new playable characters, as well as several new alternate versions of existing characters in the PS2 version. All characters now feature selection between three different fighting styles, known as Full Moon Style, Crescent Moon Style (most similar to Act Cadenza) and Half Moon Style, which changes not only the way in which life and Magic Circuit meters function, but also each characters' basic and special attacks.
Melty Blood: Actress Again: Current Code

Melty Blood: Actress Again: Current Code is a 2D fighter that was ported from the PlayStation 2 to the arcade. The game underwent location testing in Akihabara, Japan from December 19–20, 2009 and hit arcades on July 29, 2010. It runs on Sega's RingWide board, the successor to the NAOMI boards that Act Cadenza and the original Actress Again were developed on.

An upgrade for Current Code was launched on May 18, 2011, branded as Ver. 1.05, and added two new characters and made some changes to the gameplay. A final update came out on October 14, 2011 as Ver. 1.07b for the Sega RingEdge 2.
Men in Black

Men in Black is Sega Amusements International’s explosive new skill-based video redemption game. Presented in a stunning, new, retro-futuristic cabinet that takes design cues from the iconic MIB headquarters. The cabinet features an amazing chrome UFO billboard lit with animated LEDs and an “infinity mirror” . The dual Tri-Barrel Plasma Guns are straight out of the movies and is sure to attract players of all ages.

The gameplay is both fun and exciting, as players take on the roles of Agent N and Agent V to take down aliens to win tickets. They must collect powerful weapons to stay alive and defeat the final boss. Scoring over 1,000 points awards players the big ticket “Super Bonus”.

Men in Black features iconic aliens, weapons and locations from the Men in Black franchise. Multiple locations and scenarios are designed to keep players coming back for more.
Mental Money Monsters

"Mental Money Monsters" is a classic UK fruit machine (slot machine) manufactured by Mazooma Games, rather than a traditional arcade cabinet style video game. Originally released in the early 2000s, it runs on the Bell-Fruit Scorpion 4 (and later Scorpion 5) hardware system and is highly regarded by enthusiasts as a clone of the popular "Road to Riches" style gameplay format.
Mercs

The players are members of a covert counter-terrorist team of mercenaries known as the "Wolf Force". The aim of the game was to rescue the former President from rebels in the fictional African country of Zutula, which bears resemblance to the apartheid regime in South Africa. The game has six main levels, plus the final level, where your mission is to rescue the former U.S. president from the Hercules Transport. The game's arsenal include real-world machine guns, shot guns, flamethrowers, and grenade launchers. Several missions even have pilotable vehicles available.
Merlin's Money Maze

"Merlin's Money Maze" is an arcade game developed and published by Zilec-Zenitone in February 1986. It is an action maze game where the player navigates through a maze. RetroAchievements.org says the game was released in February 1986, and VideoGameGeek.com says Zilec-Zenitone was a video game company known for producing arcade games in the early to mid 1980s.
Mermaid

Mermaid was produced by Sanritsu Denki and published by Esco Tading in Japan and Rock-Ola Mfg. Corp. in North America in 1982.

Navigate your sailboat across the ocean while avoiding a wide variety of obstacles.

Nosing your tiny one-master out of the harbor, you are instantly in a race for the next berth. Along the way, you must change headings and tack, hook up with fast breezes and currents that will help your race time. Avoid land masses, choppy seas and overly-friendly dolphins that can capsize your sailboat and turn it into shark bait.
Meta Fox

Meta Fox was produced by Seta in 1989.

Meta Fox is an arcade, vertical scrolling shoot'em up. The player controls a blue plane and shoots enemies - tanks, other planes, artillery trucks, boats, helicopters, etc. He has a cannon with unlimited ammo, and several bombs. He can upgrade weapons (find the power-up "P" to do it) and additional bombs. The field The game also has multiplayer - the second player controls a red plane.

Romstar published the game in North America.
Metabee Shot

●The first in the kids medal industry! Skill-oriented authentic turn battle shooting! (3 attacks and 3 defenses per play).
●20 different enemy characters to choose from! (Attack variations for each character).

1. Insert medals into the medal slot. Up to three medals can be inserted (the number of medals paid out depends on the number of medals). Select your opponent with the button. The game starts automatically when you choose an opponent. The game style is a turn battle shooting method of attack and defense.
2. The game starts in player Attack Mode. When the player's aim is right on the screen, press the button to fire the missile.
3. In Defense Mode, enemies attack in a character-specific manner. Follow the on-screen instructions to avoid enemy attacks at the right time.
Metal Black

Metal Black is an arcade 2D side-scrolling shoot'em up, made as continuation of Gun Frontier and the Darius series.

In typical shooting game manner, Metal Black uses a two button setup, with one being used for standard shots, and the onther one for beam attacks. Both attacks can be powered up by collecting Newalone, which floats around freely in stages. The beam weapon becomes a screen covering burst attack when the maximum amount of Newalone has been collected. The Burst can be refocused to a beam by holding down the beam button.
Metal Clash

Metal Clash was produced by Data East in 1985

Metal Clash is a very non-typical 2D fighting game set in a futuristic universe. The player controls a giant flying robot (some kind of mecha) and must destroy alien robots. At the beginning of the game, small robots have to be destroyed that die from a single hit. After the destruction of the right amount of small enemies on the battlefield, a greater enemy appears - and the player duels with him. This enemy usually has some firearms.
Metal Freezer

Seibu Metal Freezer Arcade Circuit Board, Works, 1989 Original Seibu Metal Freezer Arcade game circuit board in good working condition. This is an extremely rare game board, we have been told by the seller it was a prototype game, never released. The seller picked it up back in the late 80s during a trip to Japan (he worked with Seibu at the time). We've heard from another collector that it did have a very limited release in Japan only.
Metal Gear Arcade

Metal Gear Arcade is a game developed by Kojima Productions and published by Konami. The game was announced at Konami's E3 2009 conference, where it was revealed that the game would be a reworked, networked, coin-op iteration of Metal Gear Online. It has a special interface that utilizes 3D goggles and tickets to unlock jewelry and other weapons. It was released in Japan on December 20, 2010. It was removed from many arcades due to a lack of popularity, although the arcade service itself did not end until December 1, 2016.
Metal Hawk

The player must take control of a helicopter (which is the eponymous "Metal Hawk"), and fight various enemies based on the land, in the air, and in the sea, in order to score a certain number of points for each area within a set time limit; the game employs a perspective similar to that of Namco's own Assault (which also runs upon their System 2 hardware), in which Metal Hawk stays in the center of the screen, while the play-field rotates around it. At the start of each area, Metal Hawk will fly up to its highest altitude of 400 metres - however, instead of rising up from the ground, the play-field seems to come down away from it, and when an area gets cleared, Metal Hawk will again fly up to its highest altitude and off the top of the screen. These methods of entering and leaving again reinforce the playercentric approach of the game, which also features voice samples (in Japanese).
Metal Maniax

Drive an assortment of vehicles around an arena and smash-up your opponents. The more hits made on opponents, the more points are rewarded.

Metal Maniax was a prototype driving game produced by Atari Games in 1994.
Metal Saver

Metal Saver is an arcade 2D platform game, similar to Snow Brothers, or Bubble Bobble. The player can choose from two characters - martial artist Hanbit, or girl with guns, Narae. Their task? the player must kill all the enemies on the level, and collect bonuses. Every few stages awaits a boss (like a huge spider). Game has co-op mode.
Metal Slug 2

Two years have passed since the end of Metal Slug, when Capt. Marco Rossi and Lt. Tarma Roving of Peregrine Falcon Strike Force defeated and killed the evil General Morden, who had staged a coup d'état against the worlds' governments. Various factions sympathetic to Morden have been in operation, but are considered insignificant. They have begun to act in unison, and army intelligence concludes that the only way this could happen is if Morden is still alive and is attempting a new coup. Rossi (now a Major) and Roving (now a Captain) are sent to once again battle Morden. They are accompanied by two members of the Intelligence Agency's Special Ops Squad S.P.A.R.R.O.W.S.; Sgt. Eri Kasamoto and Sgt. 1st Class Fiolina Germi.

Metal Slug 2 is similar to the previous game; the player must shoot constantly at a continual stream of enemies in order to reach the end of each level. At this point, the player confronts a boss, who is usually considerably larger and tougher than regular enemies.
Metal Slug 3

The rebellion orchestrated by General Morden to bring about a new global regime is now ancient history, and order and peace has begun to return to the world. Morden, brought back into power, was attempting another coup d'état, but government forces got wind of the plot beforehand and pre-empted the impending assault.

The gameplay mechanics of Metal Slug 3 are the same as in previous Metal Slug games; the player must shoot constantly at a continual stream of enemies in order to reach the end of each level. At this point, the player confronts a boss, who is usually considerably larger and tougher than regular enemies. On the way through each level, the player can find numerous weapon upgrades and "Metal Slug" tanks. The tank is known as the SV-001 ("SV" stands for Super Vehicle), which increases the player's offense and considerably adds to their defense.
Metal Slug 4

An organization called "Amadeus" wants to take over all the military computers in the world using a new virus they have created. It's your mission to destroy them before they accomplish their evil ambition.

The 5th episode (including Metal Slug X) of the most famous arcade-shooting-series comes bringing the unaltered classic gameplay, a new arm (Dual Machine Gun), 6 new vehicles (Motorcycle, Truck, Bradley Tank, Metal Crow Tank, Four Legged Walkmachine and Forklift Truck) as well as 2 new soldiers for the pantheon (Nadia Cassel and Trevor Spacey). The most notable introduction to the series is the Metalish System, giving to the player a new possibility to score more points: after pick up certain shield-shape emblems, a timer bar will be displayed at the top of the screen.
Metal Slug 4 Plus

This unlicensed bootleg of Metal Slug 4 was released in arcades sometime between July 2002 and November 2003. It adds some new features, like being able to swap weapons by pressing "D", obtaining a Thunder Cloud on every new life, as well as adds the ability to change, on the fly, the character status (normal, big, mummy, monkey) by pressing the Start button.
Metal Slug 5

A special disc that contains deep and intricate secrets about the Metal Slug project is stolen by a mysterious group called the Ptolemaic Army, whose specialty lies from within archaeological excavation and espionage. Marco and Tarma of the Peregrine Falcon Strike Force follow in hot pursuit against the group and in the process are joined by Eri and Fio of SPARROWS. Together once more, the quartet investigate the shrouded objective of the Ptolemaic Army.

Metal Slug 5 is a 2D side-scrolling action shooter in which players can choose from four playable characters: Marco, Tarma, Eri, or Fio, each tasked with completing five missions while battling numerous enemies.
Metal Slug 5 Plus

This unlicensed bootleg of Metal Slug 5 was released in arcades sometime between November 2003 and November 2004. It adds some new features, like a flame shot weapon missing from Metal Slug 5, as well as the ability to swap weapons by pressing "D" or changing the character status to big by pressing the Start button.
Metal Slug 5: Extend
Metal Slug 5 Extend is a romhack of Metal Slug 5.
Metal Slug 6

Metal Slug 6 stays close to the fast-paced 2D side-scrolling shooting gameplay of the original Metal Slug, but with a few enhancements. The storyline is reminiscent of Metal Slug 2, X, and 3, as it focuses on the Rebel-Martian alliance where the team, with the help of the Rebels, had to fight the Martians. In this version however, all sides team up to combat a threat together. The four original heroes, Marco, Tarma, Fio and Eri, are joined by Ralf and Clark, of King of Fighters and Ikari Warriors fame, each with different attributes and a special ability. The characters also vary by running speed, the defense abilities when driving vehicles, and the amount of ammo received.

The characters can now carry two power-ups at the same time, and choose to discard one, or give it to another player in the Co-op mode. Next to new drivable vehicles, there is also a new weapon, the Zantetsu Sword, a blade that neutralizes enemy firepower.
Metal Slug X

Metal Slug X is an enhanced version of Metal Slug 2: Super Vehicle-001/II. The main differences to the original release include:
 - Additional weapons: Stones, Iron Lizard, Enemy Chaser, Super Grenade, and Drop Shot.
 - Additional power-ups, items, and prisoners in most of the levels.
 - Additional times of the day: stages can take place at twilight, sunset, or dusk.
 - Some of the locations and vehicles in the game have been altered.
 - Increased enemy count. Some of the enemies' placement has been changed.
 - Many weapons have a stronger explosive force. Explosions yield more unexpected results.
Metal Slug: Super Vehicle-001

Metal Slug is a run and gun game reminiscent of Contra where players assume the role of captain Marco Rossi and lieutenant Tarma Roving of the Peregrine Falcon Strike Force, shooting constantly at a continual stream of enemies in order to complete each mission. At this point, players confront a boss, who is usually considerably larger and tougher than regular enemies. On the way through each level, players can find numerous weapon upgrades and the eponymous tanks. Known as the SV-001 and SV-002, the tanks increase the player's offense and add considerably to their defense.

In addition to shooting, players can perform melee attacks by using a knife. The player does not die by coming into contact with enemies, and correspondingly, many of the enemy troops have melee attacks. Much of the game's scenery is destructible, and occasionally, this reveals extra items or power-ups.
Metal Soldier Isaac

Metal Soldier Isaac II was released in February 1985 in Japan.

A cool vertical space shooter from Taito.
 It does NOT have a predecessor. The original prototype of this game was simply Metal Soldier Isaac and was called Metal Soldier Isaac II for its formal arcade release.

The music for the attract mode was remixed, then reused for the first stage of "Darius".
Metamoqester

Metamoqester is a 2D arcade fighting game, similar in concept to Red Earth or Monster Maulers. One or two players (there is a co-op mode) fight against big monsters in deadly duels. There are three different characters to choose from. The game uses four buttons - Weak Attack, Medium Attack, Strong Attack, and Shoot/Throw Weapon.
Metamorphic Force

Metamorphic Force is a 2D beat'em up game with 2.5D gameplay (like a Final Fight or Streets of Rage. An ancient evil has arisen from the past - The Evil King has risen from the dead to rule the world once more. Now the four shapeshifters known as the Metamorphic Force have been summoned by the Goddess to stop him.

Gameplay is generic: players go right, fight against various enemies, collect bonuses and duel bosses. The game has a unique system of transformation: the hero, after collecting the appropriate bonus, changes into a strong beast.
Meteor

Meteor is arcade space shooter by Hoei in 1980.

This is a clone of Atari's popular rock-blasting space game.
The game play is a bootleg version of Asteroids.
Meteoroids

Meteoroids is a rare, wide-release upright arcade video game released in 1981 by the American company Venture Line. It is a multi-directional shooter heavily based on Atari's legendary title, Asteroids. The game is historically significant because of its direct ties to a landmark legal battle that helped shape video game copyright laws.
Meteors
An Asteroids variant/clone from Amusement World.
Metro-Cross

Metro-Cross is a platform game released in arcades by Namco in 1985. It was later ported to the Amstrad CPC, Atari ST, Commodore 64, Family Computer, and ZX Spectrum.

Metro-Cross runs on Namco Pac-Land hardware, but with a video system modified to support a 2048-color palette like that used in Dragon Buster. It uses a Motorola M6809 microprocessor, with a Hitachi HD63701 sub-microprocessor (both running at 1.536 MHz) and Namco 8-channel waveform PSG for audio.

The player must take control of a man known only as Runner, who is given a time limit to run through each of the game's thirty-two rounds while avoiding obstacles and collecting drink cans. The actual running happens automatically: the job of the player is to avoid the obstacles and collect the cans by moving the Runner with the stick and adjusting his speed accordingly.

If the Runner finishes the round within the time limit, the remaining time will be awarded to him as bonus points, and he will proceed to the next round.
Metroid

Metroid is a platform shoot em up by Nintendo that was released on their Playchoice 10 machine in 1987.

You play as Samus Aran, a space-traveling bounty hunter who has been assigned by the Galactic Federation to investigate a band of Space Pirates on the planet Zebes. The Space Pirates invaded a deep-space research ship and stole an unknown, yet destructive life-form that can absorb life energy and rapidly multiply. The life-form is codenamed 'Metroid'.

As Samus you must infiltrate the planet and destroy the Mother Brain controlling the pirates before the Metroid can be used as a weapon. Along the way, Samus can acquire weapons to help her through the cavernous maze, and to defeat all hostile creatures (both pirates, and indigenous) along the way. Much of the game is based on discovery - such as secret passageways, and retracting your path to find areas using new abilities.
Miami Dice

The Miami Dice fruit machine is a highly popular, classic UK pub fruit machine manufactured by BWB. Released in the mid-2000s, it is well-known among coin-op enthusiasts for its distinct Miami Vice-inspired neon aesthetic, interactive video feature screen, and iconic "marked card" or "marked corner" mechanics used to navigate board gambles.
Michael Jackson's Moonwalker

Michael Jackson's Moonwalker is an arcade game based loosely on the 1988 movie. You and two other friends play as Michael Jackson dressed as his 'Smooth Criminal' alter ego whose mission it is to rescue all the children kidnapped by the evil Mr. Big. You have to blast all the various baddies that come at you in various waves while searching for the kidnapped children scattered around the various levels. Sometimes a rescued child will give you health which is represented as a health bar which deteriorates if you are touched or shot by the baddies.

To help you on your quest you have a limited supply of smart-bombs which sees MJ start dancing with the baddies before they all die when activated. Also on each level you can see Bubbles the Chimp and if touched you turn into a robot who can now fire lasers.
Michael Jackson's Moonwalker (Mega-Tech)

Michael Jackson's Moonwalker is based on the Michael Jackson movie. Mr. Big has kidnapped children and has nasty things in store for them, like drugging them and making them slaves. So it's up to Michael to use his magical powers and dancing talent to try to catch Mr. Big and rescue his little friends.

Michael Jackson can jump, throw magical stars, and dance to counter his opponents as he looks for the hidden children. Stages come in various shapes and sizes from some of Jackson's hit videos which take place in streets and graveyards.
Micom Mahjong
This game was only sold in Japan in 1982 and was distributed by Japan Mail Service which you had to buy by mail order.
Micon-Kit Part II

Second release in the Micon Kit series of action video games, developed by Shin Nihon Kikaku around 1978. These games are clones of Breakout, created by Atari. They were the first video games produced by SNK (Shin Nihon Kikaku). 

The player controls a paddle at the bottom of the screen and must bounce a ball to hit bricks at the top of the screen to destroy them and earn points. The player has limited lives which are lost when the ball hits the floor. The high score is shown at the bottom of the screen. New in this game is the addition of a depiction of Space Battleship Yamato from the anime of the same name as an added obstacle for the ball.
Microman Battle Charge
Microman Battle Charge (ミクロマン バトルチャージ) is a Sega STV medal game based on the Microman toyline.
Midnight Landing

Midnight Landing is the first game in Taito's arcade flight simulation series. It tasks players with safely landing a commercial jet liner making a night flight into a major city. The game begins with the plane already aloft and ready to begin its descent. Since the game takes place at night the player can't make out any scenery by eye, and has only the lights on the runway and the airplane's instruments to guide them. Despite being an arcade game, the pace is slow and deliberate; a single safe landing takes several minutes. The player controls the plane using two primary inputs: an airliner-style yoke, and a throttle for controlling speed. In addition to these physical controls, an on-screen control panel displays information about the craft's current position and speed.

The unique, deluxe cabinet recreates the interior of an airliner cockpit, including the game's primary controls - the yoke and throttle.
Midnight Resistance

The Midnight Resistance fighters are up against the awesome powers of mad scientist King Crimson and his Crimson Corps. Crimson has kidnapped your scientist grandfather and five more of your relatives, and aims to put his advanced plans to evil use.

Take control of a Resistance fighter in this scrolling shoot 'em up consisting of nine platform-based levels, each ending with a Boss to defeat. Your enemies appear on foot and in vehicles, and Crimson has also planted machine gun bays en route.

Dead enemies release keys, which can be traded in at shop points for weapons. These weapons include machine guns and flamethrowers, for which ammunition must be bought - weapons are discarded when you have no suitable ammo. The control system is unusual - you can shoot in different directions and crawl along low ledges.
Midnight Run: Road Fighter 2

Midnight Run: Road Fighter 2 is the sequel to Road Fighter, released in arcades in March 1996, and on the PlayStation in 1997. While the arcade version was released worldwide, the PlayStation version was only released in Japan and Europe. In Europe, the PlayStation version is just titled Midnight Run, removing the Road Fighter connection. Its main selling point was that it allows the player to shift back and forth between manual and automatic transmission during races. Although different from the 2-D Road Fighter, the scenery is similar to other racing games set in Japan such as Initial D Arcade Stage and Wangan Midnight, except the cars are not licensed. The player also has a unique selection of normal cars and tuned cars.
Midway's Flying Saucer

Midway's Flying Saucer is a rare, vintage electromechanical (EM) amusement arcade machine released by Midway Manufacturing Co. in September 1967. Featuring an upright cabinet style, it is an iconic rifle-style mechanical shooting gallery game where players aim at moving alien targets. The machine is highly sought after by collectors, with only a few surviving original dedicated cabinets known to exist today.
Midway`s Sportsman

The Sportsman arcade machine is a classic electro-mechanical (EM) rifle shooting gallery game produced by Midway Manufacturing Co. in 1970. Unlike the later electronic video games of the late 70s and 80s, this vintage machine relies entirely on physical components, motors, and blacklight illumination to create its gameplay experience.

Players aim a large, cabinet-mounted realistic rifle or pistol assembly at the mechanical targets to rack up points.

Midway was highly regarded for this era of electro-mechanical gallery games, releasing similar classic units around the same period like Sea Raider (1969), S.A.M.I. (1970), and Wild Kingdom (1971). Collectors today value the Sportsman for its complex internal gear-and-switch mechanics and its iconic early 1970s arcade aesthetic.
Mighty Guy

Mighty Guy is a vertical fighting game from Nichibutsu. in 1986

Mighty Guy doesn't need a gun to fend off large amounts of soldiers! This is what "Ikari Warriors" would be if they left their machine guns at home.
Mighty Monkey

Mighty Monkey was produced by Yih Lung in 1982.

By pressing the transform button, Monkey can transform into what looks like a Dragon's head. This has no firing capability, but it can eat the fireballs that some enemies fire at you.
Mighty Moto

Mighty Moto is a ticket redemption, motorcycle racing arcade game for kids from UNIS. The game is designed with a smaller footprint and a smaller mounted bike to be more suitable to kids. Play on your own, or link up for competitive play, this game is fun and entertaining for kids of all ages.

Players choose from three unique tracks to race on, avoiding obstacles and using power ups to get to the finish line. With a 32" HD LCD monitor and bright LED lights and character and motorcycle selection, this game is a family friendly smash hit.
Mighty Warriors

Mighty Warriors was produced by Electronic Devices in 1990.

A competitive one-on-one fighting game with characters who can occasionally mutate for a limited period of time.
Mighty! Pang

Mighty! Pang is a video game of action developed and published by Mitchell in 2000 on CP System II . This is the 4th installment of the series.

Only released in Japan, this last part of the series picks up elements of the previous opus without really innovating. The boy with the cap is back, there are no more choices of characters like in Pang! 3 . On the other hand, many elements of Pang! 3 are taken, for example, the dragging ice ground, dogs biting, "bubble-bombs" or blocks destroying themselves in a chain.

The game principle remains identical to Pang. The player directs a character who can move right or left (and climb the ladders in certain levels), and pull a grapple upwards. The balls are bouncing and when the player shoots one of them, it divides into two balls, which themselves divide... The more the balls are divided (and therefore smaller) and the less they bounce high: the player will have to adapt to the timings corresponding to the various sizes of balls on the screen.
Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!!

Mike Tyson's Punch-Out is one of the most popular and biggest selling video games of all time. Step into the ring as Little Mac, a 17-year-old fighter from the Bronx, ranked number three in the minor circuit. Your goal is to work your way up through the rankings so that you can challenge Mike Tyson, Kid Dynamite, in a dream fight.

But the road to the championship is long and hard. You'll have to work your way up through the minor, major, and world circuits by winning 14 bouts against some very tough opponents.

The rules of the World Video Boxing Association govern your bouts. Each match is three three-minute rounds long. Any boxer knocked down for a 10 count is Knocked Out (KO). If a boxer goes down three times, he'll find himself a Technical Knock Out (TKO). If both boxers make it to the end of the third round, the ref determines the winner.

Once you're in the ring you'll have to beat your opponent with smart fighting.
Mikie

Mikie is an arcade game The object is to guide a student named Mikie around the school locations to collect hearts which make up a letter from his girlfriend while being chased by members of the school staff. In Japan, the game's setting was changed to an office in order to avoid controversy, while the original version of the game was released internationally.

There are several classrooms to explore like the Quantum Physics Room, Locker Room, Canteen, the Aerobics Dancing Class, and the Playground. In each classroom, Mikie has to collect all the hearts that are found in each classroom to form a message. In order to collect these hearts, Mikie must stand somewhere near them and shout out. There are two type of hearts: small and large. Mikie needs to shout out only once to collect the small hearts, and multiple times to collect the large ones. When a message is formed, Mikie can exit the classroom through a door marked OUT.
MilkChan

MilkChan is a game where you use punches to propel yourself through stages. The protagonist, Milk-chan, spends her days delivering milk to people, and the ultimate goal of the game is to deliver milk to the king at the highest floor of the castle.

The gameplay is based around a simple control system of movement combined with a single punch button. Stages are particularly vertical in nature, so players must utilize Milk-chan’s arm punch to ascend to higher platforms. She can punch the ground to launch herself into the air and can also punch walls to jump diagonally. The game is highly difficult as there are a variety of gimmicks and traps in each stage, and a number of skillful maneuvers are necessary to advance.
Mille Miglia 2: Great 1000 Miles Rally

Mille Miglia 2: Great 1000 Miles Rally was produced by Kaneko in 1995.

A driving game with top-down pseudo 3-D graphics. You can select one of ten cars and depending upon which vehicle has been chosen, you can select the starting point of the race. The game can be installed in a variety of cabinets using either a joystick and buttons or a steering wheel and foot pedals for control. This is a follow on to the original Rally series.

You have 60 seconds to get from the starting line to the finish line. Finishing within 60 seconds allows you to go on to the next race. If you lose, a continue option is available.
The screen scrolls fast. The only way you know about a turn coming up is by a little indicator that flashes with a picture of the turn. There are zig-zags, hairpins and all other cool turns, most of which you have to steer into in order to make it though. The play control using a joystick is a little awkward at first, but it becomes comfortable after a while.
Millipede

Millipede is a fixed-screen shooter and the sequel to Centipede. The player controls an archer within the lower portion of a mushroom-filled garden, moving freely in all directions while firing upward. The objective is to survive for as long as possible and earn points by destroying millipedes and the other insects that invade the playfield.

A millipede enters at the top of the screen and moves horizontally until it encounters a mushroom, obstacle, or edge of the garden, causing it to descend and reverse direction. Shooting a body segment turns it into a mushroom and may divide the creature into independently moving sections. If a millipede reaches the player’s area, additional heads enter from the sides until every remaining segment has been destroyed.
Millipede Dux
A hacked version of the original Centipede board that added a bit more spice to the game.
Minasan no Okagesamadesu! Dai Sugoroku Taikai

This comedy-themed mahjong game also features board game elements. In between mahjong matches, the player rolls dice and moves along a board game track; landing on different squares provides special effects, and decides which opponents the player will face.
Mine Sweeper

Minesweeper is Amutech's version of Gremlin Industries's Blockade released in 1977; the legitimacy of its release is unknown.

This game was two player only, you must have a real live person to play against, or else the other players boat will head directly for the bottom wall, which doesn't make for a very interesting game. Each player moves their little boat around leaving a solid line of mines behind them. All moves are made on an invisible grid, so you can only turn at 90 degree angles. To win you must last longer than your opponent before hitting something (first person to hit something loses). One good strategy is to try and box your opponent in to a small section of the screen, and then just move carefully until they crash. Pushing backwards on the stick will cause you to crash into your own mines, so avoid that at all cost.
Mine, Mine, Mine

Mine Mine Mine from Aristocrat, a 25-line 10x max bet slot machine with a mining theme.

Along with the traditional A, K, Q, J 10 and 9 the game’s symbols include giant gold nuggets, a bucket of gold nuggets, a scale weighing nuggets and a jolly bearded miner juggling emeralds and rubies.

The game features two different bonuses. When three or more dynamite symbols appear anywhere on the screen the bonus feature is triggered. You get to choose either the "Free Game" bonus or the "Mine Car" bonus.

The Free Game bonus awards you with three to 10 free spins with up to three of the symbols wild.

The Mine Car bonus takes you to a mine, with the track forming a pyramid with a mine car perched at the top. The mine car is loaded with gold nuggets and colored gems (three gems for each line played). The car tips and the gold nuggets and gems fall down the tracks into a row of buckets at the bottom of the shaft.

Each bucket is labelled with a credit amount.
Minecraft Dungeons Arcade

Minecraft Dungeons Arcade is a fantasy top-down hack-and-slash game developed by Play Mechanix (in conjunction with Mojang) and released by Raw Thrills for arcades on May 2021.

Based on the 2020 action-RPG Minecraft Dungeons (itself based on the sandbox survival game Minecraft), Minecraft Dungeons Arcade changes the game to a simple hack-and-slash (similar to the Gauntlet series) and puts up to four players as adventurers against waves of enemies in nine stages from the original game.

Similar to the manufacturer's earlier arcade adaptation of the mobile Injustice: Gods Among Us game, Minecraft Dungeons Arcade features a collectible card system that allows players to earn cards (by playing a credit) for use in-game using the cabinet's dedicated card scanners. There are five card types: two for the player's appearance (Armor and Skin) and one for each of the three power-ups (Melee, Range, and Pet). Players can scan different cards at any time to change their appearance and power-ups.
Minefield

Minefield was produced by Stern Electronics in 1983.

Go for as long as you can destroying assorted enemy ground and air vehicles. Avoid hitting a mine while picking up missiles from the ground. Missile attack ground installations for extra points.
Ming Xing 100

Ming Xing 100 (also known as Star 100) is a vintage Chinese arcade gambling and slot machine game.

The game operates on the Seta ST0016 processor, an all-in-one chip that integrates a Z80 processing unit, graphics, and sound. Due to its preservation by retro communities, it is fully emulated and playable using the MAME (Multiple Arcade Machine Emulator) platform.
Mini Golf

Mini Golf was produced by Bally Sente in 1985.

A cute putt-putt golf game with 18 holes featuring loops, a waterfall, and some simple animations.
Mini Vaders

Mini Vaders (also known as Minivader) is a fixed shooter arcade game that was released by Taito Corporation in 1990; it is based on the four (five, if you count Space Invaders II) games that make up their Space Invaders series, but is not officially part of it. It utilizes a single Zilog Z80 microprocessor (running at 4 MHz), only features monochromatic graphics, and does not have a scoring system or any sound chips - and the reason is because it was only created as a test board on account of a Japanese law stating it was illegal to sell an arcade cabinet without a game in it. The invaders also will not fire off any bullets, which means the only way to lose is if they reach the bottom of the screen; UFOs will also appear over the formations (and, if you shoot them, they will turn into the word "Bomb", but given that this game does not have a scoring system, it has no effect).
Mini Vegas 4in1

The Mini Vegas 4in1 is a rare, classic upright arcade cabinet released in 1983 by Entertainment Enterprises. Rather than hosting traditional video game action, this specific machine is a dedicated gambling/casino simulator that bundles four different games into a single unit.
Mini-Boy 7

Mini-Boy 7 is a vintage 1983 arcade multi-game cabinet developed and produced by Bonanza Enterprises, Ltd.. Unlike the small handheld plastic toy consoles that flood the modern market, the original Mini-Boy 7 is a classic, software-emulated piece of retro amusement history centered entirely around casino and gambling mechanics.
Minky Monkey

Minky Monkey was produced by Technos in 1982.

You control a red boy who must bring fruits to the blank square in order to complete the message.

Minky Monkey is a platforming arcade game Thematically and visually similar to Donkey Kong Junior.
Minna Atsumare! Dodge Hero

Minna Atsumare! Dodge Hero is a dodgeball-themed medal arcade game. A medal game is an arcade cabinet that awards physical medals (tokens) from the machine when players reach score thresholds; those medals are collectable and can be redeemed according to the operator’s rules. In Minna Atsumare! Dodge Hero the player selects a character and proceeds through a sequence of dodgeball rounds and short mini-events; successful completion of rounds increases the player’s score and advances play toward medal payout thresholds.

The player aims and throws balls at opposing targets while avoiding incoming throws. Rounds present varying layouts and timing patterns; hits and round completion award points. Points accumulate toward the cabinet’s configured medal/payout thresholds. Controls are limited to aiming and throwing inputs appropriate to single-player medal-machine operation; UI and round structure are visible in preserved attract and gameplay captures.
Minna Ganbare! Dash Hero

Minna Ganbare! Dash Hero is a Japanese arcade machine released in 2000 by the manufacturer Sigma Enterprises, Inc.

It is classified as a "Medal game" (video gambling/horse racing category) rather than a traditional standard racing game.
Mirage Youjuu Mahjongden

Mirage Youjuu Mahjongden (also translated as Demon Mirage Mahjong) is a mature-themed, arcade-only Japanese mahjong game released in May 1994 by the Mitchell Corporation.

Like many arcade mahjong titles of the mid-1990s, Mirage Youjuu Mahjongden is a single-player game targeted specifically at adult audiences (Mature 18+ rating). It features standard Japanese Riichi Mahjong mechanics wrapped in a dark fantasy or supernatural aesthetic, as indicated by the "Youjuu" (monster/demon) framing in its title.
Mirai Ninja

Mirai Ninja (未来忍者, lit. "Future Ninja"), is a side scrolling beat 'em up arcade video game, released by Namco in 1988 exclusively in Japan. Mirai Ninja was adapted into the Japanese live-action film of the same name, which was also produced by Namco. The game runs on Namco System 2 hardware, and is the first Namco game to be adapted into a film.

You are a ninja fighting various enemies and bosses in this side scrolling beat-em up.
Mirax

Mirax is a shooter in which the player pilots a lone craft over a pseudo-3D landscape to repel invading forces and destroy a large enemy installation known as Mirax City. 

Players control a ship that advances over a forward-scaling playfield; enemies appear as airborne and ground targets that must be shot or avoided. Destroying ground targets can trigger satellite or flagship encounters; defeating certain waves or flagships temporarily increases the player’s firepower. Levels progress until a major enemy installation or boss (Mirax City) is reached and must be destroyed to advance. The game uses sprite scaling to simulate depth and speed, and stages increase in enemy density and projectile complexity as play continues.
Miss Bingo

Miss Bingo is a tile-matching puzzle game and a variant of Min’s earlier game Miss Puzzle, featuring updated graphics and an added two-player split-screen mode. 

The player arranges tiles to create horizontal, vertical, or diagonal chains of three or more matching symbols, which clears them from the play field. Each stage requires clearing a set number of chains before the tiles reach the top of the screen.
Miss Bubble II

Miss Bubble II is a game set across 100 levels, featuring backgrounds with digitized images of Asian women in revealing clothing, changing every three levels. The game involves navigating various platforms and confronting different enemies, similar to the original Bubble Bobble game.

Players control mice who must trap enemies in bubbles. Once trapped, the enemies can be defeated by touching the bubbles. Defeated enemies drop items that can be collected for points. Bubbles serve as temporary platforms and can spell out words for bonus points. Additionally, water bubbles create flows that can defeat enemies. A single collision with an enemy results in the loss of a life, and enemies that are not quickly defeated turn red and become faster.
Miss Mister World '96
A poorly done conversion (possible hack) of "Miss World '96" Nude including some adult male images.
Miss Puzzle (Clone of Gumbo)

Miss Puzzle is a clone of "Gumbo" with all of the nude images removed from the game. Columns of three blocks fall from the sky and the player can move the block left or right and shift the order of the blocks column falls. The objective is to match three or more blocks of the same type in vertical, horizontal, or diagonal rows in order to clear them from the play area. As the player clears more blocks the columns begin to descend at a more rapid rate.

As time progresses entire rows of blocks are added to the bottom of the play area. Occasionally after clearing a set of blocks (and more often after setting off chains of removing blocks) the bottom row of blocks will be removed from the play area. If necessary, the player can use a help which will change all of the blocks in the currently falling column into 'P' blocks. When the column lands on the stack of blocks, whichever block it falls on will be cleared from the screen, along with all blocks that match that block.
Miss World '96

Rip-off of "Gals Panic!", featuring 'adult' photographs instead of the cartoon imagery. A Qix-like game where you guide a cursor over an area and avoid various enemies. As a new twist, you get rewarded by seeing a women in various states of dress (and undress), depending on your score. The image is initially covered by an overlay, which you have to wear away, at the same time avoiding and defeating enemies. Most of the overlay is translucent, but it is opaque over the girl. Your goal is to uncover as close to 100% of the picture as possible. Each round, she will wear less clothes. After she's topless, you move on to another girl.
Miss World 2002
A Qix clone that reveals underlying image as game progresses. For mature players only.
Missile Command

Missile Command was produced by Atari in 1980.

Aliens from the planet of Krytol are attacking your cities! As the commander of a missile base, it is your responsibility to defend them. A variety of enemy weapons and planes will be incoming trying to destroy the six cities at the bottom of the screen. You need to fire missiles to destroy the incoming weapons. If anything gets through, one of your cities could be destroyed. When all of the cities are gone, the game is over. On each level you have a limited amount of ammo, so make sure most (if not all) of your shots are accurate or you could run out of ammo and leave your cities at risk! As the levels progress, there are more and more enemy weapons to destroy which come in at an increasingly faster rate.
Mission 660

Basically just a classic simple space shoot-em-up space theme. You must clear wave after wave of different types of enemy ships. Eventually you make it to a big ship which takes many hits to destroy, then the cycle starts over again.
Mission Craft
Mission Craft is a one or two player shooter game published and developed by Sun Amusement in 2000.
Mission-X

Mission-X was produced by Data East in 1982.

You are a fighter plane bombing ships, bridges, and tanks, occasionally you use your guns on other planes that attack you. At the end of a level you try to touch down your plane to the runway for bonus points.
Bomb all enemy sea and land craft, gun emplacements, bridges and transportation networks. A low flying attack gives the best hit ratio but be careful it is dangerous

This game is for the Data East DECO cabinets
Mission: Impossible Arcade

Agent, your mission should you choose to accept it, is to save the world by sabotaging enemy plans that aim to weaponize humanoid robots. You will have a range of weapons and high-tech gadgets at your disposal to complete your mission but remember time is not your side. Sega brings the multi-billion dollar blockbuster film franchise MISSION: IMPOSSIBLE to the amusements market. SEGA’s Mission: Impossible Arcade is an adrenaline-fueled video game, that is the pinnacle of great design and entertainment. The awe-inspiring 4 player Super Deluxe Attraction cabinet is designed to look like the IMF (Impossible Mission Force) safe house and features the iconic fuse along with various interiors details that convey the feel of a top-secret high-tech spy hideout.
Mister Viking

Mister Viking is a Viking-themed vertically-scrolling shoot 'em up game where you take control of a Viking searching for the lost treasure of his people.

As the character makes progress he has to fight of creatures who walk or fly in the screen from all directions. The player has the ability to shoot in all directions to fend them off. To aid the player a bit a Viking ship occasionally appears to drop special weapons like bombs and swords that can be thrown at the enemies. Some buildings also yield these special weapons when destroyed. The game can be played solo or with a friend in alternating turns.
Miyasu Nonki no Quiz 18-Kin

Miyasu Nonki no Quiz 18-Kin (translated as "Nonki Miyasu's Quiz for Adults") is an erotic quiz/trivia arcade video game published in 1992. The game was developed and published by the Japanese studio EIM (founded by the famous game designer Kenji Eno).

It is a Japanese arcade eroge quiz game. Players face a series of trivia questions; answering correctly prompts on-screen female characters to progressively remove their clothes.
Mobile Suit Gundam

Mobile Suit Gundam (機動戦士ガンダム) is a 1993 fighting arcade game released, developed by Allumer and published by Banpresto in Japan. The game can be played in English or Japanese, suggesting that Banpresto might have planned to release this game internationally. It is based on the Mobile Suit Gundam franchise and is updated and retitled in the 1994 Mobile Suit Gundam: EX Revue arcade game.
Mobile Suit Gundam EX Revue

Mobile Suit Gundam: EX Revue is a 2D head-to-head fighting arcade game developed by Allumer and published by Banpresto in 1994. Released exclusively in Japanese arcades, it serves as the direct sequel and a major technical overhaul to Bandai's original 1993 Mobile Suit Gundam arcade fighter. It is widely remembered for its fast-paced, Street Fighter II-style gameplay engine and for introducing the cult-classic original mobile suit, the MS-19 Dolmel.

The game was packaged as a standard arcade conversion kit rather than a dedicated cabinet.
Mobile Suit Gundam Extreme Vs. 2

Mobile Suit Gundam Extreme Vs. 2 is the direct sequel to arcade game, Mobile Suit Gundam Extreme Vs. The gameplay remains fairly the same from its predecessors, being a 2vs2 arena game. The graphics engine was updated, now based on the console game, Gundam Versus, resulting in more detail, vibrant color palettes and lighting effects on mobile suits.

It also adds two new Bursts in the form of Linkage and Mobility to the existing Shooting, Fighting and Extended from Maxi Boost ON. Additionally, characters may also say something special when activating burst whilst locked on to a specific target similarly to Alliance vs ZAFT series.

The game would also see a large overhaul in its playable cast, while many "clone" variants such as Haman Karn's Acguy and Lunamaria Hawke's Impulse were cut.
Mobile Suit Gundam Extreme Vs. 2 OverBoost

Mobile Suit Gundam Extreme Vs. 2 OverBoost is an update to the arcade game Mobile Suit Gundam Extreme Vs. 2 XBoost, announced at the 2022 Premium Dogfight and was released on June 28, 2023. On February 8, 2025, the game's successor, Mobile Suit Gundam Extreme Vs. 2 Infinite Boost was announced during the Premium Dogfight 2025.

The amount of bursts has been reduced with both Mobility and Raging being removed for Vertical Burst, which allows the player to perform a Boost Dive like in Gundam Versus. Additionally, activating burst individually will also provide a small buff to the player's partner. Players will now be able to customize their Vs. Screen panels such as changing a unit's alternate CG art. A mute function for a partner's in-game messages and a direct rematch function were also added. A 1v1 training mode has been added.

The game would also introduce recolors of certain units such as RX-78-3 G-3 Gundam colors for the Gundam, and Zeheart's custom colors for the Gundam Legilis.
Mobile Suit Gundam Extreme Vs. 2 XBoost

Mobile Suit Gundam Extreme Vs. 2 XBoost (pronounced "Cross Boost") is an update to the arcade game Mobile Suit Gundam Extreme Vs. 2, announced as part of the 10th anniversary of the Extreme Vs. series, with a closed beta test in November 2020, before being released on March 10, 2021.

Several changes were made to the Burst System. While Fighting and Shooting Burst would remain untouched, Mobility was changed to only provide a pure movement boost. Extended and Linkage would be merged to form the new Covering Burst, which can similarly be used defensively or to boost the partner's EX Gauge and Raging Burst would be introduced, which gives its user hyper armor and reduces their stagger from attacks.

A new addition would be the EX Burst X, when the player activates their Burst alongside their teammate. The EX Burst X will now give the team additional buffs based on their own burst.

Likely to help players coordinate their Burst, the game now displays the partner's Boost Gauge as well.
Mobile Suit Gundam: Bonds of the Battlefield

Mobile Suit Gundam: Bonds of the Battlefield features a P.O.D (Panoramic Optical Display) that resembles a Mobile Suit Cockpit. It has adjustable seats, surround sound speakers, a projector screen, and controls both at the hands and feet. A single game lasts about 10–15 minutes and mostly has 4 P.O.Ds or more. If you are with other people voice chat can be possible between players, though it is not required. Each person must insert their pilot card into its slot and money to begin gameplay. Gameplay between players oversea is possible and available.

In the game, players become pilots of giant robot mobile suits from the anime series. Pilots play through two battle scenarios lasting a total game time of ten minutes. A large monitor replays the last battle and an angled touch screen user interface is used to manage pilot battle data. Almost all text is in kanji, hiragana, and katakana.
Mobile Suit Gundam: Federation Vs. Zeon

Mobile Suit Gundam: Federation vs. Zeon is a 2001 arcade video game based on the anime television series Mobile Suit Gundam. The game follows the Universal Century (UC) Gundam time line and takes place during the infamous One Year War. The player is able to pilot various mobile suits and characters from the original Mobile Suit Gundam television series. The DX (Deluxe) version is an upgraded edition of the game with 360-degree, zero-G space battlefields.
Mobile Suit Gundam: Federation vs. Zeon DX

Mobile Suit Gundam: Federation vs. Zeon DX is a 2001 arcade video game based on the anime television series Mobile Suit Gundam. The game follows the Universal Century (UC) Gundam time line and takes place during the infamous One Year War. The player is able to pilot various mobile suits and characters from the original Mobile Suit Gundam television series. The DX (Deluxe) version is an upgraded edition of the game with 360-degree, zero-G space battlefields.
Mobile Suit Gundam: Final Shooting

Take 'Operation Wolf' add the plot, characters and mecha from Gundam 008 and you've practically got this game: Mobile Suit Gundam Final Shooting.
Mobile Suit Gundam: Final Shooting is a rail shooter where one or two players mow down Mobile Suit after Mobile Suit with the cabinet mounted laser rifles. The enemy onslaught is unending so you'll need a good aim, a strong arm and a lot of concentration. Power-ups are few so it's more than welcome when, at the middle of the stage, your Mobile Suit is repaired and supplied with a limited but powerful sub-weapon. Boss battles round off each stage and involve blasting away at a large enemy craft while simultaneously shooting down the oncoming swarms of missiles and bad guys.

The graphics are entirely made up of well animated if slightly wobbly 2D sprites, zooming in and out of the screen or popping up from the bottom or rushing in from the sides. As you may have gathered the action is non-stop.
