When the player gets their coin into the center cup, the wheel spins and stops randomly on a number, and then this number becomes the amount of tickets they win. Get coins past the BONUS line and win a larger amount!
Pharaohs Match
Pharaohs Match is a mahjong match game by Arcadia Systems, Inc. in 1988
Phelios
Artemis, the goddess of the moon, has been kidnapped by the evil ruler of the darkness known as Typhon. Apollo must traverse seven treacherous areas in order to rescue his love!
Phoenix

Phoenix is a fixed-screen shooter in which the player controls a spacecraft moving horizontally along the bottom of the screen. The ship is armed with a laser cannon and a temporary force field used to survive enemy fire and collisions. While the shield is active, the ship cannot move, although it can continue firing; after it fades, it must recharge before being used again.

Each round consists of five waves. The first two feature formations of small bird-like enemies that move across the screen, fire projectiles, and periodically dive toward the player. The third and fourth waves begin with eggs that hatch into larger Phoenix birds. These enemies must be struck in the center to be destroyed; shots hitting a wing remove it temporarily, but the missing section eventually regenerates.
Photo Play 2000

A German touchscreen multigame arcade that would allow you to play card games, strategy/logic and acrade games with a large variety of different choices. These games were updated regularly to add new games to replace ones that weren't seeing high usage.
Photo Y2K

Photo Y2K was produced by I.G.S. in 1999.

Photo Y2K is a spot the difference style game where the goal is to find five differences between two similar looking pictures. Each mistake you make costs you one life and after three mistakes it's game over. The timer also gets progressively quicker as you make your way through the game's 60 levels. You have a limited amount of helpful items that can either help you find one of the differences or restart that level's timer. Every five levels you also have the chance to play a bonus game which allows you to replenish one of your items. The game can either be played solo or cooperatively with another person.
Photo Y2K 2

A puzzle game released by Taiwan based IGS where player has to compare two photographs of bikini models to spot differences between the two images. Player then uses joystick to move cursor and highlight the area that is different to gain points before the timer runs out. The game is also known as Real or Fake 2.
Phozon

Phozon is a chemistry inspired arcade action puzzle game. The player controls a single black molecule called the Chemic which is moved around the screen with a joystick. Also floating around on the screen are the moleks, other molecules of various colours, which automatically bind to the Chemic when bumped into. The aim of each level is to pick up moleks and recreate a certain pattern that is shown in the centre of the screen. If a molek is caught in the wrong position it can be sent away with the reject button.

The game is made harder by the Atomic, a group of balls that moves around the screen and which the player has to avoid touching or a life will be lost. Most of the time the balls move in a group but at times it splits up to cover more of the screen. The Atomic can also fire alpha- and beta-rays which when hitting a molek attached to the Chemic causes it to float away.
Phraze Craze
Phraze Craze is a Puzzle game, published by Merit Studios, which was released in 1986.
Piccadilly Nights

Piccadilly Nights is a classic UK pub video fruit machine game developed by BWB / Nova. The machine runs on the iconic MPU4 video hardware platform, which was widely used throughout British arcades and pubs during the 1990s. Rather than a traditional mechanical reel layout, it features a digital screen that displays its gaming boards, reels, and bonus features.
Piccolo Poker 100

Piccolo Poker 100 is a vintage video poker arcade game released in 1990 by Novomatic in West Germany. Built onto hardware closely related to American Poker II, the title is widely known in the arcade emulation community. It can be emulated via software like MAME.
Pickin'

Pickin' was produced by Valadon Automation in 1983.

You must move all the colored blocks into the same color corral. Avoid hitting the Disrupter and the Killer.
Pieces Of Eight

Pieces of Eight is a highly popular, pirate-themed Class II mechanical-reel slot machine developed by VGT (Video Gaming Technologies, an Aristocrat Gaming company). Primarily found in tribal casinos across states like Oklahoma (such as Choctaw, WinStar, and Downstream), it is famous for its high volatility and classic gameplay.

While UK players often refer to physical casino games as "fruit machines," Pieces of Eight is functionally a North American mechanical slot machine that operates on a bingo backend.
Pig Newton

Pig Newton is an arcade game developed by Sega for Sega G80 hardware in 1983, based on Malcom Hancock's Pig Newton cartoon.

The game takes place in a tree, where the player must drop apples on wolves below to stop them cutting it down. It apparently did not survive past testing.
Pig Out: Dine Like a Swine!

In this game, a bunch of little piggies run around in a gym-like maze trying to eat up all the goodies on the road. They must avoid an evil butcher and several big bad wolves chasing them. The game is similar to Pac-Man. Each time the butcher or the wolves get near, you can stun them by throwing cans and other projectiles at them. The graphics are cute.

Up to three people can play at once. The left player controls the blue pig, the middle player operates the red pig and the green pig is controlled by the right player.

The object of the game is for the player's pig character to eat as much food and drink as many drinks as possible while avoiding big bad wolves, an evil butcher and other enemies. Up to five jars of jam must be collected before players can proceed to the next stage. Each stage has a different background such as apartment buildings, circuses, underground sewers, construction sites, fire stations, bookstores, fish-packing plants, factories, etc.
Piggy Star Dust

Piggy Stardust is a popular Category C pub fruit machine manufactured by G Squared Gaming. It is highly regarded by collectors and arcade enthusiasts for its engaging David Bowie-inspired theme and its feature-packed gameplay board.
Pigs Might Fly

Pigs Might Fly is a video ticket redemption game from Sega Amusements USA. With bright, colorful graphics and a moveable action lever, children and adults alike will be entertained by this animated arrival.

With the press of a lever send pigs flying high on a mission to strike down UFOs passing overhead. Each UFO awards a different ticket payout and there's plenty of UFO's to attack. Watch out for the pigeons that try to get in the way and slow down the flight, and when striking a UFO the pig ricochets all over the place. There are also special bonus features that invite players to gain up to 1000 tickets.
Pigskin 621AD

Play Football with Barbarians! A basic football-ish game is played on a field filled with weapons, traps, and even paid-off bystanders that will do anything to slow you down!

You are the captain of a team of barbarians, trying to make as many 'touchdowns' as possible. Not only can you pass or lateral the ball to your teammates, but you can pick up concealed weapons too (then when a defender tries to tackle you, he comes out of the ball of dust with a mace in his face!). You can play against the computer, or head to head, but if you really start wiping the floor with your opponent, they start replacing his/her teammates with all-powerful Trolls!
Pikkari Chance

Pikkari Chance is themed around animal photography, presenting players with scenes where they attempt to capture pictures of creatures using a camera.

The player uses a simple input to take snapshots of animals that appear on screen. Timing is important to catch the target in frame, and successful photos yield medal rewards. The system adapts this photography mechanic into a medal game format, where players wager tokens and receive payouts depending on performance.
Pilot Kids
A cutesy horizontal shooter where you play a kid in an airplane shooting at awesome bosses like an attack dog.
Pin Pong

Pin Pong is a simple black and white pinball game by Atari. It was one of the first (if not the first) video game to simulate pinball. A patented motion circuit generates the ball. Targets are surrounded by zones that determine the direction the ball bounces in. A gravity algorithm forces the ball downward for a realistic effect.
Pin-Bot

Pin-Bot is a conversion of the arcade pinball game by Williams Electronics. The game is played with a split screen; the bottom half of the screen remains on your flippers, while the top half scrolls to follow the ball(s) on the table. In addition to recreating the pinball game's table, lights, and sounds several video game elements have been added, such as monsters that like to eat pinballs. Up to four players can compete against Pin-Bot!
Pinball Action

Pinball Action features three separate pinball areas in addition to the starting area. Each of the additional 'faces' has a challenge which, when completed, allows a player access to a special three extra credits. The three faces feature challenges modelled on ten-pin bowling, poker, and slot machines.
Pinball Champ '95
Pinball Champ '95 is a single player action/reflex video game for Arcade, created and published by Veltmeijer Automaten in 1995.
Pinball Wizard

The Pinball Wizard fruit machine is a classic UK pub slot machine released in 1998 by the prominent manufacturer JPM (John Purewal Manufacturers). Built on JPM's well-known Impact hardware platform, this Amusement with Prizes (AWP) machine stands out for blending traditional fruit machine reel play with an interactive, pinball-themed feature board.
Pinbo

Pinbo was produced by Jaleco in 1984.

A video pinball game from Jaleco.

In additional to the standard pinball gameplay, the player must also prevent enemies from eating their pinball. If the player manages to spell "JALECO," a bonus round will be earned.

A version of this game was released by Strike in 1985. It is unknown if this was either a licensed copy or a bootleg.
Ping Pong Masters '93
A one or two player sports game published and developed by Electronic Devices Italy in 1993.
Ping-Pong King

Ping-Pong King was developed and manufactured by Taito in 1985.

A Ping-Pong/Table Tennis game from Taito. It has a maximum of 2 players, although the game only features alternating turns, not 1 on 1 competitive.
Pink Panther

The Pink Panther fruit machine is a highly sought-after, classic UK arcade gaming machine based on the iconic cartoon character and film franchise. Multiple variations of the machine have been produced over the decades by well-known gaming manufacturers like Maygay and QPS Interactive. Because they are nostalgic collector's items, they frequently appear on the second-hand market for private home game rooms.
Pink Panther Club

The Pink Panther Club fruit machine is a highly popular, classic UK coin-operated arcade game released in multiple generations by manufacturers like Maygay and QPS (Quality Products Services). These machines are iconic fixtures of British pubs and private clubs. They featured varying jackpot models ranging from vintage £5 jackpots up to massive £250 club jackpots.
Pink Panther Double Your Money

The Pink Panther Double Your Money (often styled as "Double Yer Money") is a classic UK pub fruit machine manufactured by Mazooma or QPS. It is well-regarded by collectors of retro arcade gaming gear for its low-tech, traditional style.
Pink Panther Double Your Money Top Box

The Pink Panther "Double Yer Money" Top Box fruit machine is a highly sought-after, classic pub fruit machine manufactured by Maygay during the late 1990s or early 2000s. Running on the iconic Maygay M1 hardware platform, it is famous for its distinctive top-box bonus layout and standard UK pub cabinet style.
Pink Panther: Break the Bank

The Pink Panther: Break the Bank fruit machine is a classic UK pub-style slot machine (Amusement with Prizes / AWP) manufactured by QPS (Quality Products Services) using the Adder 5 hardware system. It is distinct from the earlier, highly popular 1990s Pink Panther machines built by Maygay on their M1 platform, as well as Maygay's separate 1989 machine called Break the Bank.
Pink Panther: Clouseau's Revenge
Pink Panther Clouseau's Revenge is a fruit slot machine manufactured by Mazooma.
Pink Panther: Crack the Code

Pink Panther: Crack the Code is a classic UK pub fruit machine manufactured by Quality Products Services (QPS) and running on the Bell-Fruit Games (BFG) Scorpion 5 hardware platform (Model PR2407). Depending on the specific software cabinet configuration and whether it is set up for a standard arcade or a club environment, it is most commonly found featuring a £70 jackpot or a £5 jackpot for older/refurbished classic pub models.
Pink Panther: Jewel Heist

He’s the sneakiest animated thief there is and now the Pink Panther is hunting for valuable jewels in Pink Panther Jewel Heist! Based on the cartoon & movies that carry the Pink Panther name, Jewel Heist is an officially licensed title that is a perfect piece for your arcade or family entertainment center.

Following a classic gameplay formula, you control the Pink Panther as he descends the floors in a 100 floor building, grabbing coins and avoiding police patrols along the way. You can’t linger on a floor for too long as the moving Deadly Laser never stops trying to catch up with you. Escape with the jewel by reaching the bottom to win the Jewel Bonus jackpot!
Pink Sweets: Ibara Sorekara

Pink Sweets: Ibara Sorekara (ピンクスウィーツ　～鋳薔薇それから～, Pinku Suītsu: Ibara Sorekara) is a 2006 manic shooter by Cave released for Japanese arcades. It was released for the Xbox 360 in 2011.

Pink Sweets is the sequel to Ibara, and features the stage 1-5 bosses from Ibara as playable characters.

Players get to pilot the gals and use a barrier/shot system to defeat flitting enemies as well as end-level bosses of the pastel-colored type. Enemies besides bosses are named after food. During the game, the gals yelp and intonate various sayings to steel themselves for battle.
Pink Sweets: Suicide Club
Hacked version of Pink Sweets: Ibara Sorekara from Cave.
Pinkiri 8
Pinkiri 8 is a tabletop mahjong casino game published by Alta in 1994, developed by ALTAR interactive.
Pioneer Balloon

Pioneer Balloon was produced by SNK in 1982.

Guide a balloon across a variety of frontiers dropping bombs on your enemies. Dodge arrows shot from a covered wagon, boomerangs thrown by natives, coconuts hurled by gorillas, geyser sprays, cannonballs and deadly birds. Finally, navigate the balloon over mountains and make a precise landing at Fort Freedom.

It was also released by Rock-Ola in North America.
Pipe Dream

Pipe Dream was produced by Video System Co. Ltd. in 1990. A puzzle game where the player has to connect pipes.
Each level of this abstract puzzler challenges the player to set up a network of pipes to allow an unspecified substance known as 'flooz' to flow through as many of those as possible. The pieces are offered in random order, and there are seven different types - straight lines going horizontally or vertically, corners rotating in each of the four directions, and cross-over pieces which carry the flooz straight across horizontally and vertically. Each of these can be entered from either side. When the flooz hits a gap, or a piece which the previous piece can't flow into, the pipe is finished.

Before the flooz starts flowing from its randomly-selected starting position, the player has several seconds to start placing pieces. They can be put down anywhere.
Pipeline
A one player puzzle game published and developed by Daehyun Electronics in 1990.
Pipi & Bibis

Players control old men that attempt to set time bombs in the building, then they must escape before the building explodes. Every time you complete a level, one fourth of a woman's picture is shown. You can see the whole picture every four levels.
Piranha

Piranha was produced by GL in 1981. It was also published by U.S. Billiards.

You control a red piranha with your 4-way joystick, eating all the dots on the screen while avoiding four squids that are after you. The four corners each have an "energizer pellet" that, once eaten, allows you to attack and eat the squid who were chasing you. Clearing all edible objects from the screen advances you to the next screen.
Pirate (Fruit Machine)
A pirate themed fruit machine developed and manufactured by Igrosoft in 2005.
Pirate 2001

Pirate 2001 is a classic 8-Liner Cherry Master style video slot / fruit machine game developed and manufactured by the arcade and gaming company Amcoe. Released in 2001, it was heavily distributed as a printed circuit board (PCB) kit meant to be built into standard counter-top or upright arcade cabinets.
Pirate 2002
Pirate 2002 is another pirate themed video casino game (this time a fruit machine), it was developed and released by Amcoe in 2001.
Pirate Pete

Pirate Pete is a reworked version of "Jungle King/Jungle Hunt". Here's what makes Pirate Pete different from Jungle King/Jungle Hunt:

* An opening musical theme is used in certain parts of the game instead of the opening Tarzan yell (unlike in "Jungle Hunt", it is NOT the same one used at the end of the ocean stage).
* The player character is a heroic pirate instead of the Tarzan character.
* In the first stage, the player swings on ropes between ship's masts instead of vines between trees.
* The second stage is set in an ocean infested with sharks, instead of a river infested with alligators and crocodiles.
* The third stage adds a new enemy - snakes. They appear at the top of the screen and will kill the player if he touches them while jumping.
* The enemies in the fourth stage are sword-wielding pirates instead of spear-chucking cannibals.
Pirate Poker II
A high seas pirate themed video poker game developed and manufactured by Amcoe in 2003.
Pirate Ship

The player is the pirate captain of his ship raiding across the sea. Collect pieces of eight and gold dubloons while avoiding collisions of various enemies and obstacles in a quest for the key to Treasure Island.

This video redemption game has a wooden ship's wheel which can steer the ship left and right.
At the beginning of the game, the player can select one of three stages: The South Isles, Atlantis or The Sea Of The Dead. When the player has made it to the end of one of those stages, the game ends.

Tickets are won from the game depending on the score during the gameplay and the "X" number from one of the three treasure chests at the end of the stage.

After one of three stages has been selected, the player must steer the pirate ship while sailing across the sea. The ship must pick up coins worth 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 or even 100 points to score. The player needs 2000 points or more in order to get the key for Treasure Island at the end of the stage.
Pirate Ship Higemaru

Pirate Ship Higemaru was produced by Capcom in 1984.

This is a top-down view arcade game where the player is cast as Japanese sailor Momotaro who has to defeat all of the Higemaru pirates as well as their nefarious captain Bow.

Each stage is a fixed screen view of a pirate ship filled with barrels, oil drums, bags and more where Momotaro has to take out a set number of pirates (and a captain) before moving on to the next level. Momotaro has no weapon of his own, so he has to pick up the various barrels and items on the level and throw them at the pirates. Some items break on impact, while others are indestructible and can be used more than once. If Momotaro manages to throw a rolling barrel which hits more than one pirate in succession, the score gets higher for each pirate defeated. Some of the barrels and items hide point bonuses and for each sixteenth barrel destroyed, an invincibility bonus is rewarded to the player which lasts for a short while.
Pirate Treasure

Pirate Treasure was produced by Tong Electronic in 1982.

The player uses the joystick to move the red pirate ship across the islands to score points: small islands (25 points), medium islands (100 points), big islands (150 points), and great big islands (250 points). Avoid colliding with the black enemy pirate ship and be aware that this ship can also create a live volcano on one of the islands you raided. If you run into a volcano, your ship will explode.
Try to capture the treasure chest when you see it on one of the islands but sometimes the enemy ship will take it and move it onto another island. Your ship can sometimes move through the top, bottom and sides of the screen but at other times the edges of the screen will be blocked by red lines. Everytime you capture one of the treasures, depending on what stage you are on, the prize can be worth from 1000 to 7000 points plus a bonus for every island you raid after you have captured the treasure.
Pirates

Two pirates are tasked by their captain to find three pieces of a treasure map on the islands Shetland, La Isabela and Papeete, before finding the hidden treasure cash on the obscure island Tiuanapa. Every stage has the player in third-person perspective shooting at pirates and scenery, throwing bombs, and doing slide maneuvers to dodge enemy attacks. Powerups are obtained from shooting a flying witch repeatedly or other passing creatures. A stage is won when the enemy meter at the bottom is depleted or a boss enemy is beaten.

Trivia / History:

The organization behind "Pirates" was an obscure company from Spain, NIX. Both the game code and hardware were based on "Blood Brothers" by TAD. Hardware that could not be reproduced was replaced with chips reverse engineered from Capcom hardware. As the arcade game was only distributed locally, Capcom never caught wind of it nor took legal action. Nor did TAD, as that company had already gone bankrupt.
Pisces

Pisces is a fixed screen shooter, which was developed and manufactured by Subelectro in 1982.

Destroy the waves of aliens that come from the sides of the screen. When you finish a level you will rocket to a new level.

There are several different waves to go through in this game. The first wave is similar to Galaxian, with aliens diving and shooting at you. Another wave rips off the Pleaides wave of the birds that will dive straight down if you shoot one or both of their wings. Another wave consists of navigating your ship through an asteroid field to dock with a module before your fuel runs out, and a creepy-looking boss marks the final wave, as you must destroy its sentry ships before going after the boss itself. Then all the waves will repeat.
Pistol Daimyo no Bouken

The player must take control of Pistol Daimyo, a small Japanese lord, who has a pistol strapped to his head (and two fans strapped to his feet); he faces to the right side of the screen, and is always moving forward with the backgrounds scrolling to the left, bringing enemies into view, which are very reminiscent of Monty Python's Flying Circus. Similar to Kissy, Takky, and Hommy from Baraduke and Bakutotsu Kijūtei, he will float down to the ground if you stop holding the joystick up while he is in mid-air - and pressing that Firing Button will make his pistol fire a small cannonball. However, holding down the button will charge the pistol (much like Alice's bubble blower in Märchen Maze, and Apollo's sword in Phelios), and upon releasing the button the pistol will fire a medium or large cannonball; but even the smallest enemies take multiple hits to kill, so the small cannonballs are of little use.
Pit & Run: F-1 Race

A one or two player racing game published and developed by Taito in 1984. The player must use a 4-way joystick, to take control of a race car which competes against nine other CPU-controlled cars. As it travels the tracks, the player's race car fuel meter will decrease requiring refueling at "GVS" stations. As in Taito's own Speed Race series, there are "slip zones" on the tracks, which require careful steering in; each track also has three trials. On the second and third trials of each track, the player receives a "Turbo" tune-up when pulling into a "GVS" station for a refuel. However, the turbo boost causes the fuel meter to decrease twice as fast. Once a player has mastered all four of the tracks regardless of how many trials it has taken, the player will be proclaimed "CHAMPION" and the game will end.
Pit Boss II
A one or two player multi game published and developed by Merit Software in 1988.
Pit Boss Superstar
Pit Boss Superstar was produced by Merit Industries in 1990.
Pit-Fighter

Pit-Fighter was produced by Atari Games in 1990.

The game has three different characters of whom each of the players can be: Buzz, an ex-professional wrestler Ty, a kick-boxing champion or Kato, a third-degree black belt. Each player character has different fighting styles and techniques and they also each have their own Super Moves. The opponents are The Executioner, Southside Jim, C.C. Rider, Chainman Eddie, Angel, Mad Miles, Heavy Metal and The Masked Warrior.
You must defeat all opponents in order to become the champion. The game has 15 different matches, some opponents like Southside Jim and Angel must each be faced twice in respective matches while other opponents are only faced once. Before you can make it to The Championship Match to face the reigning champion, The Masked Warrior, you must take on two Chainman Eddies.
Pitapat Puzzle

Pitapat Puzzle is a rare, two-player arcade puzzle game developed by the South Korean company F2 System and released in 1997. Running on hardware similar to the game Cross Pang, it features a simple, cute aesthetic but offers deep, strategic tile-matching mechanics.

Players use a joystick to control a carrier that can pick up or drop coloured marbles. Pressing Button A picks up or drops a marble.
When three marbles of the same colour connect, they explode. These explosions destroy nearby boxes, turning them into fresh marbles and setting up massive chain reaction combos.
Pressing Button B manually feeds more marbles into the play field. If you manage to blow up every single marble on the screen, you earn a massive board-clear bonus—but you are only given one specific opportunity per level to achieve it.
Pitfall II: The Lost Caverns

You control an explorer called Pitfall Harry who searches for lost treasures in the jungle and caverns. He must run and jump to avoid various creatures and obstacles throughout his quest.

This is the arcade version of Pitfall! and Pitfall II: Lost Caverns, two home video games by Activision, designed by David Crane.

Pitfall Harry travels through the jungle and caverns to find all kinds of treasures including gold bars, silver bars, money bags and diamond rings.

Pitfall Harry must avoid or jump over dangers such as logs, snakes, scorpions, fires, etc. He must also swing on vines to get across mud bogs, tar pits, crocodile-infested ponds, etc. As for some crocodile-infested ponds which have no vines at all, Pitfall Harry must carefully jump on their heads but not their mouths with careful timing to get across. He can also climb up and down ladders and jump over open holes. He can also even swim across underground streams while avoiding electric eels.
Pittanko Zaurus

Arcade Video game published 25 years ago:

Pittanko Zaurus © 1995 Konami.
PK Scramble

PK Scramble is a Japanese soccer arcade game developed and published by Cosmo Electronics Corporation in 1993.

The game focuses entirely on penalty kicks.
Players select a soccer team before the match begins. To play, you choose a kicking direction and press the kick button to strike or defend against the ball.
PK Tetris

The PK Tetris arcade machine is a casino-style arcade cabinet released around 1993 by the Taiwanese developer International Arcade Museum. Running on the igspoker.cpp hardware driver, it stands out from mainstream puzzle variants by combining traditional block-stacking mechanics with gambling elements typical of coin-operated video slot or poker machines of that era.
Planet Harriers

The game is based around a twin cabinet, which allows for two players to play simultaneous single-player games, or a networked two-player game. The cabinet has a seated configuration. Control is through a joystick with a missile and bullet trigger, and view-change and bomb buttons on the main panel. A player may select one of four characters; Glenn, X, Cory or Nick. Gameplay involves the character flying from an into-the-screen perspective, shooting oncoming enemies and missiles. In a two player game, the two characters may dock together in order to recover life. Opa-Opa appears spinning above a killed player offering a continue. This character is made playable with the Easter egg of moving the player selection over X, then Nick, Cory, Glenn, Cory, Nick, Cory, Glenn, X, Cory and then Glenn again.
Planet Probe

A prototype vertical space shoot'em up game with a parallax background. 

The player controls a probe sent to a mysterious planet and is attacked by several types of enemies. Face the attacks using all the available weapons and escape from the planet to complete the mission.

This rare Japanese coin-op can be described as an elaborate evolution of Tehkan's Senjyo. There's fixed horizontal scrolling (from left to right), but your spaceship shoots vertically. You can shoot into the pseudo-3D background, to destroy the outposts located on the landscape, AND right up in the sky, to eliminate the enemy spaceships. The scrolling never stops, and environments smoothly cycle from deserts to volcanic areas, from alien oceans to futuristic cities.
Plants vs. Zombies: The Last Stand

Plants vs. Zombies: The Last Stand is an arcade machine developed by Sega in 2013. In the game, the player plays as a Peashooter in a first-person view and gets to fire at the zombies. The player only has one life before they need to insert another coin. Crazy Dave is the guide.

The player selects their initials, and are then greeted by Crazy Dave, who shows the mechanics of the game. The player can then pick from a few places to battle the zombies, such as a lawn or a grocery store market.

The only plant featured in the game is the Peashooter. However, the player can get more boosts to upgrade it to a Fire Peashooter, Snow Pea, Gatling pea, spike pea, exploding pea, bubble pea, lightning pea which is only available when it's raining, and a Threepeater with yellow peas. However, other plants are shown, but are not playable, such as Sunflower and Chomper.
Plasma Sword: Nightmare of Bilstein

In the epic battle of the Final Crusade that had occurred from within last year, Hayato Kanzaki had slayed the evil Dr. Edward Bilstein and brought the end of the Fourth Empire's terror and destruction throughout the entire universe. The fall of the Fourth Empire and the death of its leader were momentous occasions of last year and that it had signaled the restoration of peace and happiness, but all is not well from within the universe.

Rumors have been circulating about the unexpected return of Bilstein in a new cybernetic body, as well as the appearance of a ghost who eerily looks like Bilstein's old cybernetic body. At the same time, the Fourth Empire has taken the opportunity in rebuilding its strong forces and that the loyal members of the organization are quite determined to carry out Bilstein's evil will of eliminating those who stand in the way of their emperor's universal conquest.
Platoon V.3.1 US

Very little is known about this FMV laserdisc shooter.

It isn't yet emulated in MAME, but it has been recreated in Hypseus and made playable with 1 or 2 players.
Play Girls

Play Girls is an adult-themed arcade video game released in 1992 by Taito and Hot-B. The game belongs to the block-breaker/paddle genre, playing similarly to classics like Arkanoid.

One or two players control a horizontal blocker at the bottom of the screen to bounce a ball and knock down blocks and chests.
As players clear away blocks or advance through stages, the background gradually reveals images of scantily clad women.
Play Girls 2

Play Girls 2 is an arcade shooter. The player selects a character and advances through successive stages populated by waves of enemies and environmental hazards, using primary fire and stage-specific mechanics to defeat foes and clear each level. The game’s visuals includes sexualized, mature-themed imagery, including revealing character sprites and suggestive background art.
PlayBall!
According to Larry DeMar, there's only one Playball! machine in existence since it was a prototype.
PlayMan Poker

The PlayMan Poker arcade machine is a classic electronic video poker game originally released in 1981 by the manufacturer PlayMan. This early 1980s retro title, which commonly features a German-language interface, is primarily preserved today through arcade preservation efforts and emulation platforms like MAME.
Pleasant Goat and Big Big Wolf: Happy Happy Playground

Pleasant Goat and Big Big Wolf Ticket Redemption Machine is a 9 colored, three grouped buttons beat video game, featuring with 24 mini games with 9 different cute cartoon characters. It is suitable for single player or three players cooperation or competition game.

The characters is from the Pleasant Goat and Big Big Wolf animation of Chinese animated television series, including Happy Lamb, Steady Lamb, Sleepy Lamb, Beauty Lamb, Fit Lamb, Warm Goat, Little Grey, Grey Wolf, and Red wolf.

This machine comes with two game modes: pass through mode and challenged mode. The pass through mode includes five levels, and need to pass 18 mini games. Challenged mode is the individual game; player can choose four games to challenge with the machine.
Pleasure Goal: 5 on 5 Mini Soccer
A 3/4 top-down soccer game featuring big character sprites in a realistic arcade soccer game. This is an extremely rare Neo Geo game.
Pleiads

Pleiads is a multi-stage space shoot 'em up in which enemy ships fly at the player in waves in a similar fashion to games like Galaxian and Phoenix.

Ships emerge from a mothership at the top of the screen and swoop downwards in a series of patterns which players must anticipate as they shoot the ships and avoid being obliterated by the Martian onslaught. There are four stages in the game.

Enemy ships come at you in scrolling waves. Growing bird-like ships swoop down at the player's ship as more enemy ships spring forth from the mothership. During the final wave, the player must navigate around parked ships to hit landing pad right on.

The Centuri marquee incorrectly spells the game as Pleiades but the software ROMs and main screen spell the game as Pleiads.
Plotting

Plotting, released as Flipull in Japan, is a tile-matching puzzle video game published by Taito in 1989. The game bears strong graphical and some gameplay similarities to Puzznic.

The screen is broken into two halves where each player controls their own game. This strategy game starts out simple where the player hits one block at a time but it becomes more difficult when other obstacles start preventing a direct hit on the desired block.
Plumb Crazy Club

The Plumb Crazy Club fruit machine is a classic UK club-style slot machine originally manufactured by Bell-Fruit Manufacturing. Built on the popular Bell-Fruit Scorpion 4 hardware platform, it was a staple of British pubs, arcades, and working men's clubs during the late 1990s and 2000s.
Plump Pop

Plump Pop was produced by Taito in 1987.

Plump Pop is a Circus variant. Players can choose to play as a team of dogs, cats, or pigs as they bounce another one of their kind on a trampoline in order to pop balloons.

The game features 10 rounds made up of 4 parts each for a total of 40 levels with every third part being a bonus round where the player tries to catch as many falling fruits as they can with their trampoline and every 4th part being a boss battle. During the main rounds players can earn power-ups that can do things like increase the damage being dealt or increase the size of the trampoline.
Plus Alpha

Plus Alpha was produced by Jaleco in 1989.

A cutesy airplane shooter.

Some of the levels are: Wind Country, Sea Colony, Flower Town, Snow Country, Sand City, Dark Sodom, and Eden.
PMA Poker

PMA Poker is a rare, vintage video poker arcade game released in 1983 by the manufacturer PMA. The game operates on a horizontal display format and remains a classic piece of early 1980s casino-style arcade history.
Pnickies

Pnickies is a puzzle game similar to Puyo Puyo, where you stack differently coloured jelly blocks and ideally form chain reactions. The difference to Puyo Puyo is that the blocks do not disappear once a certain number of same coloured ones are connected, but instead there are star blocks which also come in the same colours as the normal blocks. To make blocks disappear the player has to form a connected group of same coloured blocks that contain two star blocks. As soon as the 2nd star block is added the affected group goes away and any blocks that were on top of parts of this group will fall down.

The game is quite basic and only has single player, two player versus, and two player simultaneous modes, but no way to play against a CPU opponent.

In versus mode the players can send black blocks to their opponent, where the number of blocks sent is influenced by how many blocks were made to disappear.
Pochi & Nyaa

Far beyond our own dimension, on a planet not too different from ours, lies a magical land that is home to all sorts of gods. But the gods the denizens worship most of all are Pochi, the god of dogs, and Nyaa, the god of cats. Every 1000 years, these two gods hold a "Pochi and Nyaa" tournament to determine which god shall rule the heavens in the millennium to come. But, in order to hold this tournament, they'll need all the mortal help they can get. And that's where our heroine, the novice mage (and sweets lover) Prim, enters the picture...

Pochi to Nyaa is a puzzle game where a single player controlling Prim must fight through a series of kooky characters in hopes of making the millennial Pochi and Nyaa tournament go off without a hitch. To do so, Prim must stack up Nyans of the same color together and set them off by turning a Nyan into a Spiky Nyan.
Pocket Gal

The first Side Pocket title was released to the arcades in 1986. It was a good attempt, but didn't get much attention.
Three years later Data East decided to improve its physics, revamp the audiovisual department, and even add some cute stripping anime girls to get our attention. The new product was renamed "Pocket Gal", which together with its sequel "Pocket Gal DX" would become the most distributed video pool arcade cabinets.

As a very straight forward pool title, simplicity and addictiveness are its strong points.
The only available game mode is a "pocket" game, in which you play by yourself or against a friend trying to pocket 6 balls. Players start with only 4 cues (scratching or failing to pocket a ball substracts from your total cues, reaching 0 means game over), and different ball effects are available by pressing the second button and selecting it with the joystick.
Pocket Gal 2

Pocket Gal 2 was produced by Data East in 1989

An adult themed pool game with four levels, each denoted by a different woman. Score enough points to cause the woman to strip and to advance you to the next level. Trick shots can be attempted between frames and when two people play, the winner is the best two of three frames.

Pocket Gal and Pocket Gal 2 are basically the same game. Pocket Gal has Japanese ROMs so all speech and text is in Japanese and Pocket Gal 2 has English ROMs so all speech and text is in English. Apart from that they are the same game.
Pocket Gal Deluxe

Pocket Gal Deluxe was produced by Data East

An adult themed pool game with four levels, each denoted by a different woman. Score enough points to cause the woman to strip and to advance you to the next level. Trick shots can be attempted between frames and when two people play, the winner is the best two of three frames.

You can perform jump shots over other balls along with other tricks. The game has a Jazz-like soundtrack.
Pocket Gals V.I.P

Pocket Gals V.I.P. is a retro adult-themed arcade pool (billiards) simulation game released for arcades in 1997. The game builds directly on the mechanics of Data East's classic Pocket Gal series (which itself was an adult spinoff of the mainstream arcade classic Side Pocket).

 You must clear the pool table by pocketing a set number of colored balls within a strict time or shot limit.
Players choose a female partner character at the start. Reaching the target "Champ Level" score quota allows you to clear the stage, unlocking rewarding anime graphics and advancing you to the next opponent.
Pocket Racer

Pocket Racer is a spin-off arcade racing game released by Namco exclusively in Japan in 1996 (with wide deployment in early 1997). Built on Namco's System 11 hardware, the game serves as a comical, "super-deformed" version of the classic Ridge Racer series, heavily drawing visual cues from the popular Choro-Q mini toy cars. The concept was originally introduced to home console players as "Buggy Mode" hidden inside Ridge Racer Revolution on the PlayStation.
Point Blank

Point Blank is a puzzle/light gun shooter that is merciless in its pace. The premise of the game is based around "quick fire" rounds that tests players' accuracy and reactions.

The game is structured in a very random manner with four non-related stages being displayed for players to choose from each time they complete a stage. Stages are comprised of accuracy tests such as having to shoot the apple off the head of a far away character with only one bullet or judgment tests, such as killing only bad guys in a sea of good guys. Other stages involve solving puzzles by shooting out keys on a keyboard to spell words.
Point Blank 2

Dan and Don return for another round of shooting action. This time there are heaps of new mini games, as well as a few that improve on what was available in the first title in the series. 

The PlayStation version supports the GunCon (or G-Con), but the player can also use normal controllers.
Point Blank 3

The third episode in the Point Blank series now has up to 8 players playing it out in the new Team Battle mode, where you take turns to fight it out, and win as many games as possible.

Also new is the Endurance mode for 1 player, where you simply have to win as many games as possible before you use up all of your credits.
Point Blank X

Point Blank X is the sequel to the target shooting legend Point Blank. Instead of a single game that you progress through this gun based adventure gives you an incredible 72 stages! You will have to be a sharpshooter to master all 72 stages!
Poitto!

Poitto! Was developed by Metro Corporation and published by Able Corporation in 1993.

Poitto! is a puzzle game where the object is to match three bottles of the same color horizontally, vertically or diagonally to clear them. Match four bottles to cast a spell and attack the opponent. Make a chain reaction to attack with multiple spells. The game has two modes. In Vs. Mode you try to make your opponent's bottles reach the top while preventing your own from doing so. When you complete bottle lines, some of your opponents bottles will be turned into "timer bottles" which cannot be made to disappear until the timer runs out. In Monster Mode you play against monsters that have bounties on their heads and you need to get the monster's platform raised to the top so as to crush them.
Poizone

Poizone is a Pengo variant with an ecological theme. The player controls the penguin Zozo as he attempts to decontaminate each of the game's 50 levels. Like in Pengo each level contains blocks that can be pushed or destroyed. It differs though in that the main objective is not to kill the enemies but to destroy a number of toxic blocks. To complete a level 90% of these blocks have to be destroyed and it has to happen before time runs out.

There are eight kinds of toxic blocks and each has its own way to be destroyed. For example some blocks has to be destroyed from a specific direction while some has to be pushed away. Destroying a toxic block in the wrong way leads to a lost life. A life is also lost when making contact with a monster. Some other blocks exist such as power pills that can be used to avoid monsters and diamonds that give bonuses.
Poka Poka Satan

Poka Poka Satan is a whac-a-mole game where the player defends a princess from small creatures that appear across the playfield. The cabinet includes dual touch-sensitive screens used either by two players or one player controlling both sides. 

Enemies appear from multiple positions on the screens, and the player must strike or tap them as they emerge. Each successful hit adds to the score, while missed or escaped enemies reduce remaining time or cause a stage failure. Later rounds introduce faster patterns and additional enemy types.
Poke Champ

Poke Champ is a Korean hack of Data East’s 1988 arcade game Pocket Gal altered for the Korean market, differing mainly in localized artwork and interface graphics. The game features cartoon-style female characters and maintains a light adult theme.

The game uses a fixed overhead view of the pool table. Players adjust cue direction and shot power to pocket balls under standard pool rules. Matches are played against AI opponents, with victory advancing the player to the next stage.
To progress, the player must earn a required point total. Points are gained by sinking balls into the correct pockets, maintaining streaks, or clearing balls in the proper order. On higher stages, simply clearing the table is not enough—precision and sequence matter.
When the required score is reached, the game displays an image of a girl, providing the game’s “adult” element.
Poker

Poker is not just a video poker game, but a compilation of several video gambling games, developed and manufactured by Greyhound Electronics in 1984.

Games include:

- Joker Poker
- Black Jack
- Horse Race
- Rolling Bones
- Casino Slots
Poker 52
Poker 52 is a video poker game developed and released by Blitz Systems in 1993.
Poker 91

Poker 91 is a classic, video-poker arcade game that is widely recognized today as an emulated ROM available via MAME.

It features traditional five-card draw video poker rules where players bet virtual credits, hold specific cards, and draw to build winning hands (like pairs, flushes, or full houses).
Poker Carnival
Poker Carnival is a video poker game developed and released by Subsino in 1991.
Poker Dice
Poker Dice is a dice based gambling game co-developed and co-released by Strata and Incredible Technologies in 1991.
Poker Ladies

You are trying to get a certain specified number of points by getting poker hands ranging from of a pair of Jacks to a royal flush. If you get to the highest point level for that girl, you can "play" with her (the game's wording) by pressing the "Deal" button repeatedly. There are nine girls. Once you get through them all there is a closing sequence then the game starts over again. The "Flip Screen" button causes the screen to flip upside down perhaps for use in a cocktail cabinet.
Poker Monarch
Poker Monarch is a video poker game developed and manufactured by Extrema Systems International in 1995.
Poker Only '97
Poker Only '97 is a video poker game developed and released by Amcoe in 1987
Poker Roulette
Roker Roulette is a video poker game produced and released by Coinmaster in 1990.
Pokkén Tournament

Pokkén Tournament is a fighting video game developed by Bandai Namco Studios and published by The Pokémon Company. The game combines gameplay elements from Bandai Namco's Tekken series with characters from Nintendo's Pokémon franchise. It was released for Japanese arcades in July 2015.
Poko-Nyan!

Pokonyan! Balloon is a 1994 Capcom release running on CPS1 hardware. The system was part of a children's "balloon ride" that is similar to Waku Waku Sonic Patrol Car where the child sits in the ride while the visuals play on the screen.
Pokonyan! Baloon

Pokonyan! Balloon is a rare, Japanese-exclusive arcade kiddie ride released by Capcom in March 1994. Built on Capcom's famous CPS-1 arcade hardware, it is less of a traditional video game and more of an interactive video ride. The machine featured a physical, swaying cabinet shaped like a hot-air balloon that children would sit inside while watching the journey unfold on a built-in screen.

 Players pilot a hot-air balloon carrying the titular character Pokonyan (from the anime/manga by Fujiko F. Fujio) and his friend. The primary objective is to float through various landscapes and collect all the airborne balloons.
Polaris

The goal of the player is to destroy all the airplanes in each level while avoiding bombs dropped from the aircraft, as well as mines launched by enemy submarines and depth charges dropped from boats that speed by.
Pole Position

Pole Position was developed by Namco and published by Atari in 1982.

Race your Indy car around the Fuji course before the timer runs out. The first run is the qualifying lap, and your starting position is determined by your completion time. Avoid road hazards and other cars as you drive, earning extra time for each completed lap

Prepare to qualify! A sophisticated game for its day, with scalable foreground objects and speech. Keep an eye out for the billboards! Also, famous for burning the power input edge connectors and finger contacts on the PCB. Several custom integrated circuits.

Pole Position was created by Namco Inc. who also manufactured the game for the entire world except for the United States. Aside from the words which are in Japanese found on and in the Namco version, the graphics on the side of the cabinet are basically the same as well as the billboards that are seen throughout the game.
Pole Position II

Pole Position II was developed by Namco and published by Atari in 1983

In the sequel to Pole Position, you are again driving an F-1 racer in a timed qualifying run, trying to achieve the pole position. Then it is off to the race, in hopes of taking that top spot. The difference in Pole Position II and it's predecessor is that now you have four tracks to select from.
Police 911

This unique game senses body movement rather than requiring the player to move individual controls.

Taking the role of a police officer, you start in Los Angeles and fight your way through the members of the Japanese mafia who are running guns from America to Japan. There are six bosses you must capture in LA and Japan, concluding with the head of the Criminal organization in Japan.
The player moves around shooting enemies and rescuing hostages. Unlike games such as Time Crisis or Maximum Force, the player uses his/her entire body in order to hide or shoot.

The player stands on a yellow foot pad, and interacts with the onscreen action by physically dodging left, right and ducking to avoid danger and reloading your weapon. Three infared sensors (L, R, Center), mounted on a bar overhead, detect the player's body position and reflect that information back to the game.
Police 911 2

Police 911, called The Keisatsukan (ザ・警察官, lit. The Police Officer) in Japan and Police 24/7 in Europe, is a series of light gun shooter arcade games. Konami released the first game in 2000.

Unlike earlier light gun games, the game was unique for its motion sensing technology, sensing body movement rather than requiring the player to move individual controls; the player's "real world" actions are reflected by the player character within the game. It also featured a unique cover system, where the player takes cover by physically ducking for cover rather than pressing a button. The 2001 Konami arcade game MoCap Boxing used similar motion-sensing technology.

Although the game was a separate canon from the Lethal Enforcers series, Konami acknowledged Lethal Enforcers 3 as the successor to the Police 911 series, thus making it a canon in the Lethal Enforcers series.
Police Squid

The Police Squid is a classic UK pub fruit machine manufactured by QPS Interactive (Quantum Prize Systems, which was later acquired by Bell-Fruit Games).

Running on the highly popular Bell-Fruit Scorpion 4 hardware platform, this Amusement with Prizes (AWP) machine has achieved legacy status in the fruit machine community through emulation.
Police Trainer

Police Trainer is a light gun arcade game released by P&P Marketing in 1996. A sequel, Police Trainer 2, was released in 2003.

Players have only three lives to complete six exams in each difficulty. Players can lose lives by either failing to reach a quota, not defusing any C4 or letting the guards hit the player. In order to complete the competition mode, players must lose one life on player 1 and lose one life on the other. If the players fail each mode, they can either try the same mode again or select a different mode. If the players completed each mode, they can select another mode until a difficulty is completed. Each difficulty consists of six stages. Players can put initials after completing the Commissioner difficulty. Shooting the incorrect targets receives a –100 points penalty.
Police Trainer 2

Police Trainer 2 is a light gun arcade game and the sequel to Police Trainer. It was released by American companies Phantom Systems and Team Play Inc. in 2003 as both a stand-up cabinet and sit-downLike its predecessor Police Trainer, players have three lives for the entire game. On simulation stages, players will have a health gauge. If the gauge is empty or if the player fails to reach a quota in a stage, one life is lost. cabinet.
Pollux

Pollux is a vertical scrolling space themed shoot 'em up game where you take control of a spaceship that has to terminate the evil main computer of a 22nd century space station.

You fight a variety of space crafts, static guns and bosses. While playing destroyed enemies drop power-ups. These include: an automatic shooting power-up (A), plus one (limited) fire bomb (B), weapon power-up (P), short speed power-up (S), plus one up (U), homing missiles and three weapon patron power-ups (straight, three-way and four directions). You can play solo or with a friend.
Poly-Net Warriors

Poly-Net Warriors is a cutesy sci-fi first-person shooter developed and released by Konami for arcades in 1993, exclusively in Japan. One of Konami's earliest arcade games to feature polygonal 3D, Poly-Net Warriors puts players in timed arena battles through the eyes of one of four different-colored robots (the "Poly-Net Warriors"). Similar to Faceball 2000, players launch balls at enemies to drain their health while avoiding opposing balls. Along with linked free-for-all multiplayer, the game features single-player matches against themed teams of three enemy robots.
Poly-Play

Poly-Play is the only arcade machine created in East Germany. It is a collection of eight different games.
Hirschjagd (Deer Hunt): the player controls a hunter whose goal is to hunt deer. The screen contains a number of trees that hunter and deer can not move through. The hunter has 10 shots in his gun, but ammunition is not subtracted if the shot is a hit. Shots are also removed if a short timer has finished counting down. While the deer can leave the border of the screen and reappear on the other side, the hunter does not have that ability. The game ends when he is out of shots. Successful hits count towards the score.
Hase und Wolf (Hare and Wolf): a Pac-Man variant. The player controls a hare and must eat all peas and carrots within a labyrinth while being pursued by a wolf. Eating a pea gains 1 point, eating a carrot 5, and eating a randomly appearing pear gains 7 points. Hare and wolf can use tunnels that allow them to leave the screen on one side and reappear on the other.
Polygonet Commanders

Polygonet Commanders is a first-person 3-D tank shooting game in which the player takes control of an armed combat tank and engages opposing forces across a series of polygon-based battlefields, fulfilling kill quotas within time limits to advance. 

The player drives the tank from a first-person viewpoint, using dual joysticks (one for each tread) to steer and turn. The objective on each stage is to eliminate a set number of enemy tanks within a time limit; destroying enemies gives additional time. Progressing through stages unlocks further battles on varied terrain.
Pong

Pong (marketed as PONG) is one of the earliest arcade video games and the very first sports arcade video game. It is a tennis sports game featuring simple two-dimensional graphics. While other arcade video games such as Computer Space came before it, Pong was one of the first video games to reach mainstream popularity. The aim is to defeat an opponent in a simulated table-tennis game by earning a higher score. The game was originally manufactured by Atari Incorporated (Atari), which released it in 1972. Allan Alcorn created Pong as a training exercise assigned to him by Atari co-founder Nolan Bushnell. Bushnell based the idea on an electronic ping-pong game included in the Magnavox Odyssey, which later resulted in a lawsuit against Atari. Surprised by the quality of Alcorn's work, Bushnell and Atari co-founder Ted Dabney decided to manufacture the game.
Pong Doubles

Follow-up game to Pong but up to four people can play. Two players on one side bat a ball to the other side where it is fielded by the other two players. You can even play one on one if you are ambidextrous.
Ponpoko

Ponpoko is a fixed screen platform game and has the player control a Tanuki traversing around a pattern, walking and jumping on platforms, climbing ladders, dodging enemy caterpillars and collecting foodstuffs.

The player has a limited time to complete the pattern before the Tanuki's hunger level drops down to starvation. The pattern is complete when all foodstuffs are collected. There are also mystery pots which may contain either a bonus item or a deadly snake. Each new pattern adds more enemies and a more difficult layout. The Tanuki dies when making contact with an enemy, falling down a great height or from starvation.
Pony Express
The Pony Express is a classic UK pub fruit machine manufactured by Bell-Fruit Games (historically the Bell-Fruit Manufacturing Co. Ltd.).
Poolshark

Poolshark is a pool game for one or two players. The rules are different from a typical pool game played in a bar. Each player receives 30 seconds to pocket as many of the 15 balls as possible. Each sunk ball is worth one point. Pocketing all balls gains a 15 second bonus round in which additional points can be scored. Depending on the operator settings there can be multiple rounds before the winner is decided. The cue ball is directly controlled by the joystick, so there are no cue sticks involved. If the player accidentally pockets the cue ball the round ends prematurely.
Poosho Poosho

Arcade game released in Korea in November 1999 the title of which translates from Korean as "Break Break". Sequel to the F2 System game "Jumping Break" released in February 1999. Game play is similar to Breakout where player controls a character on bottom of screen that is used to bounce a ball to top and destroy various items for points. A jump button also allows the paddle to jump to meet the ball.
Pootan
This game is a bootleg of "Pooyan" with some graphical changes.
Pooyan

Pooyan is a fixed-screen shooter in which Mama Pig attempts to rescue her kidnapped piglets from a pack of wolves. She rides vertically along the side of a cliff in a rope-suspended gondola, firing arrows horizontally at wolves carried by balloons. The game alternates between two main scenes, followed periodically by bonus rounds.

In the first scene, wolves descend toward the pigs’ home while throwing rocks at Mama. Shooting a balloon sends its occupant falling, while rocks can be intercepted for additional points. Wolves that reach the ground climb ladders beside the gondola and attempt to bite Mama from behind.
Pop 'n Bounce

Pop'n Bounce is a puzzle game similar to Break Out; the player must bounce a ball off a paddle in order to knock out a wall of sprites. However, in Pop'n Bounce, the sprites are of assorted living creatures instead of bricks.

Pop'n Bounce has been released for the arcade in Japan (as Gapporin) and the US. Used MVS cartridges seem to be uncommon even online. There is no difference between the Japan and US versions of the game other than the title. The game was not released for the home version of Neo-Geo.
Pop Bingo

And another game that combines standard puzzle mechanics with an unrelated game, this time Snow Pop is expanded upon with a Bingo element. Now some of the snowballs have letters written on them that are used to clear a bingo chart. The player who first completes a line on the chart wins. In between stages waits a bonus round, featuring nude photographs. Feels kinda awkward in combination with the overall cutesy style of the game.
Pop Flamer

In this action arcade game, you play the role of a flamethrower-wielding mouse.

You explore each round - there are multiple screens and scrolling graphics) - and your aim is to find and pop all the red balloons. You dodge or incinerate enemy creatures.
Pop Moto Racing

The Pop Moto Racing arcade machine (also released as Pop Moto or Pop Moto Twin Player) is a 3D motorcycle racing simulator developed by Belrare and released around 2010.

Unlike traditional simulation bike games, Pop Moto blends fast-paced motorcycle riding with Mario Kart-style combat elements, featuring a fantasy aesthetic rather than realistic city streets.
The game trades realistic physics for high-octane vehicular combat. Players drive physical replica motorcycles and can pick up various power-ups scattered across the tracks to disrupt their opponents.
Pop'n Music

The first game includes Beginner Mode, Normal Mode, and Hard Mode. Beginner is the easiest mode, starting out with a short tutorial stage, and only two songs can be chosen instead of the usual three. Mimi and Nyami are the default characters for this mode.

Normal Mode is the standard mode, with three stages per round. Characters will interrupt or block some of the play area using an ojama-like effect. Mary is the default character for Normal Mode.

Hard Mode is the final mode. While it remains mostly similar to Normal Mode, it introduces Ojama. Ojama are activated at random in each song played. The King is the default character in Hard Mode.

The CS game also includes Training Mode and Free Mode. Training Mode allows players to play a specific segment of a song, play at different speeds, or toggle ojama settings. Free Mode has all unlocked songs available for play, and isn't limited to three songs per round.
Pop'n Music 2

Pop'n Music 2 is one of the many titles in Konami's long-running rhythm game franchise. Notes scroll toward the bottom of the screen along nine tracks, and the player must tap the correct buttons in time with the music to play along. Play well, and the "groove meter" increases, but play poorly and it will drop. If the groove meter is high enough at the end of the song, the player can move on to the next song.
Pop'n Music 3

Pop'n Music 3 is a Japanese music/rhythm video game, developed by Konami and Bemani in 1999, and the third release of the Pop'n Music series.

This installment features a new game mode called Hyper Mode, where you can play song courses (in similar fashion to Expert Mode in the old beatmania games). Like the name suggests, all of the songs are Hyper charts. During game play, the groove gauge starts out as full, and cannot be replenished except by clearing stages, which give back a little health. Once the groove gauge is depleted, a message "DANGER" is shown as well as a countdown timer. During the countdown timer, if you achieve enough GREATs, the game continues; otherwise, the game ends.
Pop'n Music 4

Pop'n Music 4 (ポップンミュージック 4 Poppun Myūjikku 4?) is a Japanese music/rhythm video developed by Konami and Bemani in 2000, and the fourth release of the Pop'n Music series.
First Pop'n Music game to run on BEMANI FIREBEAT HARDWARE, which was also used for Beatmania III, KEYBOARDMANIA, and ee'MALL. The colors and graphics were noticeably more colorful and more detailed than ever as a result of the more powerful hardware. Firebeat would be used through Pop'n Music 8.
First Pop'n Music game in the series to have speed modifiers. However, the only one is 2X.
First Pop'n Music arcade game in which new AC songs have HYPER notecharts.
This is the first game that has to tell you what the BPM of a song was.
First Pop'n Music game in the series to have a distinctive interface (1-3 were essentially the same interface with color differences). In addition, all the menus feature new music re-arranged by Seiya Murai.
Pop'n Music 5

Pop'n Music 5 was the last one to have a weird fascination for naked women in the ranking screens. It was not the last one to insert random proverbs wherever possible, though. Oh, it also introduced EX charts, but very few songs had them, and they could only be played in the also new Extra Stage.
First Pop'n Music game with Internet Ranking and CHALLENGE MODE.
Unlike NORMAL MODE, CHALLENGE MODE has no stage limit, and you can play any three songs you wish.
You can still only play the same song once a credit, though.
First mainline arcade pop'n music game with 5LINE. The mode had earlier appeared in pop'n music アニメロ and in the CS games.
First pop'n music game to let you set mods before each song.
First pop'n music arcade game since the the original with no new CS crossovers in the songlist.
First pop'n music game with EXtra STAGE, which introduced a new difficulty level: EX.
EX charts can only be played in EXtra STAGE in pop'n music 5, hence the difficulty's name.
Pop'n Music 6

Pop'n Music 6 is a Japanese music/rhythm video game developed by Konami and Bemani in 2001, and the sixth release of the Pop'n Music series. Notes scroll toward the bottom of the screen along nine tracks, and the player must tap the correct buttons in time with the music to play along. Play well, and the "groove meter" increases, but play poorly and it will drop. If the groove meter is high enough at the end of the song, the player can move on to the next song.
Pop'n Music 7

Pop'n Music 7 is one of the many titles in Konami's long-running rhythm game franchise. Notes scroll toward the bottom of the screen along nine tracks, and the player must tap the correct buttons in time with the music to play along. Play well, and the "groove meter" increases, but play poorly and it will drop. If the groove meter is high enough at the end of the song, the player can move on to the next song.
Pop'n Music 8

Pop'n Music 8 is a Japanese music/rhythm video game developed by Konami and Bemani and released in May 2002 on Arcade and on PlayStation 2 on 2003. It is the 8th main instalment in the Pop'n Music series.
Pop'n Music 9

Pop'n Music 9 is one of the many titles in Konami's long-running rhythm game franchise. Notes scroll toward the bottom of the screen along nine tracks, and the player must tap the correct buttons in time with the music to play along. Play well, and the "groove meter" increases, but play poorly and it will drop. If the groove meter is high enough at the end of the song, the player can move on to the next song.

This version includes over 110 tracks, primarily from the arcade version of the same title. The arcade, free, challenge, battle, and study modes from previous releases have returned. Unlockable songs and items are obtained through a dungeon-crawling minigame at the end of every arcade play.
Pop'n Music Animelo

Pop'n Music Animelo is a game in the Pop'n Music series of video games from Konami. This version is comprised largely of anime and television show songs (hence the games sub-title "animation melody").

Gameplay is identical to other games in the series. The Pop'n Music controller features 9 buttons organized in two rows. After you select a song, the screen will show 9 colored "pop notes" descending towards the timing bar. You must watch the screen, and hit the corresponding colored buttons in time with the music and the notes on the screen.
Pop'n Music Animelo 2

Pop'n Music Animelo 2 is a game in the Pop'n Music series of video games from Konami. Like the original Pop'n Music Animelo, this version has a song list comprised of anime and television show songs. This version also contains "Double" and "Triple" modifiers, which add one or two extra notes for every note in the chart.

The core gameplay is identical to other games in the series. The Pop'n Music controller features 9 buttons organised in two rows. After you select a song, the screen will show 9 coloured "pop notes" descending towards the timing bar. You must watch the screen, and hit the corresponding coloured buttons in time with the music and the notes on the screen.
Pop'n Music Mickey Tunes
Pop'n Music Mickey Tunes is a musical video game published by Konami for several platforms in 2000. The game is a Mickey Mouse and Disney-themed installment of Konami's Pop'n Music franchise.
Pop'n Music: Sunny Park

Pop'n Music (ポップンミュージック, Poppun Myūjikku), commonly abbreviated as Pop'n, PM or PNM and stylized as pop'n music, is a music video game series in the Bemani series made by Konami. The games are known for their bright colors, upbeat songs, and cute cartoon character graphics. Originally released in 1998, the series has had over fifteen home releases in Japan as well as many arcade versions.

Unlike most of Konami's Bemani series, the Pop'n Music interface is not designed to represent any actual musical instrument. Instead, it uses nine buttons, each three-and-a-half-inches in diameter, laid out in two rows (Since the location test of Wonderland, a multitouch panel is added). Five buttons are the bottom row, the other four being the top. Like in most Bemani games, color-coded notes (in this game called "Pop-kun" (ポップ君) and anthropomorphized with faces) fall from the top of the screen in nine columns that correspond to the buttons.
Pop'n Pop
Pop'n Pop is an arcade and console puzzle game release by Taito in 1997. It has been ported to the PlayStation and Game Boy Color formats.
Pop'n Stage EX

This music game is an updated version of Pop'n Stage, called Pop'n Stage EX, and it was released on December 20th, 1999, a few months after the original, that included two extra songs, several Pop'n Music 3 songs, and more difficulties.

It shares a development between Bemani's most popular rhythm game, DanceDanceRevolution, and South Korea's popular dancing game, Pump It Up. Unlike the original Pop'n Music series, Pop'n Stage includes ten "switches" (four diagonals and a center on each side, just like Pump It Up's panel placement). This only supports one player at a time; six-switch and ten-switch modes are available (corresponding to Pump It Up's half double and full double; in other words, 6-switch mode doesn't use the four outer corners).
Pop's Pop's

Pop's Pop's is a relatively obscure retro arcade game released in 1999 by the South Korean developer and publisher Afega.

It is a one or two-player quiz/music game.
When a round begins, the game plays a music track, and the primary objective is to correctly identify or retrieve the title of the song.
Popeye (Fruit Machine)

The JPM Popeye fruit machine is a highly popular, vintage Amusement with Prize (AWP) pub slot machine developed by the prominent UK manufacturer JPM International. Released during the late 199x era, it remains highly sought after by retro arcade enthusiasts and private home games room collectors.

It utilizes a feature-rich "board game" layout on the upper glass screen. Players advance through theme-specific mechanics such as dodging the antagonist Brutus, collecting spinach power-ups, and building multiplier values.
Popeye (Nintendo)

Popeye is a fixed-screen platform game in which the player controls the title character as he attempts to collect tokens of affection dropped by Olive Oyl. Each of the game’s three stages uses a different arrangement of platforms, stairs, ladders, ledges, and other devices. Popeye must gather every required item while avoiding Brutus and the other dangers moving through the playfield.

Popeye can walk, climb, descend, and drop through specially marked ledges, but cannot jump normally. His only direct action is a punch, which destroys bottles, skulls, vultures, and certain other projectiles. Brutus continually pursues him and can reach between adjacent platforms by jumping upward or leaning downward. Popeye normally cannot harm him and loses a life if struck by Brutus, one of the Sea Hag’s projectiles, or another hostile object.
PoPo Bear

PoPo Bear is a rare, retro arcade game published by BMC (Bao Ma Technology Co.) in June 2000. It runs on its own proprietary hardware, also named "POPOBEAR". While original physical cabinets are difficult to find today, the game is well-documented and playable on modern hardware via emulation.

Designed for up to two players, the control panel features an 8-way joystick paired with 3 action buttons per player.
Popper
A rabbit hops on cubes changing their colors.
Porky

Porky was developed by Shinkai, Inc, and published by Magic Electronics in 1985

A driving/shooting game where the player controls Porky, a big pig, who attempts to shoot piglets out of the sky with sausages while avoiding the big bad wolf.
Port Man

Port Man was developed by Taito in Japan in 1982. Nova Games published the game under license in North America.

Catch the luggage that falls from the top conveyor belt and throw it up into one of four berths on the ship. You need to get four in each berth without getting hit by a rock thrown by the man on the ship, getting run over by the luggage cars or before running out of luggage on the conveyor belt. In the second level, you throw a rock up at some crates of dynamite, knocking one down. You need to catch it before it hits bottom. When a crate reaches the bottom, it explodes, removing the lowest level of your playing area. If you are hit by a rock thrown by the man on the conveyor belt or if you are on the same level with the exploding crate, you lose a life. You get points for every crate you catch. Then you return to the ship, only this time the speed has incensed.
Portraits

aim right to capture a number of animals, of four - then five - different kinds. Beware, the animals can destroy your camera. When you get high score, two lights in the cabinet, over the monitor, will light, and a b/w camera will start to capture images. So, the recordman/woman can insert a picture of him/herself between the introductory screens!
Pot of Gold (ACE)
Pot of Gold is a slot fruit machine released by ACE.
Pot of Gold (Tong Electronic/Game Plan)

Pot of Gold was developed by Ton Electronic and published/manufactured by Game Plan in 1982.

A sleuth runs through the forests of Ireland to claim the pot of gold. Avoid the deadly leprechaun who will occasionally move the gold elsewhere in the woods.
Poto Poto

Poto Poto was produced by Sega in 1994.

Place tiles so that at least four in a row or group touch each other. Use a bomb to clear a group of tiles in the blast area. Any tiles that fall are transferred to your opponent's side. Whoever's tiles reach the bottom loses.
Pots Of Gold

The Pots O Gold fruit machine is a classic, reel-based pub slot machine manufactured by the legendary British arcade brand, Bell-Fruit Gaming (Bellfruit). Depending on the era and exact model version you are referring to, it is highly regarded among collectors and arcade enthusiasts for its engaging board-game style feature play.

Standard fruit machine mechanics including nudges, holds, and completion of name or number trails to trigger a "Pots of Gold streak" feature complete with iconic 90s digital sound effects.
Pound for Pound
Pound for Pound is an overhead boxing game by Irem release in 1990 with big and detailed characters and a high difficulty.
Pound Stretcher

Pound Stretcher is a classic UK pub fruit machine (amusement with prizes, or AWP) manufactured by Ace Coin Equipment (often simply known as ACE). Originally released in the 1980s, it stands out as an iconic piece of arcade history from an era when mechanical setups dominated British watering holes.
Povar / Sobrat' Buran / Agroprom

"Povar / Sobrat' Buran / Agroprom" (повар / собрать буран / агропром) is an unlicensed arcade compilation that combines three games originally created by Ultimate Play the Game for the ZX Spectrum home computer: Cookie, Jetpac, and Pssst. The compilation replaces the original cassette interface with a coin-operated menu system written in Russian, inviting the player to insert a coin and choose one of the three titles.
- Cookie (Povar) casts the player as a chef fighting animated ingredients
- Jetpac (Sobrat' Buran) follows an astronaut assembling and refueling a spacecraft
- Pssst (Agroprom) has the player defending a sunflower from invading pests
Power Balls

Power Balls is a block breaking style action game developed and published by Playmark for Arcades.

When starting the game, players choose a character, which each have their own strengths and weaknesses.

Players then start a stage on the left side of the screen with various objects littering the right. A ball is then hit towards the right which will damage the objects. When the ball is returned towards the player they must hit the ball back or they will lose a life.

Once all of the objects are destroyed, players will move to the next stage. Every set amount of stages players will face a boss which must be hit in the same way as the obstacles.
Power Blade

Power Blade is another NES title that was converted to run on Nintendo's PlayChoice-10 cabinets. 

Game description:

It is the year 2191, and Earth's blissful existence was governed by a master computer. Then suddenly, its master control program malfunctioned, and people panicked, ensuring total chaos. Secret Agent Nova is called in to locate agents located in six sectors. These agents hold an ID card which Nova must acquire to gain access to the security room within each sector. There, he must defeat the guards and obtain secret tape units, and if Nova obtains six of these, he will be able to gain entry to the control center and defeat the guard to destroy the computer and restore order to society.

Power Blade is a platform game, in which you must run through the level, destroying various enemies, and exit through the door. However, you can't leave each sector without locating agents. By destroy enemies, you can get power-ups which restore your energy or upgrade your weapon.
Power Drift

Choose from wacky drivers, like Jason the Skinhead or Jeronimo the Mohican and rev your way through all the stomach-churning circuits! Watch the dust fly and the wheels spin as you screech over a roller coaster track and wave goodbye to your opponents. Roar over mounds of mud, drive through the desert, slip 'n' slide on snow-covered tarmac and race your way through the night to face the final lap! CAREFUL! Power Drift is no easy ride! If you're heading for a collision hold on to your seat and enjoy those 360 degree spins before you bump back down to earth!
Power Drive

Power Drive' is an arcade racing game featuring monster trucks from 1987 by Bally Midway.
