Another interesting feature of "QUARTERBACK" is the ability to keep track of over 15 categories of game play statistics and the fact that each player's salary reflects his/her overall performance in these areas. Players compete for the top salary.
Quartet

Your job is to basically find the end-of-level boss, and then defeat it to obtain the key that will open the level exit, but your task is made difficult by the planet's inhabitants. Get the jet-pack to make it easier to navigate the level and shoot any inhabitants that get in the way. These inhabitants will leave behind something that you can get to increase your score, and the inhabitants will eventually regenerate. If any one of them touches you while you have the jet-pack, you land on the ground or the nearest platform, and have to get it again; and the same rule applies to the key.
Quartet 2

Quartet 2 was produced by Sega in 1986. (Sun Corporation of America published it in North America)

Human characters collect guns and power-ups to destroy a variety of robots in a space base. Defeat the boss character and collect the key to unlock the base's door and move on to the next level. Up to two people may join in on the fun.

This game was released shortly after the dedicated Quartet. Quartet 2 is not a sequel but rather a conversion kit that could be placed in two-player cabinets. The only real difference between the two game is Quartet 2 allows up to two players to choose from the four available characters. The game has side-scrolling action and a Gauntlet-like join-in type play. The four characters each have a different name and wear a different color. They are Joe (yellow), Mary (red), Lee (blue) and Edgar (green).
Quarth Cooperative

In this romhack of the arcade game Quarth, the cooperative mode is changed in such a way that both players can play the full range of the play area and can pass each other. It is also possible to play the cooperative mode with only a single player. When you select the cooperative board by pressing the player 1 Fire button, it will start the 1 player cooperative game. When you select it by pressing the player 2 Fire button, it will start the 2 player cooperative game. You also need the Blockhole parent rom to run this game.
Quasar

Quasar was produced by Zaccaria in 1980.

Quasar is a space based shoot-em-up with four distinct phases of game-play.

The first phase is similar to Space Invaders, where UFOs appear at the top of the screen, and move towards the bottom while firing. Your space ship is confined to the bottom row, and fires vertically, with one bullet on screen at a time. The initial wave consists of 8 UFOs, but subsequent levels increase these to 16 UFOs.

The second phase has more in common with Asteroids. Your ship can move about the screen using the left, right and thrust buttons. Waves of two types of UFOs will cross the screen from either the left or the right, while firing at you. Your aim is to destroy all of the UFOs without being shot, and before an energy counter runs out. Any remaining energy is added to your score after completing the phase.

In the third phase, a quasar appears at the top of the screen, shining a tractor beam towards the bottom.
Quazzi Mo' Dough
Quazzi Mo' Dough is a classic UK pub slot fruit machine manufactured by the developer Scorpion (running on the popular Scorpion 4 hardware platform).
Queen of the Nile

Queen of the Nile is a highly iconic, Egyptian-themed video slot (or "fruit machine") developed by Aristocrat Gaming. First launched in physical land-based casinos, it popularized the famous "Ancient Egypt" genre of slot games and was later adapted into several variants—including Queen of the Nile Deluxe and Queen of the Nile Legends—as well as mobile-compatible online versions.
Quest of D

Quest of D is an arcade game developed by Sega AM2 and published by Sega on the Chihiro arcade board. It is the fifth trading card arcade game by Sega, following World Club Champion Football, Mushiking: The King of Beetles, The Key of Avalon and Love and Berry: Dress up and Dance!. It is an action-role playing game in a dark fantasy setting and is online enabled similar to previous AM2 titles Virtua Fighter 4 and Sega Network Taisen Mahjong MJ.
Quester

Quester is a block breaker video game, often compared to Taito's Arkanoid. Using a rotary knob, the player controls a paddle-like craft fixed at the bottom of the screen, the objective being to deflect a ball towards a large formation of bricks in each round. A life is lost when the player misses the ball and it falls of-screen. Some blocks contain power-up items that can help the player in the stage, such as increasing the width of the paddle, place a barrier at the bottom of the screen to prevent the ball from being lost, and a forcefield that will spit out eight other balls if touched. Some stages contain "killer meteors", which can decrease the paddle's size if touched.
Quick & Crash

Quick & Crash is a rare, highly collectible electromechanical shooting gallery arcade machine released by Namco in 1999. Instead of using a standard video monitor to display graphics, it uses an ingenious system of physical moving targets, mirrors, and sensors to create an immersive quick-draw test of speed and accuracy. The game has achieved a dedicated cult following due to its unique mechanics and satisfying theatrical feedback.

 Players must start each round with the light gun resting inside a physical holster mounted to the front of the cabinet. The game will not progress until you return the gun to its holster.
Quid Rock
"Quid Rock" is a classic UK pub fruit machine manufactured by QPS Interactive. It was built using the popular Scorpion 4 hardware cabinet platform.
Quid Vicious
Quid Vicious is a classic UK pub Amusement with Prize (AWP) fruit machine created by the manufacturer QPS. The game features a play on words based on the famous punk rock musician Sid Vicious.
Quintoon
A one player casino game published and developed by BFM in 1993.
Quiz & Dragons: Capcom Quiz Game

Quiz & Dragons: Capcom Quiz Game is a question and answer game released in arcades in 1992. The game combined elements of RPGs with that of board games to create a unique twist to the quiz game genre.

The game plays similar to a board game, where the player is given a predetermined dice roll that moves the player up to six spaces on the board; however, if the player is so given the choice, he can move to a space of his choosing if there is a fork in the road. After landing on a space, the player is given a series of questions (the amount of questions needed to be answered increase as the game progresses) in order to proceed back to the board for another dice roll. The player is given a time limit to answer the question, with points given that vary based on how fast the player answered the question correctly. If the player is successful in answering a question, one of the orbs above the enemy's portrait will light up, indicating a correct answer.
Quiz & Variety Sukusuku Inufuku

Quiz & Variety Sukusuku Inufuku (クイズ＆バラエテイすくすく犬福) is a unique, Japanese arcade game released in September 1998 by Video System Co. Ltd. The game blended traditional trivia questions with digital pet-raising mechanics, framed by a distinct sense of oddball humor. It was notably the final arcade game developed by Video System before they filed for bankruptcy, with their game copyrights later being acquired by Hamster Corporation.

The core loop revolves around adopting and nurturing an "Inufuku"—a blobby, round, white creature that is meant to look like an adorable cross between a dog, rabbit, and cat.
Quiz 365

Quiz 365 was released in September 1994 in Japan.
Sales by Taito Corp. in Hong Kong and Taiwan.
The title of this game translates from Japanese as 'New Daily Quiz Show - Quiz 365'. In this game, Japanese National Broadcast Station 'NHK' name changed to 'HNK'. Between PM and AM T.V. programs, the sponsor introductions are similar to real Japanese T.V. program's sponsors.
Quiz Aa! Megami-sama: Tatakau Tsubasa to Tomoni

Humans are blindly under the impression that they control the world. However both the Demons and Goddesses are competing for their share of control. It is up to Keiichi Morisato to maintain balance between both entities.

The player meets various characters such as Belldandy and her relatives, who challenge the player to quizzes made up of questions with multiple choice answers. The questions revolve around the Oh My Goddess! franchise.
Quiz and Variety Suku Suku Inufuku 2

As the sequel to SukuSuku Inufuku ("quickly, lucky dog"), Motto SukuSuku ("more quickly") again features the rather odd-looking dog Inufuku, who also has cameos in some of the later Sonic Wings games. The game spans a year; in January, the player adopts an Inufuku to raise. Throughout the year, the player encounters a variety of characters who challenge her/him to quizzes and competitive games. The player's performance on the challenges influences how her/his Inufuku looks as it grows up. The characters, locations, and title cards for each month that show up in the game also vary. Lord River-n-White also appears as Taro Kitashirakawa, the name he is given in Rabio Lepus, and Mao Mao also has a cameo.
Quiz Bishoujo Senshi Sailor Moon - Chiryoku Tairyoku Toki no Un

Quiz!! Pretty Soldier Sailor Moon - Luck, Intellect and Physical Strength- (Kuizu! Bishōjo senshi sērāmūn ~ chiryoku tairyoku-ji no un ~ /クイズ！美少女戦士セーラームーン ～知力・体力・時の運～) is a Japanese video game released exclusively for arcade game-machines in 1997.

After the player has chosen a Senshi, the game will begin. In order to advance, the player must throw the digital die. The player will move forward the number of steps shown on the dice; this is where he or she will encounter a monster-of-the-day (or boss). The player is then automatically entered into a quiz.

After answering several questions, the player returns to the map, and can roll the dice again. Apart from quizzes, the game has several other features; including: animated scenes, full-screen animation, voice overs, music and much more.
Quiz Channel Question

The arcade video game Quiz Channel Question is a classic trivia game published in 1993 by KM Korea Co., Ltd.. Originally featuring regional variants released across Asia—including licensed editions in Korea and Japan—it remains a nostalgic piece of retro gaming history that can be emulated today on platforms like M.A.M.E.
Quiz Chikyu Bouei Gun
Quiz Chikyu Bouei Gun is a Miscellaneous game, published by Taito Corporation, which was released in Japan in 1991
Quiz Crayon Shinchan
Quiz Crayon Shin-Chan is a Miscellaneous game, published by Taito Corporation, which was released in Japan in 1993.
Quiz Daisousa Sen: The Last Count Down

Quiz Daisousa Sen: The Last Count Down is a quiz adventure game series released by SNK. The first game, Quiz Daisōsa Sen: The Last Count Down, was first released on July 1, 1991. The second title, Quiz Meitantei Neo & Geo: Quiz Daisousasen Part 2 (クイズ迷探偵ＮＧ/大走査線パート２), was out in arcades on April 24, 1992. A cellphone application visually based on the first game was made with updated questions in 2006.
Quiz de Idol! Hot Debut

Quiz de Idol! Hot Debut is a niche, idol-themed trivia and quiz arcade game developed by Moss and published by the legendary Japanese manufacturer Psikyo in 2000. Far from a traditional shoot-'em-up that Psikyo is famous for, this game combines the elements of an idol-production simulator with fast-paced multiple-choice trivia.
Quiz DNA no Hanran

Quiz DNA no Hanran (translated from Japanese as "Quiz Revolt of DNA") is a coin-operated trivia arcade game released exclusively in Japan in 1992 by the developer Face.

As a Japanese quiz game, the interface and trivia text are entirely in Japanese characters (Kanji/Kana). Reviewers note that the game features a surprisingly fast pace—allowing players to cycle through up to five questions in rapid succession—and incorporates surreal visual motifs, including floating sprites that lend it an aesthetic reminiscent of early sci-fi fantasy games like Phantasy Star.
Quiz Do Re Mi Fa Grand Prix

Quiz Do Re Mi Fa Grand Prix is a series of music-themed trivia quiz games developed and published by Konami for arcade platforms in Japan. The games are heavily focused on music trivia, pop culture, and audio-based challenges like intro-quizzes (where players guess a song from its opening notes).
Quiz Do Re Mi Fa Grand Prix 2: Shin-Kyoku Nyuukadayo

"Quiz Do Re Mi Fa Grand Prix 2: Shin-Kyoku Nyuukadayo is a quiz game that continues the tradition of music-themed trivia challenges, where players answer questions related to various topics, with a strong focus on music and pop culture. The title roughly translates to "Quiz Do Re Mi Fa Grand Prix 2: A New Song is Coming!" reflecting its updated content and gameplay.

The game supports up to two players and uses a standard joystick and button configuration typical of arcade setups. Players are presented with multiple-choice questions and must answer correctly to progress through the stages. The game features a variety of question types, including those that require quick reflexes and knowledge of Japanese pop culture, especially music.
Quiz F1 1-2 Finish

Quiz F1 1-2 Finish is a 1992 arcade trivia and racing hybrid game developed and published by Irem.

• Choosing a Team: Players pick from four available F1-themed teams at the start, each with different handling and performance traits.
• Qualifying: Fast-paced true/false (○×) questions decide your starting grid spot based on your speed and accuracy.
• The Races: The game features a 16-Grand-Prix season. Answering trivia questions correctly drives your car forward, while wrong answers cause you to drop down the leaderboard.
Quiz Gakuen Paradise
Quiz Gakuen Paradise is a Quiz game, developed by Sankindo and published by NMK, which was released in Japan in 1991.
Quiz Gakumon no Susume

Quiz Gakumon no Susume (クイズ 学問ノススメ) is an arcade trivia game developed and published by Konami in January 1993, released exclusively in Japan. Roughly translating to "Quiz: Get That Scholarship", the game casts players as students entering a quiz academy where they answer a barrage of questions delivered by different classroom teachers. The game features over 20 distinct trivia categories and a pool of roughly 10,000 unique questions.
Quiz Gekiretsu Scramble

Quiz Gekiretsu Scramble is a quiz game and a sequel to Quiz Gakuen Paradise. It features a fast-paced trivia format where players answer questions across a wide range of topics within a time limit. 

The game’s title can be roughly translated as "Quiz Violent Scramble: Paradise Academy 2," and is set in a school-themed environment, continuing the series' focus on education-based quiz challenges. The characters Geki and Retsu, who are central to the game’s narrative, give the game its name.
Quiz Ghost Hunter

Quiz Ghost Hunter was produced by Sega in 1994.

A Japanese quiz game about ghost hunters.
Quiz H.Q.

Quiz H.Q. was produced by Taito in 1990.

A quiz game based on the popular Chase series. This was a Japan-only release.
Quiz Jinsei Gekijoh

Quiz Jinsei Gekijoh (クイズ人生劇場, translating to "Quiz Human Life Theatre") is a Japan-exclusive quiz arcade game developed and published by Taito. Released in March 1993, the game uniquely blends trivia-based gameplay with digital board game elements.

The title utilizes a Sugoroku (traditional Japanese board game) format where player progression across the board is dictated by answering trivia questions successfully. The game tracks the fictional "human life" journey of the players' avatars.
The game stands out for its extensive audio design, featuring custom music composed by Yasuko Yamada and full vocal performances by regular Taito sound personnel, including Kazuko Umino, Norihiro Furukawa, Shuichiro Nakazawa, and Naoto Yagishita.
Quiz Keitai Q mode
Quiz Keitai Q mode (クイズケータイＱモード) is a quiz game developed by Amedio and published by Taito for the Sega NAOMI arcade system.
Quiz King of Fighters

The KOF cast decides to settle their differences in a new way - quiz battles. When Art of Fighting's Yuri is kidnapped yet again, players pick one of four King of Fighters characters (alongside Samurai Shodown guest characters Haohmaru and Nakoruru) and head out on a journey to rescue her and test their knowledge. The overworld is represented as a board game with branching paths; players start their turn by rolling a die to decide how far to travel, then duel the character at that position in a quiz battle. Characters have health, which they lose at every incorrect answer; run out of health, it's game over.
Quiz Kokology

Quiz Kokology: Quiz & Shinri Game is a rare, Japanese quiz arcade game released by Tecmo in 1992. Based on "Kokology"—the Japanese psychological study of the "kokoro" (mind or spirit)—the game presents indirect, situational questions designed to reveal a player's true personality traits, feelings about relationships, and sub-conscious behaviors. In a unique stylistic choice, players are represented on-screen as bees. A sequel, Quiz Kokology 2, followed shortly after in 1993.
Quiz Kokology 2

Quiz Kokology 2 (fully titled Quiz Kokology 2: Quiz & Shinri Game) is a rare Japanese arcade trivia and personality game developed and published by Tecmo in 1993.
The game is based on the popular psychological concept of "Kokology" (derived from the Japanese word kokoro, meaning "mind" or "spirit"). Instead of testing general knowledge, the game places players in hypothetical, everyday scenarios and interprets their responses to reveal hidden personality traits, attitudes, and emotional behaviors.

Similar to its 1992 predecessor, the game acts like an interactive, gamified Rorschach test using words and situational scenarios rather than inkblots. A player might be asked an innocent question—such as designing a pattern on a plain mug or choosing how long they would wait in line for a roller coaster—and the game provides a humorous or surprisingly deep psychological analysis of what that choice says about their approach to love, sex, family, or work.
Quiz Magic Academy
Quiz Magic Academy (マジックアカデミー?) is a quiz video game developed and published by Konami and released on Arcade on July 24, 2003 in Japan. It is the first entry in the Quiz Magic Academy series.
Quiz Meitantei Neo & Geo: Quiz Daisousa Sen Part 2

Quiz Meitantei Neo & Geo: Quiz Daisousa Sen Part 2 is a quiz adventure game series released by SNK. The title of this game translates from Japanese as 'Quiz Main Detective Work Neo & Geo: Quiz Great Investigation Track Part 2'.
Quiz Mekurumeku Story
Quiz Mekurumeku Story (クイズめくるめくストーリー) is a Japanese puzzle and party quiz arcade game released by Sega in 1992.
Quiz Mobile Suit Gundam: Monsenshi

Quiz Mobile Suit Gundam: Monsenshi (also known as Quiz Mobile Suit Gundam: Tou Senshi or Mobile Suit Gundam: Quiz Warrior) is a 2006 Japanese arcade trivia game.

Players answer multiple-choice trivia questions covering characters, mobile suits, and storylines from across the Mobile Suit Gundam universe.
Quiz Nanairo Dreams: Nijiirochou no Kiseki

Quiz Nanairo Dreams: Nijiirochou no Kiseki ( "Quiz Seven Color Dreams - Miracle of Rainbow Color Village") is a Japanese board game developed by Capcom. Gameplay is a hybrid of a quiz game and a dating sim where your chances of wooing each girl depends on how fast and accurate your answers are. This game supports up to two players who can work together to achieve the ultimate goal to restore the seven crystals held by each girl and use them to vanquish the Devil.
Quiz Olympic

The Quiz Olympic arcade machine (often associated with the genre's competitive finish style) is a rare, classic coin-operated trivia game released in 1985 by Seoul Coin Corp. It was primarily created to capture the global excitement leading up to the 1988 Summer Olympic Games held in Seoul, South Korea.
Quiz Quest: Hime to Yuusha no Monogatari

Quiz Quest: Hime to Yuusha no Monogatari (Japanese: クイズクエスト -姫と勇者の物語-, meaning Story of the Princess and the Hero) is a coin-operated arcade quiz game released in July 1991 in Japan by Taito Corporation.
Quiz Rouka Ni Tattenasai
Quiz Rouka ni Tattenasai! (クイズ 廊下に立ってなさい！) is an arcade game revolving around solving quizzes. This game was port to Saturn as Sega Ages Rouka ni Ichidant-R.
Quiz Sangokushi

Quiz Sangokushi: Chiryaku no Hasha (クイズ三國志 知略の覇者) is a quiz arcade game based on the Records of the Three Kingdoms released in 1991.

Many sprites in this game were reused in the mahjong game Jangokushi: Haō no Saihai, which has a similar theme.
Quiz Sekai wa SHOW by shobai

Quiz Sekai wa SHOW by shobai is a Japanese trivia arcade game produced by Taito in 1993. It is a direct adaptation of the highly popular late-80s to early-90s Japanese television game show of the same name (loosely translated as "Quiz: The World Is Show Business").

The arcade game captures the high-energy, hectic nature of the TV broadcast. Players answer pop-culture, geography, and current-events trivia questions rooted in early-90s Japan.
Quiz Show

Say The Secret Word and Win... Quiz Show asks 250 different questions in each category. Players can select 'sports', 'general knowledge', 'movies' or 'people'. Each question displays four possible answers which appear in different colors. Hit the colored button on the control console that corresponds to the correct 'answer' color on the monitor, the contestant scores. High for a fast answer, low if it's a head-scratcher. Player can test him or herself, or challenge a partner for highest score.

TRIVIA
Quiz Show is believed to be the first game to utilize the now well-known 'arcade font' (formerly thought to have been first introduced with Sprint 2 or Cannonball, but Quiz Show predates these two games by six months). This font is likely to have been designed by Lyle Rains and has since been used by many non-Atari games manufacturers including Namco, Irem, Nichibutsu, and Nintendo.

As you can see in the description, Quiz Show contains a total of 1000 questions and 4000 possible answers.
Quiz Syukudai wo Wasuremashita

Quiz Syukudai wo Wasuremashita (クイズ 宿題を忘れました! / "Quiz: I Forgot My Homework") is a unique, board-game-style arcade quiz game developed and published by Sega in Japan in 1991.

The Plot: An adult couple is transformed into school children by an eccentric scientist named Dr. Tenma. To reverse the spell, they must compete against rival school kids across a series of stages filled with period-specific trivia questions before ultimately confronting the doctor himself.
Quiz Theater: 3tsu no Monogatari

This is the third game in a series initiated by Hot-B. Since Hot-B was a sub-company of Taito Japan, when they had bankruptcy, some staff from Hot-B joined Taito directly and this game is their first result.

The subtitle of this game translates from Japanese as 'Story of Three'.

Zuntata Record released a limited-edition soundtrack album for this game (ZUNTATA RARE SELECTION Impromptu - ZTTL-2001 ) on 12/01/2000.
Quiz Tonosama no Yabou

Quiz Tonosama no Yabou is a trivia game with strategy elements, set during the Sengoku time period of the Japanese history. Single and two-player game modes are available. Players select warlords to control, and rise to dominance by defeating other warlords in quiz encounters. Each attempt at conquering a province leads to a quiz posed by the defending warlord. The themes of the quiz may have nothing to do with the historical period and range from general knowledge to Japanese anime and video games.
Quiz Tonosama no Yabou 2: Zenkoku-ban

Quiz Tonosama no Yabou 2: Zenkoku-ban is a Japanese arcade quiz game and a sequel to the original "Quiz Tonosama no Yabou". It continues the theme of a feudal lord vying for control over Japan. The game features a variety of trivia questions related to Japanese history, culture, and general knowledge, all set against a backdrop of feudal Japan. 

The title translates to "Quiz Ambition of the Feudal Lord 2: National Edition".
Quiz Torimonochou

Quiz Torimonochou is a historical quiz arcade game produced and released by Taito Corporation in 1990. Operating on Taito's proprietary F2 hardware system, the machine was exclusively distributed within Japan.

It holds a unique place in arcade history as the first Taito title that required players to have a comprehensive knowledge of all three Japanese writing systems—Kanji, Hiragana, and Katakana—to successfully solve its multiple-choice trivia challenges. In the game, players guide two Japanese lords, Heihachi (red) and Nariyoshi (blue), through seven distinct rounds of questions to clear stages and earn bonus items like onigiri (rice balls). Due to its popularity in Japanese game centers, it was later ported to the Sharp X68000 home computer in 1992.
Quiz TV Gassyuukoku Q&Q

Quiz TV Gassyuukoku Q&Q is a trivia arcade game published by Dynax and released in January 1992 exclusively in Japan. The game's title translates into English as "Populace TV's Quiz Q&Q". It simulates a competitive TV game show environment where up to two players answer trivia questions using a specialized layout.
Quizard
First game in the series of German quiz games, Quizard 2 has you answer questions in various categories. The objective is to get as many points as possible before running out of lives.
Quizard 2
Second game in the series of German quiz games, Quizard 2 has you answer questions in various categories. The objective is to get as many points as possible before running out of lives.
Quizard 3

Third game of the series, Quizard 3 is a German quiz games up to 2 players, with a limited time to answer questions in various categories. The objective is to get as many points as possible before running out of lives.
Quizard 4 Rainbow
Fourth of the series, Quizard 4 Rainbow is a German quiz game .
Quizvaders

Quizvaders is a single-player arcade quiz game developed and published by Bell-Fruit Manufacturing Company (BFM) in 1991. Operating as a quiz machine (often referred to as a Skill with Prizes or SWP machine), it became a staple of British pub culture during the late 1980s and 1990s.
Qwak (prototype)

This prototype was never released. Qwak was a '15-puzzle' game with cute animations and it shares with MM2 the distinction of using 'Motion Objects' for text. Designers were unsure whether it was originally designed for a touch-screen or not. It could have been a joystick game that happened to be in development when they were interested in evaluating touch-screen technology. They felt that the touch-screen would make a more intuitive interface, but were apparently wrong. The most common comment at the focus-group was 'could you put a joystick or buttons on it. It would be easier'...
Qwak!

Qwak! is a single-player duck hunting light gun shooter arcade game developed by Atari and released in November 1974. In the game, ducks fly one at a time across the screen, and the player shoots at them using a light gun attached to the game cabinet. The player gets three shots per duck; ducks change direction away from missed shots and fall to the bottom of the screen when hit. A screen overlay adds images of reeds and a tree branch, and an image of a duck is added to a row at the top of the screen whenever a duck is hit. Games continue until a time limit, set by the machine operator, is reached.
R-Shark

R-Shark is a 2D vertical-scrolling sci-fi shoot'em up. The player takes the role of a headhunter, and gets to chose to go after one of eight interstellar criminals. Gameplay is similar to a myriad of other shmups: The player in a special space ship flies and shoots at enemies - main interstellar criminals are bosses. His ship has a weak main weapon, and some support in the form of homing missiles, but better weapons like a laser can be acquired. Weapons are also upgradable and offer super attacks.
R-Tuned: Ultimate Street Racing

R-Tuned : Ultimate Street Racing is an arcade racing game released by Sega on 23 October 2008 in Asia and North America, and on 17 April 2009 in Europe. The game focuses on the import scene and illegal street racing. The game runs on the Sega Lindbergh platform, and uses Virtua Fighter 5's character model engine. Players can save their progress and records by using IC cards. There are boost buttons on the steering wheel, players can use unlimited boosts to speed up during the game.

There are 2 modes of the game :

Battle mode : players try to get highest points during the race
Time attack : players try to finish the course with the fastest time

There are total 20 cars. The cars can be tuned up to higher levels for better performance. Also, comic graphic stickers and neon tubes can be added to the cars.
R-Type

R-Type is set in the 22nd century, and the player flies a futuristic fighter craft called the R-9a "Arrowhead", named for its shape, and because it is the ninth model in the 'R' series of fighter craft (but it is the first of the series to actually be used in combat; the previous models were all prototypes). The mission is to 'blast off and strike the evil Bydo Empire'. The significance of the R- in the series title refers to the production code as well as the term of endearment for the player fighter craft, the "Round Canopy".
R-Type II

The inevitable sequel to the hugely-successful original finds the evil Bydo Empire once again intent on the destruction of all mankind. The infamous Beam Weapon and Pod Laser make a welcome return, as do the beautifully rendered, organic-looking levels. R-type II doesn't do anything that the original didn't do, but the sequel is every bit as good as its illustrious predecessor, with the same tight gameplay and imaginative level design that made R-type such a classic - although R-Type II is, if anything, more difficult than its already-unforgiving prequel.
R-Type Leo

R-Type Leo is an arcade 2D side-scrolling shmup, the fourth game (although not considered a main entry) in the R-Type series. Rather than the fight against the Bydo Empire, the story background describes how a bio-computer malfunctions and takes control of an artificial planet that was built by mankind. The player tries to stop it with his spaceship. Compared to earlier installments, some changes have been made regarding the weapon systems. The Force and the Wave Cannon are removed, instead, Bit Devices are introduced that are comparable to the TOZ in Gaiares. Their firing direction depends on the movement of the ship itself. They can also be detached for direct collision damage to enemies. R-Type Leo is also the first game in the series with two players co-op.
R.C. Pro-Am

Guide your radio controlled car to victory in this racing game. You have to beat your 3 opponents on 32 tracks while avoiding obstacles like water and oil puddles and collecting bonus items like better engines and tires. You can also collect a variety of weapons to blast your opponents out of the way.

The Genesis version is basically the same game as the NES version with a few minor changes such as having 5 opponents instead of 3, spelling out CHAMPION instead of NINTENDO, and having enhanced graphics.
R2D Tank

R2D Tank is simple 2D arcade game and a sequel to Red Tank. The player controls a tank, collects dots for points and fights against enemy tanks. When an enemy tank is destroyed, a next vehicle appears on the battlefield. Mines (red dots) lie on battlefield and these can be destroyed by shooting them. Later levels have more enemies.
Ra Sceptor

Ra's Scepter is a discontinued video slot/fruit machine game board developed by Astro Corp. and released in May 2007.

Ancient Egyptian setting featuring symbols like coffins, sun medals, thrones, and treasure boxes.
Rabbids & Ladders

For centuries, the board game Snakes & Ladders has entertained generations of people. Now the concept is getting a 21st century makeover thanks to those goofy Rabbids with Rabbids & Ladders by Adrenaline Amusements.

Rabbids & Ladders is a simple concept that plays much like a board game, but with the dynamic advantages that are offered by the digital format. All players have to do is credit up, then spin the toilet paper roll controller (blame the Rabbids and their penchant for toilet humor for that one). The wheel on the screen will spin, and whichever number it lands on, that’s how many spaces you move.
Rabbids Hollywood

Are you a sharpshooter? Compete with buddies to stop the Rabbids invasion of Hollywood. Shoot all the crazy creatures during a four-player adventure and explore 3 different movie sets. Warning: comes with edgy humor and never-ending fun! Created in partnership with Ubisoft and features the popular Rabbids: 14M video games sold, 230 TV episodes, and more than 1B online views.

4-Player shooting game
3 Rabbidized movie settings
Never-ending fun!
Rabbit

Rabbit is a 2D fighting game, with cartoonish colorful graphics. The game has 8 playable characters - Wu Ling (Rabbit), Tien-Ren (hawk), Eight (ox), Hou-En (wolf), Ja-Koh (snake), Yu-Lan (fox), Rex (tiger) and Eddy (wild boar). The player chooses one from these heroes, and must defeat all opponents, plus the final boss.

Each character has a special animal spirit that helps with the battle and they have a spirit' bar to use these specials. The game uses the joystick plus 4 buttons - for light punch, heavy punch, light kick, and heavy kick.
Rabbit Punch

The royal family of Bunnyland was kidnapped by monsters and the player has to save them by beating all six levels of this side-scrolling shooter. The reason why the protagonist, a rabbit, can fly is the rocket launcher on his back. 

Just like in most shooters, the main objective is to survive the way to the end boss of each level without getting hit by enemies (three hits result in a life loss). The rabbit has three ways to defend itself: a regular gun, a strong melee punch and limited homing missiles. The power ups are shield energy refreshments, extra points, invincibility, more missiles and missile upgrades.
Raccoon Rampage

Raccoon Rampage is a 4-player water blasting game that will leave you craving for more action! Rampage through the levels, collect valuable props, and unlock weapon boosts that will help you wreak havoc on your enemies. Collaborate with your fellow raccoon agents to strategically overcome obstacles and engage in epic boss battles that will put your skills and strategy to the test. Get ready to go on a thrilling journey through filled with fun challenges!
Raccoon World

Raccoon World is a relatively rare 2D arcade video game released in 1998 by the South Korean developer Eolith Co., Ltd.

 It is a vibrant, retro action game where players control "Naudoya the Raccoon". The stages are jam-packed with fruit to collect, bombs, and bizarre enemies to fight or avoid.
Race

It is rumoured that this game was a concept/prototype taken from Atari when engineers left to form Fun Games. A very sophisticated TTL game that displays text, and has an entirely moving 'world' that exists outside of the screen boundary.
Race Day

Race Day is a classic coin-operated multiplayer arcade machine manufactured by the British amusement creator Whittaker Bros.. Known for their durable engineering, the company specialized in high-traffic multi-player equipment—such as coin pushers, slot-car machines, and mechanical racers—that became staples of the traditional UK seaside amusement arcade.
Race Drivin'

Race Drivin' is a sequel to the driving simulator Hard Drivin'. Game play is similar to the first game. The player must complete laps around the race track before a timer expires. There are several checkpoints around the track which increase player's time as he passes.

Race Drivin' has three courses, one of which is the track from Hard Drivin'. There is a new super-stunt track, and an autocross course. The player also may choose from three types of cars.
Race Drivin' Panorama

Race Drivin' Panorama was released in May 1991 in the USA (even if the title screen says 1990). Only 50 units were produced in the USA and 50 others in Ireland.

The original selling price was $13995 at its time of release.

The game utilized 3 to 5 Monitors to give you a 180 Degree View. Several 3 and 5-screen versions of this game were modified for use as driving simulators for use by human performance researchers. For a time the 5-screen version served as a platform for a police high-performance driving trainer program.
Race On!

Race On! is a classic 1998 arcade racing game developed and published by Namco. Running on the company's System 23 hardware, it is highly notable as an early arcade racer that integrated a built-in digital camera (NamCam technology) to photograph players and map their faces directly onto their chosen cars. It allowed up to eight players to compete simultaneously when four of its twin cabinets were linked locally.
Racin' Force

Racin' Force is a 3D racing game developed and published by Konami and released in 1994 on arcade platforms.

The game is a racing game all in 3D featuring low level polygons similar to Virtual racing. The player can select up to four tracks to race; Circuit Course, High-Speed Circuit, Enduro Circuit and Country Road, each track based on a difficulty level. The players race against eight opponents and the game can be played up to eight players simultaneously.

The game features a system of checkpoints where the player have to reach under a certain amount of time, and remaining time will be extended for the next checkpoint. The game also features a day/night system which add more realism to the races.
Racing Beat
Racing Beat is a Formula-1 style racing game, developed and published by Taito Corporation, which was released worldwide in 1991.
Racing Hero

Racing Hero is a 1989 arcade game from Sega which runs on Sega's X Board hardware (the same hardware used for games such as After Burner and Power Drift). In Racing Hero, the player takes part in an international race aboard a motorcycle and races against time and other vehicles. It draws much inspiration from Sega's successful Hang-On and Out Run series.
Racing Jam

This racing game boasts (at least) 24 cars and 4 different modes of play, with differing difficulty levels: Time Trial and Circuit Course racing (beginners and intermediate), uphill and downhill versions of Winding Road (expert), and several Gymkhana Racing modes. Like "Gran Turismo", it is possible to upgrade engine power and suspension.
Racing Jam DX

This version ran on a Hard Drive and ran on a custom IBM chipset that konami claimed that it could do 5 Millon polygons. It was later released on cheaper hardware in 1998.

Racing jam DX is the Konami Cobra's last game.
Racing Jam: Chapter 2

Racing Jam Chapter 2 was produced by Konami in 1999.

This racing game boasts 24 cars and 4 different modes of play, with varying difficulty levels. Modes include Time Trial and Circuit Course racing (suitable for beginners and intermediate players), and uphill and downhill versions of Winding road (suitable for Expert players). It is also possible to upgrade engine power and suspension.

Racing Jam was originally intended as a showcase title for Konami's new COBRA hardware. After rumors of a hardware switch to the lower-end Konami Hornet hardware, Racing Jam was eventually released on Konami NWK-TR hardware.
Rack 'em Up

Rack 'Em Up is a Billiards/Pool arcade game developed by Konami in 1987 with two game types: 9-Ball or Rotation.

Also known in Japan as "The Hustler".
Rack + Roll

Rack + Roll (Hex Pool in Japan) is a billiards game developed by Shinkai and manufactured by them in Japan. It was published under license to Status Games in North America.

A billiards game in which you have to get all the balls in the pockets. There is no opponent, instead you have to just get them all in the pockets, ending with the 8-ball. However, if you miss three times, the game is over.
Rad Mobile

Rad Mobile is a first person perspective racer and had the player engage into a non-stop road race across the USA while avoiding traffic and police cars under the time limit. The only player controlled car is a Ferrari 330 P4 type prototype racing against computer controlled opponents driving generic cars. The player would race with fifteen other rivals across the track, all attempting to prevent the player from winning. During some of the courses the player would have the opportunity to activate different controls, which include headlights for night driving and windshield wipers during rainstorms. If the player does not activate these controls when prompted, effects such as a restricted view of the road or a wet windshield will occur.
Rad Racer

Rad Racer is an arcade style 3-D racing game. The object of the game is to race to the goal within the given time limit. Along each course are several checkpoints which will increase the amount of time you have to reach the final destination. There are eight different stages with increasingly difficult roads, changing weather conditions, and a variety of opponents who tend to get in the way. The game also supports 3-D glasses.
Rad Racer II

Rad Racer II was produced by Square in 1990.

Drive through eight long courses with a very high difficulty level.
Rad Rally
Sega followed up on the success of Rad Mobile by making a sequel, Rad Rally for the arcades in 1991, which included several gameplay changes.
Radar Scope

Radar Scope is a shoot 'em up in a three-dimensional third-person perspective over a gradient-blue background, often described as a cross between Galaxian and Space Invaders. The player pilots the Sonic Spaceport starship and must defend the space station against enemies called the Gamma Raiders.

Gameplay involves clearing each stage of the Gamma Raiders without colliding with them or their projectiles. Each stage sets 48 Gamma Raiders in a formation, who break away and swoop down toward the player. Some will simply swoop down and fire at the player, and others will try to ram into the space station. The Sonic Spaceport has a damage meter at the bottom of the screen, which depletes with enemy fire. The player can lose a life by either allowing this meter to deplete or by colliding with a Gamma Raider or their projectile. Three types of arcade cabinets were produced: a standard upright, a tabletop version, and a rare sit-down cabinet.
Radar Zone

Radar Zone (also known as Outline) was produced by Century Electronics in 1982.

Radar Zone is a grid capture/painter type game similar to games like Amidar and Crush Roller.
Radiant Silvergun

Unlike in most other shoot 'em ups, there are no power-ups. All weapons are available from the start. Weapons can 'level up', however, becoming more powerful as the player uses them to score points. There are a selection of 7 weapons that can be used at any given time:

The game is designed so that there is almost always a 'right' weapon for any situation. The bosses in the game are designed so that they have multiple 'sections' which, if all destroyed before the 'core' of the boss, will award the players with point bonuses. Being able to apply the right weapons on any different boss is key to obtaining these bonuses. For example, a boss may have two sections located on either side of the screen. You could immediately go up to one and begin shooting it with a vulcan, or you could hover in the centre and hit both at the same time with the side bombs. This would increase your chance of obtaining the bonus before the time limit runs out and the boss self-destructs.
Radical Radial

Radical Radial is a top-down driving game combined with a vertically scrolling shoot-em-up. It has similarities to Data East's earlier Mad Aliens but with a greater emphasis on driving. You control a tire, which is radically equipped with a gun and can jump over obstacles. Your goal is to navigate through various stages without crashing.

Each stage consists of two courses. In the first, or alien course, you are traversing a strange landscape while attacked by flying enemies and having to avoid strategically placed boulders. Points are scored by shooting aliens or collecting bonuses. The second, or highway, course takes place on a busy road. There are futuristic cars that frequently change lane, emergency vehicles that clear their path by knocking cars out of the way, and dead vehicles just lying in the middle of the road. You don't have a gun in this round, but just have to overtake all of the cars without crashing.
Radikal Bikers

Radikal Bikers is a game set in a Mediterranean environment in which players show off their motorbike skills while delivering pizzas.

The game places two players in direct, head-to-head competition to deliver pizzas as fast as possible.
Radirgy

Radirgy is a shoot 'em up video game developed by MileStone Inc. and released for the Sega NAOMI arcade platform in 2005. The story follows schoolgirl Shizuru Kamigusa in an age filled with radio waves which she is allergic to. She must save her father, who is developing a remedy for her sickness, from terrorists who have taken control of his company. The game features bullet hell gameplay elements and a distinct cel shaded graphical style.

Radirgy was ported in 2006 to the Dreamcast, PlayStation 2, and GameCube for release in Japan—of which the latter two featured additional gameplay modes. O~3 Entertainment planned to localize the GameCube version in North America under the title Radio Allergy, but the release was canceled. The game was later localized for the Wii in a compilation of MileStone shooters, Ultimate Shooting Collection. Critics found the game challenging and unique, but overall an average experimental shooter.
Radirgy Noa

Radirgy Noa (also written as Radirgynoa) is a vertically scrolling shoot 'em up that was released in June 2009 for the Sega Naomi arcade platform by Milestone Inc. and the sequel to Radirgy.
Radirgy Noa features a cel-shaded graphical style very similar to that of its predecessor and 2-player co-op. Screen orientation is horizontal. Ruki Mishima, a redeemed villain of the first game, joins the cast as a player character.
Rafflesia

Rafflesia is a top view vertical scrolling shooter where the screen scrolls constantly as you fly up the screen in your spacecraft. The aim is to blast or avoid the various aliens that move around the screen to finally face the final boss Rafflesia. As you blast and avoid, you are equipped with two weapons, both are forward firing weapons but the second one is more powerful and when in use decreases your energy. Falling down the screen constantly are tears from Rafflesia and when collected these increase your energy. If you are hit by an alien or its weapon then you lose one of three lives. Two players can play with each player taking it in turn when the other player is killed.
Rage of the Dragons

In a town ruled by an evil religious cult, the battle to decide the strongest dragon begins! Each Contestant is a champion who contends with the power of mighty dragons: Black Dragon, Red Dragon, Blue Dragon, and White Dragon. Go head to head in a tag-team partnership to test your attack and defense in the heat of battle.

Rage of the Dragons is a 2D tag team fighting game. This game originally was supposed to be a sequel of 1995 Double Dragon. The player selects two heroes, and can switch between one or the other during fights. The idle character slowly recovers. Gameplay is typical of the genre - the player's characters must defeat opponents, they can use kicks, punches and they have a special power bar to make various special moves, for example Counter Attacks, Super Moves, etc.
Ragnagard
Pre-rendered pixelation puts somewhat of a damper on this fantasy fighter. Eight selectable characters and three end bosses.
Raiden

In the year 2090, Earth is invaded by extra-terrestrials. The World Alliance of Nations has developed a supersonic attack fighter, Raiden, to defend the Earth. A pilot must take control of the experimental fighter to destroy the alien warships that just happen to look like odd variations of typical military tanks and planes with gadgets attached to them.

Raiden is an over-head vertical-scrolling shooter, based on an arcade game of the same title. It features two forms of weapon upgrades and two types of missiles (normal or homing). You start the game with several bombs which you can use to destroy most enemies on the screen to get yourself out of a jam. Each level ends with a large boss or bosses.
Raiden DX

Vertical scrolling shoot-em-up that adds new features to its prequel Raiden II. Choose from three separate missions: Training special stage, Alpha levels 1-5 and Bravo levels 1-9. Collect various power-ups to increase your weaponry. Lots of secrets and bonuses including ratings based upon player performance
Raiden Fighters

Raiden Fighters' plot is not directly apparent in and of itself. The protagonist squadron must quell a massive guerrilla uprising headed by a ruthless dictator. The setting of this conflict appears to take place in eastern Asia, as the briefings for each "Mission" include a war plan superimposed over a map depicting the countries of China and Japan
Raiden Fighters 2: Operation Hell Dive

Raiden Fighters 2: Operation Hell Dive was produced by Seibu Kaihatsu in 1997.

One of the best vertically scrolling shooters yet.

This game is Raiden on horse steroids; there is no other way to describe this game. There are ten different ships, each with different weapon configurations, manuverabilities, and other attributes. The Raiden ship from Raiden II is also in this one, purple laser and all.
Raiden Fighters Jet
Raiden Fighters Jet is the third and last game in the Raiden Fighters series. This game retains the same intensity and manic gameplay as its predecessors, while introducing several new mechanics.
Raiden II

Three years after the VCD repelled the invasion of the Crystals, the remnants of the machines controlled by the Crystals regroup to form another army to resume taking over the Earth. To combat this Crystal resurgence, a new weapon is developed for the Fighting Thunder to stop the Crystals again.

Raiden IIis a vertically scrolling shooter and the second game in the Raiden series which started with Raiden in 1990. The game expands on the first Raiden's mechanics, introducing two weapons: the Bend Plasma, a lock-on weapon that deals constant low damage to enemies, and the Cluster Bomb, a fast-deploying bomb that does less damage than regular bombs but strikes a larger area.
Raiden II New / Raiden DX

Raiden II New would be best described as an officially licensed, officially produced bootleg, such is the quality of the product. The main casualty on this re-released PCB is the sound hardware, replacing the iconic tunes of the original release with short sampled audio loops of shocking quality.

The equally admired intro sequence is gone, levels 1 and 5 are swapped, and a number of in-game sequences between levels are also absent.

This isn't meant as a demonstration of good play, but mainly to show just how bad this version of the game is. The board is actually a 2-in-1 with a secret method of swapping to a revised version of Raiden DX with equally bad sound.
Raiden III

Little is known about the game's storyline, other than the fact that Earth has been overrun by aliens. It is suggested through similar ship design and flight patterns that the aliens are the Cranassians of the previous games. 
Players once again take control of the famous Raiden Supersonic Attack Fighter, red for player 1 and blue for player 2 as usual; there are no selectable ships. Two player mode is enhanced by an exclusive new attack: a beam that is usable whenever one player lines up in front of the other.

In Double play mode, both players share the live and bomb stocks, and without continue. In PlayStation 2, both players can be played from the same controller.

As of yet, Raiden III does not work in MAME, so an alternative such as Teknoparrot must be used.
Raiden IV

The legendary arcade shooter has returned once more! Raiden IV is another entry in the long-running series of vertical shooters. The game includes a direct conversion of the original arcade game, as well as an "Xbox 360 Mode" which has reworked enemy patterns and two completely new stages. Also included are a boss rush mode, a score attack mode, replay saving, and a ship model gallery.

The game looks and plays much like the previous title, and features the same upgradeable weaponry the series is known for: standard vulcan fire, high-powered laser fire, and the famous purple plasma beam "toothpaste laser". There are also three different sub-weapons to pick up. The game offers eight difficulty settings, and can be played solo, two-player cooperative, or in "dual mode" where one player controls two ships simultaneously. Extra player ships can be purchased from Xbox Live Marketplace.
Raiders
Raiders is a one or two player (alternating turns) shooter game published and developed by Century Electronics in 1983.
Raiders5
Raiders5 is a maze shooting game released by UPL in 1985.
Raiga: Strato Fighter

In the year 2135 AD, the Earth's forces face a sudden onslaught from an unknown enemy. Two MB-OG fighters, code-named Raiga, emerge as the last hope for Earth's salvation. These two brave pilots are dispatched to engage in a high-stakes battle on the enemy's turf, risking everything to defend their home planet.
Rail Chase

Rail Chase is a 1st person perspective rail shooter where you play the role of an explorer (and assistant) who has discovered the Jewels of Guaramure and is now trying to escape with them from the locals. Your means of escape is a mine-cart and as you ride along you must use your gun to help you in your escape over various stages as you are being chased by a stage boss. There are various enemies and obstacles that must be shot so not to damage the mine-cart which slowly starts to show the damage you are taking. There are enemies on the side of the tracks, in mine-carts and on various other vehicles.

If you hit obstacles which include ice-blocks, fences and flame-throwers, then the boss will catch up to you shown by a bar on the top of the screen, showing the gap between you. The bosses have various weapons and must be shot to slow them down and to finally defeat them at the end of the stage.
Rail Chase 2

Rail Chase 2 is the sequel to Rail Chase and was released for Sega Model 2 hardware in 1994. Like the original Rail Chase, the game features a pneumatic "Magical Bench Seat", which tilts and rocks with the in-game action to immerse players in the game.

The year is 1938. Journalist Flint Rickman is investigating the sudden disappearance of Mary Bates, a prominent scientist. He discovers that she has been kidnapped by the evil EKKL empire, who are holding her in their base and forcing her to develop weapons so that they can conquer the world with their military might. Flint sets out to rescue Mary, but when the empire's weapons plant explodes, the pair are forced to escape EKKL in a runaway rail car!
Rail Rush

Rail Rush Ticket Redemption Arcade Machine from Coastal Amusements is a new and exciting video arcade game based on the popular mobile app. Rail Rush is one of the most popular mobile games with over 37 million downloads to date and now has been given to life as a coin-operated arcade game.

Rail Rush is a quick game for those with a keen eye. During the game players step into the cart and begin exploring the Rail Rush world by accelerating through insanely fast rails and avoiding obstactles that fall into their path. The players job is to collect precious stones, however there are surprises along the way and special gifts to earn. Break rock eggs to reveal the special gifts and pick up all of the gems for your personal collection.

Players can also equip their with power ups to extend their chances inside the mine, while completing missions and ranking up, in order to become the ultimate explorer!
Raimais

Raimais (レイメイズ, Reimeizu) is a maze chase arcade game released in April 1988 in Japan by Taito. The object of the game is to drive your vehicle around a maze in order to clear the maze of dots while avoiding the enemy. The game consists of 32 mazes total plus boss fights (some optional, some not). The Japanese version also has a storyline and a final boss fight. The game was ported to the Famicom Disk System under the title Yū Maze the same year. It was included as part of the compilation Taito Legends 2 in 2006.
Rainbow Islands: Extra Version

Rainbow Islands Extra is a version of the classic Taito coin-op Rainbow Islands. Home console versions Include both the the original game and the reworked "Extra Version", in which the stages and bosses have been rearranged to be more challenging. As with the other versions, the game is set in the titular Rainbow Islands, where the two boys Bub and Bob (no longer small dragons as in Bubble Bobble) must free the islands from the evil monsters who have overrun them, by using the magical power of rainbows! In addition to both the Original and Extra modes, the game also includes three difficulty levels.
Rainbow Islands: The Story of Bubble Bobble 2

Sequel to Bubble Bobble, Rainbow Islands sees Bub and Bob (in 2 player mode), who are now curiously small boys rather than dinosaurs, attempting to rid the Rainbow Islands of bad guys.

Using the power to cast rainbows, trapping anything underneath, the boys must ascend vertically 4 levels each island, with a big, bad boss at the end of each.

By trapping beasts under your rainbows, then jumping on them to break them you can collect seven different colored gems, and there are also power-ups for extra speed and rainbows.
Raizin Ping Pong

This first ever virtual ping-pong game for the arcade can be played by one or two players.

Set in a variety of backgrounds from the street to a disco, select a character from among ten choices, each with their own special plays such as excellent spinning ball tactics, fast driving balls or a balanced mix. When playing, use one of two realistic paddles with built in sensors which are attached to the unit. These paddles allow for all kinds of moves, from backhand to forehand and beyond.

Complete numerous levels, battling a range of characters whose skill levels increase progressively.
Funky hip-hop music plays in the background to set the tone of the streets.
Rally Bike

Rally Bike is a bird's eye viewed motorcycle road racing game, where the player controls a motorcycle and must cross the finish line before an established number of competitor bikes. Fuel is a major obstacle, as running out of it results in game over. Any accident will cause great reduction of fuel, and stopping to refuel will cause competitor bikes to take advantage. Competitors never run out of fuel.
Rally-X

Rally-X is a top-down maze-chase driving game in which the player steers a continuously moving car through a multidirectional scrolling network of roads. The objective of each round is to collect all ten checkpoint flags while avoiding enemy cars that pursue the player. Stationary boulders obstruct some routes, and colliding with either an enemy car or a boulder costs a life.

The player can release clouds of smoke behind the car, temporarily causing pursuing vehicles that drive through them to spin out and stall. Fuel steadily decreases throughout each round, and producing smoke consumes it more quickly, requiring the player to balance defensive use of the smoke screen against the need to conserve fuel. Running out of fuel does not immediately end the round, but the player’s car slows considerably and can no longer release smoke.
Rambo

You play John Rambo. The game is a chronological retelling of the first three films.One the first mission he must escape the national guard that imprisoned him, the only way he knows how - by gunning them down. In the second mission he must protect the POWs (prisoners of war) that are held in a Vietnam prison compound. In mission 3 he must save his friend and mentor Colonel Trautman, after he is abducted on an Afghanistan mission. 

This game features a unique rage meter which is activated by pressing a button on the gun. The bar must be fully charged to be activated. This makes Rambo invincible for a short period of time. Bad guys also have an enemy attack gauge, this helps the player identify when the enemy is going to shoot or if they are reloading.
Rambo III

Rambo III is a rail shooter game that featured Rambo and Colonel Trautman as playable characters. It's based on the Sylvester Stallone movie of the same name, whereby Rambo went about the business of rescuing Colonel Trautman, who had been taken hostage in Afghanistan while helping defend the Mujahedeen from the Soviet invasion.

From a third-person perspective, Rambo would have to blast through contingents of enemy soldiers using various weapons with crosshairs, as well as fight tank bosses at the end of each level.
Rampage

The game where the nice guys don't get a look in. Grab your way through Chicago, punch up New York, and jump on San Francisco. Three indescribably nasty characters which bear a remarkable likeness to King Kong, Godzilla and Wolf-Man, need you to send them on a RAMPAGE in an enduring 150 days of destruction through 50 different cities!
Rampage (2018)

The destruction began in 1986 when Midway released Rampage to arcades and subsequently home consoles. Then in 2018, the arcade classic became the most destructive film of 2018. Now you can enjoy the building smashing mutant excitement at the arcade once more with Adrenaline’s RAMPAGE.

Combining elements from the recent film and the classic game makes for one of the most intense and exciting destructive experiences to land in arcades in modern times. Players can control one of three mutant monsters: George (the ape), Ralph (the wolf) or Lizzy (the reptile). The controls are simple: a joystick for movement, a button for smashing. The goal is to flatten the buildings as quickly as possible, moving on to the next section and avoiding getting hit by the firepower from the military. You earn points – and tickets – as you progress. How far can a mutant make it?
Rampage World Tour

Rampage World Tour is a video game released in 1997 and is the second game in the Rampage series.

Rampage World Tour is a updated version of the classic Rampage. Rampage World Tour starts off at Scumlabs International where three lab technicians, George, Lizzy, and Ralph have mutated in an accident involving toxic waste. George has turned into a gigantic ape, Lizzy a gigantic lizard or dinosaur, and Ralph some sort of gigantic wolf. The three destroy the lab they previously worked at and then embark on a path of destruction encompassing the entire globe.

The player chooses one of these three characters and begins destroying buildings, eating civilians, knocking planes out of the sky, and stepping on tanks. The ultimate goal of the game is to rid the world of Scumlabs by traveling to the cities where they are located. Being creatures of such massive size, there are many cities that must be destroyed along the way.
Rampart

Rampart was produced by Atari Games in 1990.

Build up a castle using Tetris-like pieces to form a wall enclosing your territory. Next, place cannons, and then use them to fire upon enemy boats or opposite player's castle! Then it's back to rebuilding your castle before another round of destruction.

Rampart has three modes of game play, depending on how many players are in the game:
- In a one-player game, the player has to defend his castle from an armada of sailing ships. There are two or three types of ships, each type denoted by the color and size of the ship. The larger the ship, the more shots it takes to sink it.

- A two-player game presents the players a choice of two different game modes:
A harbor mode where the play area is divided into thirds. Two-thirds of the play area is land (one-third for each player), and the last third is dedicated to water.
Ranger Mission

A 1 to 2 player 3-D military combat shooting game where players use pump-action shotguns to shoot on-screen enemies.The game has four different missions:Jungle Mission, Desert Mission, Indoor Rescue Mission and Tundra Mission.
Rapid Fire
Another of the more "kid-friendly" animated gun-shooting games. A shooting game where players try to hit as many required targets as they can without making mistakes, before time runs out.
Rapid Hero

International version of Rapid Hero was discovered called Arcadia. 
Rapid Hero is a very classic and relatively efficient shmup . At the command of a hunter who also thinks somewhat of the design of Strike Gunner STG , you will have to repel the enemy bursts avoiding of course to make you touch ... 

Two heroes are willing to carry out this mission, with a few minor differences in gameplay: the first aircraft is specialized in concentrated direct fire, the second in the deployed shot. Of course, the game offers you its selection of power-ups and special weapons, such as auxiliary and self-guided lasers. 

The course of the game is rather neat with a certain sense of staging. The big enemies arrive from afar and see their shadow emerge under a heap of clouds before presenting themselves to you is still very pleasant, as are the enemies coming out of destroyed buildings.
Rapid River

A water river rafting simulation game. The player must operate the orr to paddle and steer the raft, while negotiating obstacles such as rocks. The rocks slow you down and spin the raft if hit at speed. The stages have a timer and you must progress to a checkpoint before time runs out to continue. The player can switch between third- and first-person view
Rastan

Rastan features six stages of hacking and slashing gameplay with a boss fight at the end of each one. Numerous enemies assault you on your journey such as flying demons, chimeras, valkyries, piranhas, undead, and more. Fight through to the end and save the land of Lograth from certain doom.

The game features different weapons such as axes, maces, and fire swords, each with its own attributes like extended range or attack power, and defensive items like shields, cloaks, and armors, reducing the damage from enemy attacks. Other items include rings (increase the speed of your weapon) and jewelry for bonus points.
Rat Race

The Rat Race fruit machine is an iconic, highly collectable British arcade classic from the late 1980s. Originally manufactured using a conversion format by BWB, it became incredibly popular in UK seaside arcades, holiday camps, and pubs between 1988 and 1990.
Rave Racer

Rave Racer is a racing game and is the third arcade game in the Ridge Racer series. As with its prequels, success is dependent upon mastering the art of drifting, as this allows players to take corners at high speed. This is crucial in reaching timed check-points and overtaking rival racers.

Players can choose from either manual or automatic gears and start each place in last place. They then have a limited number of laps in which they can overtake opponents and ultimately win the race.

As well as including tracks from the earlier games, two new tracks are added to the sequel. There have also been improvement made to car handling, force feedback steering, and improved car and racetrack graphics. The new tracks contain various side roads, but some of them take more time than others to complete a full lap of the track.

The four tracks are: Ridger Racer short, City, Ridge Racer Long, Mountain. The race ends if either the timer expires or upon completion of the race.
RayCrisis

RayCrisis, known as RayCrisis: Series Termination in North America, is the third game released in the "Ray" series of Taito shooting games. Chronologically, it is considered a prequel to the first game, RayForce. First released for arcades in 1998, it supported co-op mode for two players, which the PlayStation ports released in 2000 lack; these ports are the only games in the "Ray" series to lack co-op.

RayCrisis, being a prequel to RayForce, details the events during the timeframe of the supercomputer called the Neuro-Computer Con-Human gaining sentience and rebelling against its human creators, a direct result of a misguided scientist trying to bond a human clone to Con-Human mentally.
RayStorm

RayStorm is a shoot'em-up game created for the arcades, later ported to the PlayStation and Saturn home consoles. Although there is no story connection, it is often thought of as the spiritual successor to RayForce, which had similar gameplay.

You have 2 weapons at you disposal, a vulcan gun and a lock-on missile attack. You can also do 2 special attacks by using the lock-on system in a special way. The graphics are all in 3D, but the gameplay mechanics are in 2D. There are 7 stages, each ending with a giant end boss.
Razing Storm

RAZE YOUR ENEMIES! An influential and dangerous international military organization decides to declare war against the United States. As part of an elite task force, SCAR, you’re being deployed to South America for the purpose of capturing the mastermind behind this conflict. Destroy everything in sight, from the environments to the futuristic terrorists aiming to take you down! With an arsenal of weapons at your disposal, navigate through destructible environments and raze anyone or anything that stands in your path. The future of the free world depends on you, soldier.
Razzmatazz

Razzmatazz is a lightgun arcade game developed by Sega Electronics in 1983. It runs on Zaxxon Hardware. It apparently did not survive past testing, and was never ported to home platforms, though an Atari 2600 version by the name Bear Game was planned (and also developed by Sega Electronics).

A gun shoots at ducks, and polar bears
RC De Go!

RC de GO! is a take on the Densha de Go! series, however this time the focus is on remote controlled rally cars. The player can choose from three unique RC cars, each with their own strengths and weaknesses and over 80 different customizable options to choose from including new chassis that can be used to either make a car faster or turn better, among many other unique attributes.

Players can race on fourteen different courses and have four different race modes to choose from: Practice lets the player learn the basics elements and controls of the car. Quick Race allows the player to choose from any cars and tracks available for an exhibition race. Time Attack has the player complete a course in a set amount of time and Championship puts the player on twelve different off-road and road courses in an attempt to win the championship. If a player is able to win this mode, they will have the chance to test their skills on three special unlockable tracks.
Re-Volt

Re-Volt which was released on an arcade machine by Tsunami Visual Technologies on September 24, 2004.

This 'port' of the game featured a few changes such as gameplay and graphics. It ran on Microsoft Windows 98 and came in two versions. The TsuMo Standard Non-Motion Sit Down Re-Volt and the deluxe model. 

Similar to the Dreamcast version's time trial mode and many other arcade racers, there is a global timer.

This version had two additional tracks. Those are Gabor's Venice and a new track created by Kurt Arnlund, an ex-Tsunami employee.
Reactor

In Reactor, the player controls a space ship inside of a nuclear reactor which they are trying to stop from melting down. The reactor core at the center of the screen is surrounded by a deadly kill wall. Roaming throughout the available space are positrons, neutrinos, and photons, all of which will be trying to knock the player's ship into the wall. To survive, the player will need to knock all of these attacking particles into the kill wall to destroy them. As each level progresses, the reactor core will slowly grow in size, making less and less room for the ship to maneuver in. Eventually the reactor core will melt down; to prevent this, the player will need to destroy all of the particles before the time runs out. To help out, the ship starts the game with a limited number of decoys. When a decoy is placed on the screen, all of the particles will be attracted to it instead of the actual ship.
Reaktor

Reaktor was produced by Zilec in 1987.

Another variation on an early ball and paddle video game where the paddle moves left and right at the bottom of the screen and a ball is deflected to hit bricks.
Real Battle Mahjong King

Real Battle Mahjong King (also known as Shizhan Mahjong Wang / 实战麻将王) is a classic Japanese-style tabletop arcade game released in 1998 by the developer GMS.

Unlike popular modern mobile games that use Mahjong solitaire mechanics (tile-matching puzzles), this vintage title simulates a traditional head-to-head tactical Mahjong match.

 As an arcade-era standard for single-player Mahjong, it typically pits you against AI opponents in escalating difficulty or scenario-based betting rounds.
Real Bout Fatal Fury

Real Bout changes the play controls from the previous Fatal Fury games, reducing the number of attack buttons from four to three: a standard Punch and Kick button, a "Strong Attack" button which can be either a stronger punch or kick attack, depending on the character. The game retains the three-plane "oversway" system from Fatal Fury 3, which features a main lane for fighting, with foreground and background planes used to avoid attacks or leap towards the opponent. A dedicated button is now used to make an "oversway" (or change plane) towards the background or foreground.

Real Bout introduces a Power Gauge, which fills up as the player performs normal or special techniques against their opponent or defend themselves, similar to many super move gauges featured in other fighting games. The Power Gauge allows players to perform one of three types of Special Techniques, depending of the level of the Power Gauge.
Real Bout Fatal Fury 2: The Newcomers

SNK's Fatal Fury fighting series reaches its 7th episode bringing a lot of "innovations" and some significant changes, starting from characters: all the 20 fighters from previous games return with new artworks and battle stages completely redrawn, as well as some remodelled (or new) moves.

The traditional fighting system comes with sensible modifications, like the removal of both "Rank System" (SSS, SS, S, AAA etc.) and ground breakable objects. The match system using 2 battle plans (foreground/background) remains semi-intact, because now some battle fields (like Cheng Sinzan's stage) uses a single plane, forcing the players to use only the basic defense to avoid attacks.

But the main addition of this title (and the reason for subtitle "The Newcomers") are 2 new characters entering for Fatal Fury's main cast: Rick Strowd, a mysterious fighter with a particular fighting style and Li Xiangfei, a young female Chinese martial arts fighter.
Real Bout Fatal Fury Special

The supreme trial of strength awaits! 19 of Fatal Fury's hottest heroes collide! One year since the fearsome conclusion to "Real Bout", the hungry wolves ready themselves for a new battle, "Real Bout Special" - the paramount pugilistic proving ground!

Real Bout Fatal Fury Special retains the cast of the original Real Bout, with the addition of Tung Fu Rue, Cheng Sinzan, Laurence Blood and Wolfgang Krauser from Fatal Fury Special, with Krauser serving as the new final boss. Geese Howard, who was killed off in the end of the original Real Bout, appears in this game as a hidden final boss in a special "Nightmare Match" and as an unlockable playable character in the home versions. The game also features hidden "extra" versions of Tung Fu Rue, Billy Kane, Blue Mary, and Andy Bogard, for a total of 23 (24 if counting Geese) characters.
Real Mahjong Haihai

Real Mahjong Haihai (リアル麻雀牌牌) is a Japanese adult-oriented arcade game developed by Alba and released in November 1985. Translating roughly to "Real Mahjong Tile-Tile", it relies on traditional Riichi Mahjong mechanics but gained notoriety in arcade centres for its specific reward loop: defeating opponent AI characters rewards the player with revealing, pixelated imagery of them.

At the start of the game, players are greeted by a character selection screen featuring three different female computer opponents (labeled A, B, and C). The game uses authentic Mahjong rules where you draw, discard, and attempt to build a winning hand. Winning rounds grants you a high score screen and visual rewards, while losing or forcing a draw (流局) impacts your overall point pool.
Real Mahjong Haihai Jinji Idou Hen

Real Mahjong Haihai Jinji Idou Hen (リアル麻雀牌牌 人事移動編) is a Japanese arcade video game published by Alba in 1986. It is the second entry in Alba's Real Mahjong Haihai series. The game's subtitle roughly translates to "Personnel Changing Incident Edition".

The game belongs to the "strip mahjong" subgenre popular in Japanese game centres during the mid-to-late 1980s. Players compete in traditional head-to-head Mahjong matches against different fictional female opponents. Defeating an opponent rewards the player by revealing pixelated artwork of the character.
Real Mahjong HaiPai Seichouhen
Real Mahjong Haipai Seichouhen is a mahjong game, published by Visco Games, which was released in Japan in 1986.
Real Puncher

Real Puncher is an incredibly rare, strength-testing sports arcade game released by Taito in 1994. Acting as the arcade sequel to the famous Sonic Blast Man franchise, it combined physical punching mechanics with early interactive video features.
Real Steel

Based on the box office hit DreamWorks movie which was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Visual Effects & grossed over $300 Million in worldwide sales!

Real Steel is "Robotic Boxing" at its finest ! Played on a massive, spectacular 47" vertically mounted HD LCD Widescreen Color Monitor, players pull back the huge, life-sized "Atoms" punching arm to complete against their computer-generated robotic opponent. Players must wait for the perfect time to push the robotic fist in order to score a BIG Knockout against their enemy opponent !

If players successfully " KO " the (4) enemy robotic
opponents, they get to win the big TICKET BONUS !
Reality Tennis
Reality Tennis is a one or two player sports game published and developed by TCH in 1993.
Rebound

Rebound is a volleyball video game by Atari. At first, it looks similar to Pong, but the game shown is from the side, and the ball bounces up and down and across the screen, instead of simply sliding across the screen. Each player moves their paddle under the ball in order to keep it off the ground, attempting to bounce it over the net.
Rebus

is a rare puzzle and pub quiz arcade game developed and published by the Italian company Microhard in 1995. Primarily designed for European pub quiz machines, the game relies on hardware architectures shared with other titles from the era and is fully supported via emulation platforms.

 It functions as a digital pub quiz game but prominently features adult/erotic themed imagery alongside its trivia puzzles.
Recalhorn

Recalhorn was produced by Taito in 1993. This game ran on Taito's F3 system and was tested in arcades, but never officially released. Several prototype carts were released into the wild.

Play as a young boy and his white creature pet as you progress through sidescrolling levels using a magic flute or jumping on enemies to defeat them and gather fruit for points. Along the way, you characters will befriend animals which can be summoned and ridden bestowing new powers to both defeat enemies and traverse the land. At the end of each world, youll face a boss character. Your player has 5 hearts per life.
Recordbreaker
