Recordbreaker is a multi-event sports game for one or two players, where the player tries to achieve a world-record score in each of ten competitions. The events include: 100m sprint, 4x100m relay, Triple jump, Pole vault, Long horse, 100m swimming, Weightlifting, Horizontal bar, 100m hurdles and Shot put. The events can be played in any order, although losing an event results in the end of the game.

Each of the ten events is controlled by buttons only. The 100m sprint involves repeated pressing of a single button as quickly as possible. The others events additionally require pressing another button to jump (hurdles), pass a baton (400m relay), resurface for oxygen (100m swimming) or to select the angle for throwing (shot-put) or dismounting (horizontal bar). These more complicated games have a "demo" mode to show how the game is played prior to the qualifying heat.
Red Alert

In Red Alert, the player controls an anti-aircraft turret that can move left and right across the ground, and can only fire straight up. The objective of the game is to keep the turret alive, and to keep the attackers from destroying the city. To do this, the player must maneuver their turret under the attackers, and fire upwards into them, before they drop their bombs.
Red Baron

Red Baron was produced by Atari in 1980.

In Red Baron, players take on the role of a World War I pilot as they enter the cockpit of a triplane during an intense dogfight. Players have to shoot down aerial targets like blimps and biplanes and ground targets such as pillboxes and tanks. However, continuously shooting can cause their planes guns to temporarily overheat so players have to be more judicious with their gunfire. Players also have to be careful not to crash into the mountainside they are flying over.

Shooting both aerial and ground targets will earn the player points. Points for destroying objects is always the same except for bi-planes. The farther away they are when destroyed the more points they are worth. A bonus plane is earned at 2,000, 10,000, and 30,000 points. These points.can also be adjusted to make the game more difficult.
Red Bird

Red Bird is a Spanish bootlegged/pirated version of Nintendo's Space Firebird.

It was released by a company called Codematic in 1980.
Red Clash

Red Clash is a one or two player shooter game published and developed by Tehkan in 1981.

Red Clash is a space shooter featuring a ship of blue going against ships that are red.
Red Earth

Red Earth is a 2D fighting arcade game, with the action taking place in an alternative 14th century, or a post-apocalyptic 1999 (depending on release regions). The player can choose one from four characters: Leo (a half-lion half-man), Kenji (a leader of an elite ninja squad), Tessa (a female sorceress) and Mai-Ling (a female talented martial artist).

Gameplay is similar to the Street Fighter series, with six button controls. There are some significant differences, for example, the enemy character has a much longer life gauge than the player. The opponents in the game's quest mode are unplayable monsters. There is also a two-player versus mode, but the character selection for the players is limited to the four mentioned before. Red Earth also has fatalities, something that is more associated with Mortal Kombat games rather than Capcom fighters, and it also features experience points and a password system.
Red Fox War Planes II

Red Fox War Planes II is a classic arcade shoot-'em-up game (shmup) originally released for Chinese arcades. It is a military-themed vertical scrolling shooter where players pilot combat aircraft to fight off waves of enemy planes, tanks, and bosses.
Red Hawk

A vertical shooter. Fly over various planets and destroy as many buildings, tanks, planes, etc. as you can. At the end of each stage, you have to destroy a big space ship or monster in order to get to the next level.

When destroying semi-big objects, you can collect power-ups to increase your firing speed. After finishing all twelve stages, the game shows the credits page that contains the names and pictures of the developers.

While holding down the shoot button, the special weapon recharges and fires if it's completely loaded. The special weapon and the Big Bomb differ for each player: player two launches a big Ghost Bomber that blocks all enemy fire; player one shoots big discs across the whole screen. Watch out for the special power-ups located at the very end of both sides, almost out of the screen. These are better power-ups than normal. One of these is a Fire Cat upgrade that shoots automatically around your ship.
Red Hot Ibiza

Red Hot Ibiza is a classic UK pub fruit machine manufactured by Bell-Fruit Games (Bell-Fruit Manufacturing) and released in 1999. Built on the popular Scorpion 4 hardware platform, the machine is legendary among enthusiast communities for its authentic, high-energy 1990s dance, trance, and hip-hop stereo soundtrack.

Originally operating on a £10 jackpot and 25p per play configuration, the physical machine features a traditional "Smiley 1" cabinet layout.
Red Hot Mazooma Belle

Red Hot Mazooma Belle is a classic, video-based UK fruit machine (slot machine) released in the early 1990s. It was designed and manufactured by BWB (Barcrest Video / Brent Walker Video) using the Barcrest MPU4 Video System.
The game combines elements of standard Mazooma mechanics with BWB's video cabinet technology.
Red Hot Poker

Red Hot Poker is a classic UK fruit machine (AWP) published and released by BWB in 1992. Rather than a standard physical reel machine, it is notable for using Barcrest MPU4 Video technology (MPU4VIDEO), which combined traditional physical fruit machine elements or logic with a video screen element to display card-based poker gameplay.
Red Hot X
Red Hot X (also commonly known as Red Hot X Casino) is a classic British UK pub fruit machine manufactured by the legendary amusement developer Mazooma.
Red Robin

Red Robin was produced by Elettronolo in 1984.

A colorful horizontal-scrolling platfromer from Elettronolo.
RedLine Racer

Redline Racer was produced by Cinematronics in 1986.

A top-down racing game similar to Atari's Sprint series.
Reel Fun

Reel Fun was produced by Grayhound in 1986.

Rip off of the TV gameshow "Wheel of Fortune". Uses higher dollar amounts.
Reel To Reel

Reel To Reel is a classic UK pub fruit machine manufactured by Mazooma Gaming. Released primarily as a low-jackpot classic Amusement with Prizes (AWP) machine (originally featuring a £15 jackpot layout), it is highly regarded among retro arcade hobbyists and fruit machine enthusiasts.
Reel'N Quake!

Reel'N Quake! is a vintage slot machine / fruit machine released in 1997 by P&E (or Seta 2nd Generation system architecture). It was manufactured primarily as an upright or countertop multi-line board cabinet designed for commercial arcade environments, pubs, and gaming halls.
Reely Crazy

Reel Crazy is an iconic, classic British pub fruit machine manufactured by JPM (John Purewal Machines) in 1984.

Running on JPM’s celebrated MPS microprocessor technology, this arcade favorite represents the golden era of 1980s UK coin-operated gaming. It remains highly sought-after by retro arcade collectors and enthusiasts setting up home bars or man caves.
Reflec Beat

REFLEC BEAT is Konami's new touchscreen rhythm game that focuses on versus multiplayer gameplay using a mix of classic pong with the timing based tapping widely used in the bemani series.

The game is designed for 2 players, with players competing 1vs1 via linked machines. If there is only one player, a computer opponent is used in place of the second player.

Each player has a horizontal bar across their screen. Players compete to best their opponent's score by moving to the rhythm while touching and bouncing back notes that come flying toward the horizontal bar. These notes then fly to your opponent's screen where they have to do the same thing. Depending on the BPM of the song, the notes will come really slow or really fast.

The game's simple rules and instinctive use of the touch panel allow for fun, easy, and rhythmic gaming for anyone. There are three levels of musical difficulty, and players can compete at the level of difficulty that best suits them.
Regulus

Regulus (レグルス) is an arcade shoot-'em-up game released for Sega System 1 hardware in 1983.

Players control a tank, capable of moving in eight directions. One button fires forward, while another launches bombs further up the screen. The play area continuously scrolls upwards and players need to avoid enemies and obstacles.
Relief Pitcher

Relief Pitcher was produced by Atari Games in 1992.

Baseball game with play-by-play announcer, and option of playing a standard baseball game or playing as a relief pitcher through a series of games. Doesn't use real teams or players but allows operator to choose up to 4 cities for players to select from. Keeps detailed statistics.

Each player can select the throwing arm, throwing motion overhand or sidearm, and special pitch sinker, etc. for their pitcher. The three-button control allows each pitch to be a fastball, curveball, or special pitch and the joystick controls the location and movement. The batter can choose a standard swing, power swing, or bunt with the buttons. The player can choose to play a normal baseball game from start to finish or play as a relief pitcher, and finish up computer generated games starting in the 8th or 9th inning of each.

The game offers an "All-Star" game after you make six relief appearances.
SOUND: The announcer calls the plays as they happen.
Relief Pitcher (System 1, prototype)

Atari released a game called Relief Pitcher in 1992, however the concept was originally tried 6 years earlier on their System 1 platform. The 1986 game, while built around similar ideas, is an entirely different game, with the released game being more like a sequel to it. Presentation on the prototype is much more cartoony, fitting with Atari’s other output at the time.
Renegade

Renegade (Nekketsu Kouha Kunio-Kun in Japan) is the scrolling beat 'em up by Technos which started the Kunio / Nekketsu High series. The original takes takes place in a Japanese city, whereas its western version named Renegade is set on the mean streets of Brooklyn. This conversion later produced unofficial sequels Target: Renegade and Renegade III: The Final Chapter. You must venture through to meet your girlfriend, and then rescue her from her kidnappers. This is split into five levels, taking you through the subway and the docks as well as some inhospitable streets. A wide range of aggressive moves are on offer, including headbutts, kicks, punches and flying kicks. Much of the game's violence is depicted in a fairly tongue-in-cheek style, with an element of attempted humour along the way.

Renegade first introduced several trademarks of the beat 'em up genre, including 4-directional control, punch-jump-kick play action, and enemies which can sustain multiple hits.
Renju Kizoku

Renju Kizoku is a board-game that presents a digital version of gobang (five-in-a-row) under the ruleset of renju. The game uses a traditional grid board and allows players to challenge each other aiming to align five stones in a row, rather than capturing territory as in the 

Two players (or one player versus computer) take turns placing black and white stones on the grid intersections. The goal is to create an unbroken line of exactly five stones horizontally, vertically or diagonally. To ensure balance, the first-player (black) is subject to renju restrictions such as forbidding “overline” (six or more in a row) and double-three or double-four patterns. The game concludes when a player forms a valid line of five, or no further legal moves remain.
Reno Reels

Reno Reels is a classic UK video fruit machine released in 1996 by BWB Amusements. Running on the Barcrest MPU4 Video hardware platform, it belongs to a unique era of early digital pub slots. It is highly regarded by arcade collectors for pioneering mechanics that inspired other legendary BWB machines like Monte Carlo or Bust, Miami Dice, and Gold Rush.
Rescue

Rescue was produced by Stern Electronics in 1982.

Rescue the parachuting soldiers that have fallen into the sea and transfer them to an island for safety. Avoid the enemy helicopters, ships and submarines that try to shoot you down.

You are the pilot of a helicopter flying over dangerous waters. Your mission is to rescue a varying number of paratroopers from the water below and you must do this before they are eaten by sharks. Beware of enemy submarines, ships and helicopters. You must avoid or destroy them.
After have have rescued a certain number of paratroopers, you must let them off safely on an island.

The game uses multi-level parallax scrolling to give the illusion of depth. The game may have even been the inspiration for Choplifter.

The game serves up the action via dual joystick controls.
Rescue Raider

Rescue Raider is an arcade game in which the player controls a high-mobility assault vehicle tasked with penetrating enemy territory to rescue hostages, retrieve secret documents, and destroy weapons caches before escaping to the extraction zone.

Players navigate the assault vehicle across a multi-screen map divided into successive zones. On each screen the player may drive in any direction, avoid or destroy enemy positions, collect special items (such as hostages or secret documents), and manage limited fuel and weapon power. After clearing all screens in a zone, the player must reach the extraction point to proceed to the next zone. Failure to rescue key targets or depleting fuel results in game over.
Resident Evil Survivor 2 Code: Veronica

Resident Evil: Survivor 2 - Code: Veronica is a game based on the Resident Evil franchise, similar in concept to the original Resident Evil: Survivor, though it is not actually related. It is a port of an arcade game.

As in the original Code: Veronica game, Claire Redfield and Steve Burnside must escape Rockfort Island, which is infested with zombies. In this case however, the game can be played either with the Guncon 2 lightgun or with the standard controller as a first-person shooter. Players can choose either character or can play cooperatively as both.
Rettou Juudan Nekkyoku Janshi: Higashi Nippon Hen

Travel Japan for the best in mahjong nightlife!

The title of this game translates from Japanese as 'Hot Affair Mahjong Soldier Flying Over the Archipelago: Eastern Japan Chapter'.
Return of Sel Jan II

Return of Sel Jan II is a horizontal-raster arcade videogame released in 1996 by the developer Dynax. Categorised under the board game genre, it is a single-player Japanese Mahjong game that utilises a specialised control panel configuration.
Return of the Count

Return of the Count is a classic UK pub fruit machine manufactured by Mazooma Gaming (later associated with Reflex Gaming for certain refurbishments). It features a popular horror/vampire theme—playing on Dracula and the classic Mazooma "Count" branding.
Return of the Invaders

Return of the Invaders is the third game in Taito's Space Invaders series. It's a more radical change from the original concept than Part II and features an all new full colour look.

There are several new features in the game. Most noticeable are the additions of new enemy formations, seen already in the first wave where the aliens circle around. Some aliens also, when shot, leave their positions and dive towards the player. Others can reflect the player's shots and send them back against him. The game also adds bonus stages similar to Galaga. Another new addition is that the UFOs at the top of the screen now carry weapon upgrades which they drop when shot. To get it the player needs to avoid shooting the centre of the UFO as both the UFO and the weapon will be destroyed.
Revelations
Revelations is a LaserDisc-based quiz machine developed by Nova Productions.
Revenger '84

Revenger '84 was produced by Magic Electronics USA and published by Epos Corporation in 1984.

A space shooter from Magic Electronics and Epos Corporation
Revolution X

Revolution X is a rail shooter in which the players must shoot targets including NON soldiers and vehicles, with the ultimate goal of rescuing the band. Players start the game at Club X in Los Angeles, first fighting the NON troops inside and then stealing a helicopter to fly across the city and find Aerosmith's car. They must then destroy three NON facilities in the Amazon jungle, the Middle East and the Pacific Rim. These three stages may be played in any order; however, failing to complete the Middle East stage within a set time limit will send the players back to its start for another attempt. Finally, the players advance to Wembley Stadium for the final battle with the surviving NON forces and Head Mistress Helga. Throughout the game, objects can be shot that may reveal power-ups like health-replenishing shakes, CD's, powerful laserdiscs and Super Guns, Skull Bombs and shields. Players can also find hostages and free them throughout the game for extra points.
Rezon

Rezon (レゾン) is a 1991 horizontal scrolling shoot 'em up arcade game developed and published by Allumer. It is the first game to actually display the Allumer name, as well as the first game to be self-published, though a Taito-branded release exists. It is modeled after Irem's 1987 arcade hit R-Type, with its own twist in the "Arms" system.

Rezon is unusual in that it has an exceptionally poor soundtrack, yet no other aspect of development was sacrificed. Blandia is a similar game, also by this developer; unlike that game, Rezon was never ported to any platform, so it never received a soundtrack upgrade like Blandia did.

Taking place in the year 2191, the player pilots a recently developed space fighter, the SR-91, through six stages to defend the Earth from a two-year-long alien invasion. The SR-91 uses the VAWS (Variable Armor and Weapon System) which uses the Optica Weapon Arms.
Rhythm Tengoku

Rhythm Tengoku for arcades is an expanded version of the original GBA game adapted for its new environment. In its one-player mode, it features most of the mini-games from the original game along with a new "extra stage" featuring more difficult versions of six mini-games. It also features a 2-player mode, with special 2-player variations of several of the stages.

Rhythm Tengoku's gameplay focuses more on audio cues than visual cues to convey information to players. It features a number of unique stages which have their own type of rhythm and gameplay. Players follow the rhythm (in some rhythm games as a character) until the end where they are given a score based on their performance. The gameplay and music were both well received by critics and consumers. Parallels have been drawn between it and the developer's previous work on the WarioWare series.
Rhytm Tengoku

Players start the game with two hearts. Each heart is lost when starting a Rhythm Game. Getting a Superb or Perfect gives an extra heart, as well as close the game for the rest of the Stage. If the player runs out of hearts, they will need to spend a credit to continue (or, depending on the machine's settings, multiple credits, or none if set to Freemode). The player needs to clear all five games and the Remix in the Stage with at least an OK to move on. Depending on the settings, the Remix may be unselectable, requiring the player to clear all the games in order to play it.
Ribbit!

Ribbit was produced by Sega in 1991.

A single player or two-player cooperative game where each player controls a frog that eats insects like ants and dragonflies while avoiding spiders, rats and other enemies. This game is a sequel to Frogger.
Rich Geezer

Access to the feature game is via a seven stage trail with a bonus at position 4. The trail over-runs into the win-plan. On completing the trail to position 8 or above, the player can choose to collect the win or gamble hi-lo in an all or nothing gamble. After one or more successful hi-lo gambles the option to exchange for the feature game becomes available. A bonus hi-lo number is awarded on a random basis.
Riddle of Pythagoras

An arcade Arkanoid clone that was released by Sega in 1986.

Pythagoras no Nazo: Riddle of Pythagoras is a bat-and-ball game developed by Nasco and released by Sega for arcades (using their Master System-based Sega System E hardware) exclusively in Japan in 1986.
Ridge Racer

Ridge Racer was produced by Namco in 1993.

Ridge Racer is an arcade racer that puts the emphasis on speed and fun rather than on realistic driving simulation. Choose from 4 fantasy cars (plus 9 more that you must unlock yourself) and go race in a series of equally fantastical tracks against a series of computer controlled oponents as well as the clock itself.

Other additions to the game come in the form of a hidden "extra" mode, and a music player that allows you to play any of the 6 included cd tracks as well as your own music cds.
Ridge Racer 2

Ridge Racer 2 was produced by Namco in 1994.

A driving game for one or two players

Race against a second player or alone against computer-controlled cars only (The current MAME version only supports single player)

This is the sequel to 1993's Ridge Rager.
Ridge Racer Full Scale

This version of the popular "Ridge Racer" series is famous for its unique cabinet, where players sat inside a real, modified Mazda MX-5 Miata. The car served as the game's controller, complete with functional steering, pedals, and even an ignition key to start the game. The experience is enhanced by a triple-screen display, creating a wide, panoramic view of the racing track. The game also includes physical effects like wind from the air vents and sound effects that replicate engine noises, providing a realistic driving experience.

The setup is enormous and rare, with only a few units ever produced, many of which have been lost or destroyed over time. The game itself runs on Namco's System 22 hardware, and like other titles in the Ridge Racer series, it focuses on high-speed racing with an emphasis on mastering power slides around corners.
Ridge Racer V Arcade Battle

Ridge Racer V: Arcade Battle was produced by Namco in 2001.

An arcade version of Namco's PlayStation 2 racing game.

Ridge City is holding their road race around the city, and you are ready to take on the challenge. Race against 13 computer opponents, or challenge a friend in this continuation of the Ridge Racer series.

Pick from one of four tracks, including the original Ridge Racer track, and race on tracks in "Ridge City" in one of six high performance cars. The physics are like the original Ridge Racer.

This is the first time that a Ridge Racer game appeared in the arcades since Rave Racer. Most titles in the series up until now appeared on the original Sony PlayStation, with one appearing on the Nintendo 64 under the guise of "Ridge Racer 64."
Riding Fight

Riding Fight is a futuristic crime themed auto move beat 'em-up game that puts the player in the shoes of the bounty hunters Burn Bowie (player 1) or Keith Jager (player 2) that take on a criminal organization called Death Serpent.

While riding a hover board the player has to beat-up other hover boarders that fight with their bare hands or a weapons, futuristic vehicles and bosses. You fight the enemies with hand to hand moves and kicks. Weapons from defeated enemies can be used to beat-up other enemies and health can be replenished. The game can be played solo or with a friend.
Riding Hero

Riding Hero was produced by SNK in 1990.

Riding Hero is a motorcycle racing game with three modes of play: W.G.P. mode, R.P.G. (Story) mode, and Multi-Play mode.

In W.G.P mode, you pick your bike that you want to use, and then race up to ten world circuits, including France, Germany, Italy, U.S.A, Spain, Sweden, and more. You race against the top riders. Try to aim for the top.

R.P.G. mode is interactive. You travel between locations, and explore them, and speak to any people here. You start with no bike, so you must go to the Bike Shop and purchase one. Then with some help of the owner, you can race against up to six opponents. The more races you win, the more money you earn. Keep winning and you will be able to race the Suzuki 8-hour. During this mode, a timer will count down. If this expires, you must insert a coin in order to continue.
Rim Rockin' Basketball

Rim Rockin' Basketball was produced by Strata in 1991.

This four-player game approaches basketball with a more serious attitude than some of the more well-known modern basketball games. Control one of five players on your team: Dribble, pass, shoot into the basket for score! Now repeat.
Ring Fighter

Ring Fighter (VS Gong Fight in Japan) was developed by Kaneko and published by Taito in 1984

A simple, yet fast paced boxing game from Kaneko
Ring King

Ring King is a boxing game in which the action in the ring is viewed in a 3D top-down view and a full range of moves is provided, with the standard jabs complimented by body punches and the ability to dodge, duck or raise your guard.

Each punch weakens your opponent's strength which can slightly recover during a round break. A rain of well placed blows can produce a quick knockout, but normally you must hit your opponent many times before he goes down.

The game has three play modes. There is training mode to train your player before you enter a tournament. A ranking mode where you can select one of the three championships, Rookie, Japan and World. Each championship can be played at five difficulty levels. The third mode is the tournament mode. To reach the number one spot in the ranking or tournament mode you must train your boxer well.

Before you start you must create your character and set his initial abilities, strength, speed and stamina.
Ring of Destruction: Slam Masters II

Ring of Destruction: Slam Masters II is the sequel to Saturday Night Slam Masters. This installment forgoes the multi-track stages of its predecessor, opting for a more traditional fighting game-like stage design, controls and gameplay. The number of buttons is increased to five (two punches, two kicks and grapple), and the objective is changed from pinning the opponent to force a submission, to simply depleting the opponent's health.

In addition to all the playable fighters in Muscle Bomber Duo, Slam Masters II adds four more wrestlers to the roster: Victor Ortega (who was teased in the first game), The Wraith, Rip Saber, and Black Widow.
Ring of Fire

The "Ring of Fire" arcade machine is a classic ticket-redemption alley-roller game manufactured by Bay Tek Entertainment. Similar in gameplay to standard Skee-Ball, it features an 8-foot lane where players roll balls up a ramp to land them in targeted, point-valued hoops to win tickets.
Ring Out 4x4

Ring Out 4x4 (リングアウト４×４) is a top down vehicular combat game released for Sega NAOMI arcade hardware in 1999.

A game for up to four players at once. Choose from one of eight mutated super-vehicles. The object of the game is not to race, but to be the last one standing.

Knock all of the other opponents out of the inner circle, using tactics and items which are littered across the arena. These include Long Bumpers, Sonic Bumpers, Speed Ups, Ball Bumpers and Gigantic Icons, which can all offer advantages to those who pick them up.
Ring Rage

This battlerama has eight different characters to choose from, each decked out with their own colorful costumes, personal fighting styles and special power moves. The characters are Deckard, K. O. Joe, Killer The Shaddam, Spike, Knuckle, Yasha-The Ninja Warrior, Gunboat Rodie, and B. B. Scorpion.
Challenges include battles in the ring, crazy cage matches, warehouse wars, and junkyard brawls.
Ring Riders

Ring Riders is a 3D motorcycle racing game set in a theme park. The game contains several courses with up to four racers on the track. Points are scored by riding through giant rings, doing acrobatics and the finishing position. Rings have different colours (red, yellow and green) with different points. The focus is however on the time as a 5,000 points need to be scored within the time limit to extend the time and continue racing. The game offers 20 characters to choose from. They have different characteristics based on power, weight and speed. There are two circuits: Hurricane Ride and Seaquake Ride. Both circuits can be played with different weather conditions, which determines the difficulty level (Easy, Medium, Advanced) along with different surfaces such as mud, rain, sand, snow and water. There are five bikes available with different characteristics.
Ringer

Ringer is a rare, upright electromechanical (EM) arcade game developed by Williams Electronics, Inc. and released in 1970. Centered around a horseshoes theme, the game challenges one or two players to use a physical control wheel to pitch virtual horseshoes down a pit. Because of its unique mechanical design and low remaining numbers, it is highly sought after by vintage coin-op collectors.

 Players interact with the cabinet by twisting a physical disc or wheel located on the right side of the control panel. Rotating it clockwise or counter-clockwise determines the distance and force of the throw. Spinning it too soft leaves the shoe short; spinning too hard throws it past the stake.
Rio Grande

The RioGrande is a premium, slant-top class slot machine designed for land-based casinos by the veteran casino developer Belatra Games. Far from a traditional retro arcade machine, the RioGrande combines an all-metal secure cabinet with high-end modern terminal features to give players an ergonomic and deeply immersive gambling experience.
Rio Tropico

Rio Tropico is a classic pub-style fruit machine (slot machine) manufactured by Barcrest. Released in July 1997, it was built specifically for the Dutch market using Barcrest’s widely popular MPU4 microprocessor hardware platform.
Riot

Riot is a 3rd person action game similar to Cabal. The player controls the hero as well as a crosshair to aim and shoot enemies. The central gameplay mechanic is that the player has two fire buttons, one to shoot into the background and another to shoot into the foreground. Enemies will pop up around the player, front and back, so he must aim and fire accordingly.

One or two players must shoot their way through 6 rounds of various enemies such as grunt soldiers, sword fighters, helicopters and jeeps. Shoot the occasional flying red propeller bomb for power-ups which include a grenade launcher, flame thrower, rapid fire, shotgun, health or a 1-up. The action moves through a city in ruins, the jungle, underground lairs, on top of a train, through an industrial site, flying above a city in a helicopter, through a department store and inside the final boss's lair. At the end of each round there is an end boss which transports the fight into another dimension.
Riot City

Riot City is a 2D side-scrolling beat 'em-up game that puts players in the shoes of either the American detectives Paul or Bobby. Bobby and Paul investigate a drugs syndicate known as M.I.D. Then Paul receives a telephone call that the syndicate kidnapped his girlfriend. The two are now off to save her.

You fight various different types of enemies and bosses with jump, kick and hand to hand moves. Along the way items to replenish health can be picked up. The game can be played solo or with friend. The game Riot Zone on the TurboGrafx CD can be considered a semi-port.
Rip Cord

Rip Cord was another black & white game released by Exidy in 1979. It was designed and programmed by Arlan Granger. The goal of the game is to jump out of the plane and land safely on one of the many targets down below. The challenge is to avoid the numerous enemy helicopters that occupy the sky in between your plane and the ground.

You control the timing of your jump with the Jump button, at which point your parachutist begins hurtling toward the ground out of control. Pressing the D-Ring button shortly afterwards releases the chute and slows your descent. More importantly, it allows you at this point to control your left/right position via the paddle control to help you avoid the enemies.
Rip Off

Rip-Off is a vector shoot 'em up released in arcades by Cinematronics in 1980. It is the first shoot 'em up arcade game to feature cooperative gameplay and the first game to exhibit "flocking" behavior. The objective is to prevent computer-controlled enemies from stealing eight canisters set in the center of the screen. One or two players control tank-like vehicles while game-controlled "pirate" tanks rush onto the field and attempt to drag the canisters off the edge of the screen. Enemies can be defeated by shooting or colliding with them. The game speed and difficulty increase with each successive wave until all the canisters have been taken ("ripped off").
Ripper Ribbit

Ripper Ribbit stars a cartoon frog with an endless appetite for insects. Set against colorful swamp and pond backgrounds, the player must snap up bugs while avoiding hazardous ones. There’s no story beyond the premise — the focus is purely on quick reactions and accuracy.

The game runs on LAI’s “Game Room” hardware platform — the same light-gun system used in Lethal Justice and Egg Venture — but reconfigured as a single-screen skill game. Instead of shooting enemies, the player uses a reticle (representing Ripper’s tongue) to catch insects as they fly or crawl across the screen. The goal is to capture as many valid targets as possible before the timer expires. Wrong hits or slow reactions reduce the score and end the round early.

Play is round-based, with each new stage increasing in speed and insect density. Bonus bugs and special targets occasionally appear for extra points or tickets, depending on machine configuration.
Rise of the Robots

Electrocorp, the world's leading manufacturer and developer of advanced robotics ran the Leader Project to develop a multi-task, ultra-intelligent, self-aware robot to manage every aspect of the factory plant. The end result was the Supervisor Droid, a machine capable of assuming any form and accessing any database. But when an EGO virus infected the Supervisor's self-awareness, it started to consider its need above of those of the company, infecting the other robots in the plant and declaring itself their leader. Electrocorp then sent its top-secret ECO32-5 Cyborg to infiltrate the plant and destroy the supervisor.

Rise of the Robots is a versus fighting game. The player controls the ECO32-5 Cyborg and must fight all the other robots in the plant until finally meeting the Supervisor Droid. The controls consist of 3 buttons for punches and 3 buttons for kicks (one for each in the Game Gear version), and jumping, moving, crouching and blocking are performed with the directional pad.
Risky Challenge

Professional treasure hunters Vic and Vinnie went down deep into the dungeon, looking for the treasures of an ancient kingdom. No Sooner has they reached the bottom than the dungeon began to crumble with tremendous sound. Now they made up their minds and started climbing up to the exit. making use of falling blocks.
Rival Schools: United By Fate

Rival Schools: United by Fate is a competitive fighting game produced by Capcom in 1997.

The main fighting game is best described as a polygonal Marvel vs. Capcom game, with some notable differences. Control wise, the game imitates Star Gladiator's four button setup.

A player chooses a team of two characters, and fights against another two character team. The actual fights, however, are one-on-one fights, with the partner only participating by being called in when a player has enough 'vigor' for a Team Up attack, done by pressing a punch and kick button of the same pressure. The Team Ups are some kind of double team attack by the character and partner, or (for most female characters' Team Ups) heal the main character or give them more vigor. After the end of a round, a player (win or lose) has a choice to fight the next round with the partner from the previous round, or to keep their main character in play.
River Patrol

River Patrol was produced by Orca in 1981.

The game consists of a bird's eye view of a tug boat steaming down a tropical jungle river. There are rocks to be avoided, as well as crocodiles and other deadly river denizens. You have to accelerate if you wish to move upstream. If you cut engines (stop press accelerate button) you will drift downstream. The river itself becomes more difficult to navigate as the game progresses. Tighter squeezes and sharper turns make quick wits absolutely essential. The biggest problem is pin-point navigation. It isn't easy to snake through a couple of rocks about six feet apart or make quick turns away from dangerous beasts without running ashore or into a crash-inducing obstacle.
The object is to rescue the drowning people who periodically appear in the river, flailing their arms madly in the air. Passing the ship over the floaters accumulates points, and, as the journey continues, the tug boat gathers more and more of the rescued.
Riviera Hi-Score
Riviera Hi-Score (also known simply as Riviera) is a coin-operated video poker arcade game released by Merit Industries in 1986/1987.
Road Blaster
An animated laserdisc game where you play a sports car-driving avenger who is chasing after the gang of bikers that killed his wife.
Road Burners

Road Burners was produced by Atari in 1999.

A highly detailed motorcycle racing game in Washington D.C., London, Paris, Las Vegas, or the Isle of Man.
It features a tilting motorcycle and the ability to be hooked to other like machines for up to 8 simultaneous players.
The player's score is based upon the distance accumulated in the time limit. Players must pass checkpoints to earn additional time.
Road Champion
A timed car racing game where players try to race ahead of the opposing cars and cross the finish line first to become the winner.
Road Fighter

Road Fighter is a top view racing game. You have to reach the finish line before time runs out. Don't crash into the wall, cars or trucks. Because if you do you will lose gasoline. You can get additional gasoline by picking up fuel items. Especially avoid the purple cars, they do change lanes! And remember... oil makes road slippery...
Road Fighters 3D

Road Fighters is the Japan-only sequel to the original Road Fighter, released in arcades in 2010. The game features 3D-enhanced graphics, with a mounted pair of goggles used to view the effect. Tracks are set in real-life locations and are all based on race courses from previous Konami racing titles, including Enthusia Professional Racing and the GTI Club series. The game includes numerous licensed vehicles, which can be saved using Konami's e-AMUSEMENT Pass containing tuning and customization data. This game is Konami's answer to Sega's Initial D Arcade Stage 4 and Namco's Wangan Midnight Maximum Tune in terms of card-based games, or Taito's Chase H.Q. 2 in terms of rebooted sequels.

Its opening theme "Take Me Higher" was composed (together with the system music) by Sota Fujimori and it was included on beatmania IIDX 18 Resort Anthem as a playable song.
Road Riot 4WD

Road Riot 4WD was produced by Atari Games in 1991.

A game featuring four wheel drive racing with the addition of vehicular combat.

The game features 3 difficulty levels (rookie, intermediate, and pro). Players start out on a simple beginner track and after completing that, get to compete on 11 different tracks in various different locales to win the series championship. Some locations are located in the United States like New Jersey and Las Vegas, while other tracks are located on other continents such as Africa,Australia, and even Antarctica. Each of these tracks has a host whose team of 3 vehicles the player has to beat.

The players vehicle is equipped with an unlimited amount of missiles that can be used to shoot at opposing vehicles to slow them down. Crashing into certain obstacles will earn the player hazard pay which increases their score.
Road Riot's Revenge

A race offroad in which you use guns and missiles to slow the other trucks.

Road Riot's Revenge was a prototype produced by Atari Games in 1993.
Road Runner

Road Runner was produced by Atari Games in 1985.

In Road Runner, the player takes control of the Road Runner. The Road Runner must run along the road, avoiding trucks, landmines, falling rocks, etc. and also not get caught by Wile E. Coyote. The Road Runner must also eat birdseed along the way or he will become faint and Wile E. will catch him.

The Road Runner can earn points for eating the birdseed and also by making Wile E. get hit by trucks, falling rocks, etc.

The Atari 2600 version has a difference from the other versions, in that the Road Runner isn't required to eat the birdseed but can do so for the points.
Road Runner (Midway)

A shooting game that takes place in a desert where players try to shoot roadrunners, buzzards and other animals. It is the same game as Midway's Road Runner gun game with only slightly different back glass and cabinet graphics.
RoadBlasters

Road Blasters was produced by Atari Games in 1987.

RoadBlasters is a futuristic racing action game. The goal is to reach the finish line in one piece throughout each of 50 levels. Numerous enemies are out on the road to try and stop you, including armored cars, motorcycles, cannons on the side of the road, landmines, and more.

Your vehicle is equipped with a machine gun to help you out, and occasionally a weapons plane will fly in and drop additional power ups that can be collected. Some of these are the U.Z. canon, cruise missiles, and speed boost. Your car has a very limited amount of fuel, however more can be picked up along the way by crossing the halfway point of a level, or by collecting the red and green fuel spheres that appear in the road or after destroying certain enemies. On many levels collecting fuel is critical otherwise you won't be able to reach the finish line.
Roads Edge

Roads Edge (known in Japan as Round Trip RV) is a 3D off-road racing game developed and released by SNK for arcades (running Hyper Neo Geo 64 hardware) on September 10, 1997.

It is the first game by SNK to use real-time 3D polygon rendering and the first game (out of seven) to use the Hyper Neo Geo 64 arcade hardware. Players race in SUVs and pickup trucks through courses that loop around the endpoints, requiring them to avoid head-on collisions with other racers. Up to four cabinets can be linked up for multiplayer support.

It received a sequel a year later, titled Xtreme Rally.
RoadWars

In Road Wars you are set charging up a long hilly road, trying to make a road safe after a protection malfunction. Crucially, this involves shooting out the barriers at the side of the road (and avoiding falling into the gaps they create). You always play against another droid, who can be treated as friend or foe - pushing them into the gap at the side you've just created is a particularly neat trick, especially when playing a human opponent.

You are armed with a laser gun, which can be directed seperately from your main direction of motion. The roads include a range of hazards, including barriers and spikes, although bonus weaponry and a speed-up can be gained. Contact with these (or your opponent) will gradually drain your shields, and once these are gone you have little chance of surviving for long.
Robin Hood

The Robin Hood Arcade Machine is a video redemption shooting game that uses a life life crossbow in place of a gun mechanism, and is a collaboration project between ICE and GameWax.

The game is themed after the famous English folklore hero, known for his highly-skilled archery, and puts players hand-eye coordination to the ultimate test as they try to points and earn tickets!

The aim of the game is for players to aim for the bulls eyes that appear, earning points for each target they hit to win tickets (a play-for-fun mode is also available).

In the first round players are trying to hit moving targets. Once a player has completed the first round, they have the option to risk half of their tickets, and show their sharpened skills, by entering the Super Bonus Round to win the ticket jackpot.
Robin's Adventure

"Robin's Adventure" is a 2004 video slot / fruit machine arcade game developed by Amcoe. Rather than being a traditional joystick-and-button action game, it is a Cherry Master-style 8-liner gambling and skill-spin machine designed around a Robin Hood theme.

It runs on a video slot layout (8-liner) and features an optional "Skill Spin" function common in amusement-with-prizes (AWP) machines.
Robin's Adventure 2
Robin's Adventure 2 is a slot fruit machine published and developed by Amcoe in 2004.
Robo Army

In a futuristic city named Neo-Detroit, a scientist named Jeed kidnaps two police officers, Maxima and Rocky, and transforms them into cyborgs, but failed to implant on them a chip that would make them obey his will. They eventually escape his grasp and decide to defeat the mad scientist.

There is no character selection in Robo Army: Player 1 controls Maxima and Player 2 controls Rocky. Both cyborgs must cross six levels before reaching the end boss. During these levels, they will face the Professor's henchmen, as well as a sub-boss and a boss in each stage. The two heroes can of course fight with their fists and feet, but they can also defend themselves by collecting improvised weapons (car carcass, barrel, destroyed robot arm). They each have a power gauge allowing them to launch powerful attacks according to the power gained. Maxima and Rocky can also be transformed for a brief moment into an invulnerable armored vehicle.
Robo Wres 2001

Robo Wres 2001 was produced by Sega in 1986.

As the name implies, Robo Wres 2001 is a game about robots that wrestle in (what then was) the future. Six robots from six countries fight in a tournament that, apart from the robot element, is closer to American, Mexican or Japanese wrestling than the classic kind of wrestling. Each player uses three keys or buttons to execute various attacks in the classic "button masher" beat'em'up manner, with different button combinations triggering different techniques according to the proximity between the combatants. Each robot has its own arsenal of special moves. The ring is viewed from an elevated position and allows movement in two dimensions. The losing robot is turned into scrap ready for recycling, with the winner going on the next round.
RoboCop

Patrolman Alex Murphy was killed on the streets of Detroit. The major corporation there, Omni Consumer Products (OCP) saw an opportunity to sell a new kind of law enforcement officer to the troubled city. They took what was left of Murphy, encased it in titanium armor, wiped his memory and created RoboCop. Now it's up to RoboCop to clean the streets of Detroit and eliminate the one responsible for his murder, Clarence Boddicker. But it looks like Clarence might not be the kingpin of this town...

Based on the 1987 movie of the same name, RoboCop allows the player to control RoboCop. The majority of the game is a side scroller. RoboCop can punch and shoot enemies. He can move left, right, duck, and jump. Different weapons can be picked up from enemies, and items to restore power. Following levels, RoboCop will have to match a criminal's face to the proper mugshot and engage in a first-person shooting bonus round.
RoboCop 2

Based upon the movie sequel of the same name. You play RoboCop whose mission is to find and destroy cyborg drug dealer Cain, the corrupt RoboCop-II while following your directives to serve the public trust, protect the innocent and uphold the law.

The game follows the basic premise of the movie, but has some major sequential differences. It is mostly side-scrolling shoot-em-up, with some levels viewed from behind RoboCop and providing a targeting reticle with which to kill generic criminals.
RoboCop 3

RoboCop 3 is a platform shoot em up by Ocean Software in 1992

Cadillac Heights is on the brink of destruction thanks to Omni Consumer Products' idea to turn the rundown neighborhood into Delta City which means that many innocent people must be kicked out of their homes. However Robocop feels sorry for the innocent families and realizes that it's up to him to take back the city and give it back to the people.
Robot

Robot is a 1974 pong variant that is advertised as a self-aware, competitive player despite being a logic based game. Robot can play against 1 player (25¢), 2 players (50¢). 2 players can also play against each other (25¢), or 2 teams of 4 players can play against each other (50¢).
Robot Bowl

Robot Bowl was a black & white bowling alley game designed and programmed by Edward Valeau and Howell Ivey of Exidy. The game featured one or two robot bowlers playing with the standard bowling rules. To control the outcome, the game had five buttons: left, right, shoot, hook left, and hook right. "Hooking" the ball was the key to getting a good score, as you could only hook the ball after it had been thrown. This made it easy to pick up a spare, but the game made up for it by making splits very common.

Robot Bowl was available in two different dedicated cabinets, an upright and a cocktail, both of them used the same internal hardware.

The Robot Bowl upright was of the common 1970s 'short cabinet' design, as the machine had no marquee and was only as tall as the monitor. Some machines also had a decorative 'ball return' on the front at the very bottom of the cabinet. There is an interesting story behind that.
Robotron: 2084

You are a mutant human, who by some freak of nature has the ability to shoot energy pulses from his body in eight different directions! Your job is simple: save humanity from their own creation -- the ROBOTRONS! The gameplay is pretty unique for the time. You can move and fire in any of eight directions. You get thrown in a room with various evil baddies strewn about, you've got to kill all the robots while at the same time finding some way to grab humans and avoid death.
Roc'n Rope

Roc'n Rope was produced by Konami in 1983.

You play an archeologist whose mission is to return the missing feathers to the golden Phoenix. Use your harpoon-gun to fire a rope to higher platforms and then climb up. Use your flashlight to dazzle stun the attacking dinosaurs and cavemen.
Rock 'n Rage

It's another sold out show for one of the world's greatest rock bands - but this night is far from ordinary! A strange force from another dimension has eyes for the band's sexy lead singer Sheena, and has chosen this night to make its move. And to ensure that it has Sheena all to itself, it's taking Sheena through various periods in history. With Sheena gone, her band could be history! It's up to two of Sheena's bandmates, John and Rick, to save their singing eye candy before disaster strikes!

Rock'n Rage is a 8-way scrolling fighter in which John and Rick must battle through five time periods to save the lead singer of their band from a cruel fate. During game play, our two intrepid rockers can break pots to find note guns that allow them to attack from a distance, and point items that increase players' current score.
Rock Climber (Igrosoft)

Rock Climber is a slot machine game developed by Igrosoft in 2004.

Not to be confused with the Taito game of the same name
Rock Climber (Taito)

Rock Climber was produced by Taito in 1981.

Avoid obstacles such as monkeys and bears as you attempt to climb a mountain.
Rock Duck

A collect'em up with a twist. Avoid the roaming Smart Cat and Durty Pig, bounce sets of items in a row or column to change them from books to other items and then to sweetys and to Pye if you are lucky and after a few bounces. Sweetys and Pye are power ups.
Rock Tris

Rock Tris is an erotica-themed, tile-matching arcade game developed and released by South Korean arcade manufacturer Yun Sung (also associated with Soft Vision/Yeonsung Electronics) in the mid-1990s. Heavily based on a 1991 Taiwanese MS-DOS game called X-Rock, it combines classic Tetris-style puzzle gameplay with adult background images that gradually reveal themselves as the player clears blocks.

The gameplay acts as a direct clone of Tetris or Columns. Successfully matching and clearing blocks removes layers of a foreground screen to reveal adult/sexy photographs in the background.
Rock'n 3

Rock'n 3 is a rare, Japan-exclusive rhythm arcade game developed and published by Jaleco in December 1999. It is the third entry in Jaleco’s short-lived Rock'n Tread music game series.

A single-player music game where you hit buttons in time with falling on-screen notes and musical prompts to score points.
Rock'n 4
Rock'n 4 is a one player rhythm game published by Jaleco in 2000, developed by Jaleco Ltd..
Rock'n MegaSession
Rock'n MegaSession is a one or two player rhythm game published by Jaleco in 1999.
Rock'N Roll II

Rock 'n' Roll II is the hexagonal pusher based on the same award winning cabinet design of Disco Fever. It is the follow up to the original Rock 'n' Roll with ingenious new additions, such as a unique dispensing hopper that pays out bonus coins or tokens onto the playfields after an operator adjustable number of coins in. Rock 'n' Roll gives the choice of having the successful 50 coin splash feature with random jackpot payouts.

Gameplay

Players insert their money for a normal push of coins and also to push foward the coins of a higher value, or the prize tokens which are dispensed from a hopper, onto the playfield, after an operator adjustable number of coins in, adding play appeal. They may also play for the added incentive of a random jackpot payout and coin-splash feature which is an optional extra. Each time the random jackpot is initiated, the coin is diverted into a transparent container which is in full view of the player.
Rock'n Tread
Rock'n Tread is a one player rhythm game published by Jaleco in 1999.
Rock'n Tread 2
Rock'n Tread 2 is a one player rhythm game published by Jaleco in 1999.
Rocket Money
Rocket Money is a retro UK fruit machine originally produced by Red Gaming (and sometimes associated with Barcrest or Bell-Fruit hardware like the MPU5 system).
Rocket Science

Rocket Science is a classic UK pub fruit machine developed and released by QPS running on the Bell-Fruit Manufacturing Scorpion 4 hardware platform.

Developed as a traditional pub-style slot machine by QPS, a manufacturer well-known in the UK amusement industry alongside brands like Mazooma and Bell-Fruit.
Rockin' Bowl-O-Rama

1950s themed video bowling game with a retro-styled cabinet. Rockin' Bowl-O-Rama is a future-retro styled video bowling game for one to four players. In addition to regulation bowling it features three variations: Trick Shot, where players compete to convert difficult spares; Ten Pin Poker, where players are dealt a playing card for each mark and try to get the best poker hand; and Blackjack Bowling, where players get three full racks of ten pins each per frame and try to knock down twenty-one without going over. Teasers which look like animated 50s TV commercials taunt or cheer the player. The game includes an onscreen jukebox loaded with thirty tracks of music from the 1950s.
Rockin' Kats

Rockin' Kats is widely recognized as a classic 1991 action-platformer developed by Atlus for the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES). However, it did have a dedicated presence in arcades as part of Nintendo's official PlayChoice-10 arcade system.

Instead of an independent, standalone arcade cabinet designed solely for the game, Rockin' Kats was distributed as an expansion cartridge for the PlayChoice-10 arcade machine. This unique arcade system allowed players to choose from a menu of up to ten different NES games and play them using a timed credit system.
Rockman EXE The Medal Operation

Rockman EXE: The Medal Operation (ロックマンエグゼ ザ メダル オペレーション) is a medal arcade game from the Medalusion series released in 2005 only in Japan. This is the second medal game to the Rockman EXE series with the first released in 2002 as Medal Network: Rockman EXE.
Rod-Land

Rod-Land was produced by Jaleco in 1990.

Two cute fairies must use their rods to catch the enemies and then slam them around on their way to the castle. This game was a Japan only release.

The player(s) control one or two fairies called Tam and Rit armed with a magic wand (rod). Following the concept of Taito's Bubble Bobble, the rod doesn't kill the monsters directly, but only leaves them immobilized, crying. To kill them, the rod can grasp them in a magic force-field and the player can smash them down over her head until they disappear and leave a power-up behind.

Each level is only one small screen composed of monsters, platforms, ladders and, later, tunnels. Unlike other games of the genre, the players can never jump, but have to use ladders. They can conjure one custom ladder above or below them in order to go to the appropriate platform.
Rogan Dosh

Rogan Dosh is a classic UK pub fruit machine themed around Indian cuisine, playing on the name of the popular curry dish, lamb rogan josh.

The physical machine was designed by QPS (Quality Products & Services) and built on the popular Bell-Fruit Manufacturing (BFM) Scorpion 4 hardware platform.
Rohga Armor Force

A good-looking horizontally scrolling shoot 'em up with a few unique features that make it stand out in the crowd.

2 players can join Team Rohga and take on the dark forces of Lagnalok in this sequel to Vapor Trail. Choose from 4 pre-built battle suits or construct your own using one of four possible parts from 3 categories - Arm, Body and Leg Unit.

When your battle suit runs out of energy or is destroyed by the enemy, you will eject out of the cockpit and continue fighting.

The arcade versions outside Japan have a number of things cut. There is no story intermissions between the stages and there is no stage selection leading to 4 different endings found on the Japanese version, but the game cycles through all 12 stages like in the Japanese version's expert mode.
Roll Fruit

Roll Fruit is a classic arcade video slot machine released by the legendary developer Igrosoft in 2003. Running on retro arcade hardware (such as the Zilog Z80 processor), it represents the golden era of land-based casino and pub gaming before transitioning into the digital emulation space.

While Roll Fruit itself is a niche piece of arcade history, it shares its foundational DNA, layout, and software design with Igrosoft's flagship smash-hit, Fruit Cocktail (affectionately known by players as "Strawberries" or "Klubnichka").
Roll Me Over Casino
Roll Me Over Casino is a slot fruit machine by Bellfruit.
Roller Jammer

Roller Jammer was produced by Nichibutsu in 1984.

A roller derby/fighting game from Nichibutsu.
Rollergames

Rollergames is a coin-operated arcade game by Konami, made in 1990, and based on the television show of the same name. This arcade game is faithful to the show unlike the NES version of RollerGames, which is a side-scrolling game. The game is for two players and features all the skaters and managers from the league.
Rolling Crush
Rolling Crush is a puzzle game developed and released by Semicom in 1999.
ROLLing eX.tre.me

Rolling Extreme by Gaelco is an exciting arcade simulator that takes the popular Olympic sport of the luge and gives it a street twist!

No other game on the modern market offers quite the experience that Rolling Extreme does, since those are focused on motorized vehicules. After you coin up to play, choose from one of four characters then compete against several opponents on one of three intense circuits! The deluxe cabinet design allows you to feel like you are manning a street luge board and you can even attack opponents with the punch ability!
Rolling Gunner

With its reliance on BAC, humanity had forgotten how to operate even basic transportation, let alone weapons. After the attacks from BAC and the subsequent social chaos, the human population was reduced by half. However, there was a group within Lerman Matsunaga that foresaw the dangers of a dependence on Buster Engines and the BAC that controlled them. This group led the third stage of energy development, an anti-BAC weapon developed in secret that would render Busterium inert, called the Rolling Gun. The third stage of energy development, the military package of the Rolling Gun and the mothership named the Anti-BAC Suppression Independent Control Armament "Rolling Gun" Deployment Warship RF-42R STORK was rolled out. March 18th, 2061 - "Operation Downfall" Commences The mission: to destroy BAC, which has turned Lerman Matsunaga into a fortress.
Rolling Thunder

Rolling Thunder is a side-scrolling action game produced by Namco originally released in 1986 as a coin-operated arcade game which ran on the Namco System 86 hardware.

Rolling Thunder is the world's most powerful secret police force and you are its best agent. Your mission is to stop an underground conspiracy to conquer the world and to save agent Leila, who has been captured. Starting out armed only with a handgun, you have to make your way through heavily guarded hallways and secret passages to find Leila and stop the enemy.
Rolling Thunder 2

As super agent Leila or Albatross, only you command the street smarts and weapons expertise to thwart Geldra's plan for world domination! In ROLLING THUNDER 2, you'll infiltrate an evil empire that spans the globe from Miami's palm trees to Giza's towering pyramids. Jackhammering machine gun fire forces you to dive for cover through exploding grenades and spent shell casings. Wiping off powder burns, choking on smoky air; it's now or never. Take aim, and empty your magazine, spinning to drop that last terrorist creep behind you. Fingers numb from recoil, you slam your last clip into your pistol... time to move on.
Rolling Thunder Club

The Rolling Thunder Club fruit machine is a classic British pub slot machine manufactured by Mazooma Games. It was built on the popular Bell-Fruit Scorpion 4 hardware platform, which powered many iconic UK gaming machines throughout the late 1990s and 2000s.

Unlike standard Amusement with Prizes (AWP) machines found in normal pubs, "Club" versions featured higher token stakes and larger jackpot payouts tailored for private member clubs.
Roman Legion

"Roman Legion" is a popular historical-themed video slot game developed primarily by Gamomat (and often associated with Amatic or Konami in different cabinet/regional variations). While often referred to colloquially as a "fruit machine" by players in the UK, it focuses strictly on a military Roman aesthetic rather than traditional fruit symbols.
Rompers

The player must take up control of Chap, a gardener wearing a straw hat, who must collect all the keys in sixty-one maze-inspired gardens in order to rescue his girlfriend, Rumina; he can push the walls in the gardens over to crush the various enemies that pursue him, but they shall immediately be resurrected in the form of eggs which hatch after a few seconds. Each round also has a preset time limit to ensure that the player does not dawdle - and once it runs out, a green-haired female vampire known as Tsukaima (who cannot be crushed by the walls) shall appear in search of Chap's blood, as the Yamaha YM2151-generated song (and all the enemies) speed up.
Ronnie O'Sullivan's Rocket Money

"Ronnie O'Sullivan's Rocket Money" is a classic UK fruit machine (arcade slot machine) developed and published by Bell-Fruit Games (BFM).

The game was built on Bell-Fruit's Adder 5 hardware platform and themed around the legendary snooker champion, Ronnie "The Rocket" O'Sullivan. It features traditional arcade fruit machine mechanics—such as nudges, features, and a snooker-themed trail—built around a £70 jackpot payout system.
Rootin' Tootin'

You are a tuba, trying to collect musical notes and bonus items for points while avoiding other instruments. Runs on the "DECO Cassette System" hardware. It was known as the 29th video game made for this system (Cassette no. 29).
Rotary Fighter

Rotary Fighter was produced by Kansai Seiki Seisakusho Co in 1979.

A clone/bootleg of Space Invaders with slightly altered graphics.
Rough Racer

Rough Racer is a top-down racing game released by Sega in 1990. It was only released in Japan on the Sega System 24 hardware.

Rough Racer is similar to Atari's Sprint series. The object, like other Sega racing games such as Power Drift and Hot Rod, is to finish in third place or better. The player has the option to continue if he or she places fourth.

Like Sprint and Leland's Super Off Road, the player has the option to spend money earned on upgrades for their cars after a race, such as a shield, high-grip tires as well as nitrous—which can be used as a weapon as explained below.

Four cars compete on the track, with an added enemy (known as "Bandit Racers") who is there to sabotage the race and disrupt the progress of the players and computer opponents—usually road equipment. These must be avoided, or can be rammed using nitrous. Causing them to crash will cause them to drop coins. Coins can also be earned by smashing through brick walls that reveal shortcuts in later races.
Rough Ranger

Rough Ranger was produced by SunA Electronics in 1988.

One or two players work their way through military base to rescue a girl.

Almost the exact same type of game as Rolling Thunder -- even some of the characters are the same -- but the play control is not as good as the original.

The game software was designed by SUNA Electronics and licensed to Sharp Image for manufacture. Some marquees for the game say "Distributed by Capcom."
Rougien

Rougien was produced by Sanritsu in 1982.

A weird space shooter in which you fly a space shuttle who has to shoot down aliens, and a boss that could only be described as a giant set of lips.
Roulette

Roulette was produced by Whittaker Bros.
Five slots per player position allow the player to easily place bets with LED indication of colours backed.
Round Up 5: Super Delta Force

Round Up 5: Super Delta Force is a driving game based on ideas from Chase H.Q. and Out Run where you must drive over five stages to catch up with five escaping criminals.

As you drive a fork in the road appears and you must decide which route to take which then decides which criminal you are going to attempt to catch. As you drive you must avoid hitting other vehicles or the side of the road as this will slow you down but you do have limited boosts to drive faster as you aim to get to the criminal within 60 seconds. Once you have caught up with the criminal the clock resets to 60 seconds and you retain all your boosts but he is surrounded by a large biker gang. You must knock down all the bikers before you can smash into the escaping criminal three times to arrest him. You now move to the next stage and catch the remaining criminals. If you run out of time at any point you can continue where you stopped.
Round-Up

Round-Up is an arcade video game released in 1981 by Centuri. This game is also known and released by Taito as Fitter.

The object of the game is for the player to maneuver his white robot within a maze, capture a red character robot as they move about the maze, and race to the center to change the 9 white balls located there to red. The player may only change one white ball to red at a time after he has captured a red robot, and must evade 4 chaser monsters in the process. Bonus point may be earned when capturing the elusive 'red king' that appears on the screen. Capture him and you will momentarily immobilize the chasers. Play is over when the chasers have captured all of the player's robots.
Route 16

Route-16 is a video game released in arcades by Tehkan and Sun Electronics in 1981. The game was licensed to Centuri for distribution in the United States. It was ported to the Arcadia 2001 console. 

The player controls a car and must explore a maze divided into sixteen rooms. The player must collect all the money bags while avoiding colliding with opponents' cars or running out of fuel. Every time the player goes out of a room, a map is shown, indicating the position of every car and all the money bags. There are also flags that can be driven over to invert the roles, so the player can crash the opposite cars and stop them for a few seconds, while getting bonus points.
Route 66

The Route 66 fruit machine is a classic amusement-with-prizes (AWP) pub slot machine designed and manufactured by the legendary British arcade brand JPM (JPM International). It is fondly remembered by classic arcade enthusiasts as a staple of the vintage era of British pub gaming.

Like many classic JPM titles, it centered on traditional gameplay loops highly favored by collectors—featuring traditional fruit symbols, manual nudges, high-low gamble mechanics, and strategic feature trails.
Rovers Return

The Rovers Return fruit machine is a highly collectible, British pub-style Amusement with Prize (AWP) machine based on the iconic pub from the TV soap Coronation Street. First released in June 1995 by Maygay Machines Ltd under their M1/Epoch technology hardware, the game has seen several variations, refurbishments, and cabinet designs over the decades.
Royal
Royal is a video poker game with a pool theme and a hack of 1996 game Pool 10.
Royal Gum
Royal Gum is a video casino card game by an unknown company.
Royal Mahjong

Royal Mahjong is a riichi mahjong (two-player variant) gambling game developed and released by Nichibutsu for arcades exclusively in Japan in 1981.

An early arcade mahjong game based on the game Janputer, Royal Mahjong is the progenitor of the "BET" variant of the genre, where the scoring and time systems are replaced with credit gambling.

Players in the game bet with their insert credits, and can earn additional credits by winning mahjong hands (with higher-value hands granting additional credits). Arcade operators can change the maximum amount of credits that can be bet at once (1, 5, 10, or 20) and the chance of the game providing a winnable hand (from 50% to 96%).
Royal Vegas Joker Card

Royal Vegas Joker Card is a classic video poker arcade game released in 1993 by the developer Fun World. It is an entry-level card-based gaming machine that operated primarily in casinos, bars, and amusement arcades. Today, it is mostly recognized as a retro title kept alive through emulation software.
Royle Banker

The Royle Banker fruit machine (often catalogued as Royle Banker) is a classic UK pub slot machine manufactured by Bell-Fruit Manufacturing. It runs on the famous Bellfruit Scorpion 4 hardware platform, which was a staple in British pubs and amusement arcades during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

As an Amusement with Prize (AWP) machine, it relies on traditional fruit symbols, nudge/hold mechanics, and a cash ladder or bonus board that allows players to gamble their winnings upwards.
Rugby

Rugby is a rare arcade game produced by the Italian manufacturer Sidam in 1976.
Despite its name, it is actually a video pinball game—specifically an unauthorized "bootleg" copy of Atari's popular Video Pinball.
Ruleta RCI

Ruleta RCI is a classic, multiplayer electronic casino roulette game designed specifically for Spanish amusement arcades. Operating as a 6-player mechanical or video-assisted cabinet, it was originally distributed throughout Spain.
Ruleta RE-800
Ruleta RE-800 is a vintage electronic roulette arcade machine that is preserved and emulated via the MAME database.
Ruleta RE-900
The Ruleta RE-900 arcade machine (often referred to in the context of the roulette wheel or casino game room) is a puzzle and Easter egg featured in the survival horror game Resident Evil: Requiem.
Rumba Lumber

Rumba Lumber was produced by Taito in 1984.

You control a lumberjack that attempts to cut down trees.
Run and Gun

Run and Gun was produced by Konami in 1993.

A fast-paced five-on-five basketball game with only two rules: shot clock and out-of-bounds. The cabinet is a unique design with dual monitors showing opposite ends of the court in proper perspective. Very addictive gameplay!

This game is known as Slam Dunk in Japan.
Run and Gun 2

Run and Gun 2 was produced by Konami in 1996.

A five-on-five basketball game. Compete for the championship either by yourself or team up with a friend. The game offers both joint and competitive play.

This is a direct sequel to Run Gun. The graphics have been majorly improved with the help of the Konami System GX.

A standard five-on-five basketball game. The gameplay is similar to the original but it seems slower overall.
Run for Your Money

RUN FOR YOUR MONEY presents a brand new game strategy with its main feature providing fortuitous forays around its Blue, Yellow and Red RUN FOR YOUR MONEY cash trails.

FEATURE ENTRY
3 ‘Money’ symbols or Win/Feature Exchange.

FEATURE LADDER
Hi-Lo climb takes you up towards the RUN FOR YOUR MONEY trails and presents Features, Nudges and Bonus Positions offering:
‘Hi-Lo Hints’, ‘No Lose’, ‘Change that Number, ‘Bust’, and ‘Skill Stop’ chances along the way.

THE COLOUR OF MONEY
Blue, Yellow and Red RUN FOR YOUR MONEY cash trails can be won, with ‘Money Money Money’ giving you a RUN FOR YOUR MONEY on all three colours!

Cash Explosion, Hidden Features, and Mystery Nudges all contribute to the intriguing play appeal of this exciting new Barcrest game.

THERE’S NO TIME TO LOSE! 
MAKE A DASH FOR THE CASH!
Run Run Puppy

Run Run Puppy (known in Japanese as らんらんぱぴぃ / Ranranpapii) is a rare arcade medal game developed and manufactured by Konami in the year 2000.

Players can insert up to 3 medals per play. Pushing the single main control button instructs the on-screen puppy to leap or interact. The core objective involves throwing bones for the puppy to jump and catch. Successfully completing mini-tasks three times or hitting a lucky alignment rewards the player with a payout of arcade medals, triggering a "chance game" mode for bonus prizes.
Runaway

Runaway was produced by Atari in 1982.

This prototype got to field test (August, 1982) but was never released. This prototype re-appeared 16 years later at the 1998 California Extreme show.
Rush'n Attack

Rush'n Attack is an action-platform game tin which the players assume the roles of the United States special operations Green Berets who are infiltrating an enemy military base to save POWs from execution by firing squad.

There are four distinct sections of gameplay, taking in a Missile Base, a Harbour, a Bridge, and an enemy Prison Camp. Extra weapons with limited ammunition can be collected along the way, which will make the task a lot easier. The level is divided into 3 horizontal levels, which can be moved between either by jumping or using ladders, and this gives a chance to avoid the more threatening mobs of enemy fighters.
Rush'n Attack (PlayChoice-10)

PlayChoice-10 is an arcade machine which can consist of as many as 10 different games previously available only on the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) home console. The games for this system are in the modular form of circuit boards which are plugged into one of the ten open slots on the PlayChoice-10's motherboard.

There are four distinct sections of gameplay, taking in a Missile Base, a Harbour, a Bridge, and an enemy Prison Camp. Extra weapons with limited ammunition can be collected along the way, which will make the task a lot easier. The level is divided into 3 horizontal levels, which can be moved between either by jumping or using ladders, and this gives a chance to avoid the more threatening mobs of enemy fighters.
Rushing Heroes

A modern and realistic 3-D football simulator with attractive graphics and sound. Select from a large selection of teams with various levels of four abilities: passing, running, blocking, tackling. The game has excellent graphics and very good speech from the announcer who commentates on the gameplay. There are a large number of running and passing plays to select from, including a kick/punt. The quarterback can pick from several players to throw to. There are numerous defensive plays in the categories of passing, running, and blitz. This game certainly breaks the genre of the poorly designed sports game.
Rygar

An evil being known as Ligar is about to conquer the land of Argool. Such is his power that no living creature dares to cross paths with him. But the legendary warrior Rygar rises from his grave to restore peace and justice. Armed with his famed weapon Diskarmor, Rygar begins to traverse the vast lands that lead to the lair of the demon, as his minions are trying in vain to stop him...

Originally released on the arcades, Rygar is a side-scrolling action game. The player controls the titular hero, advancing through stages populated by hostile creatures. Beside the Diskarmor, a weapon that looks like a shield with a chain attached to it, the hero can use a variety of other weapons, including projectiles that can be fired in four directions. Various "powers" are scattered through the levels and can be collected. The effects of these powers include increasing the fire power of the equipped weapon, adding time to the clock, temporary invisibility, extra points, etc.
Rygar (PlayChoice-10)

PlayChoice-10 is an arcade machine which can consist of as many as 10 different games previously available only on the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) home console. The games for this system are in the modular form of circuit boards which are plugged into one of the ten open slots on the PlayChoice-10's motherboard.
Ryu Jin
Ryu Jin is a vertically scrolling shooter for 1 or 2 players (co-op), developed by East Technology and published by Taito Corporation, which was exclusivley released in Japan in 1993.
RyuKyu

Solitaire Poker, known as Ryukyu (琉球) in Japan, is a puzzle game developed by ASCII and Login Soft for various Japanese home computers. It was ported to Sega System 16 arcade hardware by Success and Sega in 1990. Face ported it to the Sega Game Gear the following year, with Sega releasing it overseas as Solitaire Poker.

Solitaire Poker. That's certainly an odd sounding combination, but that's exactly what it is. It's even more interesting that you realize that there is a touch of bingo in there too. Your objective is to draw face-down cards from one of four different piles and draw these cards into five different "hands" that are scored as traditional poker values. However the hands may be scored in any combination... vertical, horizontal or diagonal on the game board... (that's where the bingo element comes into play).
Ryuuha [BET]

Ryuuha is a rare, Japanese medal mahjong arcade game released in 1987. Developed by the prominent arcade developer Nichibutsu (Nihon Bussan) and published by Central Denshi, the machine operated on a betting/medal system, which was highly popular in Japanese amusement centers during the late 1980s.
Ryuusei Janshi Kirara Star

Ryuusei Janshi Kirara Star is a strip mahjong game with a space-anime theme and very extensive animation. The game features three girls with two strip sequences each. The game allows the player to select the first opponent, but following opponents are played in sequence.

As a unique feature, not every winning hand played by the player will lead to a strip sequence. Lesser winning hands will instead add time to a quiz game that can be played between hands. The game will display how many seconds of playtime the player has earned for the quiz game and the player can select whether to attempt the quiz sequence, or skip ahead to the next hand and earn a longer time limit.
