His army of vicious ninja controls the city as he summons sudden firestorms, earthquakes and avalanches! Lizard henchmen guard terrified hostages that you must rescue. Dodge through the inferno! Hurl yourself across crumbling buildings. Conjure up total devastation with powerful ninja magic. Heave an onslaught of Death Stars - the last things the evil ones see! Shinobi's fearless attack dog Yamato joins your race through danger. He combines the strength of three men, razor jaws, and the speed of a Shinobi Sabre. You're Shadow Dancer. They've dishonored you. They die!
Shadow Dancer (Mega-Tech)

The Mega-Tech System is an arcade cabinet released by Sega in 1989, and Western counterpart to the Mega 6. It was based on the Sega Mega Drive home console, and was designed similarly to Nintendo's PlayChoice-10: players chose games from a menu of eight titles, with credits buying more play time (usually 1 minute per credit) rather than extra lives or continues; reaching a game over screen does not end the play session, and players can start over or choose a different game as long as there was some play time remaining. The Mega-Tech was not released in North America, though did see use in Asia and the PAL regions.

The master of stealth and the death-dealing art of Shuriken returns to avenge the murder of his friend Kato. The ultimate evil is Sauros, a crazed reptilian monster with the power to invoke cataclysmic catastrophes.
Shadow Fighters
A Fighter / Versus game put out in 1993, developed by Sega Enterprises and distributed by Dutech Inc.
Shadow Force

Shadow Force is a 2D side-scrolling beat 'em-up game that puts players in the shoes of either ninja Kai, swordfighter Blunet, muscleman Tengu or beastman Coyote. The human race is threatened by dr. Wong and his Teaser organization. And now it’s up to you to stop him and his evil organization.

As you make progress you encounter over twenty different enemies. These include soldiers, samurais, blobs that take your form, monsters and bosses. You have the ability to transform in to these enemies and fight in their form. Between the stages you play a versus fighting game and the order of the first three stages is free to choose. Along the way health can be replenished by consuming food. The game can be played solo or with a friend.
Shadowland

Yokai Dochuki (妖怪道中記, lit. "Phantom Travel Journal") is Namco's first 16-bit arcade platform game, released in Japan in 1987 and running on the company's then-new System 1 (which was initially known as "System 87") hardware.

The game was later ported for Famicom (NES), PC Engine (TurboGrafx-16), and Virtual Console. The game was never released in North America, but an English-language arcade version of unknown origin exists, called Shadowland.

The player controls a boy called Tarosuke, a boy who must travel through a scary world fighting demons and other monsters. Press and hold down to increase the power of your shot.
Shakatto Tambourine!

Shakatto Tambourine! is a Sega NAOMI arcade game released exclusively in Japan in 2000. It is very similar in nature to Samba de Amigo, but rather than rely on maracas, the game uses tambourines.

Like Samba de Amigo, Shakatyo Tambourine! was followed by an update, Shakatto Tambourine! 2001. In a strange turn of events Shakatto Tambourine! was never brought to a Sega home platform, but was brought to the Sony PlayStation in the form of MiniMoni. Shakatto Tambourine! Dapyon!, complete with tambourine controllers built similarly to the Sega Dreamcast's Samba de Amigo Maracas (provided by Sammy).
Shakatto Tambourine! Cho PowerUp Chu!

Shakatto Tambourine! Cho PowerUp Chu! (シャカっとタンバリン！超PowerUpチュッ！) is a rhythm game developed and published by Sega for the Sega NAOMI GD-ROM arcade system. It is an update to Shakatto Tambourine! 2001, which was the sequel to Shakatto Tambourine!.
Shakatto Tambourine! Motto Norinori Shinkyoku Tsuika!!

Shakatto Tambourine! Motto Norinori Shinkyoku Tsuika!! (シャカっとタンバリン！ もっとノリノリ 新曲追加!!) is an arcade game developed and published by Sega for the NAOMI platform, and is the sequel to Shakka to Tambourine!.

That lively and cheerful game has been upgraded with new songs and new elements! ! The second in the "Shakatto Tambourine!" series. 18 songs such as "Mini Moni. Janken Pyon!" and "Lion Heart" have been added, and a total of 26 songs can be selected. New features such as hidden balls with bonus points and continuous arrows for simultaneous 2P have been added.
Shamisen Brothers Vol 1

Shamisen Brothers is an obscure arcade rhythm game developed by Kato's, a company which otherwise mainly developed prize and medal games. The gameplay consists of strumming a shamisen to the rhythm of various popular songs, from enka to J-pop.
Shanghai

Shanghai is a legendary tile-matching Mahjong solitaire video game originally created by Activision in 1986. The Japanese developer and publisher Sunsoft licensed the game and brought it to arcade halls in 1988, turning it into a massive coin-op success and kickstarting a long line of arcade-exclusive sequels.
Shanghai II

Shanghai II is a variant of the puzzle game also known as solitaire mahjong.

144 mahjong tiles are arranged in rows and stacked upon each other in various patterns. The player's goal is to remove pairs of matching tiles that do not have adjacent tiles from both sides until the whole board is clear.

This variant features 6 patterns named after animals: Tiger, scorpion, monkey, snake, panther and dragon. The player can choose to display hints or reverse any amount of moves. A mode with a time limit is available as well.
Shanghai III

Shanghai III (not to be confused with some ports of Shanghai II: Dragon's Eye with "Shanghai III" in the title) is a mahjong solitaire game developed by Success and released by SUNSOFT (under license from Activision) for arcades in Japan on November 1993, with an overseas release sometime after.

The third in the studio's arcade ports of the Shanghai series (after Shanghai II), Shanghai III features a new progression system, allowing players to tackle a new set of 12 puzzle configurations in any order they choose. It also revamps the power-up system, adding two additional ones (one for peeking under tiles and one for adding time to the timer) while adding a bonus mini-game between rounds to earn them (resembling a game of concentration).

In addition to the standard two-player mode (which no longer has mid-game joining), the game also introduces a new two-player versus mode known as "2-Player Taisen".
Shanghai IV: Ryuumon Hiyaku

Shanghai IV: Ryūmon Hiyaku, the sub-title loosely translated to "Dragon Gate Leap", is a mahjong solitaire game developed and released by Success (under license from Sunsoft) for arcades digitally via the ALL.Net P-ras MULTI Version 3 service for Sega's PC-based ALLS UX hardware on March 16, 2023. It is the fourth numbered arcade installment of the Shanghai series of mahjong solitaire games, bringing it back to its traditional roots with a single no-gimmick single-player game mode. It features both standard arcade controls (with a button to help speed up the cursor) and touchscreen controls. Players progress through 20 stages of unique layouts and are scored based on their speed, with a global leaderboard for those using their supported IC card.
Shanghai Kid

Shanghai Kid was developed by Nihon Game (now known as Culture Brain) in 1985. It had several publishers including Taiyo System in Japan, and both Data East and Kitcorp in North America. 

In Japan this game is called "Hokuha Syourin Hiryū no Ken".

In Shanghai Kid, you play a Shaolin monk that travels to America to enter various fighting tournaments.

The game is a one on one versus fighter. In order to win, you must use your punch and kicks, along with joystick combinations, to attack specific points on the enemy; if you try attacking the wrong point, your attack may be blocked, or countered with an even stronger attack that can damage you heavily. The same applies to your enemy; you can counter their attacks with a strong blow, or by throwing them over your shoulder.

As you fight, a power meter will fill up. Once it flashes, you will be able to perform a flying super kick that will cause massive damage if it connects.
Shanghai Matekibuyuu

Shanghai Matekibuyuu (Shanghai True Valor) is a puzzle game developed by Sunsoft and published by Tecmo and Activision on arcade in 1998. Later ported to PlayStation.

The title of this game translates from Japanese as 'Shanghai Story of True Valor'.
Shanghai Sangokuhai Tougi

Shanghai: Sangoku Pai Tougi (often romanised as Shanghai Sangokuhai Tougi or Shanghai: Sangoku Haitōgi) is a 2002 Mahjong Solitaire arcade game developed by Warashi and published by Taito. Rather than using a standalone dedicated arcade cabinet, the game was released as a software expansion kit running on Taito G-NET hardware—a proprietary, PlayStation 1-based arcade motherboard.
Shanghai: Shoryu Sairin
A one or two player puzzle game published and developed by Warashi in 2000.
Shanghai: Triple Threat

Another version of the ancient game of Mah-Jong. The player is presented with an arrangement of tiles, lined up together and stacked, with either 2 or 4 of each of an array of patterns. These must be removed by matching pairs, but only tiles which are visible and have a space to the left or right can be removed.

This release in the Activision's Shanghai series includes three games along with the Classic Shanghai. In The Great Wall, the tiles are stacked vertically, and fall when lower tiles are removed, a lá Tetris. In Beijing, gaps are created to slide groups of tiles along. The Golden Tile sees two players attempt to clear a set layout at once. The Triple-theme continues with three game modes: Solitaire, 2-player "Pandamonium", and Arcade. Three themed tile sets complete the "Triple Threat".
Shark
You control a shark who must swim through a maze of shark traps and nets and attack a swimmer before she reaches the shoreline. The first shark to eat five swimmers wins.
Shark Attack

You control a great white shark who attacks scuba divers armed with spear guns. Devour all divers and avoid all spears. Levels are numbered and indicated by flashing skulls. Shark Attack was the first Video Game to have Quadrofonic sound.

This game was licensed and also manufactured by Game Plan. It was also licensed to the company Game World by Pacific Novelty of L.A. in the U.S.A.
Shark JAWS

The player controls a deep-sea diver trying to catch small fish while avoiding a great white shark that is trying to eat him. Points are scored by running over the fish to catch them. The graphics are monochrome, and the game is controlled by a single joystick (no buttons).
Shark Party
Shark Party is a one player casino game published and developed by Subsino in 1996.
Shark Treasure

Shark Treasure or Kaitei Takara Sagashi is an arcade game set at sea. The player controls a ship and diver. The ship floats on the water, and at the right time, the diver descends into the water. The diver has to watch out for sharks, and has harpoons for hunting. The diver descends to the bottom of sea to get the treasures, then he needs to get back on board the boat. The game uses monochrome graphics.
Sharpshooter
A one or two player shooter game published and developed by P & P Marketing in 1998.
Shatekids

Shatekids is a shooting game about cutting the strings that hold suspended characters so they drop into a winning hole. Its theme resembles carnival and amusement park prize booths where players shoot strings to release rewards.

The player presses a button to fire projectiles at a yellow string attached to a character. Cutting the string causes the character to fall; if it lands in the goal hole, medals are awarded. A two-bet option is available in which all payouts have two additional medals added.
Sheng Dan Wu Xian
Sheng Dan Wu Xian is an arcade video slot fruit machine by IGS in 2002.
Sheriff

You control a sheriff who has been surrounded by bandits. You can move around in the middle of the screen, and pick off the bandits that have you circled in. The longer you play the quicker they move. Luckily you can move one direction, while firing another.
Shh...! Welcome to Frightfearland

Fear has gripped the city. Over 100 people have gone missing… presumed taken by a group of lunatic carnival characters. Two special agents follow leads to the entrance of a dilapidated amusement park. They now know what they must do… enter Frightfearland to find and free the captives… and close the gates forever!
Shienryu

Caravans are colony ships that venture into deep space in search of Earth-like planets. Eventually, Caravan 7861 discovered a a suitable planet in another star system. Nearly a hundred years later, the new mother planet became overrun by aliens under the command of the mysterious Shienryu. Fortresses were built with the goal of preventing any human development. Eventually, a special team called Burn Dragoon was established, comprising the best pilots who had to use all their skills against the alien threat.

Shienryu is a vertically scrolling shoot-em-up. The player-controlled ship starts with the default vulcan gun, which can be later switches to laser beam or missiles. Power-ups include weapon upgrades, speed enhancement (up to three times), bombs that can be used alongside the main weapons (up to twenty), temporary invulnerability, firepower and speed boost, and various items that increase the player's points.
Shikigami no Shiro

When holding down the attack button, the player moves at slower speed, and all on-screen items are automatically retrieved. The player character is invulnerable when a special attack is in effect. When the player character is close to an enemy bullet, the points gained from destroying enemies and retrieving items is multiplied by a factor based on the distance between the bullet and the player character's center. The closer they are to the bullet, the higher the scoring. When destroying enemy in shikigami mode, the multiplier also applies to the number of items dropped by enemy and all items dropped by the enemy are automatically retrieved.
Shikigami no Shiro III

A continuation of the Shikigami series, CoS III is a standard vertical-scrolling sci-fi shooter, featuring ten different characters each with their own special weapons and abilities.

There are five different stages to play in, each of them divided into two chapters and has the standard huge, wild-looking bosses to destroy. The player also has the option to switch between aircraft in mid-flight in one-player games or you can play with a friend in co-op. There are fifty-five possible story elements and a Tension Bonus system that rewards the player by putting themselves in danger by getting close to enemies and dodging enemy fire and it also has a gallery mode.
Shin Gouketsuji Ichizoku: Matsuri Senzo Kuyou

Is the seventh installment and the latest entry in the Power Instinct series. It was released by Atlus in Japan on August 8, 2009. In Senzo Kuyou, Atlus added some new characteristics like ability to dash in the air and perform "Aerial Combos" which have a similarity to those in the Marvel vs. Capcom series. Another new feature is that all the characters have "Chain Combos" that are performed by pressing the four buttons in order (A, B, C, D) and for first time in the series the "Guard Break" bar that fills when the character blocks an attack. Once the bar is full, the player will become vulnerable to an attack for a short time.
Shin Koihime Musou: Fighting Maidens of the Romance of the Three Kingdoms
A 2D fighting game spin-off from the Koihime Musou franchise, where where the generals of the Romance of the Three Kingdoms have been reimagined as anime heroines.
Shin Nihon Pro Wrestling Toukon Retsuden 3 Arcade Edition
A sports\wresting game created by TOMY and Yuke's and released by Namco in December 1997 on Namco System 12 hardware. This game is also known as "New Japan Pro Wrestling - Toukon Retsuden 3"
Shin Nihon Pro Wrestling Toukon Retsuden 4 Arcade Edition

Shin Nihon Pro Wrestling Toukon Retsuden 4 Arcade Edition (新日本プロレスリング 闘魂烈伝4) is a wrestling game developed by Yuke's and published by Tomy for the Sega NAOMI arcade platform. It is a variant of Shin Nihon Pro Wrestling Toukon Retsuden 4, released for the Sega Dreamcast the same year.
Shingen Samurai-Fighter

The game play is simple, you have 2 attack buttons and 1 jump button. The 2 buttons have a right and left direction, meaning that you can't attack on the direction where you're going. The right button has a right attack button, and the left button has a left button. The jump button has automatically the attack instead of requiring to press to attack button while jumping. You can get power ups that spell "Samurai*".

The power ups that spell "Samurai" have the abilities in each piece are: "Sa" - Speeds up your player, "Mu" - Gives you a shield, "Ra" - Enchances your sword, and "I*" - more health. Getting all the pieces lets you have 2 sharp knifes that are projectiles, however, you lose this ability when the stage/section is cleared.
Shining Force: Cross

Shining Force Cross is an arcade entry in the Shining series of games. It is a spiritual sequel to Quest of D. It is an action RPG for arcades, but has no trading card elements.

It was updated four times across its lifespan, with subtitles Raid, Elysion, Exlesia and Exlesia Zenith. The online support ended on November 1, 2016.
Shining Force: Cross Elysion
Shining Force Cross Elysion is an an update to Shining Force Cross Raid.
Shining Force: Cross Exlesia
Shining Force Cross Exlesia is an an update to Shining Force Cross Raid.
Shining Force: Cross Raid

Shining Force Cross Raid (シャイニング・フォース クロスレイド) is an update to Shining Force Cross. It was not ported to any home systems.

CPU : Intel Pentium E2160 CPU @ 1.8 GHz
Graphics : A “nVidia GPU” 384MB of GDDR3 RAM and supports Shader Model 4.0 and 2x 1920×1200 displays.
Audio : 5.1 ch HD Audio
Memory : 1GB de DDR2 PC2-6400 RAM
Network : Onboard Gigabit LAN, Compatible ALL.Net
Storage : 32GB SSD drive for storage
Operating System : Microsoft Windows Embedded Standard 2009
Shinobi

Shinobi is a side-scrolling action game starring Joe Musashi, a modern-day ninja sent to rescue hostages kidnapped by a criminal organization. The game is divided into five missions, each consisting of several stages and ending with a boss battle. In most stages, Joe must locate and rescue every hostage before he can proceed to the exit.

Joe attacks distant enemies by throwing shuriken, but automatically switches to punches, kicks, or other close-range attacks when an opponent approaches. Rescuing certain hostages grants a temporary weapon upgrade, replacing his shuriken with a firearm and strengthening his melee attack with a sword. He may also use a powerful ninjutsu technique once per stage, eliminating most ordinary enemies on the screen or inflicting heavy damage on a boss. Completing stages without using ninjutsu, or under other special conditions, can award additional bonus points.
Shinobi (Mega-Tech)

Shinobi (忍 -SHINOBI-?) is a side-scrolling action game produced by Sega originally released for the arcades in 1987. In Shinobi, the player controls a modern day ninja named Joe Musashi who goes on a mission to rescue his kidnapped students from a group of terrorists. Shinobi was later adapted by Sega to their Master System game console, followed by conversions to other platforms such as the Nintendo Entertainment System, PC Engine, and various home computers, as well as downloadable emulated versions of the original arcade game for the Wii and Xbox 360. The success of Shinobi inspired the development of various sequels and spin-offs.
Shinobi / FZ-2006
ISG Selection Master Type 2006 (Korean System 16 bootleg), differs greatly from the original Shinobi Arcade.
Shinobi III

History (MEGA PLAY)

The Mega Play arcade machine is Megadrive hardware converted into a JAMMA compatible board that could hold 4 games at a time. The game programs were modified for the Mega Play hardware; ordinary carts would not work. Said to be 12 official releases, of which 11 are confirmed: Bio-hazard, Columns III, Golden Axe II, Grand Slam, Mazin Wars, Shinobi III, Sonic I, Sonic II, Streets of Rage II, Tecmo World Cup, and Gunstar Heroes. Flyer for the hardware showed "Streets of Rage I", which may be the 12th. Bootleggers released: Aladdin, Bare Knuckle 3, Mortal Kombat 3, Super Street Fighter 2, and Sunset Riders which which may also have been used with the platform.
Not to be confused with, nor compatible with, Mega-tech arcade hardware.
Shock Troopers

Shock Troopers is a 1-2 player game where players select one of eight characters to play as. Each character has their own attack. Players also have to choose one of three routes to take. The object of the game is to go toward the end of the level and defeat the end-of-level boss, which is usually a huge vehicle. Crates that are scattered throughout the levels can be broken into to reveal new weapons and power-ups.

There is a team mode where players have to select three characters. The characters can be switched on-the-fly during gameplay, which is useful if one of them is badly injured. Players can use the other teammates until life-ups can be found.
Shock Troopers: 2nd Squad

As one of four playable characters each with unique methods of attack and power-ups, go through the level and destroy any enemies that get in your way, and defeat the boss at the end of that area. When you have completed the first area, you need to select a path to continue the game on.

Shock Troopers: 2nd Squad enables shot locking, close proximity attacks, and evasive maneuvers allowing for flexible operation. In addition to the four characters, versatile modes of attack are featured using powerful vehicles and special shots. Letters that make up certain keywords can be collected throughout the game, and by collecting each letter in the keyword, you will receive a high score.
Shocking

Shocking was produced by Yun Sung in 1997.

You enter various rooms, each with a different challenge to complete. Solve puzzles to get through mazes, and kill monsters along the way.
Shogun Warriors

Shogun Warriors plays similarly to some other 2D versus fighting games during its release, which the player's character fights against his or her opponent in best two-out-of-three matches in a single player tournament mode with the computer or against another human player. It is controlled with an 8-way joystick and 4 buttons that perform weak and strong versions of punches and kicks. In one player mode, after selecting a character, the arcade randomly selects an opponent. The opponent order goes randomly and always leaves the last four bosses in a certain order. Some characters stabbed by ones armed with katanas or other sharp weapons can cause blood to spurt out, which became popularized a few months later by Midway's Mortal Kombat. The main unique feature of Shogun Warriors is its "grabbing system".
Shoot Away II

Shoot Away II was produced by Namco in 1993.

Another projection game featuring skeet shooting. Players use rifles to shoot clay pigeons as they fly across the panoramic screen.
The panoramic projection screen is 68 to 102 inches wide and has an actual picture of a real meadow landscape. The scoring system unit and rifle holders are placed in front of the projection screen.

The game play is a lot like the original Shoot Away except that there are more variations.
Shoot Out (Chicago Coin)

The 1975/1976 Chicago Coin Shoot Out is a classic Western-themed, electro-mechanical (EM) "Dale-style" rifle arcade game. Released by the Chicago Coin Machine Manufacturing Company just before they transitioned their arcade division to Stern Electronics, it stands out as one of the last major EM gun games of its era.

The game is timed for exactly one minute with unlimited shots.
Regular single targets pop up from behind barrels or in saloon windows, remaining visible for only a few seconds. Hitting regular light-animated targets yields 100 points.
 If a player manages to score 3,000 points within the initial minute, they are rewarded with an additional 60 seconds of extended play.
Shoot the Bull

Shoot the Bull is a darts arcade game that was released by Bally Midway in 1985; it runs on Namco Pac-Man hardware, but was released a whole year after their old Japanese licensors had terminated their 5-year-long partnership. Up to four players can select from one of four modes: (the eponymous) "Shoot the Bull", "Black Out", "301" and "Poison 301 Pro" - and they must use a trackball to aim their darts at the on-screen board (with a single button to throw them). In "Shoot the Bull" mode, you have to aim at the bullseye in the centre of the board, while in "Black Out", you have to aim at the lit areas of it; however, in "301" and "Poison 301 Pro" modes, the players begin with a score of 301 and must try and reduce it to exactly 0 (and the last one must either land in a doubles section, or the bullseye).
Shooting Gallery
A single player lightgun shooter game published and developed by Seatongrove in 1984.
Shooting Love, 2007
Shooting Love. 2007 is a Sega NAOMI arcade shoot-'em-up game developed by Triangle Service. It contains two games; Exzeal, which is a sequel to Trizeal and Shmups Skills Test.
Shooting Master

Gangster themed light-gun shooter. The title screen has a background animation of a princess, kidnapped from "castle land" by gangsters and carried to "gangster land". The first stage scrolls right, following the princess as she runs along a city street, away from the gangsters. You can be shot a number of times before losing a life, but are penalized with shots if you shoot the princess or if she is struck by a gangster. Other stages include a forest, warehouse and castle.
Shooting Star

Shooting Star was produced by Nova Wordwide in 1994. They say he is unbeatable. There is only one way to find out. Match your aim against his. Use the authentic, weighted rifle, hear the shots ring out, watch the big 20" screen in all its brilliant glory.
Shootout
Shootout is a shooting gallery-style arcade game developed and published by Data East in October 1985.
Shootout at Old Tucson

Shootout at Old Tucson is a live-action laserdisc video game, released by American Laser Games in 1994 in the arcade. The game saw a limited production run and was the only release by the company never to be ported from the arcade. Soon after the game appeared on the market, American Laser Games went out of business, which, along with technical issues which limited its popularity in the arcades, further contributed to the title's obscurity. Shootout at Old Tucson was also one of the first games by American Laser Games developed based on 3DO technology. The game was filmed at Old Tucson Studios.
Shootout Pool

Shootout Pool is a true to life pool simulation video game set in the dimly lit back rooms of pool hustling. It features realistic physics, which faithfully recreates the experience of a real life pool table.

The game uses a miniature pool cue and an ergonomically designed control unit which gives the player the real feel of playing either 8 ball or 9 ball pool. The intuitive interface control unit and realistic physics allow you to impress your challengers with true to life pool techniques and shots including Backspin, Swerve, Top, Side, Masse and Jumping.

The game has 4 playing modes:

1. Versus the computer. Where the player has a choice of playing against 12 different computer generated opponents each with their own specialty trick shot and ability level.

2. Versus another player.

3. Practice. Where players can fine-tune their pool prowess.

4. Tournament Mode. This feature allows operators to run an in house tournament.
Shootout Pool: Prize
An updated version of "Shootout Pool", an arcade billiards game controlled with a realistic miniature cue-controller. Runs on the Sega "NAOMI GD-ROM System" hardware.
Shot Rider

Shot Rider was produced by Seibu Kaihatsu in 1985.

A racing game by Seibu Kaihatsu.
Shougi

Shougi (released in September 1980) is a historical arcade game developed by Alpha Denshi Co. (later known as ADK). It holds the distinct honor of being Alpha Denshi's very first arcade video game, digitising traditional Japanese chess into a tabletop coin-op format.
Shougi Part II

Shougi Part II is a classic arcade board game released in 1982 by the legendary developer Alpha Denshi Co. (later known as ADK). Following up on their original 1980 arcade release of Shougi, this title brought the traditional Japanese game of chess into arcade centers across Japan, long before the developer pivoted to more famous Neo Geo action titles.

It allows players to test their tactical skills against an early computer AI implementation of Shogi, featuring basic text and piece animations typical of 1982 hardware.
Showdown

Showdown was produced by Exidy in 1988.

A shooting game with a Western motif. The player uses a gun, mounted to the cabinet, to play a game of poker with Tex (or Doc in some versions), Dolly and Rawhide. The game is essentially just a poker game where you have to shoot at the cards using the light gun.
Showdown (Sega)

Showdown is a full octane game that takes in breathtaking scenery based on real life locations in the USA and Japan, blended with classic cars with tons of character. From pick-up trucks to funeral hearses, the handling on this machine is spectacular, and it gives the players a real connection with the events on screen. Each gamer will have to jump, swerve, overtake and find new routes in order to come out on top of their opponents.

In Race Off mode, drivers are free to go where they like; Demolition mode changes all that, and players have to destroy opponents' vehicles before they come back with a vengeance. In Knockout mode, speed is the key element: it's a no-rules joyride to the chequered flag. Crossroads takes drivers through a series of intersections; one poses the very real risk of being run right off the circuit.
Shrewlock Holmes

The Shrewlock Holmes fruit machine is a popular UK pub gaming machine manufactured by Reflex Gaming. Named after a playful, animal-themed pun on Sherlock Holmes, it features a detailed, brightly lit board layout that makes it a highly sought-after piece for home games rooms, man caves, and garage setups.
Shrike Avenger (prototype)

Shrike Avenger is a prototype that was produced by Bally Sente in 1986.

This is a flight simulator game from Bally/Sente. Only 12 cabinets were made.
Shu Zi Le Yuan

Shuzi Leyuan (数字乐园, which translates to "Digital Paradise") is a classic retro arcade game released by the Taiwanese company IGS (International Games System) in 1996.

Players manipulate and organize numbers on a grid, akin to an action-puzzle board game.
Shuffleboard

Shuffleboard was produced by Midway Manufacturing Co. in 1978.

Shuffleboard is a simulation of a shuffle board. Two players (or one versus the computer) slide pucks on a field using a large trackball. The goal is to make them land in fields which are worth different amounts of points. Once the pucks are in a field they can still be knocked away by the next player.
Shuffleshot

Shuffleshot is an arcade shuffleboard-style sports game. Players compete in short rounds to score points by sliding pucks into marked scoring zones on a single play surface, with the emphasis on head-to-head or small-group matches.

Rounds support one to four players. Each player uses a trackball to send pucks across the play surface and two action buttons for supplemental inputs. Points are awarded based on where pucks come to rest in the scoring lanes; matches are decided by total points after the allotted shots.
Shuihu Feng Yun Zhuan
Based on the classic 14th-century Chinese novel Water Margin, it is set in ancient China and follows three selectable characters fighting waves of enemies with swords.
Shuriken Boy
Medal game published 24 years ago where you throw shuriken at your enemies for points.
Shuttle Invader

Shuttle Invader is a Space Invaders clone that was released only in Japan by Omori Electric Co., Ltd. It features a tank rolling back and forth between bunkers while shooting shuttle invaders. The game has a black and white monitor but the screen is painted with multicolored lines to simulate color play. Very little information is available on the game, as the Omori company now makes automobile gauges and other auto electronics.
Shuuz

Shuuz was produced by Atari Games in 1990.

The game of horseshoes hosted by a cartoon horse! A variety of comical distractions occur throughout the game. The game has a redneck theme and all the characters have their own sayings and quirky behaviors.

During the game there are unusual things taking place in the surroundings: a guy on a lawnchair drinking beer watching you, cows grazing, a snake scuttling across the play field, an airplane flying above advertising beer, a chicken walking by, a chipmunk digging up from below, and many others.

The game follows the same rules as standard horseshoes. Roll the trackball to pitch the horseshoe at the stake. The velocity that the trackball is initially spun will determine the angle and how far the horseshoe will actually travel. Each of the four players have their own unique throwing style, strengths and weaknesses. In order to excel at this game, players must master each skill.
Shuzi Leyuan

The game challenges players by presenting puzzles that require arranging numbers in specific sequences. The mechanics are designed to be intuitive, providing a learning curve that caters to both beginners and more seasoned players. The interface is user-friendly, allowing for quick adaptation and prolonged engagement.

While it might not have gained massive mainstream attention, the title holds a special place for fans of classic puzzle games. It showcases the creativity and skill of IGS during a time when the company was making strides in the gaming industry, offering diverse entertainment options during the golden age of arcade gaming.
Side by Side

Side by Side is a classic 3D arcade racing game series developed and published by Taito Corporation, debuting in 1996. Running on the Taito JC System Type-C hardware, it is widely recognized as the direct predecessor to Taito's acclaimed Battle Gear franchise.

The game holds a distinct place in retro-gaming history for being one of the earliest titles to heavily focus on Japanese touge (mountain pass) racing and drifting mechanics, arriving just as the real-world culture and series like Initial D were exploding in popularity.
Side by Side 2

Side by Side 2 (originally released in Japan as Side by Side 2 Evoluzione) is a classic 3D arcade racing game developed and published by Taito in May 1997. Powered by the Taito JC System arcade hardware, it is heavily inspired by early Initial D culture and the Japanese mountain pass (touge) drifting scene.

The core gameplay focuses on drifting downhill through challenging Japanese mountain passes featuring tight switchback turns.
Side by Side 2 Evoluzione RR

Side by Side 2 Evoluzione RR is an arcade racing video game developed and published by Taito in May 1997. Running on the Taito JC System arcade hardware, it represents the definitive final revision (Version 3.1 J) of the Side by Side 2 game software.

The game focuses heavily on Japanese touge (mountain pass) time trials and street racing, featuring licensed tuner cars from major Japanese manufacturers—serving as a direct spiritual predecessor to Taito's later Battle Gear franchise.
Side Pocket

The primary play mode, called "Pocket Game", is a straight pool game set within a limited number of lives; the player must achieve a predetermined score to advance through four or five levels, each with increasing number of balls. The player earns points by potting balls, potting balls on consecutive shots, and potting balls in numerical order. On occasion, a flashing star appear in a pocket, and if the player pots a ball into that pocket in the same shot, a bonus will be awarded in the form of points, extra lives or a bonus round. One life is lost if the player scratches or fails to pot a ball in two consecutive shots.

In the two-player mode, the player can choose between Pocket Game or 9-Ball Game. In two-player Pocket Game, the game plays similarly, except the two players take turns and there are no lives; if one player misses or scratches, control of the ball simply changes to the other player.
Side Splitter

The Side Splitter is a classic UK pub fruit machine (AWP) manufactured by Mazooma Games. It is highly regarded by collectors of vintage and retro arcade cabinets for its traditional reel-based gameplay, nudges, holds, and interactive bonus board mechanics.
Side Trak

Side Trak is a black & white man-versus-machine game where the goal is to pick up all of the waiting passengers with your train while avoiding the computer-driver "killer engine" which aims to take you out in a head-on collision. You can control your train via the "fast" button which allows you to temporarily increase your speed on the tracks. You can also use the joystick to switch between several tracks at various junction points.

Each time you make a complete circuit around the track and pass the start marker on the outside track, another car is added to your train. Passengers picked up from the outermost track are worth 10 points. Passengers picked up from each successive inner track are worth an additional 10 points. On top of that, passengers picked up when you have additional cars in tow add another 10 points to car.

Side Trak is the first of several games that were developed on a common Exidy platform which would eventually become host to their most popular games.
Sidewinder

Sidewinder is a 1988 vertically scrolling shoot 'em up developed by Synergistic Software and released for arcade cabinets by Arcadia Systems. The game stands out in retro history because it was built for the unique Arcadia Multi-Select system, an innovative but short-lived arcade platform based on customized Commodore Amiga computer hardware.

In Sidewinder, you pilot a spacecraft through enemy territory, battling waves of cannon-fodder ships, static turrets, and moving obstacles.
Sigma Poker 2000

The Sigma Poker 2000 is a classic video poker slot machine manufactured by Sigma Game, Inc. (a prominent Japanese gaming corporation) and originally released in 1998. Sigma was notable for being the very first foreign-owned slot machine manufacturer to receive a gaming licence in Nevada, bringing unique game designs to Las Vegas and international casinos throughout the 1980s and 1990s.
Silent Dragon

In the 1990's, a dark force appears on our planet. it's the evil Dr. Bio, the twisted genius behind "Bio-Roid". By using advanced biotechnology, he creates mutant life forms with superhuman strength, terrorizing the human population. To stop the evil doctor, four men, each with courage and fortitude, are chosen to wage a just war against these creatures. And now, that battle has begun!
Silent Hill: The Arcade

The game takes place in 1993, when a group of five students and members of an occult club travel to Silent Hill to solve the mystery of Toluca Lake. It is known that seventy-five years ago a boat called "Little Baroness" disappeared with all the crew and passengers on the lake, and the bodies have never been found. The next morning after the arrival, students Eric and Tina (the protagonists) discover that one of their club members is injured while others are missing, and that the whole town is crawling with monsters.

Silent Hill: The Arcade is a rail shooter in the vein of The House of the Dead games, complete with off-screen reloading and weapon power-ups. The players will shoot down hordes of monsters in various familiar (and not so) locations including Brookhaven Hospital, Silent Hill Historical Society, Lakeside Amusement Park etc., on their way to the heart of the catastrophe — a little girl aboard the Little Baroness.
Silent Scope

Silent Scope was produced by Konami in 1999.

A shooting game where you battle terrorists and rescue hostages.

Using a mounted sniper-rifle peripheral, you can see targets up close and personal through the scope, or view them from a great distance on the arcade monitor. Taking out the enemies is tricky business, however. If you wait too long, you will be spotted and draw fire. If you are careless with your aim and miss, they will home in on your position. You will also have to monitor your ammunition carefully or you will be gunned down while reloading your rifle.

The game has three modes of play: Target Practice, Time Attack, and Story. Target Practice lets you practice your sniper skills; Time Attack challenges you to clear several stages with a fast time and a high accuracy rating; Story mode has a variety of intense missions.
Silent Scope 2: Dark Silhouette

Silent Scope 2: Dark Silhouette (Silent Scope 2: Fatal Judgment in Europe, and Silent Scope 2: Innocent Sweeper in Japan) was produced by Konami in 2000.

Pick up your sniper rifle and get ready to take down the terrorists. Story mode takes you through a day in the life of a sniper, out to stop a deadly threat to the President and the rest of the world. Choose from 2 characters, Jackal and Falcon, each with a different angle to each level of the action. Multiplayer mode is also included on the PS2 version.
Silent Scope EX

A light gun game from Konami. You play the role of a sniper who takes out terrorists with his rifle.

This game uses a completely new cabinet than its prequels, Silent Scope and Dark Silhouette: Silent Scope 2, with "specially shielded speakers" to surround the player in the game's sounds. Two machines can be linked up to allow cooperative or competitive play for two players. The "EX" in the title is short for "Extreme." Sogeki is the Japanese version of Silent Scope EX.
Silent Scope: Bone Eater

Silent Scope: Bone-Eater is a rail shooter developed by tri-Ace and published by Konami, released for arcades in 2014. It is the 5th game in the Silent Scope series, not counting Silent Scope Complete.

Bone-Eater plays similarly to previous entries, but features a new anime-like art style.
Silent Scope: Fortune Hunter
Silent Scope: Fortune Hunter was produced by Konami in 2002.
Silhouette
Silhouette is a video slot fruit machine by ACE in 1982.
Silk Worm

Silk Worm was produced by Tecmo in 1988.

Silkworm is a classic horizontally-scrolling shoot-em-up. The main difference between this game and many other side-scrolling shoot-em-ups is that you will be on land as well as in the air.

The first player would play as a helicopter, but if a second player joins the game, they would play as a jeep. Both players would have to protect each other as well as themselves. After a certain number of kills, a "goose" helicopter would form on the screen. If the players managed to destroy it they would get a weapon's powerup. This would go on throughout the entire game, and a "goose" could appear even during the fight with the end-of-level baddie
Silver Game
Silver Game is a casino card arcade game by an unknown company in 1983.
Silver Land

You are a cross-country-skiing hunter. You try to gather rabbits while avoiding trees. Also look out for foxes, tigers and Panda bears. This game is a bootleg of "River Patrol" and is almost the same but with the sprites changed so you are a skier on a snow slope instead of a tug boat on a river.
Silver Millennium

Silver Millennium was released in May 1995.

4000 units were produced at factory. This game is considered as one of the rarest video game ever developed in South Korea. At this time, many Japanese company released their games in Korea and they was more interesting than Korean games. Korean gamers were not interested in their Korean games.

One year after the release, Silver Millennium boards were converted to "Pasha Pasha".

Beside this, Silver Millennium is a true jewel from South Korea. It's even a pioneer in what we call 'Maniac Shooters'

In 2007, Para JP want to do a sort of 'remake' of the game, but the project was canceled at a certain stage of development and the game was never released.
Silver Strike LIVE

In 2010, the world of Silver Strike changed forever with the release of Silver Strike LIVE. Similar to IT's partner product, Golden Tee LIVE, SS LIVE allows players to compete in online tournaments against one another at all times around the country. Customizable bowlers and bowling balls also made their debut in Silver Strike LIVE, while Spare Challenge – an all-new game mode was also introduced. Finally the world's greatest bowling game gave players the chance to put their skills up against the entire online USA.
Silver Strike X Bowling Home Edition

From the bar to your basement—bring Silver Strike X home!

Celebrate one of the greatest bowling games ever made! Silver Strike X, the offline version of Silver Strike LIVE, is the perfect piece for your basement or man cave. 

* Plug and Play: Just unpack your Showpiece™ cabinet, move it where you like it and enjoy HD bowling on a screen size of your choosing!
* Game Modes Galore: Test out your skills on Classic Bowling or enjoy the wonders of Vegas Bowling, where you’ll earn a playing card for each mark!
* Customize The Look: Change your sex, appearance, hat, shirt and more! Be the character you’ve always wanted to be!
* Customize the Feel: Find the bowling ball that best suits your game. Do you go heavy? Do you throw a big-breaking ball? The choice is yours.
* Local Leaderboards: All your greatest games and achievements will be saved and stored on the game! The race for home bragging rights is on!
SiN

SiN is a first-person shooter video game developed by Ritual Entertainment and published by Activision. It originally released on PC in 1998. It uses a modified version of the Quake II engine. SiN is set in the dystopian future of 2037, where John Blade, a commander in a security force named HardCorps in the megacity of Freeport, is tasked to rid the city of a recreational drug that may be tied to the rival biotechnology megacorporation, SinTek.

An arcade version of the game was released in 2001. It is a computer-simulator where the player wanders through labryinths of streets and buildings battling various enemies with a selection of different weapons.
Sinbad 2000

The Sinbad 2000 fruit machine is a classic pub fruit machine published by Nova (and manufactured in variants by BWB) that was released in 2000. It is heavily sought after by arcade historians and fruit machine collectors due to its rarity and unique cabinet variants.
Sindbad Mystery

Sindbad Mystery (シンドバットミステリー) is an arcade game that was released by Sega in 1983; it runs on their G80 Raster hardware, but with an extra Z80 running at 4 MHz to drive two Texas Instruments SN-76496s for the sound.

Described as an "Intelligent Puzzle Game" upon the title screen, the player must use a 4-way joystick to take control of the eponymous Sindbad (as in "The Sailor"), and direct him around various different mazes to collect thirty question marks (to reveal the parts of the maze on a treasure map at the top of the screen), while avoiding the various enemies - and, once he collects one question mark in a particular part of the maze it will reveal the location of a treasure item for that round.
Sinistar

Sinistar is a multidirectional scrolling shooter in which the player pilots a spacecraft through an asteroid field while enemy Workers construct the title creature. The ship can move freely in any direction and is equipped with lasers and a limited supply of homing Sinibombs. A scanner shows the locations of nearby planetoids, enemies, and Sinistar.

Firing repeatedly at a planetoid releases Sinisite crystals, which are collected and converted into Sinibombs. Maintaining a steady barrage produces additional crystals, but firing too rapidly may destroy the planetoid. Workers compete for the same crystals and carry them away to assemble Sinistar, while faster Warrior ships protect them and attack the player.
Sir Prize

The original Sir Prize was a great British pub machine. There was another one called the Jolly Joker that was practically the same machine with different symbols.

It had a dual coin mechanism, for sixpences and tokens. Sixpences (half a shilling) tripped that gadget on the left side for two games and went to the cash box, and tokens just tripped the token relay for one and went to the hopper. This meant it could pay out up to 20 tokens for the maximum legal prize (5 shillings), allowing the traditional 18 for bells. It had a time jackpot - hitting the secret combinations pound-pound-bar or bar-bar-pound turned it on, and then the next 10 games paid out maximum coins if a single Sir Prize symbol turned up on the payline, which it did nearly every pull. Hold and Draw was controlled by the Hold relay.
Skat TV

Skat TV is a vintage German video amusement and gambling machine released in 1994 by ADP-Automaten GmbH (a subsidiary of the Gauselmann/Merkur Group).

 It featured a variety of casual and competitive modes, including Next Mode, Hyper Mode, Synchro Mode, Random Mode, and Twin Mode.
Skater

Skater was known as the 30th video game made for this system (Cassette No. 30). In this game you try to skate along and dip to allow your legs to straddle the holiday gifts, which you then pick up and increase your score.
Skeet Shot
Skeet Shot is an Action game, developed and published by Romstar, which was released in 1991.
Skelagon
Skelegon (known in Japan as "SF-X", which stands for 'Space Fighter-X') is a horizontal scrolling shooter for 1-2 players.
Ski Champ

Ski Champ is a sports game, developed and published by Sega, which was released in 1998.

A downhill skiing game where the player holds on to the ski poles and uses his/her body to move the platform left or right to steer.

The game is the sequel of Sega Ski Super G.
Skill '98

The Skill '98 (often stylized as Skill 98 or Skill '98 Euro) is a legendary, classic Skill with Prize (SWP) emulator and multi-game system that became incredibly popular in UK pubs, arcades, and clubs during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

Unlike traditional "Amusement with Prize" (AWP) fruit machines that rely almost entirely on chance and pre-determined payout percentages, the Skill '98 system was built on player skill, speed, and knowledge.
Skill Cherry '97

Skill Cherry '97 is an arcade slot machine game launched in 1997 as part of the highly popular Cherry Master style of "8-Liner" fruit machines. Developed as a printed circuit board (PCB) system often distributed by companies like Dina Corporation, these machines became staples in arcades, convenience stores, and personal recreation rooms.

The defining trait of the '97 edition is its integrated voice synthesizer, making it widely known in the arcade community as the "Talking Skill Cherry '97".
Skill Trek

The Skill Trek is a classic UK fruit machine (slot machine) manufactured by Barcrest, often paired in arcade history or venues with its sister machine, Ten Quid Grid.

It is classified as an amusement with prizes (AWP) / SWP fruit machine, featuring traditional reel gameplay with low-stake options standard to its era.
Skimaxx

Ski Maxx was produced by I.C.E. in 1996.

Skimaxx is a water skiing video game with a hydraulic board and 2 player linking.
Skins Game

Skins Game was produced by Midway Games in 2000.

A realistic golf game where you play up to 18-holes on one of three authentically recreated courses from Arizona, Illinois, or Florida. Skilled players can use the keypad to store secret codes. The game had four modes of play. The Tournament mode allowed players to compete against others around the world for cash and prizes when the Midway Tournament Network was operational. The Competitive mode was realistic simulation with control for forward and back spin. The Extreme mode allowed the player to control the ball in air in addition to forward and back spin. The Hole In One contest allowed you to control the ball in the air and apply forward or back spin. You had three chances to get a hole in one to move to the next hole. All four modes include power ups such as Mulligans, Power Shots, Perfect Power Shots, Anti-Hazard Shots, and Grenade golf balls that would explode.
Skull & Crossbones

Fight as either Red Beard or One Eye through various pirate themed levels, like ships and forts, and even some non-pirate themed levels, battling ninjas, skeletons, and others in a quest to get back your hard earned money from an evil wizard. You can also fight side by side with a friend (who controls the pirate you didn't choose).

Fighting works like fencing, with a few different moves to use, including parrying. The levels scroll through with a boss at the end of each. You gain money by vanquishing foes and digging for treasure where X marks the spot.
Skull Fang

Skull Fang was produced by Data East Japan in 1996.

An air combat shooter that has a chase theme.

Waste the Competition!

Data East's SKULL FANG blows other shooters out of the sky with an arsenal of great features:
*4 Different Planes - Each with different levels of attack, defense, speed & maneuverability!
*2 Unique Play Modes - Choose from Auto-Scroll Mode or advanced, variable throttle Chase Mode!
8 Power-Ups - Increase your Fighter or Bomber weapons, power and maneuverability!
*Hidden Flight Techniques - Attack from above, use air brakes, side thrust and High Ion Shields!
Skullgirls 2nd Encore

Hear Skullgirls' story as never before, try your hand at all new trials and challenges, and see how long you can last in Survival! Also unlocks all five additional characters: sing zombie opera with Squigly, and make beautiful music with Big Band! Unleash Eliza's skeletal Parasite, and howl at the moon with Beowulf! And, finally, learn why humans cry with Robo-Fortune. All while taking advantage of the full range of color options so you'll look spiffy in your next match! It's everything you want, in one convenient package!
Sky Adventure

Sky Adventure was produced by SNK in 1989.

Choose between four plans to repel the attack of Colonel Claud. Flying over various terrain you are attacked from the air and the ground from a variety of flying machines, animals, plants, and huge boulders. Score is kept on an "Act" basis, and a higher score at the end of each act will net you larger bonus, as in an extra ship or more fire power.

While you are required to choose your plane at the beginning of each ACT you can swap it on the fly!
Sky Alert

Sky Alert was produced by Metro in 1993.

A vertical air combat shooter from Metro.

Sky Alert is a vertically scrolling shoot'em up. There are two planes to choose from: Type A and Type B. Both have two primary weapons which can be changed during the game as well as one bomb attack. Type A plane has a laser supported by short range napalm bombs and a wide range attack with homing rockets. While Type B has a spread vulcan cannon accompanied by missiles and a powerful autocannon with spread missiles.
Sky Army
Sky Army is a horizontal helicopter shooter produced by Shoei in 1982.
Sky Base

Sky Base was produced by Omori Electric Co. in 1982.

The player controls a space ship, moving left to right at the bottom of the screen.
Sky Bumper

Sky Bumper was produced by Venture Line in 1982.

Use the joystick to loop your plane and make points by blasting enemy helicopters. Shoot the gates to move from one area to the next. A neat feature is the ability to bounce off 'borders' with your plane, like a bumper car.
Sky Challenger

Sky Challenger is a rare arcade game released by Sega in the year 2000. It operates on the classic Sega ST-V (Sega Titan Video) arcade hardware, which was famously based on the Sega Saturn console architecture.

The game is a unique flying simulator where the player controls a hang glider. The core objective revolves around a character (selectable as male or female) navigating through the air to safely land on a circular piece of terrain containing a treasure. Unlike traditional arcade flight games that use joysticks, Sky Challenger uses a trackball coupled with five buttons for its unique control scheme.
Sky Chuter

Sky Chuter was produced by Irem in 1980.

In Sky Chuter, the player guides their missile launcher that must fire at planes that appear from the left and right edges of the screen, then make their way down towards the player. While they are homing in on the player, not only does the planes fire down on the player, but they also release parachutes containing bombs that must be dealt with before they reach the surface. Once the player manages to kill the last airplane, the game proceeds to the next pattern. If the player loses all their lives, the game ends.
Sky Destroyer

The player controls a World War II Japanese monoplane of color green, furrowing the sky over enemy waters.

The pilot has to avoid missiles and destroy a variety of enemies like Submarines, Aircraft, a Navy Destroyer and a Mid-Boss Heavy bombers and the final Bosses to clear next stages and go to bonus zone.

At each new phase the color of the sky changes according to day cycle, starts (night, Morning and afternoon) later a hostile island, could view on the horizon and the attack of the enemy becomes more intense.
Sky Fox

Sky Fox was produced by Jaleco in 1987.

A multi-stage space shoot 'em up. Fight women riding on dragons, eliminate a screen-full of aliens, dodge and/or shoot large asteroids, and destroy end bosses.

A multi-stage game like that of Gorf. Your ship is equipped with two kinds of fire power. The first is an unlimited use shot that is slow and hard to control. The other is a limited-quantity fast shot that is much more effective. You can earn more of these fast shots by collecting power-ups released by enemies that have been destroyed. Battle against women (foxes?) riding on dragons, large "Space Invaders", giant spiders, and huge asteroids.
Sky Kid

Sky Kid was produced by Namco in 1985.

You play a bi-plane pilot on missions to bomb enemy targets. Left to right scrolling screen, shoot at enemy planes and trucks. Fly down and pick up the bomb as you go along. Cartoon-style graphics and great music.

A great fun game, features 40 levels of game play with increasing difficulty and longer missions, with multiple targets to bomb as you go along. Avoid on-coming enemy planes, ground fire and air-balloons. Nice feature in that if you are shot down you can hit the loop button repeatedly to get control back of the plane. Some hidden bonus features, such as shooting the three dancing girls that appear when you complete a mission they turn into flowers. Excellent music and the graphics are all in a cartoon style.
Sky Kid Deluxe

Sky Kid Deluxe was produced by Namco in 1986.

You play a bi-plane pilot on missions to bomb enemy targets. The game has a left-to-right scrolling screen where you shoot at enemy planes and trucks. Fly down and pick up the bomb as you go along.

A great game featuring 40 levels of game play with increasing difficulty and longer missions, with multiple targets to bomb as you go along. Avoid on-coming enemy planes, ground fire and air-balloons. Nice feature in that if you are shot down you can hit the loop button repeatedly to get control back of the plane. Some hidden bonus features, such as shooting the three dancing girls that appear when you complete a mission (they turn into flowers). Excellent music and the graphics are all in a cartoon style.

An updated version of the original Sky Kid, more than a true sequel.
Sky Lancer

Sky Lancer was produced by Orca in 1983.

You control an astronaut that shoots at aliens.
Sky Love
A one or two player shooter game published and developed by Omori Electric Co. in 1979.
Sky Raider

Sky Raider puts the player in the role of a bomber. Using a flight stick the player controls a aiming reticle over a scrolling landscape. The player drops bombs in order to destroy targets such as bridges, oil depots, cities, factories, airplanes and power pylons. Each hit scores points and the goals is to get as much points as possible within the time limit.
Sky Robo

Sky Robo was released in July 1989 in Japan. It was Nichibutsu's last non-mahjong/hanafuda arcade video game. It is one of rarest games developed by Nichibutsu.

Mandora, the final boss of Nichibutsu's "Terra Cresta", appears in the final stage of the game.
Sky Shark

Flying Shark, released in North America as Sky Shark, is a 1987 vertical scrolling shooter arcade game developed by Toaplan and published by Taito in Japan, Electrocoin in the United Kingdom, Model Racing in Italy, and Romstar in North America.

In 1989, the game received a sequel titled Zame! Zame! Zame!.
Sky Skipper

Sky Skipper was produced by Nintendo in 1982.

You pilot a plane and must rescue animals from cages where they were placed by gorillas. To do this, you fly over a gorilla and drop a bomb, knocking the gorilla off its feet. Once this is done, the animals will be out of their cages and you just touch each one to rescue it. The animal cages will only be open for a limited time, then the gorilla will get back on its feet. You must then knock it down again.

You mustn't take too long rescuing the animals or you will run out of fuel. If you run out of fuel, run into a gorilla or the course walls or, strangely, a cloud, you lose a plane. You begin the game with four planes.
Sky Smasher

Sky Smasher was produced by Nihon System in 1990.

A difficult vertical scrolling shooter with nice graphics. Can be played with 1 or 2 (simultaneous) players.
Sky Soldiers

Sky Soldiers is a vertical scrolling Shoot em' Up, players travel back in time starting in Great Britain 1945, Germany 1915, Japan 1945, Germany 1944, Vietnam 1974, France 1914, Russia 1974 and finally the space station in the present time, 2110. Each time stage has two levels, both ending in a boss battle save for the final stage, resulting in a total of 15 Areas.

The ship's weapon system is accessed in the beginning of each stage. The ship’s main shot consists of a semi-automatic Wave Shot. The ship’s bomb weapons include forward firing missiles, fireballs, homing missiles and the buster bomb. The ship can be equipped with only one bomb weapon from either category at a time. The ship can only be loaded with a certain number of Bomb weapons and they can only be resupplied at the end of the level. The only pick-up item in the game is a parachuting human pilot shot down from malfunctioning fighter planes/jets; collecting these pilots results in random bonus points.
Sky Target

Sky Target is a 1995 arcade game by Sega. A rail shooter featuring a number of planes including the default F-14D Super Tomcat, it is best remembered for its semi-official connection to Sega's earlier hit After Burner. Although never billed as a sequel, its overt similarities to the 1987 classic were nonetheless referenced in official promotional materials and recognized by the media.
Skycurser

SKYCURSER is a frantic, hard-action shoot ‘em up drawing crowds of players at arcades and across the globe. Available today as a dedicated cabinet or JAMMA conversion kit, SKYCURSER is an exciting new chapter in arcade gaming’s rich history.

The year is 1996. A cataclysmic plague descends on earth. As its infection spreads, hope fades. But you and your dog fight back. Piloting the prophetic weapon, SKYCURSER, you take flight to destroy the Necrostar’s mutant hordes and save the planet.
Skydiver

The object of the game is to guide a skydiver from a travelling plane to a like-colored ground target. The player must watch the wind speed and direction and judge the target position, plane speed, and duration of freefall before pulling the rip cord. After that, the player must guide the skydiver onto the target by moving the rip cord control either left or right.

The skydiver jumps from the plane whenever the player pushed the Jump button. The skydiver's parachute is opened when the rip cord is pulled. The rip cord control can be moved either left or right to help guide the diver on to the correct landing pad. Points are scored for successfully landing on the target. The target point score is determined by the lenghth of freefall -- the longer the fall, the larger the point score. A double bonus score is awarded for spelling "SKYDIVER".
Skylanders: Cloud Patrol

The popular Skylanders have finally landed in the arcade thanks to this new mobile-to-arcade port by Adrenaline Amusements.

In Skylanders Cloud Patrol, players join the “Skylanders” as they patrol the Skylands for escaped trolls. Players start by choosing their favorite Skylander, and then take to the skies in a flying gunship to help put those troublesome trolls in their place. Tap to shoot or slide your fingers across targets creating amazing knock out combos! Score the highest combo area to win more tickets or points, and show friends who rules the skies.
Slap Shooter
Slap Shooter (not to be confused with Slap Shot for the Sega Master System) is a single-player ice hockey game released by Sega to Japanese arcades in 1986.
Slap Shot

Slap Shot was produced by Taito in 1994.

A hockey game that plays similar to the air hockey tables found in arcades.
Slashout

Slashout is the third installment to the Spikeout series, released for Sega NAOMI hardware in 2000. Unlike other games in the series, Slashout has a completely different setting, based in a medieval fantasy world with different characters—gameplay remains similar, however.
Slick Shot

Slick Shot was produced by Grand Products (renamed to Incredible Technologies shortly after this game came out) in 1990.

Players choose one of two billiard games: Slickshot or 9 ball. Using a real cue stick and ball on a small pool table surface, a player must shoot the ball into the game cabinet to simulate the shot on the video screen. Infrared sensors on the table slate calculate the speed and direction the ball is traveling.
Slime Kun

In Slime Kun, the player controls a warrior on a quest to rescue a princess. Along the way, the warrior must confront and defeat slimes of increasing strength. 

The game uses a janken-style (rock-paper-scissors) battle mechanic: three buttons correspond to rock, paper, and scissors. As the character automatically advances toward the castle, the player faces three successive slime encounters (green, then blue, then red); the player must win each encounter in janken to proceed. 

When the player succeeds in the mission, they are awarded real balls (capsules) containing small figurines as prizes.
Slipstream

Slipstream was produced by Capcom in 1995.

A rare F-1 racing game by Capcom.

An arcade Formula 1 racing game developed by Capcom for the Sega System Multi 32 arcade hardware and released in 1995. As the final title released for the Sega System Multi 32, it was one of the last arcade racing games to utilize 2.5D sprite-scaling techniques. Its principle gameplay mechanic was the "Slipstream" turbo meter, which slowly builds up and activates a temporary turbo boost when full, similar to the nitrous boost in later racing games.
Slither

Slither was produced by Century II and manufactured by both GDI and Century II in 1982.

The attack begins with a few snakes as the bonus score winds down. When you blast all the snakes, you get the remaining bonus points. Then, additional snakes attack in waves. Everytime the bonus reaches zero, new snakes of a different color will attack. As the snakes are concentrated on, pterodactyls and mutant gorillas move across the screen to increase the danger and challenge. Additional points are scored by blasting those intruders and the closer they are downed by your blaster, the higher the score.
Mutant gorillas can place additional vegatation on the screen which you will have to blast your way through. As the score increases, the snakes get mad and start to chase your blaster which will then have to be manuevered with great skill to avoid attacks. If mutant gorillas touch any of the snakes, the snakes will be invisible except for the eyes.
Sliver

Sliver was produced by Hollow Corp. in 1996.

An adult puzzle game by Hollow Corp.
Slot Carnival
Slot Carnival is a classic arcade fruit machine game released in 1985 by the manufacturer Wing Co., Ltd.
Slot Poker Saiyuki

Slot Poker Saiyuki is a Japanese casino-style arcade video game released in 1998 by the developer World Station Co., Ltd.. It blends video poker and slot machine mechanics, drawing its visual theme and title from Saiyuki (the Japanese name for Journey to the West).
Slots

Video Slot Machine published 28 years ago

You could find these machines in almost any bar in Belgium around the year 2000. After a year or 2 these were banned in the entire country. After that you could still find a machine here and there, but they would no longer give cash prizes.
Sly Spy

As Agent 006, you are the world's only hope: the terrorist organization known as the D.V.S. has captured the blueprints to a new, powerful weapon known as the "Red Rock Rover". Your mission is to infiltrate several islands occupied by the D.V.S. and retrieve each part of the blueprints. The shareware version only has the first episode available; the registered version consists of three installments, packed as separate executables.

Secret Agent is a side-scrolling platform game, where your objective is to complete 15 levels, allowing you to gain access to the "main fortress" which is the 16th level. On each level, you have to find and destroy a radar dish, and also find a bundle of dynamite and place it at the exit to blow it open.
Smash & Grab

Smash & Grab is a classic UK fruit machine manufactured by Barcrest during the late 1980s. Running on the iconic MPU4 hardware platform, it remains a highly regarded nostalgic title within the arcade community and fruit machine emulation circles.
Smash Court Pro Tournament

Smash Court Pro Tournament contains 8 real top tennis players. You can select between 4 popular male players and 4 popular female players . The male players in the game are Pete Sampras, Andre Agassi, Patrick Rafter and Yevgeny Kafelnikov. While the female players are Anna Kournikova, Martina Hingis, Lindsay Davenport and Monica Seles. The Tournaments are held at the Australian Open, the U.S. Open and Wimbledon.
Smash T.V.

The year is 1999. The world's most popular television show is Smash T.V., an ultra-violent contest between two armed-to-the-teeth combatants, set loose in a series of deadly arenas that are filled to bursting with hordes of mindless beasts and killer robots. The aim of the game is to blast everything in sight and try to grab more cash and prizes than the other guy. Toaster ovens, VCRs, fancy cars and luxury holidays are there for the taking... for anyone who can survive long enough to enjoy them.

Smash T.V. is an insane shoot-em-up from the brain of Eugene Jarvis, creator of Robotron: 2084. It retains that game's frantic style of play and two-joystick control method, but adds plenty of gore, violence, a hint of satire and that all-important two player mode.
Smashing Drive

Smashing Drive puts you in the driver's seat of an insane, outrageous taxi on the busy streets of New York City. Your job is to simply race from point to point in the fastest time possible.

The key to success in Smashing Drive lies in two features: crazy power-ups and hidden shortcuts. Almost all of the power-ups transform your taxi in some way that allows you to smash your way through traffic with ease. And the shortcuts usually involve crashing through the insides of buildings, like movie theaters and sports arenas.
Smokey Vs The Bandit
Smokey Vs The Bandit is a slot fruit machine by MDM Leisure.
Snacks'n Jaxson

Snacks 'n Jaxson was produced by Bally Sente in 1984.

Snack 'n Jackson sees you playing a clown sitting at a dining table, overlooked by two cabinets on either side. From these cabinets and from the player's perspective, food is swirling around the clown's head. The objective is to stick out the clown's neck and grab all the food he can possible eat, whilst avoiding spicy food like green peppers and soap boars. All this while bouncing a dismembered nose, which can be used to sneeze away the unwanted items and grabbing back the nose before it crashes through the window behind you. For each meal you must catch 6 sets of foodstuffs (each set indicated by a number on your clown's chest). One has to eat/play for breakfast, lunch, snack and dinner time to advance to the next day. Bonus rounds between days see your gather bonus point for extra noses (essentially continues).
Snake Pit

Snake Pit was produced by Bally Sente in 1984.

Snake Pit is a 2D top down arcade game. The player controls a character trapped in a snake pit. He must kill snakes by whipping them (like Indiana Jones). If he kills all snakes (and other creatures, like scorpions), he will go to the next level. Each snake is very dangerous, and kills the player instantly. The game has a non-typical controls scheme - a trackball for moving and joystick for whipping.
Snakes & Ladders

The Snakes & Ladders fruit machine manufactured by Bell-Fruit Games is a classic piece of British arcade history. While several manufacturers released machines based on this theme (most notably JPM and Crystal), Bell-Fruit produced its own prominent versions.
Snap Jack

Snap Jack was produced by Universal in 1982.

Guide a dot-munching, stretch-legged character through right-to-left scrolling scenes of landscape and tunnels. Avoid, among others, jelly fish and of course the kettles and boots on the overhead conveyor.

This game is a cross between Pac-Man and Scramble.
Snapper

Snapper is a Snake style game. You controls a hungry snake through various levels, will need eat all the balls as you grow and avoid colliding with his own body, while avoiding enemies to open the exit to the next level.
Snezhnaja Koroleva

Snezhnaja Koroleva is a Mini-Games game developed by Terminal in 1988 for the Arcade.
This game is based on a 1957 Soviet animated film named "Snezhnaya Koroleva" (The Snow Queen) directed by Lev Atamanov in moscow and is based on the story of the same name by Hans Christian Andersen.
Snezhnaja Koroleva is a single player platformer
Sniper

Released by Williams Electronics, Inc. in March 1971, Sniper is a rare, upright electromechanical (EM) rifle arcade game. Built with an army theme, it followed Williams' 1970 game Bonanza and swapped out cowboys and horses for soldiers and tanks.
SNK vs. Capcom: SVC Chaos

SNK vs. Capcom: SVC Chaos primarily utilizes the command system of The King of Fighters series, incorporating light/strong kicks, punches, cancels and charging attacks. Unlike its predecessor, Capcom vs. SNK 2, this game lacks both air guards and a "groove system", instead focusing on quicker gameplay.

Characters are provided with a basic 3-level bar system for executing super-special attacks with basic filling options attributed to strikes and damage. Additionally, the sprites from the various series received new models and some special effects were changed in the command lists (for example, the player cannot increase the damage of the Zujou Sashi used by Choi Bounge by tapping the buttons anymore).
Snow Board Championship

Snow Board Championship was produced by Gaelco in 1996.

Snowboard Championship is a 2D arcade snowboarding game on courses with gameplay similar to Zigurat's World Rally games. Using a side-scrolling bird's-eye view the snowboarder moves forward automatically and the player has to react quickly to turns and obstacles as signalled by arrows. There are three riders to choose from, representing Europe, Japan and USA, and several courses player either in the Beginner of the Championship mode.

Most of the focus is used on the steering, but a single button is used to run and get extra speed after slowing down, for instance after bumping into a board. The racing is always done alone, but each course consists of a qualifying run followed by a real race. To qualify, the course needs to be finished not exceeding the time limit. After completing a course it is possible to do the same course again or to move on to the next course.
Snow Bros. 2: With New Elves

Snow Bros 2: With New Elves (おてんきパラダイス Otenki Paradise) is a platformer developed by Toaplan and published by Hanafram in April 1994. It is the second and last official game in the Snow Bros series and the last game developed by Toaplan before they declared bankruptcy in 1994.

The game consists of 6 worlds. The player must clear the screen of enemies to advance to the next stage. The game supports 4 players, but requires a 4 player harness for the additional players.
Snow Bros.: Nick & Tom

Nick and Tom are two Princes living the dream with two beautiful princesses. When suddenly the evil King Scorch freezes Prince Nick and Tom and kidnaps the Princesses. Now Nick and Tom find themselves with abilities dealing with snow and ice. These two Snow Brothers will need to hunt down the evil King Scorch and rescue the princesses.

Snow Bros. is a fixed-screen platform game where players must defeat all enemies on each level (screen), 50 altogether. The Snow Bros use snow as their weapon, throwing it at the enemies to stun them. When lots of snow is thrown at an enemy, it becomes covered in a flurry and unable to move. These can be rolled into giant snowballs and pushed or kicked into other enemies. If left alone, enemies will eventually defrost and become angry at the player. The enemy filled snowballs are a much stronger weapon then the regular handful of snow and are the only effective weapon Nick and Tom have against the bosses.
Snow Brothers 3: Magical Adventure

Snow Brothers 3 - Magical Adventure is a platform arcade game released in 2002 by the Mexican Syrmex. Although the manufacturer has announced the continuation of the series as an original Snow Bros in reality it is a clone. The 50 levels that make the game are almost the same as the first Snow Bros except for sprites and backgrounds, here replaced by forografiche images. The only other difference is that to take the place of snowballs there are footballs.

At the end of the game a screen with seven half-naked girls and the words Thank Snow Brothers.
Snowball
The "Snowball" fruit machine refers to classic UK pub gaming hardware produced by JPM (Jones Pocket Meters).
Soccer (Ramtek)

Soccer is a Pong variant with a soccer theme. 2 or 4 players can compete in a game of soccer, bouncing a ball across the screen with their paddles. When the ball enters the goal the scoring team wins a point.
Soccer (Taito)

Soccer was an early team sport video game, and an early video game to be based on soccer, specifically association soccer. Soccer was also a ball-and-paddle game, but with a green background to simulate a playfield, allowed each player to control both a forward and a goalkeeper, and let them adjust the size of the players who were represented as paddles on screen. Nishikado claims Soccer to be "Japan's first video game" .

Taito's soccer features two different cabinet. A Standart and a Deluxe.

There is a game of the same name released in the same year by Ramtek, but there are two different games.
Soccer Brawl

In the future, soccer is in a state of decline as attendances grow smaller while hooliganism is rising. The authorities have decided to allow the players on the pitch to win by any means including fighting and using weapons to attract the fans back. Eight countries of seven players which include England, Germany, Spain, USA, Japan, Brazil, Korea and Italy compete in a league to be the best in the world.
